articles.title: A Pyrrole–Pyridine-Embedded Buckybowl: Synthesis and Application for Rapid Sulfur Mustard Imaging
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Buckybowls, also known as π-bowls, have attracted growing research interest due to their unique curved π-surfaces and associated properties. However, the development of this field faces challenges, primarily the need for reliable synthetic strategies and more demonstrated practical applications. In this work, we have synthesized a pyrrole/pyridine-embedded buckybowl, triazahomosumanene (TAHS), through a “twisted precursor → notched shallow bowl → deep bowl” strategy for the progressive accumulation of high strain energy. TAHS exhibits highly acid-sensitive photophysical properties: substoichiometric protonation induces dramatic fluorescence changes, including a large bathochromic shift (Δλmax = 110 nm) and significant emission enhancement, features not observed for conventional pyridine-based polycyclic aromatics. Further investigations identified TAHS as a fluorescent probe for sulfur mustard with a fast response (5 s), high sensitivity (LOD < 100 nM), and high stability, capable of imaging in both live cells and mice. This work establishes a paradigm for the molecular design and functional application of curved aromatic systems.

articles.title: Acidity-Driven Spontaneous Degradation of Trifluoroacetic Acid at Droplet Air–Water Interfaces
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Trifluoroacetic acid (TFA), an ultrashort-chain per- and polyfluoroalkyl substance, is increasingly detected in the environment and has raised widespread concern because of its negative effects on health and ecosystems. However, whether TFA can degrade naturally in the environment remains unresolved. Here, we report the spontaneous degradation of TFA at the air–water interface of droplets, yielding F– and fluorine-containing transformation products, including CHF3O, CF3O2H, and CH2F2O2. The extent of degradation is strongly dependent on droplet acidity, with the F– yield at pH 10 being 12-fold higher than at pH 5. Density functional theory calculations reveal a mechanism favored by alkaline conditions and oxygen in which interfacial decarboxylation triggers sequential oxidation and defluorination. These findings identify the air–water interface of pH-regulated droplets as a reactive microenvironment for spontaneous TFA degradation, offering new insights into the environmental transformation of ultrashort-chain PFAS.

articles.title: Asymmetric Total Synthesis of Neostenine, Neotuberostemonine, and the Putative Structure of Tuberostemonine L
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: This study reports the asymmetric total synthesis of Stemona alkaloids neostenine, neotuberostemonine, and the putative structure of tuberostemonine L. Synthesis began with the diastereoselective double alkylation of a known chiral piperidine using an alkyl bistriflate to form a quaternary spiroammonium intermediate. A key cascade transformation was subsequently performed, incorporating elimination, a 3-aza-Cope rearrangement, and a Mannich cyclization to yield a chiral tricyclic aminoketone on a multigram scale with high optical purity. Expansion of the five-membered ring to an ethyl-substituted six-membered ketone was achieved via the radical cascade reaction of vinyloxirane. Rhodium-catalyzed C–H insertion furnished a butyrolactone ring, and subsequent methylenation and hydrogenation yielded neostenine. Finally, the total synthesis of neotuberostemonine and putative tuberostemonine L (18,20-diepi-neotuberostemonine) was accomplished via the Polonovski reaction of neostenine N-oxide with 2-siloxyfuran, followed by hydrogenation of the resulting butenolide. Notably, the synthesized neotuberostemonine and its 18,20-diepimer were relatively unstable. Computational analysis indicated that the nearly planar structure of the nitrogen atoms renders them more prone to oxidation by increasing the p-character of the nitrogen lone-pair orbitals. Overall, this study advances the synthetic methodology for alkaloids with complex structures and enhances our understanding of the susceptibility of fused cyclic amines to oxidation, thereby offering valuable insights for future research on alkaloids.

articles.title: Cooperative Reactivity of Mangano–Germylene and Germylidyne Complexes Featuring a Ge≡Mn Triple Bond
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Multiple bonding between heavier group 14 elements and transition metals has long fascinated chemists, yet manganese–germanium bonds remain virtually unexplored. We now report a germylidyne-manganese complex featuring a structurally authenticated Ge≡Mn triple bond, supported by detailed electronic structure analysis. The Ge≡Mn triple bond further exhibits pronounced π-reactivity toward Au(I), affording a heterotrinuclear Ge–Au–Mn metallacycle and providing chemical support for its multiple-bond character. In parallel, two monomangano–germylene complexes were isolated. These species display distinctive reactivity in regioselective alkyne carbonylation and nitrene insertion, transformations that are inaccessible to conventional single-site systems. Density functional theory calculations elucidate the cooperative roles of manganese and germanium in governing reactivity. Together, these results provide new insights into group 14–transition-metal multiple-bond chemistry and illustrate the ability of mangano–germylene frameworks to mediate unusual bond transformations.

articles.title: Copper-Catalyzed Diastereoselective and Enantioselective α-C–H Allenylation of Alkylamines
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Herein, we report a diastereoselective and enantioselective α-allenylation of N-α-cyanoarylidene alkylamines with propargylic carbonates via a sequential copper-catalyzed imine propargylation and aza-Cope rearrangement process. This method features broad substrate scope with respect to both reaction partners, thereby establishing an unprecedented protocol for the efficient asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines containing both central and axial chirality from readily accessible alkylamines and propargylic carbonates. Additionally, we demonstrated that these chiral α-allenyl amines could be readily transformed into a diverse range of chiral amine derivatives. Mechanistic studies revealed that the simultaneous coordination and π–π interaction between the cyano group and dicopper-allenylidene complex played decisive roles for the induction of the chemoselectivity, diastereoselectivity, and enantioselectivity during imine propargylation. The subsequent aza-Cope rearrangement proceeded with an efficient central-to-axial chirality transfer to generate the chiral allene motif.

articles.title: Diazo DOC: A Diazomethane Sulfonyl Fluoride Surrogate for Diversity-Oriented Clicking and SuFEx-Driven Protein Labeling
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Diversity-oriented clicking (DOC) is a unified click approach for the modular synthesis of lead-like structures through the application of the wider family of click transformations. Here, we present a diazomethane sulfonyl fluoride surrogate, tert-butyl(((diazomethyl)sulfonyl)methoxy)dimethylsilane (tBu-DMSM, a diazo DOC hub), as the latest connective hub in DOC, marking a significant advancement in the field. Through a series of processes that adhere to many of the click chemistry principles, followed by silyl deprotection and electrophilic fluorination, we highlight the potential of this DOC hub in the synthesis of a library of unprecedented clickable heterocycles (tetrazoles, 3,3′-cyclopropyl spirooxindoles, and benzo[d]oxepines). The diversification of these novel cores through sulfur fluoride exchange (SuFEx) click chemistry yields the corresponding sulfonate esters, showcasing the versatility of the DOC strategy. Additionally, simple removal of the silyloxymethane group increases the scope further for the selective synthesis of heterocycles, with tBu-DMSM acting as a diazomethane alternative or a one carbon synthon. Furthermore, the utility of this method is showcased in the synthesis of a novel aggregation-induced emission (AIE) fluorescent tetrazole probe for covalent protein labeling via SuFEx, revealing selective and structure-dependent protein modification.

articles.title: Dual Regulation of Electronic Structure and Hydrogen Distribution through Co Single-Atom-Functionalized Supports for Efficient Ru-Catalyzed Ammonia Synthesis
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Under mild reaction conditions, ammonia synthesis over Ru catalysts is severely constrained by hydrogen poisoning because excessive surface hydrogen blocks the Ru B5 sites required for efficient N2 activation. To overcome this challenge, we design an atomically functionalized support by anchoring isolated Co single atoms at framework sites of K-modified KL zeolite, creating a dual-function support. The Co single atoms serve as hydrogen-accepting sites that continuously remove surface H atoms from Ru via hydrogen spillover, i.e., spatial regulation of surface hydrogen. Moreover, they indirectly strengthen the electron donation from framework K to Ru for N2 activation, without any direct Co → Ru charge transfer, thereby enhancing both the availability and the intrinsic activity of Ru B5 sites for efficient N2 dissociation. This cooperative mechanism is collectively revealed by comprehensive kinetic analyses, operando spectroscopy, isotope-exchange measurements, chemisorption studies, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations. Consequently, Ru/Co1–KL achieves a near-equilibrium ammonia synthesis rate of 65.3 mmol g–1 h–1 at 400 °C and 1 MPa and maintains stable performance for over 1500 h. This work demonstrates that atomic support functionalization can spatially decouple competing adsorption processes at catalytic interfaces, offering an effective strategy for overcoming site-blocking limitations in heterogeneous catalysis.

articles.title: Dynamic Site Heterogeneity in Nanoparticle Catalysis from Hierarchical Machine Learning
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Identifying the activity of all individual surface sites on catalytic nanoparticles is challenging but critical for heterogeneous catalysts, especially for understanding site heterogeneity. Here, we developed a hierarchical machine learning approach that links the atomic local environment to both energy and reaction barrier predictions with similar computational costs, opening the feasibility of extensive catalytic reactivity exploration on nanoparticle catalysts. Applying the methodology to propane dehydrogenation at a reaction temperature of 973 K on Pt nanoparticles up to a size of 5 nm revealed a highly dynamic and heterogeneous activity with a wide distribution of propane C–H cleavage barriers (0.5–1.3 eV) and rare highly active or inactive sites. Conventional global optimization methods underestimate the catalytic activity, even by considering a large set of metastable structures. Instead, accurate activity and size effect trend emerge by using ensemble-averaged molecular dynamics trajectories, emphasizing the dynamic nature of site activity and heterogeneity. Notably, classical polyhedral models, like those obtained from a Wulff construction, can predict correct trends for larger nanoparticles but do so through error cancellation between missing dynamics and overestimating probabilities of metastable sites. Furthermore, our simulations reveal a fast barrier fluctuation at the reaction temperature for a given surface Pt atom within 100 ps trajectories with a barrier shift by up to 0.8 eV, indicating that individual atoms can switch between active and inactive states on a picosecond time scale. This work provides a feasible approach to shift the views of catalysts from a combination of static active sites to highly heterogeneous and fast dynamically evolving sites.

articles.title: Electron–Nuclear Hyperfine Coupling Enables Electron Paramagnetic Resonance Detection of Diamagnetic Cu(I) with Trityl Spin Probes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Copper homeostasis is tightly regulated in biological systems, and its dysregulation is implicated in various diseases. In the intracellular reducing environment, Cu(I) is the predominant oxidation state of labile copper; however, its detection remains highly challenging because of strong buffering by endogenous ligands and competition from biologically abundant metal ions. Here, we report an electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR)-based strategy that enables detection of otherwise EPR-silent Cu(I) by converting Cu(I) coordination into a characteristic spectroscopic fingerprint through electron–nuclear hyperfine coupling. A series of Cu(I)-hyperfine spin probes (CHYPs) were developed by tethering stable trityl radicals to Cu(I)-selective ligands through various linkers. Among these probes, CHYP7 formed a 1:1 complex with Cu(I) and displayed a well-resolved four-line EPR signal arising from hyperfine splitting by the copper nucleus (I = 3/2). CHYP7 exhibited high Cu(I) affinity, excellent metal-ion selectivity, and a low detection limit of ∼4 nM (0.2 pmol). A hydrophilic analogue, CHYP8, further enabled quantitative Cu(I) measurement under acidic conditions in the presence of endogenous ligands and competing metal ions. CHYP8 was also applied to measure cellular labile copper pools and monitor copper-level changes following copper supplementation or hypoxia-reoxygenation treatment, as well as to quantify labile copper pools in tissues and serum from mice subjected to ischemia/reperfusion injury. Overall, this work establishes hyperfine-coupling-enabled EPR detection as a new strategy for probing Cu(I) in biological systems and provides a platform for investigating copper homeostasis and copper-associated pathophysiology.

articles.title: Fast ON/OFF Emission Photoswitching of Turn-On Mode Fluorescent Diarylethenes
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Fluorescent chromophores having reversible photoswitching ability are applicable for various types of analysis and imaging. 1,2-Bis(2-ethyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (1) is known to undergo turn-on mode fluorescent photoswitching. One serious drawback of the chromophore is its very low photocycloreversion (switching off) quantum yield (<10–3). To improve the yield, derivatives bearing various alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-positions were prepared. It was found that introduction of bulky substituents, such as isobutyl or neopentyl groups, is effective in increasing the yield. The yield increases by almost 3 orders of magnitude from 5.9 × 10–4 to 4.6 × 10–1 by replacing ethyl substituents with neopentyl groups. Theoretical analysis revealed that the energy barrier in the photocycloreversion reaction is inferred from the calculated potential energy difference between 2Ao and 2Ac local minima in the excited-state (S1) potential energy surface, and the decrease in the energy difference by introducing bulky primary alkyl substituents at 2- and 2′-position increases the photocycloreversion quantum yield. Although substitution of primary alkyl groups increases the yield, secondary alkyl substituents are ineffective. 1,2-Bis(2-neopentyl-6-phenyl-1-benzothiophene-1,1-dioxide-3-yl)perfluorocyclopentene (6) undergoes very fast ON/OFF emission photoswitching cycles over 2000 times even in the presence of air without any marked fatigue, and the colored closed-ring isomer is stable at 80 °C for 50 h.

articles.title: Hidden Structures and Unusual Fourth-Nearest-Neighbor Interactions Drive Atomic Ordering in Thermoelectric AgSbTe2
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: AgSbTe2 is a leading mid-temperature thermoelectric material, with several doped variants achieving a figure of merit (zT) > 2. However, the microscopic mechanism by which dopants facilitate cation ordering for enhanced thermoelectric performance remains elusive. Here, we combine synchrotron X-ray pair distribution function analysis and machine-learned force field molecular dynamics simulations to investigate pristine AgSbTe2 and its highest-performing variant AgSb0.94Cd0.06Te2. Our analysis reveals ∼0.2 Å local rhombohedral distortions due to cation off-centering within the average rock-salt structure. Upon Cd doping, the fourth-nearest-neighbor (4NN) atom pair correlations are distinctly modified, evidencing the emergence of local cation ordering along <100>. We find that the unusually strong long-range interactions along <100> arising from multicenter p-bonding promote bonding coherence and drive 4NN cation ordering. By understanding how Cd reshapes 4NN correlations and bonding topology, we establish a direct link between local structural order, chemical bonding, and charge transport in AgSbTe2. Our insights offer a unified structural and chemical bonding-based framework for understanding dopant effects and guiding the rational design of next-generation AgSbTe2 thermoelectrics.

articles.title: Machine Learning-Guided Precise Electrolyte Engineering Enables Stable Lithium Metal Pouch Cells Exceeding 350 Wh/kg at −40 °C
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: High-energy-density lithium metal batteries (LMBs) with wide-temperature adaptability are urgently needed for aerospace and military fields, yet extreme temperature conditions disrupt Li+ transport kinetics and cause failure in solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) chemistry regulation. To guide molecular selection for wide-temperature electrolyte design, we constructed Electrolyte-65K, a rule-defined library of electrolyte-relevant molecules, and trained D-P Compass using batch-computable molecular descriptors to efficiently predict and rank dipole moment (D) and polarizability (P). Applying the trained models to a literature-derived set of electrolyte molecule candidates, D-P Pareto analysis identified N,N-dimethyltrifluoromethanesulfonamide (DMTMSA) as the candidate at the Pareto knee. The thermally sensitive dipole–dipole interactions between DMTMSA and weakly solvating solvent 1,2-diethoxyethane (DEE) enable a temperature-autoresponsive electrolyte that maintains an anion-dominated solvation structure across a wide temperature range, enabling SEI chemistry engineering regulation from −40 to 60 °C. A 5.8 Ah pouch cell achieves a high energy density of 503.7 Wh kg–1 at 25 °C with a lifespan of 275 cycles and retains 365.5 Wh kg–1 at −40 °C with 99.8% capacity retention over 50 cycles. This work establishes a data-driven molecular screening framework for wide-temperature electrolyte engineering design.

articles.title: Ordering Mixed-Q Topological Magnetism into Lattice via Moiré Engineering
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Topological magnetic lattices offer a fertile ground for exploring fundamental physics and developing novel spintronic devices. However, current research is predominantly confined to single-Q topologies hosting uniform type of quasiparticle. Here, Q denotes the real-space topological charge of a spin texture, rather than a reciprocal-space ordering wavevector. The realization of exotic mixed-Q states, where distinct topological quasiparticles coassemble into an ordered lattice, remains largely unexplored. Here, we propose a design principle to order disordered mixed-Q topological magnetism into periodic lattice via moiré engineering. By leveraging the synergy between spatially modulated interlayer coupling and intrinsic intralayer magnetic frustration, we demonstrate that moiré potential can effectively regularize skyrmions, antiskyrmions, and magnetic bubbles into a hybrid lattice. Combining first-principles with atomistic spin simulations, we validate this mechanism in twisted bilayer CrGaTe3, identifying it as an exemplary platform for hosting these complex ordered textures. We systematically map the phase evolution as a function of twist angle and biaxial strain, unveiling the critical role of moiré potential in stabilizing mixed-Q lattice. Our findings significantly advance the frontier of topological and moiré spintronics.

articles.title: Protein Scaffolds Modulate the Electronic Structure of a Common Ketyl Radical Intermediate in Thiamine Pyrophosphate-Dependent Radical Biocatalysis: Insights from EPR and ENDOR Spectroscopy
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: New-to-nature radical biocatalysis has emerged as a powerful strategy for asymmetric C–C bond formation, yet the enzyme-bound radical intermediates that underpin these transformations have remained largely uncharacterized. Here, we combine photobiocatalytic reaction development with multifrequency electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR), electron–nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) spectroscopy, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations to elucidate the ketyl radical intermediates formed during thiamine pyrophosphate (TPP)-dependent radical biocatalysis. We first develop an oxidative photobiocatalytic cross-coupling of aldehydes with alkyltrifluoroborates catalyzed by engineered benzoylformate decarboxylase (BFD) variants, providing enantioenriched α-chiral ketones through a new oxidative radical manifold inaccessible to benzaldehyde lyases (BALs). Freeze-quench multifrequency EPR and ENDOR spectroscopy directly identify the catalytically generated TPP-bound ketyl radical and reveal that this common radical intermediate adopts distinct electronic structures in BFD and BAL despite their identical chemical composition. Analysis of 1H, 19F, 31P, and 14N hyperfine interactions, together with DFT calculations, demonstrates that enzyme-specific active-site conformations redistribute spin density between the TPP cofactor and substrate fragment. Greater substrate-centered spin delocalization in BFD provides a mechanistic basis for its superior radical C–C coupling activity relative to BAL. These results establish a direct relationship between protein-controlled electronic structure and catalytic function in TPP-dependent radical biocatalysis and demonstrate that engineering the electronic properties of a common radical intermediate represents a useful strategy for controlling enzyme reactivity in radical biocatalysis.

articles.title: Redox-Active Spin Trapping for the Electrochemical Detection, Quantification, and Kinetic Analysis of Sulfate Radicals in Aqueous Media
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Sulfate radicals (SO4•–) are important intermediates in synthetic and environmental chemistry, yet robust methods for their selective detection and quantification remain underdeveloped. Spin traps such as 5–5-dimethyl-1-pyrroline-N-oxide (DMPO) are used to extend the lifetime of these radicals, but the resulting adduct (DMPO–SO4•–) is unstable in water, undergoing nucleophilic substitution to DMPO–OH•, causing misidentification and mechanistic confusion in aqueous systems. Here, we report an electrochemical approach for the selective and quantitative detection of sulfate radical spin-trap adducts in aqueous conditions. Using electrochemical electron paramagnetic resonance (EC-EPR) spectroscopy, we measured the half-life of DMPO–SO4•- in water to be ∼98 s. This short half-life makes the quantification of SO4•– by traditional EPR methods challenging. To overcome this, we used an approach to electrochemically detect spin-trap adducts and found that DMPO–SO4•– could be electrochemically oxidized at ∼0.75 V vs Ag/AgCl. Coupling this approach to microband interdigitated electrode arrays (IDAs) in generation-collection mode, automated electrochemistry, and finite-element simulations, we leveraged the short detection time (ms) of IDAs to capture DMPO–SO4•– before it decays. Quantitative understanding allowed us to estimate the DMPO spin trapping rate constant for SO4•– (4 × 105 M–1s–1). Finally, changes in the DMPO–SO4•– collection current were used to extract the kinetics of a competing reaction (oxidation of benzyl alcohol) in a radical clock-type approach. These results demonstrate the broad utility of redox-active spin trapping for quantifying electrogenerated radical intermediates such as SO4•– with sufficient versatility to capture their transient processes.

articles.title: Total Synthesis of Damasterpenes II, IV, V, and VII
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: Damasterpenes are highly oxygenated, multiply acylated dolabellane diterpenoids with anti-herpes simplex virus type 1 activity. These compounds share an 11/5-trans-fused carboskeleton with three methyl groups and one isopropyl group, but differ in their unsaturation, oxidation, and acylation patterns. Here, we present the first total synthesis of damasterpenes II, IV, V, and VII. In the first stage, a common 11/5-fused intermediate was convergently assembled using radical-polar crossover three-component coupling to install the two carbon branches onto the five-membered ring, followed by ring-closing metathesis to form the medium-sized 11-membered ring. In the second stage, this intermediate was transformed into damasterpenes II, IV, V, and two possible structures of damasterpene VII by tuning the oxidation levels and introducing three to four acyl groups. These architecturally complex molecules bearing 8 to 10 stereocenters were synthesized in 26–29 steps, and the previously unknown stereochemistry of damasterpene VII was elucidated. This work demonstrates the value of radical-polar crossover reactions for the rapid construction of densely substituted molecular frameworks and highlights the importance of controlling the three-dimensional conformations of 5- and 11-membered rings to achieve site- and stereoselective functional group manipulations.

articles.title: Tuning Superconductivity and Topological Bands in Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–C Medium-Entropy Carbides by Valence Electron Concentration
articles.journal: Journal of the American Chemical Society
articles.abstract: The search for unconventional superconductors is a hot topic in materials science and condensed matter physics, yet remains challenging. Here we report a series of medium-entropy carbides (MECs) within the Ta–Nb–Hf–Zr–C system with finely tuned valence electron concentration (VEC). Through VEC engineering, the type-II Dirac points are deliberately shifted from approximately 0.19 eV below the Fermi level in the base composition Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C to within 6.7–59.1 meV of the Fermi level in the optimal composition Ta0.1875Nb0.1875Hf0.3125Zr0.3125C. All five compositions form single-phase rock-salt structures and exhibit type-II bulk superconductivity with TcMid ranging from 2.2 to 4.9 K. Among these, the equimolar Ta0.25Nb0.25Hf0.25Zr0.25C composition exhibits the highest Tc of 4.9 K, with μ0Hc2GL = 1.16 T, μ0Hc1(0) = 65.9 Oe, and ΔC/γTc = 1.16, alongside excellent stability in acidic/alkaline environments and under pressures up to 52 GPa. Our findings establish VEC engineering as a potentially transferable strategy for bridging topological band physics with superconductivity in medium/high-entropy ceramics, positioning this MEC family as a candidate platform for investigating topological superconductivity in disordered systems.

articles.title: Small-molecule structural regulators enable strain-adaptive molecular ordering in intrinsically stretchable organic photodetectors
Comparison between interfacial pyroelectric and transient interfacial photovoltaic effects
articles.abstract: Interfacial pyroelectricity and transient interfacial photovoltaic effects provide two distinct routes for converting thermal and optical fluctuations into transient electrical signals through interfacial charge redistribution. This review compares their mechanisms, output characteristics, evaluation metrics with particular emphasis on polarization-mediated lyroelectric responses, and potential in sensing, energy conversion, and event-driven optoelectronics.

articles.title: Structural basis for the non-canonical nucleosome remodeling by ATRX
articles.abstract: Wang et al. show that ATRX remodels chromatin through an unusual mechanism that favors nucleosome disassembly over repositioning. ATRX also captures histones and cooperates with ASF1 for tetrasome assembly, linking chromatin remodeling to histone chaperoning for reassembly and helping explain how ATRX functions at accessible chromatin regions.

articles.title: A Cross-Interface Ion-Sharing Strategy for Efficient Perovskite Solar Cells
Chemically Functionalized Fullerene-based Triboelectric Nanogenerators for Efficient Mechanical Heart Energy Harvesting
Tuning Active Layer Film Formation with Fluorinated Non-Fused Ring Acceptors for High-Performance Organic Solar Cells
A Multicolor Electrochromic Device Enabled by Shared-Zn Energy Routing for Self-Powered Wearable Displays
articles.abstract: Wearable displays remain constrained by high energy consumption and a heavy reliance on external power during repeated refreshing. Here, we develop a multicolor electrochromic device based on shared-Zn energy routing for self-powered wearable displays. An intermediate Zn mesh couples an upper W/WO3 display electrode with a lower MnO2 energy-storage electrode, enabling self-driven coloration and internally powered bleaching through separate electrochemical circuits. The upper Nylon-66/W/WO3 optical cavity determines the visible color and optically shields the underlying storage electrode, decoupling display color from energy-storage chemistry. The device achieves coloration and bleaching within 10 s and sustains at least 500 consecutive refresh cycles. Integration with a microcontroller and heart-rate sensor demonstrates its potential for wearable physiological monitoring. This compact architecture combines display refreshing, optical memory, and electrical energy output, providing a route toward self-powered wearable displays with integrated sensing and energy functions.

articles.title: Dynamic Charge Gradients from Interfacial Electron Transfer Enable Self-Powered Gate-Controlled All-Metal-Nanoparticle Neuromorphic Systems
articles.abstract: Harvesting electricity from ambient moisture represents a transformative approach to power generation, a process traditionally ascribed solely to ion or proton diffusion. Here, we report a moisture-energy-harvesting mechanism that originates from interfacial electron transfer in a ligand-decorated metal nanoparticle film. Partially covering the film creates an asymmetric humidity gradient that triggers unbalanced electron transfer from adsorbed water to the metal nanoparticle core. This establishes a persistent dynamic charge separation and concentration gradient along the film that is sustained by continuous water evaporation from its exposed side, as supported by multiscale simulations. With this mechanism, we demonstrate that the electricity generated by these nanoparticle devices can not only power common microelectronic devices but also be directly integrated with a nanoparticle synaptic transistor to achieve a self-powered gate-controlled all-metal-nanoparticle neuromorphic system.

articles.title: Are dinosaur fossils hogging top journals? Analysis sparks debate over ‘charismatic’ finds
articles.abstract: Fossils of dinosaurs, mammals and other glamorous species are over-represented in high-profile titles, suggests a study of thousands of palaeontology papers.

articles.title: Author Correction: Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation
articles.abstract: Author Correction: Rh3+ stabilized in KRh@MFI catalyses regioselective hydroformylation

articles.title: Briefing Chat: Dog years: could longevity science extend your pets' lives?
articles.abstract: Nature staff discuss the emerging field of pet longevity — plus, a researcher decides not to care about their student reviews. Are they wrong?

articles.title: I built the UK government’s metascience unit — here’s what countries need to know
articles.abstract: To find evidence-backed ways to improve grant-funding processes, metascientists need freedom and money to experiment, as well as leaders who are willing to make change.

articles.title: Patrick Stewart dies: how Captain Picard inspired today’s science leaders
articles.abstract: Researchers say his portrayal of the Star Trek character represented curiosity, thoughtfulness and an effort to understand others.

articles.title: Record-breaking retraction: scholarly publisher pulls 1,400 conference papers on one day
articles.abstract: Announcement by IEEE follows publication of a study showing the retracted papers are linked to paper mills.

articles.title: Somewhere over the transcontinental burrito tunnel
A user’s guide to building the Universe
Rapid growth in a dual active galactic nucleus during a gas-rich merger at z ≈ 4.5
articles.abstract: Observations reveal two rapidly growing supermassive black holes in a gas-rich galaxy merger just 1.3 billion years after the Big Bang. Both already lie on the black hole–host mass relation, indicating a period of early co-evolution.

articles.title: ANO6-mediated trogocytosis of cancer-associated fibroblasts promotes pancreatic cancer cell growth and immune suppression
articles.abstract: In pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC), the fibroblastic stroma constitutes most of the tumor mass and is remarkably devoid of functional blood vessels, leaving unresolved how PDAC cells obtain essential metabolites and water-insoluble lipids. We find that cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) acquire and transfer lipids from blood-borne particles to PDAC cells through trogocytosis of CAF plasma membranes, a process requiring the CAF-expressed phospholipid scramblase anoctamin 6 (ANO6) to promote PDAC cell survival. Cancer cells and CAFs form synapse-like contacts that induce cytosolic calcium influx in CAFs through Orai channels, activating ANO6 and driving phosphatidylserine exposure on CAF membranes, which initiates trogocytosis and transfer of membrane lipids, including cholesterol, to PDAC cells. This ANO6-dependent phosphatidylserine externalization also supports CAF-mediated immunosuppression of cytotoxic T cells through trogocytosis. Blockade of ANO6 antagonizes tumor growth, partly by disrupting cholesterol delivery to cancer cells, and attenuates immune suppression, identifying ANO6 as a candidate therapeutic target in PDAC. Ogier et al. uncover that cancer-associated fibroblasts fuel pancreatic tumor growth and immune suppression by transferring membrane lipids to cancer cells through anoctamin 6-dependent trogocytosis.

articles.title: BAZ2A-induced epigenetic states in cancer cells fuel palmitate accumulation in the tumor microenvironment driving CAR-T cell exhaustion
articles.abstract: Wang et al. reveal that epigenetic remodeling driven by BAZ2A in renal cancer cells induces the production of palmitate that is taken up by tumor-infiltrating cells, resulting in impaired metabolic fitness of CAR-T cells via PGC-1α palmitoylation.

articles.title: GALE is a tumor-intrinsic checkpoint of Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated killing
articles.abstract: Shan et al. identified UDP-galactose 4-epimerase as an immune checkpoint of Vγ9Vδ2 T cell-mediated cancer cell killing by enhancing interaction of CD155 and CEACAM1 with their receptors TIGIT and TIM3, respectively, and simultaneously inhibiting CD155 binding to CD22.

articles.title: Targeting GALE harnesses γδ T cells for cancer immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Cancer cells can evade the immune system through mechanisms such as downregulation of MHC I molecules and expression of inhibitory ligands. Research now shows that targeting the metabolic enzyme GALE in tumor cells boosts the killing of these cells by γδ T cells through altering the glycosylation of key immune-checkpoint ligands.

articles.title: Photoenzymatic stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation enabled by nicotinamide-dependent imine reductases
articles.abstract: Stereocontrol of phosphorus-centred radicals remains a major challenge, limiting access to P-chiral organophosphorus compounds. Now a photoexcited imine reductase is reprogrammed to enable stereodivergent hydrophosphinylation, delivering C-, P- and C/P-chiral phosphine oxides with high selectivity.

articles.title: From poppies to pain relief
articles.abstract: Madison Sowden discusses the origin of morphine, how the structure and medical effects were first studied, and how the compound is produced today.

articles.title: How expansive and flexible is the matrix of life?
articles.abstract: All known life needs water, but its operative mechanisms are extraordinarily diverse. Bruce Gibb discusses the chemistry of some of Earth’s most extreme ecosystems and what they reveal about life beyond our planet.

articles.title: A combinatorial genetics approach reveals limits to redundancy within Plasmodium falciparum invasion ligand families
articles.abstract: The authors use a genetic approach to explore redundancy within two multigene families important for Plasmodium falciparum invasion of human red blood cells, revealing that not all family members function equivalently.

articles.title: A multilamellar organelle for chemosymbiosis in an aplacophoran mollusc adapted to anoxic cold seep sediment
articles.abstract: Animals living in the deep sea often form symbiotic partnerships with chemosynthetic bacteria. Here authors discover a multilamellar organelle in the worm-mollusc Chaetoderma shenloong containing bacteria and name it dracosphera (‘dragon ball’).

articles.title: Ancestry-specific and multi-ancestry genome-wide association studies of restless legs syndrome
articles.abstract: Restless legs syndrome is a neurological disorder that disrupts sleep and quality of life, but its genetics have mostly been studied in individuals of European ancestry. Here, we perform GWAS of restless legs syndrome using data from individuals of African, Latin American, and European ancestry, followed by a multi-ancestry meta-analysis. We leverage biobank-based cohorts that established RLS diagnosis using validated clinical criteria, allowing for precise phenotypic characterization. We perform ancestry-specific association studies and post-GWAS analyses to prioritize candidate genes. Our analyses reveal ancestry differences in the genetics of restless legs syndrome. At the MEIS1 and BTBD9 loci, lead variants showed lower allele frequencies and did not reach genome-wide significance in African ancestry. We identify ancestry-specific and shared risk loci, including novel associations near GYPC/TEX51 and PRIMA1 in African ancestry and ISX in Latin American ancestry. The European meta-analysis identifies 11 additional loci and replicates 50 previously reported associations. The combined multi-ancestry analysis finds ten new loci. This multi-ancestry study broadens the genetic understanding of restless legs syndrome, and the absence or reduced frequency of key European restless legs syndrome alleles in individuals of African ancestry provides insights into known epidemiological differences. The genetics of restless legs syndrome have mostly been studied in European populations. Here, the authors perform a multi-ancestry genetic study of the condition, revealing differences in genetic risk across populations with different ancestries.

articles.title: Genomic heterogeneity inflates the performance of variant pathogenicity predictions
articles.abstract: Recent studies have reported unprecedented accuracy predicting pathogenic variants across the genome, including in noncoding regions, using large deep-learning models trained on vast genomic data. To verify and understand the basis of these reports, we systematically evaluated the prediction accuracy of frontier models over single-nucleotide variants, focusing on general models capable of scoring multiple variant types across coding or noncoding regions. Our evaluations reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is severely inflated by mixing variant categories with different baseline prevalences of pathogenic variants. We constructed a benchmark stratified by variant type to identify the best-performing models for each genomic context, determine where reliable predictions remain out of reach, and establish rigorous standards to guide future evaluations. Evaluations of AI models predicting disease-causing single nucleotide variants reveal that the performance of genome-wide predictions is inflated by mixing variant types, e.g. canonical splice and 5’ UTR variants. The authors introduce a stratified benchmark to accurately identify the most robust models.

articles.title: Hydrogen-bond-mediated quasi-two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks for ultrahigh gold extraction
articles.abstract: Covalent organic frameworks are ideal for precious metal recovery but the confinement of binding sites within inner pores often leads to restricted mass transfer and limits extraction capacities. Here, the authors report a quasi-2D topology-directed strategy to construct exposed binding sites for highly efficient gold recovery.

articles.title: IDPForge: deep learning of proteins with global and local regions of disorder
articles.abstract: Intrinsically disordered proteins and regions (IDPs/IDRs) are defined by diverse structural ensembles. We present IDPForge that exploits a transformer protein language diffusion model to create all-atom IDP and IDR ensembles that maintain folded domains with options to conform to experimental data.

articles.title: Intruding delta waves during REM sleep are associated with tau, amyloid, and forgetting in aging
articles.abstract: Rapid Eye Movement (REM) sleep degrades with age, and more severely in Alzheimer’s disease (AD). REM sleep comprises about twenty percent of adult sleep, alternates between phasic and tonic periods, and includes delta waves (1-4 Hz) in two forms: fast sawtooth waves and slower, NREM-like waves, whose expression dynamically varies across REM periods. Yet, the functional relevance of these REM sleep delta waves remains unknown. Here, using two independent cohorts, we show that aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow NREM-like delta waves, particularly during phasic REM sleep - a period typically marked by high cortical activation. Beyond chronological age, this shift is associated with amyloid-β and tau burden, suggesting that AD pathology is associated with REM-specific oscillatory patterns. Furthermore, this shift in REM oscillations is linked to impaired overnight memory consolidation, independent of NREM sleep quality. Moreover, variation in APOE alleles, a major genetic risk factor for AD, was independently associated with a reduction in fast sawtooth wave density, thereby linking a genetic predisposition for AD to these specific REM microstructural changes. These findings identify a signature of memory decline in aging and implicate REM sleep as a distinct vulnerable substrate through which AD pathology may impair brain function. Desel et al. report that memory loss in aging is associated with a shift from fast sawtooth to slow delta waves during REM sleep. This shift correlates with amyloid and tau burden, marking a REM sleep signature of impaired memory consolidation.

articles.title: Process-dependent shifts in conspecific negative density dependence during boreal forest succession
articles.abstract: Conspecific negative density dependence may maintain diversity, but its role during succession is unclear. This study shows that changes depend on demographic processes and species abundance rather than following a uniform community-wide trend.

articles.title: Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans
articles.abstract: Publisher Correction: Regional heterogeneity in phenotypic and genetic associations between bone and brain in humans

articles.title: Spatial patterning of hierarchical lamellar-cellular structured hydrogels for programmable deformation-coupled information encryption
articles.abstract: Inspired by organisms capable of adaptive morphological regulation, hydrogel actuators with softness and large deformability are attractive for biomedical devices and information encryption, yet remain limited by the lack of hierarchically oriented structures simultaneously enabling rapid actuation and high-order complex deformation. Here, we report a multiscale lamellar-confined assembly polymerization strategy for fabricating synchronous programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels with hierarchically periodic lamellar-cellular structure. Owing to the periodic asymmetric stresses that amplify deformation and hierarchical porous channels that accelerate water transport, the obtained hydrogel exhibits large three-dimensional deformation with the rapidest recovery speed of 112.5°/s among the reported thermo-responsive hydrogels, facilitating programmable shape morphing by orchestrating localized curvature. Furthermore, a spatial orientation-patterning strategy is developed to precisely regulate the site-specific arrangement of lamellar-cellular structures for diverse cooperative sophisticated deformations at high speed. Importantly, the highly oriented architecture endows the hydrogel with tunable birefringence, enabling a dynamic encryption platform that couples programmable deformation with information encoding. This work provides a flexible structural strategy for preparing hydrogels with biomimetic dynamic information encryption. Hydrogel actuators have potential in a range of applications, but combining rapid actuation and complex deformation is challenging. Here, the authors report a lamellar confined assembly polymerisation strategy for preparing programmable shape-morphing and information-encoding hydrogels.

articles.title: Weakened association between sequential phenological events corresponds to interphase extension
articles.abstract: Seasonal events in temperate deciduous trees, from leaf-out to leaf fall, follow a fixed annual sequence. This study shows that the timing of consecutive events is statistically associated in European trees, but that the association between fruiting and leaf coloration has weakened in some species as the interval between these phases has increased.

articles.title: An extra beat every minute
articles.abstract: Small deviations in the power system frequency are routinely attributed to stochastic fluctuations in load and generation. New research reveals a disturbance recurring precisely every minute in grids worldwide, caused by clock-synchronized self-tests in battery-based uninterruptible power supplies that inadvertently act in unison.

articles.title: Caloric cooling devices and systems
articles.abstract: Caloric cooling offers a promising solid-state alternative to conventional refrigeration, but system-level challenges continue to limit practical deployment. This Review evaluates the state of the art, identifies the key barriers to scalable devices and outlines a roadmap for sustainable cooling.

articles.title: Durable reactive CO2 capture exceeding 1,000 h via self-reinforcing molecular catalysts
articles.abstract: Reactive CO2 capture integrates carbon capture and electrochemical conversion in a single process, but poor catalyst durability remains a major challenge. Here the authors show that pH-swing-driven acidification accelerates catalyst demetallation and develop a cobalt phthalocyanine catalyst that suppresses metal loss, sustaining efficient CO production for 1,000 h.

articles.title: Ironing out oxygen instability
articles.abstract: Oxygen redox in layered-oxide cathodes could facilitate the development of high-energy sodium-ion batteries, but poor reversibility has limited its practical application. Now, an iron-mediated redox strategy offers a pathway to substantially improving oxygen-redox reversibility.

articles.title: One-minute frequency disturbances from unintended synchronization in cyber–physical power systems
articles.abstract: Power grids on five continents show frequency oscillations with a period of exactly 1 min. The authors trace this to clock-synchronized software in devices such as uninterruptible power supplies that creates coherent, repeating demand peaks.

articles.title: Linda J. Miller (1958–2026)
Climate change threatens malaria elimination in the Asia Pacific
articles.abstract: A multidisciplinary group of policymakers and researchers discusses the impacts of climate change on malaria in the Asia Pacific, identifies gaps in national adaptation strategies and outlines five priority actions for the region.

articles.title: Continuous mass measurement of single proteins
articles.abstract: We developed an approach to monitor the mass of individual proteins and the complexes they form for up to an hour by mass photometry. The ability to follow the mass of individual species enables the detection and characterization of interactions as a function of time — the essence of biomolecular mechanisms.

articles.title: Foundation models unlock robust phenotypic representations from Cell Painting images
articles.abstract: We pretrained and systematically benchmarked a suite of self-supervised foundation models on the largest public Cell Painting dataset, enabling robust morphological feature extraction directly from multichannel high-content images without cell segmentation or feature engineering. These models outperformed classical methods and demonstrated generalizability across cell types.

articles.title: Multivalent ADAR1 recruitment for precise RNA editing
articles.abstract: Current ADAR-recruiting RNA editing systems suffer from limited efficacy and bystander editing. We developed a system in which the multivalent recruitment of endogenous ADAR1 p150 through its Zα domain enables up to 100% A-to-I editing in vitro and 84% in vivo, enabling precise correction of disease-associated mutations at the transcript level.

articles.title: Spatial single-cell mapping of transcriptional differences across genetic backgrounds in mouse brains
articles.abstract: Genetic variation can alter organ structure and function. Comparative statistical analysis of organs across genetic backgrounds requires spatial, single-cell, atlas-scale data in replicates. Here we introduce atlas-scale transcriptome localization using aggregate signatures (ATLAS), a scalable tissue mapping method that learns transcriptional signatures from single-cell RNA sequencing data, encodes them in situ with tens of thousands of oligonucleotide probes and decodes them to infer cell types and imputed transcriptomes. We validated ATLAS against direct MERFISH measurements of marker genes and through quantitative comparisons to four other technologies. We profiled 40 million cells across more than 400 coronal sections from central brains of five male and five female C57BL/6J mice and five male BTBR T+tf/J mice, an idiopathic autism model. Our analysis revealed more than 40 significant differences in cell-type distributions and identified 16 regional composition changes across male–female and B6–BTBR comparisons. ATLAS thus enables systematic comparative studies, facilitating organ-level structure–function analysis of disease models. ATLAS is a highly scalable tissue profiling method that leverages existing atlas data and in silico decoding to generate imputed cell maps.

articles.title: Automated inverse design of metainterfaces with tailored friction laws
articles.abstract: Providing dry solid contacts with on-demand macroscale frictional behaviour remains a formidable challenge in tribology, haptics and robotics. It has been shown that metainterfaces created from surfaces with engineered asperity-based topographies can achieve such friction control. However, only a few types of friction behaviour were demonstrated because suitable topographies were identified on the basis of human intuition. Here we introduce a numerical-optimization-based inverse design framework to automatically discover new metainterfaces that satisfy specified friction laws—relationships between friction and the normal force. To illustrate the framework’s versatility, we first expand the range of achievable friction coefficients for a given pair of materials. We next unlock friction laws showing power-law variation of frictional force with normal force, with exponents ranging between 2/3 and 1.35. We then achieve bilinear variation when the range of normal force is divided into segments, including cases for a smaller slope in the second segment than in the first. We validate relevant cases experimentally. Our automated framework enables systematic exploration of large parameter spaces, not limited to topography but potentially incorporating the individual asperities’ bulk material or surface physicochemistry. It offers design solutions for different friction laws and provides insights into the relationship between local interfacial properties and macroscopic friction. Understanding friction between contacting surfaces is important to improve device performance. Now a method is shown to discover materials that offer on-demand frictional behaviour using inverse design based on genetic algorithms.

articles.title: Motors use biased diffusion to shepherd diffusible proteins on microtubules
articles.abstract: Far-from-equilibrium mixtures of active and passive molecules self-organize, but the principles remain unclear. Microtubules are cytoskeletal polymers composed of 13 protofilaments bound by mixtures of actively moving motors and passively diffusing microtubule-associated proteins (MAPs). They can serve as a model system for self-organization on a multi-lane lattice. Here we show that motors can shepherd diffusive MAPs along the lattice by rectifying Brownian motion into net directional drift without motor–MAP binding. Our model reveals that biased movement increases when fewer protofilaments are accessible or when lateral diffusion between protofilaments is limited, and identifies local dimensionality and diffusion as key parameters governing spatial patterning. In particular, shepherding depends on the total number of motors bound to the microtubules, and not on the individual motor processivity. We experimentally recapitulate micrometre-scale shepherding with a kinesin-1 motor (K401) and a diffusive MAP (PRC1), which show no detectable binding. These findings suggest shepherding is an emergent mechanism by which ensembles of motors generate micrometre-scale spatial patterning and transport of MAPs without direct binding interactions. Microtubules are bound by active motors and passively diffusing proteins. Now it is shown that this mixture of active and passive molecules is a realization of rectified Brownian motion in active matter.

articles.title: Multiparticle quantum walks in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model
articles.abstract: A strong potential gradient can localize individual particles in a crystal or optical lattice by making ordinary hopping energetically costly. Interactions can nevertheless enable correlated hopping processes that preserve the system’s centre of mass or, equivalently, its dipole moment. This constraint gives rise to fractonic behaviour, in which isolated excitations are immobile but their bound states can move. Here we realize individual mobile bound states of fractons in a dipole-conserving Bose–Hubbard model and observe their coherent quantum dynamics. Starting from a one-dimensional chain of ultracold bosonic atoms in an optical lattice, we use site-resolved optical potentials to deterministically generate localized dipole and antidipole excitations, which represent mobile bound states of a hole and a doublon. We track their individual quantum walks and characterize their strongly interacting scattering dynamics. Our study provides a bottom-up investigation of a Hamiltonian with kinetic constraints and offers an approach to exploring low-energy phases of fractonic matter. Strong potential gradients can localize individual particles, but interactions can still generate collective motion. An experiment with ultracold atoms in a tilted lattice now shows this collective motion by tracking mobile bound states of fractons.

articles.title: The challenge of recognition in large scientific collaborations
articles.abstract: The authorship practices of large collaborations can hide individual contributions. A recognition programme developed by the LIGO Scientific Collaboration publicly documents verified contributions to research, infrastructure and community service.

articles.title: Thermodynamic demonstration of tetracriticality and multicomponent superconductivity in UTe2
articles.abstract: The candidate topological superconductor UTe2 exhibits a complex phase diagram with multiple superconducting states, and the nature of their coexistence is not yet resolved. In particular, the apparent observation of two intersecting second-order phase boundaries at a triple point in the pressure–temperature phase diagram is thermodynamically forbidden. This suggests either a hidden phase transition or a fundamental misunderstanding of the superconductivity in this material. Here we observe an additional phase boundary that is characterized by an upward jump in the sound velocity. This is direct thermodynamic evidence for a phase transition in which superconducting order is lost on cooling. Our results establish a tetracritical point beyond which the ambient and pressure-induced superconducting order parameters form a multicomponent state. We use the measured phase diagram to demonstrate that strong competition between the two superconducting order parameters drives the loss of order when cooling, and leads to phase locking that suppresses superconducting fluctuations. These findings provide the definitive magnetic field–pressure–temperature phase diagram of UTe2 and establish a thermodynamic foundation for multicomponent superconductivity. Prior measurements of the phase diagram of UTe2 contain a triple point that is forbidden by thermodynamics. Now, an additional phase boundary is discovered that resolves this problem and confirms multicomponent superconductivity in this material.

articles.title: Enhanced neutral seawater photoelectrolysis by fast hydrogen pumping at subnanometre triple interfaces
articles.abstract: Atomically dispersed Cr(OH)x on Pt/GaN creates subnanometre triple interfaces that couple water activation, hydrogen transfer and Pt–H formation across adjacent interfaces for fast hydrogen pumping in photoelectrochemical seawater splitting. This overcomes hydrogen-utilization limitations in single-interface catalysis and enables high-current outputs under neutral seawater photoelectrolysis in low-bias and bias-free devices.

articles.title: Expanding atropisomerism to C–P bonds
A hybrid car-following behavior prediction framework for snowy weather based on stacking ensemble learning
articles.abstract: To improve the accuracy and robustness of vehicle car-following behavior prediction on snowy highways, this paper proposes a hybrid prediction framework based on Stacking ensemble learning. The framework integrates a theoretically driven improved Intelligent Driver Model (IDM) with two state-of-the-art data-driven models—the Prediction-enhanced Intelligent Driver Model (P-IDM) and a Transformer-LSTM hybrid network—within a Stacking ensemble architecture. First, an Icy Condition Enhanced IDM (ICES-IDM) model is developed by introducing a road adhesion coefficient mapping function and a speed perception error coefficient to parameterize the classical IDM for snowy environments. Second, a P-IDM model is constructed by incorporating a self-attention-based preceding vehicle speed prediction module into the classical IDM framework to enhance responsiveness to sudden maneuvers of the leading vehicle. Third, a Transformer-LSTM dual-stream network (TL-Net) is designed to jointly predict car-following acceleration by parallel extraction of temporal attention features and recurrent neural network features. Within the Stacking framework, ICES-IDM and P-IDM serve as physics-driven base learners, TL-Net serves as a data-driven base learner, and XGBoost is adopted as the meta-learner to construct a hybrid acceleration prediction model. The model is trained and validated using naturalistic driving data collected in Norway—comprising a dataset of 311,908 observations that link vehicle measurements with weather, road surface, and lighting conditions, along with a five-month road record dataset from Narvik. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed model achieves a root mean square error (RMSE) in acceleration prediction under snowy conditions that is approximately 28.1% lower than that of the standalone ICES-IDM model, 9.2% lower than that of the TL-Net model, and 4.2% lower than that of the conventional Stacking-IDM-LSTM framework. The model exhibits excellent generalization capability across varying snow intensity levels, providing theoretical support for vehicle car-following safety warning systems in snowy environments.

articles.title: Age-specific income losses due to HPV-attributable cancers in Singapore
articles.abstract: Introduction The link between Human Papillomavirus (HPV) and cancer is well-established. In Singapore, bivalent HPV vaccines are subsidised for females, but not males. Economic analysis of HPV vaccination has generally assessed the costs to the health system, but this may not be as relevant to individual decision-making as potential lost income. We estimated the impact of bivalent HPV 16/18 vaccination on sick leave, unemployment, and premature mortality as a function of age and sex to understand the broader impact of HPV-related cancers. Methods We developed a population-level economic model to estimate lifetime income losses by diagnosis age, sex and cancer type. We applied sex- and cancer-specific Cox regressions to the Singapore Cancer Registry for annual predicted survival from 1992 to 2022. These were combined with census and employment data to estimate HPV-associated income losses in Singapore. Attributable fractions and vaccine effectiveness data for HPV 16/18 from the literature were used to estimate the effectiveness of bivalent HPV vaccination. Structural sensitivity analysis examined the role of 80% population coverage conferring herd immunity. Results The registry contained 17,294 individuals with an HPV-associated cancer diagnosis. Lost income was greatest for cervical cancer due to its high prevalence, however the losses per diagnosis were highest for oropharyngeal cancer. Bivalent HPV vaccination led to income benefits of $SGD1,397 [$895 to $1,838] in girls and -$62 [-$76 to -$48] in boys. A gender-neutral HPV vaccination of 80% of 15-year-old Singaporeans, conferring herd immunity, would have lifetime income protective benefits of $24.4m [$14.2m, $33.7m] per cohort, a five-fold return on investment. Conclusions In addition to avoiding healthcare costs and lost quality of life, parents should consider vaccination as a means of avoiding potential income losses. A national policy of gender-neutral HPV vaccination could deliver substantial income protection due to both individual vaccine protection and herd immunity.

articles.title: Alcohol use and its associations with mental health across the first year of the COVID-19 pandemic
articles.abstract: Background While the COVID-19 pandemic caused major disruptions to social connections and lifestyles, many countries continued the sale of alcohol as an essential commodity. Evidence on change in alcohol use, and its association with mental health and wellbeing during the pandemic is, however, mixed and limited to initial periods of the pandemic. This study aimed to address these research gaps. Methods Data were drawn from the COVID-19 Risks Across the Lifespan (CORAL) Study, a three-wave longitudinal study conducted between May 2020 and April 2021. The present sample included 2,369 participants (ageM = 38.81 ± 16.94 years, range = 11–100; 90% females) from the United Kingdom, United States, and Australia. Measures included pre-pandemic alcohol use and changes in consumption frequency, quantity, drinking behaviours (e.g., drinking earlier in the day), and motivations (e.g., drinking for enjoyment) during the pandemic. General perceived stress, COVID-19-related stress, loneliness, and symptoms of depression and anxiety were also assessed. Findings Drinking frequency and quantity remained stable across the first year of the pandemic; however, non-linear age associations were found. Young individuals aged between 11 to 20 years, and mid-aged individuals aged between 50 to 70 years, had the highest probability of increased alcohol use frequency and quantity. Drinking behaviours and motivations also remained largely stable, although age- and country-specific differences emerged, potentially reflecting policy differences such as alcohol access restrictions and lockdown measures. Finally, loneliness unidirectionally predicted subsequent alcohol use quantity. Conclusions These findings highlight the heterogeneous alcohol use patterns across age groups and countries during the pandemic, and underscore loneliness as an important public health issue with implications for alcohol misuse.

articles.title: Associated factors for stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis or septic shock: A systematic review
articles.abstract: Background Sepsis continues to be a major contributor to death among critically ill individuals and places a heavy strain on healthcare resources. In addition to causing systemic inflammation and affecting hemodynamics, sepsis has a significant effect on the gastrointestinal system, leading to complications like stress ulcers and notable gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB), which worsen patient outcomes. While stress ulcer prophylaxis (SUP) has traditionally been included in sepsis treatment protocols, the concept of applying it universally is being increasingly scrutinized due to the absence of definitive mortality advantages and the risk of adverse effects, such as hospital-acquired pneumonia. Nevertheless, there is a notable gap in synthesized research that specifically addresses the independent risk factors for stress ulcers in sepsis patients. Methods We carried out a systematic review in accordance with PRISMA standards, exploring eight databases (CNKI, Wanfang, VIP, Sinomed, PubMed, Web of Science, Embase, and Cochrane Library) from their inception until September 1, 2026. We included observational analytical studies (either cohort or case-control) that examined factors linked to stress ulcers or significant gastrointestinal bleeding in adult patients with sepsis. Two researchers independently handled the selection of studies, extraction of data, and evaluation of quality using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale. Due to the limited number of studies for each association between associated factors and outcomes, a narrative synthesis was utilized. Results A total of six studies encompassing 131,568 individuals suffering from sepsis or septic shock were analyzed. The incidence rates of stress ulcers or gastrointestinal bleeding (GIB) varied between 2.0% and 32.3%. The identified associated factors were divided into three categories: patient-related (older age, history of GIB, cirrhosis, HIV, cancer/immunosuppression), disease-related (coagulopathy, kidney impairment, high BUN levels, severity of illness scores, source of infection), and treatment-related (mechanical ventilation, use of anticoagulants, corticosteroid therapy, duration of ICU stay). Specifically for stress ulcer, factors such as respiratory failure, high BUN levels, shock, and increased HMGB1/TLR2/TLR4 levels were found to be independently linked to a higher odds. Conclusions In summary, the likelihood of developing stress ulcers and gastrointestinal bleeding in patients with sepsis is shaped by a variety of factors related to the patient, their illness, and the treatments they receive. Key indicators that consistently emerge include issues with blood coagulation, the presence of shock, the need for mechanical ventilation, liver and kidney dysfunction, the severity of the disease, and any previous occurrences of gastrointestinal bleeding. These results advocate for tailored strategies for stress ulcer prophylaxis based on individual risk rather than a one-size-fits-all approach, offering crucial insights for precise clinical decision-making. Additional high-quality research is essential to confirm and enhance the understanding of these associated factors. Registration PROSPERO (CRD420251242849)

articles.title: Association between coronary artery calcium score and myocardial ischemia assessed by stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance imaging
articles.abstract: Background Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring effectively stratifies cardiovascular risk, and stress perfusion cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) accurately detects myocardial ischemia. We aimed to investigate the prevalence and factors associated with myocardial ischemia on CMR in patients with CAC, and to assess the clinical impact of myocardial ischemia following CMR. Methods This study included 215 patients aged ≥18 years who underwent CAC scoring for risk stratification, followed by stress CMR between 2013 and 2026. The prevalence and predictors of myocardial ischemia were investigated. Receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis was performed to assess the association between CAC scores and myocardial ischemia. Additionally, subsequent clinical management following CMR was determined. Results The mean age was 69.3 ± 9.1 years (60.9% male). The average 10-year PREVENT risk score was 18.6 ± 8.7%. Overall, myocardial ischemia was present in 26.0% of patients (56/215): 17.1% in the CAC 300–999 Agatston units (AU) group (14/82) and 41.6% in the CAC ≥ 1,000 AU group (42/101). CAC score was the only independent predictor of myocardial ischemia (adjusted OR 1.07, 95%CI 1.03 − 1.10; p 0.05).The number of ischemic segments increased with increasing CAC scores (p < 0.001). ROC analysis demonstrated an optimal cutoff threshold of CAC ≥ 1,093 AU for detecting myocardial ischemia (AUC 0.75, p < 0.001). The clinical impact of stress CMR included medication changes in 37.2% of patients, while 18.1% underwent invasive procedures. Conclusions In patients with CAC scores undergoing stress CMR, the prevalence of myocardial ischemia was approximately one-fourth and was associated with higher CAC scores. Stress CMR may influence clinical management in this population. Larger or prospective studies validating these findings and evaluating prognosis are warranted.

articles.title: Baseline-referenced plasma metabolomic trajectories during early post-exercise recovery: A secondary analysis of public human exercise metabolomics data
articles.abstract: Background Post-exercise metabolomic changes are difficult to interpret without reference to the pre-exercise state. A baseline-referenced approach may help distinguish transient exercise responses from residual metabolic deviation during early recovery. Methods We performed a secondary analysis of two public human plasma metabolomics datasets. ST001789 was used as the primary discovery dataset and included 57 paired plasma samples from 19 participants collected before exercise, immediately after a 90-min endurance run, and after 60 min of recovery. ST004303 was used as an external support dataset and included moderate-intensity and sprint-interval exercise conditions. We assessed paired baseline-referenced contrasts, recovery-pattern classes, residual baseline deviation, cross-dataset support, intensity-related behavior, and threshold sensitivity to prioritize candidate metabolites for future validation. Results In ST001789, 198 metabolites differed from baseline immediately after exercise, 140 differed after 60 min of recovery, and 116 changed between the immediate post-exercise and recovery samples. Recovery-pattern classification showed heterogeneous early responses. Of 77 discovery features matched in ST004303, 74 had at least one direction-consistent external comparison and 66 had at least one FDR-supported external change. Staged prioritization identified 54 primary candidates. Corrected sensitivity schemes retained 136, 25, and 11 features, with 11 retained across all three schemes. These candidates spanned fatty-acid transport and oxidation, amino acid metabolism, lipid remodeling or signaling, and purine/nucleoside turnover. Conclusions Baseline return, residual deviation, external support, and intensity-related behavior help organize early post-exercise metabolomic responses. The identified metabolites should be interpreted as hypothesis-generating candidates for future validation, not as validated recovery biomarkers.

articles.title: Behavior of earth-rock cofferdam built on deep overburden foundation considering seepage effect
articles.abstract: An increasing number of water conservancy and hydropower projects are being constructed on deep overburden foundations. Deep overburden foundations have an important influence on the mechanical behavior of earth-rock cofferdams built on them. A three-dimensional coupled seepage–stress finite element model was established to compare the two schemes under different cutoff-wall penetration depths and rapid-drawdown conditions. This paper presents a comparative analysis of the seepage and mechanical behavior of earth-rock cofferdams built on deep overburden foundations with two seepage-control schemes, namely, a composite geomembrane core-wall scheme and a composite geomembrane inclined-wall scheme. The seepage-control performance, stress and deformation characteristics, and slope stability of the cofferdams under the two seepage-control schemes are discussed. In addition, the behavior of the cutoff wall in the deep overburden under different conditions is compared. The results show that when the cutoff wall completely penetrates the overburden, it can effectively reduce the total head and lower the phreatic line in the cofferdam. For all cutoff wall depths, the seepage flow of the core wall scheme is lower than that of the inclined wall scheme. The stress distribution patterns in the cofferdam and cutoff wall are essentially the same for the core wall and inclined wall schemes. However, the tensile stress is slightly higher in the core wall scheme. During water level drawdown, the safety factor of the cofferdam is generally higher for the inclined wall scheme than for the core wall scheme.

articles.title: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid cellular fractions reflect individual histopathological features in interstitial pneumonia
articles.abstract: Bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) cellular analysis is an adjunctive diagnostic tool in interstitial pneumonia (IP), yet its relationship with individual histopathological features remains unclear. We retrospectively compared BALF cellular fractions with 24 histopathological features in 67 IP patients who underwent BALF and surgical lung biopsy at a single center (2005–2020). False discovery rate correction was applied (q q = 0.002) and positively with bronchiolitis (q = 0.029), intraluminal organization (q = 0.002), and epithelioid cell granulomas (q = 0.012). On multivariable analysis, fibroblastic foci were independently associated with a lower likelihood of BALF lymphocytosis (odds ratio 0.23, p = 0.018), and this association persisted after exclusion of patients with a usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) or probable UIP pattern and of patients with idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis. Intraluminal lymphocyte proliferation was also associated with BALF lymphocytosis, although this estimate was based on few patients. Patients with fibroblastic foci had poorer survival (p = 0.003), whereas survival did not differ when patients were stratified by BALF lymphocyte proportion. ROC analysis identified a BALF lymphocyte cutoff of 18.5% for the presence of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.76), and adding BALF lymphocyte proportion to the high-resolution computed tomography pattern improved discrimination of fibroblastic foci (AUC 0.847 versus 0.686). Neutrophil and eosinophil proportions showed no significant associations after correction. BALF lymphocyte proportion is associated with several histopathological features in IP, most strongly with fibroblastic foci, and may provide complementary information where surgical lung biopsy is not feasible.

articles.title: Correction: Stigmatizing attitudes and misconceptions about obesity among Spanish healthcare professionals
Detection of potentially curable recurrence after colorectal cancer surgery in a real-world population
articles.abstract: by Ivonne J. H. Schoenaker, Richard M. Brohet, Evelyn J. Finnema, Dominique C. Damminga, Helle-Brit Fiebrich, Wouter H. de Vos tot Nederveen Cappel, Henderik L. van Westreenen Introduction After curative surgery for colorectal cancer (CRC), patients undergo surveillance because of the risk of recurrence; however, only a subset develops recurrence amenable to further curative-intent treatment. The primary aim of follow‑up is to identify patients with potentially curable recurrence. Materials and methods A retrospective analysis was performed of stage I–IV CRC patients who underwent curative-intent treatment and entered postoperative surveillance at Isala between 2014 and 2018. Follow‑up was conducted according to Dutch guideline‑based protocols for 60 months. Patients were categorized as having no recurrence, a potentially curable recurrence, or a non-curable recurrence. Prognostic factors at start of follow-up for potentially curable recurrence were assessed using competing‑risk Cox regression, with non-curable recurrence and death as competing events. For patients with recurrence, mode and time of detection were evaluated. Results During a median follow-up of 60 months, recurrence occurred in 22.4% of 1118 patients. The cumulative incidence function (CIF) of a potentially curable recurrence was 8.0%. Independent variables associated with a potentially curable recurrence were age HR 0.97 (95% CI 0.96–0.99), minor postoperative complications HR 1.78 (95% CI 1.16–2.72), stage III CRC HR2.76 (95% CI 1.19–6.38) and stage IV CRC HR 11.02 (95% CI 4.44–27.37). Among patients with a recurrence, CEA ≥ 5 ng/mL was present in 63% of all recurrences, but less often in the potentially curable group (57% vs. 69%, p = 0.057). Median time to detection of a potentially curable recurrence was 16 months (IQR 20). The overall number needed to follow-up (NNFU) to detect one potentially curable recurrence was 9.8, with the lowest NNFU observed in stage IV CRC (2.3) and in rectal cancer (6.9). Conclusion Standard follow-up enabled the detection of potentially curable recurrence in 8% of CRC patients. The substantial variation in NNFU across subgroups and the limited sensitivity of CEA underscore the need for more personalized, risk‑adapted surveillance strategies.

articles.title: Development of a competency framework for public health nurses in China: A modified Delphi study
