Overexpression of the efflux pumps, often caused by dysfunction of related transcriptional factors, is well known as a common mechanism underpins multidrug resistance. Previous work showed direct regulatory link of CpxR-CpxS, an OmpR-EnvZ family two-component system, with the expression of the predominant MexAB-OprM efflux pump in P. aeruginosa. However, the contribution of this regulatory link to the development of antibiotic resistance has not been fully elucidated. In this work, it has been shown that deletion of cpxR, but not cpxS, reduces the emergence of multidrug resistant colonies almost 1000 times lower compared to the parental wild type P. aeruginosa PA14 following sub-lethal antibiotic exposure, suggesting that apart from CpxS, other sensory component(s) or pathway(s) can also mediate CpxR activity in the development of antibiotic resistance in P. aeruginosa. We further demonstrate that when glucose is used as the sole carbon source, it leads to increased expression levels of mexA and reduced antibiotics susceptibilities in the PA14{Delta}cpxS strain in a cpxR dependent manner. GtrS, another EnvZ family sensor kinase, but not the well-known AckA-Pta pathway, mediates this glucose effects. Both in vivo and in vitro evidences support that GtrS can activate CpxR in a cross-talk manner in the absence of CpxS. Besides gtrS, at least four other sensor kinase genes (envZ, tctE, phoR and colS) can exert activation effect upon CpxR in the PA14{Delta}cpxS strain. Having the risk of multiple way to antibiotic resistance development, cpxS null mutations can be emerged in P. aeruginosa clinical isolates. Since many OmpR-EnvZ family two-component system have been shown to be engaged in antibiotic resistance, its potential risk of exacerbating antibiotic resistance in ESKAPE pathogens has been discussed.

articles.title: Cryo-EM structures of the YsaN ATPase reveal dodecameric and tetradecameric assemblies in the Yersinia enterocolitica T3SS
articles.abstract: Bacterial pathogens deploy sophisticated nanomachines such as the Type III Secretion System (T3SS) to inject effector proteins directly into host cells, thereby subverting cellular defenses and promoting infection. Central to this machinery is a conserved homo-oligomeric ATPase that fuels substrate unfolding and translocation. Despite extensive structural and biochemical studies, the precise mechanism of T3SS ATPase oligomer assembly and regulation remains incompletely understood, events crucial for the overall functionality of the T3SS. Here, we report high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of the Yersinia enterocolitica T3SS ATPase YsaN, captured in two previously uncharacterized oligomeric states, a dodecamer (12-mer) at 3.51 [A] and a tetradecamer (14-mer) at 3.80 [A] resolution. Both assemblies exhibit helical-like symmetry and conformational heterogeneity. A conserved longitudinal fissure interrupts the helical lattice and appears to mediate interconversion between the two states, while an N-terminal interface stabilized by inter-tier disulfide bonds and an extensive non-covalent network locks the assembly together. Molecular dynamics simulations reveal that ATP hydrolysis drives a global, correlated compaction upon transition to the ADP-bound state. Together, these structural, biochemical, and MD simulation data establish T3SS ATPases as dynamic, oligomerically plastic molecular motors and provide a mechanistic framework for chaperone-effector dissociation and substrate translocation.

articles.title: Defining cell type-specific diurnal gene expression in the mouse retina
articles.abstract: The mammalian retina exhibits daily oscillations in gene expression that contribute to retinal physiology and visual function. However, the extent to which these temporal patterns differ among retinal cell types remains incompletely understood. We performed single-nucleus RNA sequencing in the mouse retina over the day and night, identifying rhythmic genes in the six major retinal cell types. Distinct diurnal gene expression patterns across photoreceptors, interneurons, retinal ganglion cells, and Muller glia correspond to their diverse functions across the light cycle. Even core circadian clock genes exhibited differences in paralog expression and rhythmicity across the retina. In contrast, dopamine signaling via the DRD4 receptor is highly rhythmic across most retinal cell types, suggesting dopamine signaling may be a key rhythmicity cue in the retina under diurnal conditions. This dataset highlights the complexity of daily transcriptional regulation in the retina and provides a resource to explore cell-type-specific diurnal rhythms.

articles.title: Dietary tryptophan rescues growth impairment during giardiasis independently of parasite burden
articles.abstract: Giardiasis is an intestinal disease caused by the parasite Giardia duodenalis. Intestinal barrier dysfunction during Giardia infection has been linked to childhood growth stunting, particularly in communities with prevalent malnutrition and repeated exposure to Giardia. In pediatric cohort studies, growth stunting has been strongly associated with asymptomatic Giardia detection in fecal samples. Several studies have described potential mechanisms by which Giardia disrupts the epithelial barrier, but less is known about factors that may support epithelial homeostasis in response to infection. Microbiota-derived tryptophan metabolites that activate aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AHR) signaling are a key pathway involved in epithelial barrier homeostasis. We tested whether dietary tryptophan availability influenced host growth outcomes and aryl hydrocarbon receptor activity during giardiasis. We used established murine Giardia malnutrition models and compared host growth, a correlate of barrier dysfunction, with a tryptophan-supplemented diet group. Giardia-infected mice fed a low-protein diet failed to gain weight whereas infected mice fed an isocaloric regular protein diet gained weight similar to diet-matched controls. Tryptophan supplementation of the low-protein diet rescued this diet-dependent and infection-induced weight defect in C57BL/6J and BALB/c mice. This growth rescue was associated with increased intestinal Cyp1a1 expression, a canonical AHR target, but without a reduction in infection burden. Glycine supplementation, used as a non-essential amino acid control that is not expected to generate AHR ligands, did not produce the same effect, suggesting that the growth rescue observed with tryptophan supplementation was not due to general amino acid supplementation. Measurements of circulating tryptophan metabolites in plasma showed limited and inconsistent differences across experimental groups, which may suggest that the growth rescue phenotype may be dependent on local intestinal or mucosal AHR-associated signaling rather than an increase in circulating metabolites. Our findings show that dietary tryptophan availability shapes host growth outcomes during giardiasis. This may also be important as it highlights that host nutrition may be a key contributor to post-infection growth impairment in young children.

articles.title: Direct cortical feedforward and feedback pathways differentially shape visual responses and selectively engage looped circuits
articles.abstract: Nearly every computational account of hierarchical cortex rests on assumptions about the influence of direct cortico-cortical inputs and which neurons they act upon. Yet, disentangling their direct functional contributions from indirect, multisynaptic influences remains difficult. We examined how feedforward (FF) and feedback (FB) pathways between mouse primary visual cortex (V1) and posteromedial cortex (PM) modulate visual responses, combining retrograde labelling, multi-area two-photon imaging and optogenetic perturbations. High or low activity in either pathway was associated with both excitation and inhibition of neurons in the targeted areas. FF activity was associated with stronger additive changes, while FB activity was related to stronger multiplicative modulations and improvements in visual decoding. Optogenetic manipulations causally confirmed these asymmetries. Both pathways preferentially modulated reciprocating "looped" neurons, with FF exciting them and FB either exciting or inhibiting them. These findings demonstrate that feedforward and feedback pathways serve distinct functional roles within recurrent cortical loops.

articles.title: Distinct profiles and antibody production by splenic and lymph node antibody-secreting cells in Trypanosoma cruzi infection
articles.abstract: Evidence from bone marrow and intestinal lamina propria studies indicates that antibody-secreting cell (ASC) characteristics are shaped by the local microenvironment; yet whether secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct ASC populations during infection remains unclear. Here, we investigated plasmablasts (PB) from the spleen and inguinal lymph nodes (LN) in acute Trypanosoma cruzi infection. Although PB from both tissues expressed canonical ASC markers, they displayed distinct transcriptional, phenotypic, and functional profiles. Splenic PB upregulated genes and proteins associated with inflammation, immunomodulation, and B-cell interactions. Activated and naive B cells also exhibited tissue-specific transcriptional programs, suggesting that local cues influence B-cell differentiation. Consistent with these differences, spleens from infected mice contained more T follicular helper cells, whereas LN were enriched in regulatory T cells. High-dimensional flow cytometry identified multiple PB subsets differentially represented between tissues. Functionally, splenic PB secreted higher levels of IgM, IgA, and IgG, including both parasite-specific and autoreactive antibodies. In contrast, LN PB preferentially produced IgG against peptide 72 of the shed acute-phase antigen (SAPA), despite lower overall T. cruzi-specific antibody production. These findings demonstrate that secondary lymphoid organs harbor distinct PB populations adapted to their local microenvironments during acute infection

articles.title: Does Short Molecular Dynamics Rescoring Improve the Ranking of p38α Inhibitors over Docking? A Replicate Benchmark
articles.abstract: Rescoring docked ligands with molecular dynamics (MD) and end point free energy methods such as MM/GBSA is widely used, but its benefit over docking for series of close analogs is uncertain. We compared AutoDock Vina scores with Md based MM/GBSA energies for 29 neutral p38 kinase inhibitors (PDB 3FLY) from the Open Force Field protein-ligand benchmark, whose IC50 values from a single publication span 3.8 kcal/mol in estimate {Delta}G. Each ligand was docked with three random seeds and simulated in two independent 20 ns replicas started from the benchmark pose (AMBER99SB-ILDN, GAFF2, TIP3L; GROMACS). MM/GBSA energies were calculated from 251 frames per trajectory without an entropy term. All 58 simulations remained stable with the ligand bound. Vina scores correlated weakly with experimental {Delta}G (Spearman {rho} = 0.28 98% CI -0.15 to 0.62), as did replica averaged MM/GBSA energies ({rho} = 0.24 -0.18 to 0.62). The difference was -0.03 (-0.50 to 0.43), so the methods were not distinguishable. Independent replicas of the same ligand differed by 3.3 kcal/mol on average, comparable to the experimental range. Raising the interior dielectric constant from 1 to 2 gave a nearly identical ranking ({rho} = 0.96 between the two sets of scores; {rho} = 0.37 against experiment, -0.04 to 0.69). In an exploratory analysis, ligands size alone correlated with affinity ({rho} = 0.60, 0.28 to 0.82), whereas neither computed score tracked size. For this narrow range series, short MD rescoring gave no measurable improvement over docking, and replica variability limited its resolution.

articles.title: Estrogen remodels large-scale cortical dynamics to promote behavioral persistence
articles.abstract: Sex-steroid hormones remodel the brain on slow timescales of hours to days to coordinate adaptive behaviors with changing bodily physiology. Yet how this slow remodeling reorganizes and constrains neural computations that govern behavior on a moment-to-moment timescale remains poorly understood, particularly in cortical regions that support flexible social decision-making. Here we combined longitudinal high-density neural recordings, quantitative behavioral phenotyping and estrogen-receptor manipulation in female mice across low and high estrogen states. Tracking behavior and neural dynamics using this dense sampling approach revealed that high estrogen increased signatures of behavioral and neural persistence. High estrogen reversibly increased male-directed social preference and behavioral persistence, effects that were abolished by estrogen receptor alpha knockdown in the medial prefrontal cortex. In the mPFC high estrogen produced more persistent neural states that were more closely aligned with ongoing behavior, increased state discriminability, and compressed within-state dimensionality. At the single-neuron level, estrogen increased tuning selectivity, lengthened intrinsic timescales, and stabilized social representations across days, even within the same neurons tracked longitudinally. High estrogen also strengthened recurrent connectivity during the resting state, exhibiting preferential connectivity between similarly tuned ensembles. Finally, incorporating these connectivity changes into a mean-field dynamical-systems model was sufficient to reproduce increased behavioral and neural-state persistence. Together, these findings show that estrogen oscillates cortical computations across multi-day timescales, flipping the prefrontal cortex from flexible to persistent regimes that play a role in sustaining potentially costly social behaviors.

articles.title: Extreme Slowdown of dsDNA and RNA:DNA Hybrids in Solid-state Nanopores for LiCl concentrations above 4 mol/L
articles.abstract: Solid-state nanopores enable single-molecule detection and characterization through ionic-current measurements, but rapid translocation can limit the resolution of molecular features. Here, we investigated the translocation of 7.2 kb dsDNA and 3.3 kb RNA:DNA hybrids at LiCl concentrations extending to 7 mol/L. Both constructs exhibited a substantial increase of {gtrsim} 500% in mean translocation time when increasing LiCl concentration from 2--3 M to 7 M . We also observed a decrease in translocation frequency at increasing LiCl concentration. Both observations indicate a reduction in the effective electric driving force. Further analysis indicates a substantial decrease in the relative width of secondary peaks induced by labels on the molecule. Our results show that increasing salt concentration beyond 4 mol/L is an accessible way for increasing translocation time in solid-state nanopore sensing, with possible implications for barcode sensing resolution.

articles.title: Fatty acid synthase coordinates mTOR signaling and histone crotonylation during cardiomyocyte hypertrophy
articles.abstract: Background: Epigenetic modifications are central to the regulation of cardiac gene expression during disease. Among these, histone crotonylation (Kcr) has recently emerged as a key modulator of chromatin structure and transcriptional activity. Here, we identify a novel signaling axis linking fatty acid synthase (FASN) to mTOR activation and hypertrophic gene expression through histone crotonylation. Methods: FASN expression, mTOR activation, and histone crotonylation were assessed in mouse hearts and isolated cardiomyocytes using immunoblotting. FASN was silenced by siRNA or inhibited pharmacologically using TVB-2640. Hypertrophic gene expression was quantified by RT-qPCR. Cardiomyocyte hypertrophy was evaluated by immunofluorescence-based cell size analysis. p300 acetylation and crotonylation were assessed by immunoprecipitation and immunoblotting. CUT&RUN-seq and RNA-seq were performed to identify FASN- and Histone H3K18cr-regulated genes during hypertrophic stimulation. Bioinformatic analyses of human RNA-seq and genome-wide association study (GWAS) data were conducted to investigate the clinical relevance of these findings. Results: Histone crotonylation was markedly elevated in hypertrophic myocardium and cardiomyocytes. This increase was driven by upregulated FASN expression in response to hypertrophic stimuli. Genetic or pharmacological inhibition of FASN suppressed histone crotonylation, hypertrophic gene expression, and cardiomyocyte enlargement. Mechanistic studies suggested that FASN regulates histone crotonylation through mTOR-associated signaling and changes in p300 activity. Transcriptomic analyses further revealed that FASN enhances the expression of hypertrophy-associated genes enriched for histone crotonylation marks. Analysis of human sequencing datasets demonstrated a positive association between FASN expression and molecular markers of hypertrophy in patients with hypertrophic cardiomyopathy (HCM). Furthermore, GWAS analysis identified a variant at the FASN locus associated with heart failure as the underlying cause of death and increased FASN expression in cardiomyocytes. Conclusions: Our findings identify FASN as an important regulator of mTOR signalling and histone crotonylation during cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. These results support a potential mechanism linking altered lipid metabolism to epigenetic regulation and pathological cardiac remodelling.

articles.title: Functional Mammary Gland Organoids From Human Induced Pluripotent Stem Cells
articles.abstract: The human mammary gland arises through sequential lineage restrictions from surface ectoderm to hormone-responsive bilayered epithelium, yet a tractable in vitro model that captures these events has remained elusive. Here, we established a stepwise differentiation protocol that directs human induced pluripotent stem cells (hiPSCs) into mammary organoids (MGOs) by sequential induction of non-neural ectoderm, mammary placodes, and lineage maturation in a defined medium. The resulting MGOs reproducibly formed polarized basal (KRT14+, TP63+) and luminal (KRT8+, GATA3+) layers, with ~25% of luminal cells expressing oestrogen receptor (ER). MGOs accumulated lipids, expressed {beta}-casein upon prolactin stimulation, and retained lineage fidelity after serial passaging. Upon transplantation into cleared mouse mammary fat pads, MGOs generated branched mammary ductal networks. Single-cell transcriptomics confirmed the emergence of basal, luminal hormone-sensing, luminal secretory, and stromal populations, transcriptionally aligned with adult human breast epithelium and responsive to endocrine disruption. These findings demonstrate that hiPSCs can be reprogrammed into functional mammary epithelium, providing a platform to dissect development, endocrine signalling, and breast cancer pathogenesis.

articles.title: GLESKit: an MCP-based system for gene-level biomedical investigation and evidence synthesis
articles.abstract: Biomedical investigation at the gene level requires researchers to combine expression data, functional annotations, pathways, interaction networks, genetic associations, drug evidence and literature. Accessing these resources involves databases, analysis tools and scripts that require bioinformatics expertise, complicating the production of clear, reviewable reports. We present GLESKit, a gene centred system that connects these steps through the Model Context Protocol and retains data, analyses, sources and reports within a study workspace. We evaluated report production with 15 author curated GeneReportBench tasks and question answering with a gene level subset of BixBench, a reference biology benchmark for agentic systems. GLESKit completed all 15 reports with a mean committee score of 0.904, although evidence quality varied, and earned positive credit on 35 of 39 scored human BixBench questions with a mean of 0.438. In paired tests, configurations with skills scored 0.145 higher across 20 questions and 0.085 higher across five reports.

articles.title: Goat Milk-derived Extracellular Vesicles modulate glial responses in vitro and attenuate neuroinflammation in vivo
articles.abstract: Milk-derived extracellular vesicles (MEV) represent a naturally derived, potentially scalable platform for immunomodulation, yet their effects on central nervous system (CNS) glial inflammation at defined particle-to-cell ratios remain insufficiently characterized. Here, we investigated the immunomodulatory effects of goat milk-derived MEV in cellular and murine models of neuroinflammation. MEV-enriched preparations were obtained by sequential filtration, ultrafiltration, and size-exclusion chromatography, and characterized by scanning electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and dynamic light scattering. In LPS-stimulated BV2 microglia-like cells, MEV at 250 and 2500 particles per cell significantly reduced CD40 expression. In primary rat mixed glial cultures, microglia, astrocytes, and oligodendrocytes internalized MEV. At 250 particles per cell, MEV significantly reduced CD40 and IL1{beta} gene expression at the mixed-culture level. In both cellular models, MEV also increased markers associated with an M2-like microglial phenotype under resting conditions. Following intrathecal administration in healthy mice, MEV did not induce significant changes in the inflammatory gene markers assessed at 8 h. In an LPS-induced mouse model of neuroinflammation, intrathecal MEV administration reduced CD40 protein expression towards control levels within 24 h and shifted the inflammatory marker profile towards a pro-resolutive state, as indicated by increased Arg1 levels and elevated CD206/CD86 and IL10/IL6 ratios. These findings identify goat milk-derived MEV-enriched preparations as potential modulators of CNS glial inflammation and support further investigation of their therapeutic potential.

articles.title: Harness engineering enables a multi-agent LLM system to generate cross-domain hypotheses beyond single-investigator reach
articles.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used to generate scientific hypotheses, and a more capable model is widely assumed to drive output quality. We tested this with a biology-focused multi-agent system coupling an LLM to five Model Context Protocol servers exposing 66 external tools. Upgrading the Synthesizer and Critic from Claude Sonnet 4.6 to Opus 4.8 initially appeared to improve quality, count, and reliability. Under a fully matched harness (identical prompts, schema, hypothesis count, and queries), the differences vanished: scores were indistinguishable on an iPSC-reprogramming task and favoured Sonnet 4.6 on a CHO cell-line-engineering task (18.4 vs 17.4; Welch t = 2.89, p < 0.05). The dominant, controllable driver of quality is therefore the prompting harness, not the model tier. We then introduce the ABCD-Stack (contract-gated prompting, diversity-first generation, adversarial refinement, and cross-family evaluation), which builds these properties in as architecture and shifts outputs toward explicitly falsifiable, causally framed hypotheses beyond the reach of a single-domain investigator. The hypotheses are falsifiable by construction but not yet experimentally validated.

articles.title: Heterogeneous self-couplings enable scale-invariant memory and cognitive flexibility without criticality
articles.abstract: The hierarchical organization of the brain underlies its ability to process information across multiple time scales and support flexible behavior through context-dependent computation. Here, we study a recurrent neural network model with heterogeneous self-interactions across nodes, capturing key features of neuronal circuits, including intrinsic diversity of dynamical time scales and multistable low-dimensional manifolds. We investigate the emergence of scale-invariant dynamics without assuming criticality, challenging the view that power-law statistics necessarily arise from self-organized critical states. We show that heterogeneous self-interactions alone are sufficient to generate scale-invariant memory in subcritical regimes, while enhancing the network's dynamical richness and computational capacity. Notably, this mechanism promotes the spontaneous emergence of hierarchical organization. We assess the functional implications of this framework using short-term memory tasks and the Wisconsin Card Sorting Test, which probes cognitive flexibility and adaptive rule switching. Compared to models with heterogeneous time constants, our approach achieves comparable performance with more parsimonious synaptic modifications, while preserving scale-invariant dynamics.

articles.title: Hierarchy of spindle forces in prometaphase
articles.abstract: Dramatic movements characterize rapid assembly of mitotic spindle in prometaphase: chromosomes congress to the spindle equator, while spindle poles segregate rapidly elongating the spindle. Direct biophysical measurements of forces driving these movements are lacking, but the forces could be learned from the rapid pole and chromosome movements. We analyzed 3D trajectories of chromosomes and spindle poles in the wild-type and PRC1-depleted cells during early prometaphase and reconstructed the spindle forces. This analysis posits that (i) chromosomes do not interact with each other, except for a short-range steric repulsion, (ii) effective pole-chromosome forces are repulsive at short and attractive at long distances, (iii) dominant forces of spindle poles segregation are interpolar in origin. The important implication of these results is that the pole-pole segregation is robust, largely insensitive to regional variations inside the cell and to complex process of chromosome congression.

articles.title: Imbalance between RNA-binding proteins and the WAVE regulatory complex underlies the toxic gain-of-function effects of the CYFIP2 Arg87Cys variant in neurodevelopmental disorders
articles.abstract: Pathogenic variants in cytoplasmic FMR1-interacting protein 2 (CYFIP2) cause neurodevelopmental disorders, with hotspot substitutions at arginine 87 (Arg87) associated with particularly severe symptoms. CYFIP2 functions both as a component of the WAVE (Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome protein family verprolin-homologous protein) regulatory complex (WRC), regulating the actin cytoskeleton, and as an interactor of RNA-binding proteins (RBPs) involved in mRNA processing/translation. Although Arg87 variants reduce CYFIP2 protein stability, heterozygous knock-in mice carrying Arg87Cys (Cyfip2+/R87C) show markedly more severe phenotypes than heterozygous knockout (Cyfip2+/-) mice, supporting a toxic gain-of-function mechanism. However, how the dual roles of CYFIP2 contribute to this mechanism remains unclear. To address this, we examined Cyfip2+/R87C mice at postnatal week 7, before overt neuronal loss and gliosis, focusing on the progressive dispersion of hippocampal cornu ammonis 1 (CA1) pyramidal neurons, a phenotype absent in Cyfip2+/- mice. Single-nucleus RNA sequencing suggested candidate alterations related to translation and cell adhesion/migration in CA1 pyramidal neurons. Complementarily, human embryonic kidney 293T cells expressing CYFIP2 Arg87Cys showed defects in proliferation and morphology, accompanied by altered expression of cell adhesion-related genes. Quantitative proteomic analysis of the CA1 region uncovered an imbalance between CYFIP2-associated protein networks, characterized by increased RBPs and reduced WRC components. Phosphoproteomic analysis further revealed altered phosphorylation of synaptic and translational regulators. Consistently, whole-cell recordings and biocytin-based morphological analyses showed increased frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents and altered dendritic morphology in Cyfip2+/R87C CA1 pyramidal neurons, most prominently in the more severely dispersed deep-layer neurons. Moreover, the cell adhesion molecule Eph receptor A3 was reduced, possibly as a result of RBP dysregulation. Together, these findings suggest that an imbalance between RBP- and WRC-associated pathways underlies the gain-of-function effects of CYFIP2 Arg87Cys and contributes to early neuronal phenotypes, most notably CA1 layer dispersion. This mechanism, distinct from CYFIP2 haploinsufficiency, supports allele-specific therapeutic strategies for Arg87 variants.

articles.title: Impact of heat and sex on embryonic brain growth in dragons with temperature induced sex-reversal (Pogona vitticeps, Lacertilia: Agamidae)
articles.abstract: Climate warming can influence sex determination and embryonic growth in oviparous reptiles that rely on external temperatures during development. Warmer incubation temperatures can stimulate growth in ectotherms until oxygen supply can no longer keep pace with growth rate; at which point metabolically expensive organs like the brain suffer. We aimed to understand the impact of heat and sex on brain development in central bearded dragons, Pogona vitticeps (Agamidae), a uniquely thermosensitive species that exhibits sex-reversal at warm incubation temperatures. Three sexual phenotypes are possible in P. vitticeps: genetically driven ZW females and ZZ males, with the latter phenotype thermally overridden at incubation temperatures >32C to induce ZZ sex-reversed females. To visualise changes in brain anatomy, we used buffered Lugols iodine to perform contrast-enhanced micro computed tomography (microCT) and synchrotron propagation-based phase-contrast CT scanning. A total of 57 embryos were sampled across developmental stages and incubated at two temperature treatments: cool (28C, n = 26) and warm (36C, n = 21). Using high-resolution models of neuroanatomy, we found that the telencephalic region of the forebrain is significantly larger in individuals with ZZ genotypes (males and sex-reversed females) compared to concordant ZW females. Although incubation temperature significantly influenced growth rate and body size during development, overall brain size was not significantly different across temperature treatments. Our results indicate that the effects of genotypic sex on brain development are more important than thermal influences, and thus the brain may be somewhat buffered to the effects of warm incubation temperatures in this arid-adapted dragon.

articles.title: In vitro propagation of Okra accessions (Abelmoschus esculentus l. Moench) through Nodal Cuttings
articles.abstract: Okra (Abelmoschus esculentus l. Moench) is an important multi-purpose vegetable crop and conventionally propagated by seed. Therefore, this study was set up to develop a regeneration protocol for three Okra accessions through nodal cuttings. The treatments were laid out in factorial arrangement of completely randomized design (CRD) design. Days to shoot and root initiation; percent of root and shoot initiation; number of shoot, leaf and root; length of shoot and root and survival rate of acclimatized plantlets were recorded for mean comparison. To induce shoot from nodal cuttings, MS medium supplemented with three levels (0.5, 1, and 1.5 mg/l) of 6-benzylaminopurinem (BAP) in combination with three levels (0.5, 1, and 1.5mg/l) of a-naphthalene acetic acid (NAA) were used. The maximum mean number of shoots was recorded on MS medium supplemented with 1.5 mg/l BAP + 2 mg/l Silver nitrate (AgNO3) for the three accessions.The maximum mean number of roots were recorded on media supplemented with 2mg/l Indole-3-butyric acid (IBA) and at accession Mandura. The tallest length of root was achieved on media without growth regulator and at accession Mandura. The maximum survival rate was recorded on accession Mandura followed by accession Akobo and Diga Leka after a month of acclimatization. Finally, in this study an efficient regeneration protocol from nodal cutting experiments was developed for large-scale multiplication, propagation and conservation of Okra.

articles.title: Injector-based pump-probe serial synchrotron crystallography of CrPhotLOV1 at the MicroMAX beamline
articles.abstract: Time-resolved serial synchrotron crystallography (TR-SSX) has become a powerful approach for investigating structural dynamics in proteins under near-physiological conditions. Its successful application, however, depends on robust sample delivery, reliable pump-probe synchronization, and reproducible data-processing strategies. Here, an injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX workflow at the MicroMAX beamline is applied to investigate the structural dynamics of the LOV1 domain of the blue-light photoreceptor phototropin from Chlamydomonas reinhardtii (CrPhotLOV1). Room-temperature serial datasets were collected for an independently measured laser-off dark state together with four light-activated pump-probe time windows (0-350, 500-850, 1000-1350 and 1500-1850 {micro}s after a microsecond laser pulse). All four time windows and an interleaved pump-probe dark reference were recorded in a single run with the JUNGFRAU detector at 2 kHz. Because thioether adduct formation in CrPhotLOV1 is complete within about 20 {micro}s and the adduct persists for hundreds of seconds, the four delays probe the same photoadduct state and serve as independent replicates. The workflow was evaluated in terms of data quality, light contamination in the pump-probe dark reference, difference Fourier analysis, extrapolated electron-density maps and refinement of light-state models. Consistent activation levels were obtained across all time points, enabling reliable structural interpretation of the light-activated state. Difference Fourier maps and refined extrapolated models reproducibly revealed formation of the characteristic FMN-Cys57 thioether adduct together with localized rearrangements within the chromophore-binding pocket. The refined light-state structures agree closely with previously reported CrPhotLOV1 models. These results establish a robust and reproducible workflow for injector-based pump-probe TR-SSX at the MicroMAX beamline, suitable for routine time-resolved studies of light-responsive proteins.

articles.title: Interpretable Deep Learning of Endogenous Fluorophore Concentration and Entropy for Lung Tissue Classification
articles.abstract: Fluorophore concentration measures and local histogram entropy describe different aspects of endogenous fluorophore maps. We investigate whether their combination improves discrimination between normal and cancerous lung tissue and which features contribute to predictions. Chemometric fluorescence microscopy (CFM) provides concentration maps of tryptophan, elastin, reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH), and flavin adenine dinucleotide (FAD). A neural network based on generalized additive models with structured interactions (GAMI-Net) is used to compare concentration-only, entropy-only, and combined representations through explicit main effects and pairwise interactions. The mean areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (ROC AUCs) across five-fold cross-validation were $95.9\% \pm 0.7\%$, $96.4\% \pm 1.6\%$, and $98.4\% \pm 0.7\%$, respectively; variability is reported as standard deviation (SD). Their aggregate differences are consistent with the hypothesis of complementary predictive information. FAD entropy, NADH concentration, and NADH entropy were the leading main effects in the combined model. The learned log-odds contributions include a U-shaped elastin-entropy relationship and nonmonotonic tryptophan relationships. By exposing how concentration and entropy enter predictions, this interpretable framework turns label-free fluorescence classification into specific, testable hypotheses about tissue metabolism and extracellular-matrix organization, motivating specimen-grouped and external validation.

articles.title: Intrinsic immune receptor triggering mechanism informs rational chimeric receptor design
articles.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) couple antigen recognition to T-cell activation and immune homeostasis. As an eight-subunit assembly, TCR activation operates as a highly coordinated, multi-subunit signaling event. However, which subunit serves as the primary trigger upon ligand engagement still remains unresolved. we identify CD3{varepsilon} as a triggering subunit whose intracellular domain (ICD) is released from the plasma membrane during TCR activation. Elevated membrane tension facilitates this transition from a membrane-proximal to a membrane-distal conformation. The released ICD forms condensates through phase separation with free or co-receptor-associated Lck. These condensates recruit additional CD3{varepsilon} ICDs from neighboring TCRs, triggering resting receptors and promoting further recruitment of TCRs and Lck to amplify proximal signaling. The CD3{varepsilon} ICD alone support robust T cell activation independently of its own ITAM. We observe a similar triggering mechanism in several activating receptors in T and nature killer (NK) cell. These findings support a unifying model in which designated subunits initiate multi-subunit immune receptor activation through phase separation with key kinases. Guided by this model, we engineered triggering molecules (TRIG) that lack canonical intracellular signaling modules. These TRIG molecules recruit endogenous immune receptors in a ligand-dependent manner and efficiently activate both T cells and NK cells. This mechanism provides a basis for designing chimeric receptors that activate immune cells through endogenous receptor signaling.

articles.title: Iron as a critical determinant for survival, oxidative stress, and infectivity of Leishmania parasites
articles.abstract: Iron is an essential for all living organisms, including humans, and is present in RBCs & other iron-binding proteins that play crucial roles in oxygen transport, DNA synthesis & electron transport. Similarly, iron also plays a critical role in parasite biology. The unicellular Leishmania parasites scavenge essential iron inside host macrophages. We investigated the impact of iron on parasite growth, apoptosis, oxidative stress, and the expression of proteins involved in ROS, thiol metabolism, Fe-S clusters, and infectivity in macrophages. Our findings revealed that optimum iron concentrations promote parasite proliferation, whereas higher levels induce toxicity, leading to DNA fragmentation and caspase-like activity. Iron supplementation enhances parasite tolerance to oxidative stress by decreasing intracellular ROS and increasing total intracellular thiol content in a concentration-dependent manner. However, iron depletion increases ROS levels and decreases total thiol content in a concentration-dependent manner, which disrupts redox homeostasis. To support our finding, we further exposed these treated parasites to menadione, which supports that iron-supplemented cells can better survive under oxidative stress than the depleted cells. Furthermore, extra iron availability increases the expression of key metabolic proteins, Fe-S clusters (Nbp35, Frataxin, IScU) and thiol metabolism (TryS, TryR, CS, SAT, cTXN, cTXNPx), while under iron-depleted conditions these proteins were downregulated except frataxin. In vitro infectivity demonstrated that iron supplementation enhances parasite infectivity, while iron depletion impairs percentage infectivity. Our study demonstrates the roles of iron in the survival, redox regulation, and virulence of L. donovani, which can correlate with the role of cellular iron homeostasis in VL pathogenesis.

articles.title: Kinase-phosphatase cycles drive self-sustained oscillations of protein condensates
articles.abstract: Phase-separated protein condensates organize biochemical processes in cells. ATP-driven enzymatic reactions can change the physical properties and even trigger the dissolution of such condensates. Here we use molecular simulations to show how ATP-driven kinase and phosphatase reactions modulate the organization of TDP-43 low complexity domain (LCD) condensates. TDP-43 phosphorylation is enhanced by condensation, as CK1{delta} preferentially binds to and acts in TDP-43 LCD condensates, whereas dephosphorylation by the phosphatase calcineurin occurs predominantly in the dilute phase. This differential recruitment of kinases and phosphatases, together with the slow redistribution of kinases into newly formed condensates, triggers oscillatory appearance and disappearance of TDP-43 LCD condensates. The oscillations are self-sustained, persisting at constant chemical driving, showing that an antagonistic kinase-phosphatase pair can endow a condensate with autonomous dynamics rather than only setting its structure.

articles.title: Koala retrovirus dynamics in the Snowy Monaro, NSW
articles.abstract: Koala Retrovirus (KoRV) is in transition from exogenous virus to endogenous element and shows distinct profiles between northern and southern koala populations. Northern animals carry high proviral copy numbers of endogenous KoRV-A and a range of exogenous subtypes, while southern koalas instead generally only possess degraded and recombinant versions of the virus. In this study we investigated the KoRV profiles of koalas in the Snowy Monaro (SM) region of southern NSW, which is at the intersection between northern and southern populations. We found that SM koalas have lower KoRV loads and proviral copy numbers than koalas from other northern populations. Plasma RNA subtype profiles were very consistent between individuals with all animals having KoRV-A at low relative abundance and high proportions of subtypes D and L. This pattern of subtype profiles is unique compared to other populations studied and suggests that KoRV-D and/or L may be endogenous in southern NSW or that KoRV-A is effectively suppressed in koalas from the region. Despite these unique profiles, in agreement with findings from other regions, higher KoRV loads were associated with C. pecorum shedding. Further, KoRV loads were temporally stable with no consistent changes found over time in koalas in the wild or koalas rescued from burnt habitat after fire and brought in for rehabilitation. Further studies into the role KoRV plays in disease susceptibility in southern NSW and into the endogenization status of KoRV-D/L will provide important insights into this model of retroviral endogenization and guide koala conservation efforts in the region.

articles.title: Label-free volumetric dynamic atlas of fresh mouse organs using dynamic full-field optical coherence tomography
articles.abstract: Dynamic full-field optical coherence tomography (D-FFOCT) enables label-free visualization of tissue microarchitecture and endogenous intracellular dynamics. Here, we establish a volumetric atlas of ten fresh mouse organs using a mobile D-FFOCT imaging platform. The system enables large-area imaging of approximately 1 cm2 within 15 min with 1,024 frames per field of view, achieving 0.75-{micro}m lateral resolution and imaging depths of up to 200 {micro}m. Large-area mosaics, three-dimensional reconstructions, and comparisons with conventional histology reveal diverse organ-specific tissue architectures. Beyond morphological characterization, quantitative analysis of dynamic intensity and mean fluctuation frequency across nine organs reveals distinct dynamic signatures and tissue heterogeneity. Longitudinal imaging of brain, liver, and intestinal tissues further demonstrates organ-dependent temporal changes in endogenous dynamics following excision. Finally, we publicly release raw D-FFOCT imaging datasets from all ten organs, providing an open resource for quantitative tissue characterization, algorithm development, and reproducible research. Together, this study provides a comprehensive, openly accessible optical atlas of fresh mouse organs, establishing a foundation for systematic tissue characterization and advancing the broader application of D-FFOCT in biomedical research.

articles.title: Laminin-Derived Peptides Bind Neuropilin-1 at the VEGF-A165 Binding Pocket
articles.abstract: Neuropilin-1 (NRP-1) is associated with glioblastoma progression and contains a b1-domain pocket that binds the C-terminal region of VEGF-A165. Whether laminin-derived peptide fragments can associate with this site is unknown. AlphaFold 3 complex prediction followed by 15 μs of all-atom production molecular dynamics simulation, trajectory-based pocket occupancy and interaction analyses, and FoldX energetic scoring was performed to compare binding of the laminin-derived pentapeptide Ac-Tyr-Ile-Gly-Ser-Arg-NH2 (peptide 1) with its retro (Ac-Arg-Ser-Gly-Ile-Tyr-NH2, peptide 2) and retro-inverso (Ac-arg-ser-Gly-ile-tyr-NH2, peptide 3) analogs. Peptide 1 showed the highest mean equilibrated occupancy of the canonical VEGF-A165 pocket (60.3 +/- 34.6%) compared with peptide 2 (25.9 +/- 32.7%) and peptide 3 (21.4 +/- 29.5%), while sampling interactions with canonical pocket residues including Asp320, Tyr297, and Tyr353; FoldX binding-energy estimates were similar across peptides despite their differing pocket persistence. Complementary nanoDSF measurements using recombinant NRP-1 and synthetic peptides yielded apparent dissociation constants in the low micromolar range for all three peptides (12.7 μM - 33.3 μM), providing experimental support for the predicted interactions. These results support persistent, sequence-dependent association of peptide 1 with the VEGF-A165 binding site of b1-NRP-1 and identify peptide analogs as a candidate for further optimization as an NRP-1-binding peptide.

articles.title: Linking clinical border morphology to cell-scale growth mechanisms in melanoma: a segmentation-to-simulation alignment study
articles.abstract: An irregular border is among the most informative visual cues for melanoma, yet the prevailing quantitative treatment of that irregularity, the box-counting fractal dimension, has rarely been connected to the cell-scale mechanism that produces it. We measured seven boundary descriptors on 1,581 lesions from the 2018 International Skin Imaging Collaboration archive segmented by an automatic thresholding route, retaining the expert ground-truth route as a sensitivity arm, and compared their medians across benign, in situ, and invasive grades. We then built a hybrid cellular automaton and swept four canonical cell-level mechanisms, scoring every simulated boundary with the same measurement code used on the patient images, before testing two mechanisms that lift the empty-neighbour division rule and aligning them to the observed malignant signature with a variance-based sensitivity analysis. The malignant signature is lobulation, not roughness: compactness rises from 1.351 to 1.810, solidity falls from 0.910 to 0.853, and convexity falls from 0.936 to 0.839 from benign to invasive lesions, with areas under the curve near 0.74, while the fractal dimension varies by only 0.024 across the three grades. All four canonical mechanisms, including loss of contact inhibition, converge on near-circular clusters at a distance of 1.147 to 1.166 from the malignant target. A long-range spatial heterogeneity in the growth rate, by contrast, reproduces the observed signature to a distance of 0.187, with the correlation length of the field, not its amplitude, the dominant parameter by total-effect index. A smooth, long-range growth-rate field is therefore sufficient to generate the lobular borders that characterise invasive melanoma, whereas the empty-neighbour assumption common to cellular automata is not. Because the winning field is imposed rather than emergent, the study resolves the alignment between border morphology and cell-scale mechanism while leaving open how such heterogeneity could arise from cell-autonomous dynamics.

articles.title: Lipopolysaccharide chain length and coat assembly keep guanylate-binding proteins upright on bacterial membranes
articles.abstract: Guanylate-binding proteins (GBPs) defend host cells by assembling on intracellular pathogen membranes. For human GBP1, this requires a switch from a compact, closed conformation to an extended, open one, whereas for murine orthologues the open state is not known. How the open state behaves at a membrane has remained inaccessible to experiment. Using all-atom and coarse-grained molecular dynamics simulations covering over 0.5 ms, we followed human GBP1 and murine GBP2 as monomers, dimers, and higher-order assemblies on phosphatidylcholine membranes, Shigella flexneri lipopolysaccharide (LPS), and phosphoinositide-containing bilayers. Closed GBPs dock through their prenyl anchor with minimal lipid selectivity. Open GBPs, by contrast, are intrinsically unstable: monomers fold back into membrane-bound resting states, and dimers tip over unless supported, either by long LPS O-antigen chains or by neighboring molecules within a coat. The open state thus appears to be maintained not by the nucleotide alone but by the protein's molecular environment.

articles.title: Compensation of hyperexcitability with simulation-based inference
articles.abstract: The activity of healthy neuronal networks is tightly regulated, and a shift toward hyperexcitability can cause various problems, such as epilepsies, memory deficits, and motor disorders. Numerous cellular, synaptic, and intrinsic mechanisms of hyperexcitability and compensatory mechanisms to restore healthy activity have been proposed. However, quantifying multiple compensatory mechanisms and their dependence on specific pathophysiological mechanisms has proven challenging, even in computational models. We use simulation-based inference to quantify the interactions of putative compensatory mechanisms in a spiking neuronal network model. Various parameters of the model can compensate for the changes in other parameters to maintain baseline activity, and we estimated their compensatory potential. Furthermore, specific causes of hyperexcitability – interneuron loss, excitatory recurrent synapses, and principal cell depolarization – have distinct compensatory mechanisms that can restore normal excitability. Our results show that spiking neuronal network simulators could generate hypotheses about the mechanisms of pathophysiological network mechanisms.

articles.title: Distinct gradients of cortical architecture capture visual representations and behavior across the lifespan
articles.abstract: The microstructure of cells within the human cerebral cortex varies across the cortical ribbon, where changes in cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture are thought to endow each region of the cortex with its unique function. While fine-scale relative to a cell, these changes at the population level impact architectural properties of the cortex measurable in vivo by noninvasive MRI, such as the thickness and myelin content of the cortex. This raises the question of whether or not we can use these in vivo architectural measures to understand cortical organization, function, and development more broadly. Using the human visual cortex as a test bed, we demonstrated two architectural gradients, one in which cytoarchitecture and myeloarchitecture converge and another in which they diverge. These two gradients underlie the structural and functional topography of the visual cortex, even predicting the presence of new visual representations. Moreover, the two gradients show distinct visual behavior relevance and lifespan trajectory. These findings provide a more general framework for understanding the human cortex, showing that architectural gradients are a measurable fingerprint of functional organization and ontogenetic routines in the human brain.

articles.title: Fitness level, but not sex, affects exercise-induced pain modulation
articles.abstract: In a previous study by our group (Nold et al., 2025), we investigated exercise-induced pain modulation after high-intensity compared to low-intensity exercise in a heterogeneous sample of diverse fitness levels. Exploratory analyses suggested an interaction of sex, fitness level, and drug treatment, indicating that males showed increasing hypoalgesia after high- compared to low-intensity exercise with increasing fitness levels, which was diminished when naloxone was administered. In contrast, these effects were not evident in females. These exploratory findings warranted further investigation to determine if and to what extent exercise-induced pain modulation depends on fitness level and/or sex. In this current study, we investigated an all-female sample (N=21) of high fitness levels using a similar paradigm as in the previous study, comparing heat and pressure pain ratings after high-intensity and low-intensity exercise. Our data show an interaction of exercise intensity and stimulus intensity in heat pain, with greater pain relief following high-intensity exercise, especially at the highest stimulus intensity. Despite results for pressure pain not reaching significance, a similar trend was evident. These results suggest that females at a high fitness level also show exercise-induced pain modulation for high-intensity compared to low-intensity exercise. Furthermore, we pooled the data of the current and previous study, providing evidence for fitness level but not sex to moderate exercise-induced pain modulation in heat pain. These findings suggest that exercise-induced pain modulation depends on fitness level but not on sex.

articles.title: Glutamate receptor composition at Drosophila neuromuscular junctions depends on developmental stage and muscle identity
articles.abstract: The neuromuscular junction (NMJ) of larval Drosophila is widely used for studying synaptic transmission. Larval body wall muscles express five ionotropic glutamate receptor (iGluR) subunits that assemble into two tetrameric complexes, with subunit composition determining the strength and plasticity of synaptic transmission. Because NMJ function has been extensively characterized in larvae, it has commonly been assumed that adult fly NMJs share this molecular composition, despite substantial differences between life stages. Here, we systematically compare glutamate receptor expression across larval and adult Drosophila muscles. We find that adult leg and flight muscles exhibit different iGluR expression than larvae, lacking expression of several receptors previously considered essential. Adjacent muscles within the adult femur express distinct iGluRs, suggesting specialization of flexor and extensor muscles. Finally, the glutamate-gated chloride channel (GluClα) is expressed extrasynaptically in adult but not larval muscle fibers. Our results reveal unexpected heterogeneity in glutamate receptor expression across muscles and developmental stages, demonstrating the need for muscle-specific analyses in flies and other animals.

articles.title: Oxytocin neurons signal state-dependent transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal
articles.abstract: Core body temperature (Tb) is defended within narrow limits through thermoregulatory behaviors like huddling, nesting, and physical activity, as well as autonomic responses like brown fat thermogenesis. While Tb displays regulated fluctuations across different behavioral states and rest/arousal cycles, the neural control of these transitions remains poorly understood. Here, we investigate the relationship between oxytocin neurons of the paraventricular hypothalamus (PVNOT) and behavioral and autonomic thermoeffector pathways across physiological states in mice. First, we show that PVNOT neurons are activated during social thermoregulation. We then demonstrate that in vivo PVNOT calcium dynamics align with transitions from rest to thermogenesis and behavioral arousal. Counter to our initial hypothesis, these dynamics were observed in both social and non-social contexts. Using a computer vision model to track thermoeffector pathways, we demonstrate that precisely timed stimulation of PVNOT neurons during low-Tb resting states increases thermogenesis followed by behavioral arousal. We therefore suggest a model in which PVNOT neurons facilitate homeostatic state-dependent transitions in thermo-behavioral states.

articles.title: SVEP1 enables efficient binding of angiopoietin-2 to the TIE1 receptor, allowing receptor phosphorylation and downstream signaling
articles.abstract: The molecular mechanisms that drive (lymph-)angiogenesis are crucial to understanding diseases, such as lymphedema, that are caused due to malformations of the lymphatic vasculature. Recently, an interaction between the secreted protein Svep1, a key regulator in lymphangiogenesis, and the transmembrane receptor Tie1 was shown in zebrafish, humans, and mice. Here, guided by in silico AlphaFold-multimer structure predictions of SVEP1 complexes, we assert with protein binding studies that the human CCP20 domain is the primary binding site for TIE1. We further demonstrate that SVEP1 mediates strong binding of ANG2 and TIE1, and that combined stimulation of hdLECs with SVEP1 and ANG2 leads to phosphorylation of TIE1. TIE1 activation by SVEP1 and ANG2 enables downstream signaling and, in turn, potentiates nuclear exclusion of FOXO1 and phosphorylation of AKT compared to SVEP1 or ANG2 alone. We present a model in which ANG1/2 dimers bind to both SVEP1 and TIE1, resulting in the recruitment of multiple TIE1 receptor molecules to a multimeric complex at the cell membrane, potentially amplifying its signaling capacity.

articles.title: "It Just Puts You Out!" Tranq Sleep, Sensory Discernment, and the Experience of Consuming Xylazine-Adulterated Fentanyl in Rural North Carolina
articles.abstract: Background: Xylazine, a veterinary sedative not approved for human use, has emerged as a consequential adulterant in the U.S. illicit fentanyl supply. Although a growing body of qualitative research has documented the experiences of fentanyl consumers exposed to tranq in large Northeastern cities, little is known about how xylazine is experienced in rural or Southern regions where the evolution of the illicit drug supply often lags behind its urban equivalents. This study examines how fentanyl consumers in west-central North Carolina detect, comprehend and respond to the widespread adulteration of fentanyl markets with xylazine. Methods: Between September and December of 2025, a seasoned interviewer conducted 25 in-depth, semi-structured qualitative interviews with fentanyl consumers recruited from both fixed and mobile syringe service programs in Gaston and Burke County, North Carolina. Interviews explored sensory discernment strategies, pharmacologic effects, and behavioral responses to the presence of xylazine. Data were analyzed using a combined deductive-inductive thematic approach in QSR NVivo 14.0. Results: Participants described a distinctive repertoire of sensory strategies for identifying xylazine in their fentanyl supply, including the appearance of drug residue on foil, bitterness and chemical odor when smoked, and altered viscosity when injected. A minority described an inability to detect xylazine through sensory cues. Participants consistently distinguished a profound involuntary sedation they called tranq sleep from the familiar opioid nod, characterizing it by nearly instantaneous loss of consciousness with severe withdrawal upon awakening. While nearly all participants expressed strong aversion to xylazine, a meaningful minority valued its amplifying effects to improve a diminishing fentanyl high. Conclusions: This study offers among the first qualitative description of xylazine exposure in a rural fentanyl market. Findings extend the xylazine literature geographically and pharmacologically and underscore the urgency of harm reduction responses tailored to the distinctive harms of xylazine. In particular, adverse health outcomes that accumulate during episodes of protracted and unarousable sedation, including physical injury, victimization, and the severe withdrawal syndrome that follows upon awakening.

articles.title: A connection-level genetic atlas of human cortical functional connectivity at rest and during a task
articles.abstract: Genetic studies of cortical functional connectivity have analyzed aggregated traits, which fails to show which connections a variant acts on. We present a connection-level genetic atlas: genome-wide association analyses of 64,620 connections among 360 cortical areas in UK Biobank participants of European ancestry at rest (n = 52,983) and during an emotion-processing task (n = 45,010), with replication in an independent sample (n = 15,546). We identified 247 resting and 96 task loci; 193 resting loci were new to fMRI genetics and 112 replicated. Most loci affected connections between networks. Colocalization linked APOE {varepsilon}4 to lowered posterior default mode connectivity and a cognition locus to left posterior temporal (PHT) connections; the right PHT was a replicated hub. Genes near the loci included 155 drug targets, 50 with psychiatric indications and 15 targeted by approved psychiatric drugs. Resting connectivity was more heritable and colocalized more often with complex traits than task connectivity, whereas task connectivity was more strongly associated with circulating metabolites. The atlas provides summary statistics for every connection in two brain states.

articles.title: A regenerative stem cell phenotype marked by ANXA1 defines aggressive colorectal cancer biology
articles.abstract: Background: LGR5 and ANXA1 are markers for specific intestinal stem cell states. LGR5+/ANXA1- crypt base columnar cells (CBCs) maintain homeostasis, whereas ANXA1+/LGR5- regenerative stem cells (RSCs) are present in fetal and repairing epithelium. Both states have been described in colorectal cancer (CRC), yet their clinical significance remains unclear. We aimed to determine how ANXA1 and LGR5 expression relates to molecular subtype, immune microenvironment and outcome in CRC. Methods: Dual-colour in situ hybridisation for ANXA1 and LGR5 was performed on tissue microarrays from 2163 patients in the randomised SCOT trial ( ISRCTN59757862 ). AI-based digital pathology quantified marker-positive area by compartment and image based consensus molecular subtype (imCMS). Markers were related to clinicopathological, molecular and immune data, and to survival using Kaplan-Meier and multivariable Cox analyses. Results: ANXA1 and LGR5 showed inverse enrichment among a diverse group of parameters. ANXA1 was highest in CMS1 and LGR5 in CMS2, with CMS3 and CMS4 being intermediate. ANXA1 dominance was associated with right-sidedness, mismatch repair deficiency, BRAF-V600E mutation, high stromal content, T4 stage, low stromal FoxP3 and high epithelial CD68 density. Combining both markers improved prognostic discrimination compared with either alone (cancer-specific survival p<0.001; recurrence-free interval p=0.004), with ANXA1 dominance remaining an independent predictor of recurrence after adjustment (HR 1.43, 95% CI 1.08-1.90, p=0.014). Conclusion: Relative ANXA1 enrichment defines an aggressive, stroma-rich, macrophage-enriched CRC subgroup with poor prognosis.

articles.title: Anatomical comparison populations and threshold transport in vascular transcriptomic classification
articles.abstract: Background: High vascular transcriptomic discrimination may obscure dependence on comparison populations, gene selection, and score scale. We examined these properties separately. Methods: GSE100927 compared surgical atherosclerotic tissue with lesion-free deceased-donor arteries: 104 arrays formed 95 complete-label groups, versus 96 arteries reported originally; independent donor identities remained unresolved. Within held-out folds, pooled area under the receiver-operating-characteristic curve (AUROC) was decomposed into nine case-bed-control-bed comparisons. Seven fixed rules underwent ten repeated three-fold splits. The primary ridge model used sample-wise gene ranks and training-only selection of 200 genes. External tests involved 32 paired plaque/intact patients in GSE43292 and 29 early/advanced specimens in GSE28829. Post-result explorations added random and disjoint gene-panel controls, feature stability, frozen-score accounting, source-only threshold learning, and individual-failure analyses. Results: Primary mean held-out-fold pooled AUROC was 0.9968, versus a within-bed mean of 1.0000 and contrast -0.0032; the empirical ceiling constrained this contrast to be nonpositive. Paired external AUROC was 0.877 (conditional 95% interval 0.792-0.947), with plaque ranked higher in 29/32 patients. Histological AUROC was 0.986 (0.942-1.000). All primary external probabilities fell below 0.5. Both source-derived thresholds also gave zero external sensitivity. Twenty outcome-independent random panels retained source AUROCs of 0.9932-0.9992, while external ranking varied substantially. Across 30 primary fits, 619 genes were selected at least once and 45 every time. Fixed-score failure analyses distinguished shared from model-specific discordance. Conclusions: Strong source ranking did not establish a unique gene signature or transferable technical thresholds. Procurement confounding, uncertain donor identities, inherited preprocessing, changed endpoints, and the exploratory status of added analyses limit interpretation. This is a comparison-population audit, not a clinically calibrated risk model.

articles.title: Are Longer Waits Associated with Lower Satisfaction and Worse Recovery? A Retrospective Observational Study of Hip and Knee Replacement in England
articles.abstract: Objectives: To examine whether longer waits for hip and knee replacement were associated with higher post-operative patient dissatisfaction and smaller patient-reported functional improvement, and whether worse post-operative satisfaction was associated with smaller functional improvement, in National Health Service (NHS) care in England. Design: Retrospective observational study linking respondent-level Patient Reported Outcome Measures (PROMs) to provider-year Referral to Treatment (RTT) waiting times, with a supplementary comparison of the wait-dissatisfaction relationship in general practice. Setting: NHS-funded hip and knee replacement in England, 2017, 2018, 2022 and 2023, excluding the pandemic-affected years 2019-2021. Participants: 107,700 hip and 122,756 knee replacement PROMs respondents, and all 42 Integrated Care Boards (168 ICB-year observations) for the general practice comparison. Primary and Secondary Outcome Measures: Post-operative dissatisfaction (fair or poor on a five-point satisfaction scale) and Oxford Score improvement (post-operative minus pre-operative score). Secondary outcomes were EQ-5D improvement and the full five-category satisfaction score. Results: Each additional 30 days of average wait was associated with a 0.05 increase in the log-odds of post-operative dissatisfaction for hip (95% CI 0.03 to 0.08) and 0.04 for knee (0.03 to 0.06), and with smaller Oxford Score improvement (hip -0.26 points, -0.44 to -0.08; knee -0.11 points, -0.22 to -0.01). Mean Oxford Score improvement fell monotonically across satisfaction categories, from 26.11 points (hip) and 22.74 points (knee) among patients reporting excellent satisfaction to 2.62 and -0.01 points among those reporting poor satisfaction. In general practice, the wait-dissatisfaction association was close to zero but too imprecise to rule out an association of the size seen for hip and knee replacement. Conclusions: In this focused surgical pathway, waiting times, post-operative satisfaction and patient-reported recovery were consistently associated, and satisfaction carried information about patient-reported recovery, not only about the experience of care. Performance frameworks that apply a common satisfaction measure across care settings should not assume it carries the same outcome content in each.

articles.title: Assessing HIV vulnerability among young women in South Africa: A comparison of three risk assessment tools
articles.abstract: Background: Young women in sub-Saharan Africa remain disproportionately affected by HIV. However, self-perceived HIV risk may not align with reported sexual behaviours or other dimensions of risk. Behavioural measures, such as the Balloon Analogue Risk Task (BART), may capture risk-taking propensity not reflected in conventional self-report measures. We compared self-perceived HIV risk, behaviour-based HIV risk, and behavioural risk-taking propensity among young women in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Methods: We conducted a cross-sectional survey between July and November 2025 among self-reported HIV-negative women aged 18-30 years in KwaZulu-Natal, South Africa. Self-perceived HIV risk was assessed using the Perceived Risk of HIV Scale (PRHS), behaviour-based HIV risk using the Vaginal and Oral Interventions to Control the Epidemic (VOICE) Risk Score, and behavioural risk-taking propensity using BART. Spearman's rank correlation coefficients were used to examine convergence between the three measures. Results: Among 250 participants, median age was 22 years (IQR 20-25), all identified as Black, and 53.6% were attending school or college. Overall, 42.0% were classified as high risk by VOICE, 6.0% by PRHS, and 33.1% of participants with complete BART data were in the highest tertile of risk-taking propensity. Mean age differed across VOICE categories (p = 0.036), but not PRHS (p = 0.111) or BART categories (p = 0.698). PRHS categories were associated with anal intercourse, oral intercourse, consistent condom use, ever having sold sex, and age-disparate partnerships (all p < 0.05). VOICE categories were not significantly associated with the assessed sexual behaviours, while BART categories were associated with vaginal intercourse in the past month (p = 0.042). Correlations between PRHS, VOICE, and BART were weak and non-significant (Spearman's rho = 0.001-0.057; all p > 0.05). Conclusions: Self-perceived HIV risk, behaviour-based HIV risk, and behavioural risk-taking propensity showed limited convergence in this sample. The measures also differed in their associations with participant characteristics and reported sexual behaviours, suggesting that they capture distinct dimensions of risk. Further research should investigate whether integrating behavioural measures with conventional self-report assessments improves understanding of HIV vulnerability and informs prevention approaches tailored to young women.

articles.title: Atlas-Based MRI Spatial Phenotyping in Pediatric Low-Grade Glioma
articles.abstract: Pediatric low-grade gliomas (pLGGs) arise throughout the developing brain, and their anatomic distribution is related to age, molecular subtype, and extent of resection (EOR). In clinical studies, pLGG location is commonly represented by a single manually assigned anatomic category, which does not quantify the full spatial extent of tumors spanning multiple brain regions. We developed and evaluated a reproducible, publicly available pediatric atlas-based framework integrating voxel-wise probabilistic mapping with patient-level atlas-derived spatial features. In this retrospective study, preoperative MRI from 349 patients with pLGG was registered to the Haskins pediatric template using EasyReg. Probabilistic maps showed differences in tumor distribution by age, molecular subtype, and EOR, including greater optic pathway and suprasellar involvement at 0-2 years and greater cerebellar involvement in KIAA1549-BRAF fusion tumors. Atlas-derived spatial, tumor morphometric, and clinical features distinguished gross total resection/near total resection from subtotal resection or biopsy/no-surgery (Replication area under the curve, 0.864). Substituting 107 automatically computed regional overlap features for the manually assigned location variable in previously published clinico-imaging risk stratification models did not significantly alter discrimination (smallest P = 0.12). Together, these group- and patient-level analyses demonstrate the utility of the framework for quantitative spatial phenotyping in imaging and clinical studies of pLGG.

articles.title: Automated Versus Conventional Annular Suturing in Totally Endoscopic Aortic Valve and Ascending Aorta Replacement: A Prospective Randomized Trial
articles.abstract: Background Totally endoscopic aortic valve replacement (AVR) combined with ascending aorta replacement (AAR) remains technically demanding, with prolonged CPB and ischemic times. Annular suturing is a principal technical limitation; automated devices aim to simplify this step and improve efficiency. This study compared early clinical outcomes between automated and conventional annular suturing in totally endoscopic AVR with concomitant AAR. Methods Between August 2023 and February 2026, 86 patients undergoing totally endoscopic AVR with concomitant AAR via right anterior minithoracotomy (RAMT) were randomized 1:1 to automated annular (RAM group; n=43) or conventional suturing (conventional group; n=43) in this single-center trial. Primary endpoints were technical success and procedural times; secondary endpoints included complications and 30-day mortality. Results Baseline characteristics were comparable, bicuspid aortic valve morphology was more frequent in the RAM group (74.4% vs. 53.5%; P = 0.043). Automated suturing was associated with shorter median procedure (120.8 vs. 144.0 minutes; P = 0.004), CPB (90.0 vs. 105.0 minutes; P = 0.005), and aortic cross-clamp times (62.0 vs. 74.0 minutes; P = 0.003), respectively. No stroke, conversion to sternotomy, paravalvular leakage, or 30-day mortality occurred in either group. Hospital stay was shorter with automated suturing (6.0 vs. 7.0 days; P = 0.037), while total treatment cost, accounting for incremental device cost, did not differ significantly (P = 0.421). Conclusions Automated annular suturing appears to be a safe, efficient alternative to conventional suturing in totally endoscopic AVR with AAR, associated with reduced operative and ischemic times and shorter hospital stay without compromising early outcomes.

articles.title: Beyond Billing Codes: An Agentic Large Language Model Pipeline for Extracting Glaucoma Procedural Data from Free-Text Clinical Notes
articles.abstract: Purpose: To evaluate the accuracy of a large language model (LLM)-based agentic workflow to extract procedural data from free-text glaucoma clinical notes in the electronic health record (EHR). Design: Cross-sectional. Subjects: 1,250 subjects in the Bascom Palmer Ophthalmic Repository. Methods: Randomly sampled clinical notes from glaucoma encounters dated 2014 to 2024 were labeled by two glaucoma specialists (with an adjudicator as needed) for prior glaucoma-related procedures (name, date, details) and recommended future procedures (name, details). Notes were split into development (10%), validation (10%), and test (80%) sets. Five LLMs (Claude Opus 4.6, DeepSeek-V4 Pro, GPT-5.5, Grok 4.1, and Qwen3.6-35B-A3B) were accessed in Microsoft Foundry through HIPAA-compliant containers. The extraction pipeline comprised a three-step agentic workflow (extraction, validation, and conditional revision) followed by text standardization. Detection of procedure data was evaluated using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, and F1-score. Among positive cases, performance was evaluated using exact-match accuracy and Jaccard Index (JI). Prior procedure labels were also compared with EHR glaucoma-related Current Procedural Terminology (CPT) codes. Main Outcome Measures: Accuracy, exact-match accuracy, JI. Results: A total of 1,984 (992 notes * 2 eyes) labels were evaluated for each task in the test set. Prior and future procedures were identified in 1,057 (53.3%) and 152 (7.7%) eyes, respectively. Accuracy ranged from 0.965 (Grok) to 0.996 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.969 (DeepSeek, Qwen)-0.978 (Claude) for future procedures. Among positive cases, exact-match accuracy ranged from 0.681 (Grok) to 0.890 (Claude) for prior procedures and 0.704 (Grok)-0.849 (Claude) for future procedures; JI ranged from 0.827 (Grok) to 0.956 (Claude) and 0.734 (Grok) to 0.883 (Claude), respectively. Among all 1,760 prior procedures present in adjudicated labels, only 441 (25.1%) were captured by CPT-coded EHR data. Conclusions: A secure agentic LLM pipeline accurately extracted glaucoma procedural data from clinical notes, recovering data largely absent from structured EHR fields. Claude performed best across both tasks. Limited agreement between labels and CPT codes likely reflects procedures performed at outside institutions and the limited granularity of CPT coding. This approach may support a scalable, comprehensive characterization of procedure burden among glaucoma patients for research and clinical applications.

articles.title: Building a community-academic partnership in public housing: Lessons from applying the CBPR Partnership Readiness Model
articles.abstract: The DASH (Dietary Approaches to Stop Hypertension) eating plan has been shown to reduce hypertension; however, adherence is low among low-income African American (AA) women, who experience a disproportionate burden of hypertension. To better understand barriers to DASH among low-income AA women, specifically AA women living in public housing, we established a community-academic partnership using a project advisory board (PAB). This paper applies the CBPR Partnership Readiness Model to assess community stakeholder readiness for the partnership. PAB members were recruited through ongoing research and volunteer work in the target community. We developed a 33-page PAB workbook clarifying study goals, member roles and expectations, and hypertension information. A questionnaire was used to gather feedback on members' experiences. PAB membership increased by 150% after the first year following a second recruitment phase. Members reported satisfaction with progress toward local food equity initiatives and with partnership sustainability. Findings indicate the model was helpful in evaluating the PAB formation process for a project involving public housing stakeholders. PABs can help build local support for community-engaged projects. When members can see the advantages of their involvement, partnerships are strengthened.

articles.title: Calibrated large language models demonstrate a consistent advantage in a randomized longitudinal medical education intervention
articles.abstract: Medical trainees increasingly use large language models to review lecture material, but the educational value of that output depends on how it is generated, with prompt and model choice rarely measured. We tested a calibrated pipeline converting Neurology Grand Rounds recordings into summaries and quizzes in a year-long randomized study. In Phase 1, six summary and six question prompts across two models were scored with 2,692 rubric annotations. Claude Prompt 0 produced the best summaries (composite 76.9%) and GPT Prompt 1 the best questions (79.6%); quality varied widely by prompt, and neither model won both tasks. In Phase 2, students in 11 clerkship cohorts over a year were randomized within cohort to receive a summary before each quiz. Summary recipients reported reviewing more and studying faster and scored higher in 9 of 11 cohorts (p = 0.026), although the between-student difference was small (+0.28 of 10 points; P = 0.28).

articles.title: Clonally expanded B cell populations are a distinguishing feature of chronic Chagas cardiomyopathy
articles.abstract: Chagas disease, caused by the parasite Trypanosoma cruzi, affects 10.5 million people worldwide, resulting in over 8000 deaths per year.
