articles.title: Correction to ‘The underappreciated roles of fog and dew on vegetation and biocrusts’
Jenn Brophy
Light‐induced phyB‐NPR1 interaction activates systemic acquired resistance
articles.abstract: Model showing phyB‐mediated fine‐tuning of defence responses via NPR1. Summary Light perception by phytochromes controls different aspects of plant–environment interactions including plant immunity; however, the underpinning molecular mechanisms are less well‐understood. Upon localized attack on leaves by avirulent pathogens, the systemic accumulation of salicylic acid (SA) is required for the establishment of systemic acquired resistance (SAR) throughout the plant to curtail pathogen spread. We demonstrate that light‐mediated Small Ubiquitin‐like Modifier 1 (SUMO) conjugation to phytochrome B (phyB) is critical for increasing cellular SA levels to orchestrate SAR upon avirulent bacterial infection. SA promotes SUMOylation of phyB, which enables it to interact with the SA receptor, Nonexpressor of Pathogenesis‐Related 1 (NPR1) via its SUMO1‐interacting motif. SUMOylation of phyB is enhanced by the accumulation of SUMO‐Conjugating Enzyme (E2) (SCE1) and the degradation of SUMO protease Overly Tolerant to Salt 1 (OTS1) in SAR‐induced systemic tissues. Using confocal imaging, we show that SUMOylated phyB undergoes liquid–liquid phase separation together with NPR1 in nuclear bodies. We further validated through immunoprecipitation, ChIP and RNA‐seq analysis that SUMOylated phyB associates with NPR1 and TGA transcription factors in nuclear photobodies to induce the expression of PR1 gene. We reveal a post‐translational modification mechanism in which light‐induced SUMOylation of photoreceptors promotes SAR by regulating NPR1 function.

articles.title: Trait‐based plant ecology: some history and some future
articles.abstract: Schematic of plant species range boundaries, some mechanisms that might set them, and some traits that might explain them. Summary Since around the year 2000, trait‐based ecology has become self‐aware as a strand of research within ecology. How did this happen? What is trait‐based ecology now? And where might it go in future? This paper offers selective answers to those questions. We first outline the history leading up to the emergence of trait‐based plant ecology during the 1990s. Second, we assess briefly what has been achieved up to mid‐2020s. Third, we discuss two challenges (among many) for trait‐based plant ecology over the next 25 yr. One is about the boundaries of species ranges along temperature gradients. Some of these boundaries may be decided by thermal tolerance, others by biotic interactions such as competition or pathogens. How can we identify which applies to which species? Which traits, feasible to measure across many species, might help with this? A second major challenge is about the global zonation of vegetation physiognomy or biome types. How well can we explain this in terms of traits, and from first principles, meaning via eco‐evolutionary models for why different trait values should be competent and competitive in different settings? First‐principle rules for how ecosystems are constructed should be central to ecology as a discipline. Resumen Desde aproximadamente el año 2000, la ecología basada en caracteres funcionales se consolidó como una línea de investigación autoconsciente y distintiva. ¿Cómo surgió, qué representa actualmente y hacia dónde avanzaría? Este artículo ofrece algunas respuestas selectivas. Primero, resumimos los antecedentes históricos que condujeron al desarrollo de la ecología vegetal basada en caracteres funcionales en los años 1990. Segundo, evaluamos los logros en la década de 2020. Tercero, examinamos dos desafíos (entre los muchos que existen) para los próximos 25 años. El primer desafío se refiere a los límites de distribución de las especies a lo largo de gradientes térmicos. Algunos pueden estar determinados por la tolerancia térmica y otros por interacciones bióticas, como la competencia o los patógenos. ¿Cómo podrían distinguirse estos mecanismos y qué caracteres, factibles de ser medidos en muchas especies, podrían ayudar? El segundo desafío involucra la zonación global de las fisonomías de vegetación y los biomas. ¿Hasta qué punto pueden explicarse mediante caracteres funcionales y primeros principios, es decir modelos eco‐evolutivos, cuáles valores de caracteres deberían ser competentes y competitivos en diferentes ambientes? Las reglas fundamentales que explican a partir de primeros principios cómo se construyen los ecosistemas deberían ocupar un lugar central en la ecología.

articles.title: Tree and neighborhood damage have distinct effects on delayed mortality after a severe hurricane
articles.abstract: Directed acyclic diagram (DAG) illustrating causal relationships between variables to estimate the effects of individual and neighborhood damage on delayed mortality. Summary Tropical forest resilience, biodiversity, and carbon sequestration depend on tree survival. Disturbance events, such as hurricanes, generate distinct forms of damage at the individual‐tree and neighborhood scale, providing a unique setting to disentangle the causal contributions of mortality drivers. Leveraging post‐hurricane census data for nearly 4000 trees in the Luquillo Forest Dynamics Plot, Puerto Rico, we used a causal inference framework combined with Bayesian multilevel models to estimate the effect of individual‐ and neighborhood‐scale damage on delayed tree mortality following Hurricane Maria (2017). Individual damage effects depended on species identity and tree size. Stem break emerged as the most lethal form of damage across the community. Neighborhood damage was associated with elevated mortality following Hurricane Maria, independent of focal tree damage. This effect was strongest among large trees, consistent with disproportionately high physiological stress resulting from greater inherent metabolic demands, refoliation energy costs, and evapotranspiration following canopy recovery. Severe biomass loss (> 75% crown loss) buffered large trees from negative neighborhood effects, revealing a positive pruning effect on survival. Our study advances mechanistic understanding of delayed tree mortality, while also suggesting how mortality patterns may shift with expected increases in disturbance severity under a warming climate. Resumen La resiliencia, la biodiversidad y el secuestro de carbono de los bosques tropicales dependen de la supervivencia de los árboles. Las perturbaciones, como los huracanes, generan distintos tipos de daño tanto a escala del árbol individual como de su vecindario, proporcionando un escenario único para desentrañar las contribuciones causales de los factores determinantes de la mortalidad. Utilizando censos de aproximadamente 4000 árboles en la Parcela de Dinámica del Bosque de Luquillo, Puerto Rico, usamos un método de inferencia causal combinado con modelos multinivel bayesianos para estimar el efecto del daño a escala individual y de vecindario sobre la mortalidad diferida de los árboles tras el huracán María (2017). Los efectos del daño individual dependieron de la identidad de la especie y del tamaño del árbol. La rotura del tronco resultó ser el tipo de daño más letal en toda la comunidad. El daño en el vecindario se asoció con un aumento de la mortalidad tras el huracán María, independientemente del daño sufrido por el árbol focal. Este efecto fue más fuerte entre los árboles grandes, lo cual concuerda con un estrés fisiológico desproporcionadamente alto debido a mayores demandas metabólicas inherentes, costos energéticos de refoliación y evapotranspiración tras la recuperación del dosel. La pérdida severa de biomasa (> 75 % de pérdida de copa) amortiguó los efectos negativos del vecindario sobre los árboles grandes, revelando un ‘efecto poda’ positivo sobre la supervivencia. Nuestro estudio avanza en la comprensión mecanística de la mortalidad diferida de los árboles y, además, sugiere cómo los patrones de mortalidad pueden cambiar con los aumentos esperados en la severidad de las perturbaciones bajo un clima en calentamiento.

articles.title: When wounds cool: a physical cue for plant repair
A target-domain augmentation and class-wise alignment framework for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis
articles.abstract: Cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis often has to adapt to a new operating condition with only a few labelled target samples. This setting creates two coupled problems. First, the sparse target support set cannot describe the target fault distribution sufficiently. Second, the same fault class may occupy different feature regions across source and target conditions, which weakens source-domain pretrained classifiers. Existing methods usually improve few-shot learning or reduce domain shift, but they rarely enrich the labelled target-class representation before class-wise source-target alignment. To address this limitation, this paper proposes a target-domain augmentation and class-wise alignment framework for few-shot cross-condition bearing fault diagnosis. The rime optimization algorithm (RIME) is first used to optimize the variational mode decomposition (VMD) parameters K and α, and fault-sensitive components are selected using envelope entropy and adjacent modal-frequency overlap. The reconstructed signal is converted into symmetric dot pattern (SDP) images to provide a noise-suppressed polar representation. The fast generative adversarial network (FastGAN) then generates auxiliary target-domain SDP samples from the limited labelled target support set, making each target fault class less sparse. On this basis, class-wise maximum mean discrepancy (CMMD) is embedded into a Swin Transformer classifier to align source and target features within each known fault category. Experiments on the Case Western Reserve University (CWRU) and Xi’an Jiaotong University–Shenyang Blower Works (XJTU-SY) datasets show that the proposed framework improves target-domain few-shot adaptation, achieving 93.33% and 97.58% accuracy under the G20 and G50 XJTU-SY target-augmentation settings, respectively.

articles.title: Assessment of light sensitivity using the Ocular Photosensitivity Analyzer: Discomfort threshold, pain threshold, and tolerance in healthy volunteers
articles.abstract: Photophobia encompasses a continuum of light-induced experiences from mild discomfort to overt pain and intolerance, yet clinical tools rarely quantify these distinctions, leaving many patients undiagnosed and untreated. This study employed the Ocular Photosensitivity Analyzer (OPA), a compact instrument for quantitative sensory testing (QST) with light, to investigate three perceptual levels in healthy adults: visual photosensitivity discomfort threshold (VPDT), visual photosensitivity pain threshold (VPPT), and an exploratory outcome, visual photosensitivity tolerance level (VPTol). Twenty-nine participants ages 19−34 underwent standardized OPA testing, during which they identified when light first became uncomfortable, painful, and intolerable. After each trial, participants rated the peak pain intensity (PI) and peak unpleasantness (UP) using visual analog scales. Measured illuminance values differed significantly across the perceptual levels (RM-ANOVA, N = 28, F(1.69, 45.6)=37.06, p ηp² = 0.58; Mauchly’s W = 0.82, p = 0.072), indicating sensory levels are differentiable. Post hoc t-tests revealed VPTol exceeded VPPT (N = 28, t(27)=−2.29, p = 0.030, dz = 0.43)), and both exceeded VPDT (VPTol: N = 29, t(28)=−7.69, p dz = 1.43, VPPT: N = 29, t(27)=−7.69, p dz = 1.47). Friedman’s test revealed UP (N = 28, χ2(2)=17.64, p Kendall’s W = 0.32) and PI (N = 28, χ2(2)=22.36, p Kendall’s W = 0.40) differences across perceptual levels and post hoc Wilcoxon tests showed UP and PI increased between VPDT and VPPT (UP: N = 29, Z = −4.34, p r = 0.57, PI: N = 29, Z = −4.58, p r = 0.60) and UP increased between VPDT and VPTol (N = 28, Z = −2.92, p = 0.007, r = 0.39), suggesting that both affective and sensory dimensions of pain vary across perceptual levels. Although preliminary, these findings are consistent with a multidimensional framework of photophobia. Additionally, the OPA’s ability to differentially quantify VPDT, VPPT, and VPTol offers a novel approach to characterize light sensitivity that may aid future assessment of abnormal light sensitivity.

articles.title: Changes in ware–decoration associations in ceramic assemblages from Wacheqsa, Chavín de Huántar, Peru
articles.abstract: by Christian Mesía-Montenegro Ceramic differentiation can involve altered associations among continuing attributes without wholesale categorical replacement. At Wacheqsa, Chavín de Huántar, Peru, this study compares ware composition, decorative techniques, and their associations in 1,308 decorated or surface-treated sherd observations from five archaeological contexts. Early Platforms and Water Flood constitute the earlier Urabarroid aggregate; Stone Rooms, Midden, and Late Platforms constitute the later Janabarroid aggregate. These labels describe ceramic affinities within pre-existing context sets, whose stratigraphic networks are only partly connected and whose formation histories differ. On identical common support of nine wares and six techniques (n = 334/822), ware-margin Hellinger distance is 0.430 (95% fixed-count interval 0.392–0.481), technique-margin distance is 0.588 (0.551–0.634), and joint distance is 0.734 (0.714–0.793). A homogeneous-association model rejects a common ware–technique association after aggregate-specific margins are fitted (G2 = 118.59; pboot = 0.0001); the result persists without Midden (G2 = 90.16; pboot = 0.0001). Early Platforms differs from each later context, and stamping/impression is prominent in all three later samples, although those contexts retain distinct joint profiles. Nine of eleven ware categories occur in both aggregates, with pronounced differences in the association of polished wares with incision and stamping/impression. The contrast is consistent with differing decorated repertoires across activity and depositional settings, including contexts associated with collective consumption. Local superpositions and the published chronology support a temporal interpretation, but the contribution of elapsed time cannot be separated from differences in activity and deposition.

articles.title: Correction: Molecular Mechanism of Mutant p53 Stabilization: The Role of HSP70 and MDM2
articles.abstract: by Milena Wiech, Maciej B. Olszewski, Zuzanna Tracz-Gaszewska, Bartosz Wawrzynow, Maciej Zylicz, Alicja Zylicz

articles.title: Dynamic analysis and spatiotemporal evolution of multi-stage knowledge dissemination under AI-enabled dual-channel “Interpersonal–Human-Machine” interaction
articles.abstract: With the deep integration of digitalization and artificial intelligence technologies into enterprise knowledge management, AI-assisted learning is reshaping the channels through which knowledge is acquired within organizations. Meanwhile, knowledge dissemination is evolving from traditional interpersonal interaction toward human-machine collaborative interaction. In light of this transformation, this study develops a multi-stage 2SEIR-CA dynamic model of knowledge dissemination under an AI-enabled mechanism that incorporates dual-channel “interpersonal–human-machine” interaction. Specifically, employees are classified into five states: employees who have not yet mastered the knowledge, employees with limited knowledge mastery, employees with strong knowledge mastery, knowledge-disseminating employees, and knowledge-exited employees. On this basis, the next-generation matrix method is employed to calculate the basic reproduction number of the system and to analyze the existence and stability of equilibrium points. An optimal control model is then established to derive strategies for promoting knowledge dissemination, and a cellular automaton model is introduced to characterize its spatiotemporal evolution. The results show that the system exhibits a pronounced threshold effect: when key dissemination parameters exceed their critical levels, knowledge can continue to diffuse within the organization; otherwise, it will gradually decay. Second, the AI-enabled mechanism enhances knowledge transformation efficiency and contact intensity, thereby significantly promoting the transition of employees with strong knowledge mastery to knowledge-disseminating employees. Third, the optimal control strategy proposed in this study can optimize transformation pathways across different stages under resource constraints, thereby improving overall dissemination efficiency and maintaining the structural stability of the dissemination system. Fourth, the spatiotemporal simulations demonstrate that, under optimal regulation, knowledge dissemination can form a stable diffusion pattern with high coverage. Under the assumptions and parameter settings of the proposed model, the findings provide theoretical insights into the dynamic mechanisms underlying AI-enabled knowledge dissemination and offer model-based implications for knowledge management practices in organizations.

articles.title: Eating behaviour and glycaemic control: A cross-sectional study in adolescents with diabetes
articles.abstract: Background Achieving early glycemic control in adolescents with diabetes is associated with improved short- and long-term health outcomes. The aim of this study was to examine the relationship between eating attitudes and glycemic control, as well as the factors associated with eating attitudes and glycemic control, in adolescents with diabetes. Methods This descriptive cross-sectional study included 143 adolescents with diabetes, aged 10–19 years, who attended a research hospital between February and April 2024. The data were collected using a Descriptive Information Form, Eating Attitudes Test (EAT) and an information form questioning the values of some metabolic variables. Results The mean age of the participants was 14 ± 2.3 years and 49.7% had diabetes between 1–5 years. The mean total score of the EAT scale was 16.62 ± 8.30. The mean score of the “Dieting” subscale of the EAT scale was 10.39 ± 5.58, the mean score of the “Bulimia food preoccupation” subscale was 2.33 ± 3.03 and the mean score of the “Oral Control” subscale was 3.79 ± 3.08. There was no significant difference between the mean EAT total score and glycemic control. Conclusions The mean EAT-26 total score was below the commonly used cutoff score, and no significant association was found between EAT-26 scores and HbA1c. Differences in EAT-26 total and subscale scores were observed according to selected demographic and clinical characteristics, including BMI, treatment modality, and treatment adherence. These findings describe self-reported eating attitudes in the study sample and support the inclusion of eating-related assessment within the holistic care of adolescents with Type 1 DM.

articles.title: Effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6–23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia: A cluster-randomized controlled trial
articles.abstract: Background Appropriate complementary feeding is essential for children’s growth and cognitive development. However, these practices remain inadequate in the study area. Therefore, this study aimed to evaluate the effect of nutrition counseling on complementary feeding practices among mothers with children aged 6–23 months in West Gojjam Zone, Northwest Ethiopia. Methods A two-arm, parallel, cluster-randomized controlled trial was conducted from June 2023 to December 2024 in rural districts of West Gojjam Zone. Thirty clusters (15 per arm) were assigned to either an intervention group (n = 401), which received Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling by Women’s Development Army leaders, or to a control group (n = 401), which received routine education. The intervention was delivered monthly for nine months from infant age 6–8 months. The primary outcome was appropriate complementary feeding practices. Secondary outcomes included minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, acceptable diet, and egg/flesh food consumption. Data were collected via interviewer-administered questionnaires. The intervention effect was analyzed using Generalized Estimating Equations with adjustment for potential confounders. Statistical significance was set at p < 0.05. Results The difference-in-differences in appropriate complementary feeding practices between groups was 13.2 percentage points. After adjustment, mothers in the intervention group were nearly 2.5 times more likely to practice appropriate complementary feeding than controls [AOR = 2.49, 95% CI: (1.40, 4.42)]. Children of counseled mothers were also more likely to achieve minimum dietary diversity [AOR = 1.75, 95% CI: (1.04, 2.93)], minimum meal frequency [AOR = 1.62, 95% CI: (1.01, 2.61)], and minimum acceptable diet [AOR = 2.13, 95% CI: (1.26, 3.59)] compared with controls. Conclusion Health Belief Model-based nutrition counseling was positively associated with improvements in appropriate complementary feeding practices, minimum dietary diversity, meal frequency, and acceptable diet. Integrating such counseling into routine maternal and child health services may strengthen child nutrition programs in similar rural settings. Trial registration ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT05871346).

articles.title: Enhanced enfortumab vedotin sensitivity in a cisplatin-resistant bladder cancer model
articles.abstract: Objective Enfortumab vedotin (EV) and cisplatin (CDDP) are central treatments for advanced urothelial carcinoma, yet the influence of prior CDDP exposure on subsequent EV efficacy remains unclear. In this report, we characterized EV-related drug responses in a CDDP-resistant bladder cancer subline. Methods A CDDP-resistant subline (HT1376-CR) was generated from parental bladder cancer cell (HT1376/P) through continuous exposure to CDDP. Sensitivities to CDDP, EV, and the EV payload monomethyl auristatin E (MMAE) were compared between HT1376-CR and HT1376/P. Nectin-4 expression, EV binding, and drug-resistance-related gene expression were evaluated. The effect of ABCB1 silencing on drug response was also examined. In vivo EV responses were explored using xenograft models. Results HT1376-CR cells showed increased sensitivity to EV in vitro and in vivo. HT1376-CR cells were more sensitive to MMAE and showed greater G2/M accumulation after MMAE exposure. In contrast, cell-surface nectin-4 expression and EV binding were reduced. ABCB1 was markedly upregulated in HT1376-CR, and ABCB1 silencing increased sensitivity to CDDP, MMAE, and EV within the resistant subline. Conclusion The CDDP-resistant HT1376 subline showed enhanced sensitivity to EV, and ABCB1 suppression further increased EV sensitivity within this resistant subline.

articles.title: Explainable machine learning framework with Granger-based temporal predictive validation for monitoring fiscal risk in national health insurance expenditure
articles.abstract: by Gwangsu Lee Rising health insurance expenditure (HIE) poses fiscal risks and challenges to the sustainability of public insurance systems. Despite growing interest in data-driven analysis, empirical evidence on the associations between macroeconomic, social, and financial conditions and national HIE remains limited, particularly across provider types. This study introduces an explainable machine-learning framework with temporal predictive validation to analyze and forecast HIE using 60 macro-financial and socioeconomic indicators. The framework is applied to three monthly expenditure series from Korea’s National Health Insurance system (2000–2023). Predictive performance and interpretability are assessed using two univariate autoregressive baselines, three regularized linear indicator-based benchmarks, and six nonlinear indicator-based ensemble models. LightGBM serves as the primary explanatory model, and SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) quantifies indicator contributions and captures autoregressive persistence. Beyond associational insights, temporal predictive validation using lagged regression and Granger-type temporal predictive tests examines, within a prespecified exploratory lag window, whether SHAP-identified indicators show statistically supported exploratory lagged monitoring relevance. These results are interpreted as hypothesis-generating temporal monitoring evidence rather than as evidence of structural causal effects. Although persistence-based baselines achieved the strongest short-term forecasting accuracy, indicator-based models provided model-conditional explanatory information beyond autoregressive controls. The results indicate that shared macroeconomic pressures and provider-specific factors are associated with HIE predictions. The cost-of-living index is consistently associated with expenditure patterns across categories, whereas domestic demand and external conditions indicate provider-specific associations for medical institutions and pharmacies. Only a subset of predictors retained exploratory lagged monitoring support, underscoring the distinction between model-based predictive importance and hypothesis-generating monitoring signals. This integrated framework may inform transparent fiscal risk monitoring hypotheses and contextual review of public HIE.

articles.title: Expression of Concern: Pedestrian POSE estimation using multi-branched deep learning pose net
Factors associated with choosing diagnostic radiology as a future specialty among Palestinian medical students: a multicenter cross-sectional study
articles.abstract: Background Understanding factors influencing specialty choice is essential for workforce planning and curriculum development. Recruitment into diagnostic radiology remains challenging in several regions, particularly in low- and middle-income settings. This study aimed to identify factors associated with Palestinian medical students’ consideration of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty, with particular emphasis on educational exposure, perceptions of artificial intelligence (AI), and cognitive influences. Methods A multi-institutional cross-sectional study was conducted to evaluate factors influencing the choice of diagnostic radiology as a future specialty among Palestinian medical students between 2 November 2025 and 5 February 2026. Data were collected using a previously validated questionnaire adapted from Almuhanna et al. Descriptive statistics were performed, followed by bivariate analyses and multivariable logistic regression to identify independent predictors of considering radiology as a future specialty. Adjusted odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were reported. Results A total of 427 students participated (56.7% female; mean age 21.75 ± 2.1 years). Among 300 valid responses regarding radiology intention, 102 students (34.0%) reported considering radiology as a future specialty. In multivariable analysis, lack of exposure to radiology research (OR = 0.14, 95% CI 0.06–0.34, p < 0.001) and lack of preclinical radiology teaching (OR = 0.26, 95% CI 0.12–0.54, p < 0.001) were independently associated with a lower likelihood of considering radiology. Enjoyment of diagnostic problem-solving tasks (OR = 3.35, 95% CI 1.39–8.09, p = 0.007) and exposure to tele-radiology (OR = 3.96, 95% CI 1.72–9.12, p = 0.001) were independently associated with higher likelihood. Lifestyle, impact on patient care, and work environment were the most frequently reported motivating factors. Conclusions Palestinian medical students’ interest in radiology is strongly associated with modifiable educational exposures, cognitive engagement in diagnostic reasoning, and perceptions of evolving technological practice. These findings support the potential value of structured undergraduate radiology exposure, research opportunities, and mentorship initiatives to improve awareness and interest in radiology.

articles.title: Few-shot recognition of lane-changing intention in connected vehicle environment: A meta-transformer approach
articles.abstract: This paper proposes a Meta-Transformer model for few-shot accurate lane-changing intention recognition in connected vehicle environment. Given the velocity, acceleration, distance headway, time headway and time to collision of a vehicle at past time steps, a transformer model is developed to recognize the lane changing intention of the vehicle at the current time step. The multi-head attention layer of the Transformer model is capable of effectively extracting features from the multivariate time serie input. This enhances the accuracy of lane-changing intention recognition. The Transformer model is combined with a model -agnostic meta-learning (MAML) algorithm to be able to perform well with small amount of training data. The meta-learning consists of meta-training and meta-testing. During the meta-training, a task is sampled from the distribution over tasks. The tasks include recognition of intention of lane-keeping, lane-changing to left lane, and lane-changing to right lane. The model is trained with few samples and feedback from the loss function defined on the tasks. The loss function is defined as the categorical cross entropy of the errors between the labels and the results generated by the proposed model. During the meta-testing, the model is tested on new data from the distribution of the transition from a feature and the label to another feature. The model is trained by minimizing the test error. Experimental results show that the proposed model can achieve 8.7 percentage points higher accuracy than a transformer model.

articles.title: Field study on compaction effect and energy evolution characteristics of highway subgrade under low-amplitude vibration
articles.abstract: Subgrade compaction is a critical procedure in highway construction. To elucidate the dynamic characteristics and energy transfer mechanisms throughout the entire compaction process, this study utilized four test lanes to conduct field experiments on highway subgrade under varying numbers of rolling passes. Comprehensive measurements and analyses were performed regarding the dynamic characteristics of vibration waves, energy distribution, and the evolution of soil compactness during operation. Furthermore, the compaction efficiency and energy transfer within the subgrade were quantitatively evaluated. The results indicate that the dynamic behavior of subgrade materials varies significantly across different compaction stages, which are consequently categorized into three distinct phases: loose, optimal compaction, and over-compaction. In this experiment, the third rolling pass represented the optimal compaction state, characterized by distinct resonance peaks, a regular frequency spectrum, and highly efficient energy transfer. As compactness increases, the horizontal propagation of vibration waves strengthens, whereas vertical attenuation accelerates, causing energy to concentrate beneath the vibration source. Additionally, the proposed method for evaluating compaction efficiency based on the energy transfer coefficient corroborates the three-stage evolution of the process, offering a direct, quantitative indicator for real-time quality assessment and endpoint determination. These findings provide new theoretical insights and empirical data to support intelligent and refined process control in subgrade compaction.

articles.title: Genomic dissection of environmental responsiveness and cross-environment productivity in fenugreek
articles.abstract: Dissecting the genetic basis of genotype × environment interaction (G × E) is important for breeding crops with stable or responsive performance across production environments. Using previously published seed-yield data from 107 Egyptian fenugreek accessions evaluated under two contrasting field environments, we investigated whether yield potential and environmental responsiveness share a common genetic basis. Seed yield per plant was measured in Giza (SYP_G; reference environment) and Wadi El-Natrun (SYP_W; contrasting environment). Nine derived indices were calculated to characterize environmental responsiveness, productivity, and stability: relative performance index (RPI), yield plasticity index (YPI), stress tolerance index (STI), log response ratio (LRR), mean productivity (MP), harmonic mean (HM), tolerance index (TOL), stress susceptibility index (SSI), and AMMI stability value (ASV). The near-zero correlation between SYP_G and SYP_W (r = 0.107) indicated substantial genotype reranking across environments, while several response indices were closely related to SYP_W and therefore predominantly reflected environment-dependent yield expression. Phenotypic analyses also identified contrasting performance strategies, ranging from highly responsive accessions, such as G15 (RPI = 3.629), to highly stable accessions, such as G41 (YPI = 0.001). These phenotypes were integrated with 38,142 SNPs using univariate association-mapping approaches. In addition, SYP_G and SYP_W were subjected to multivariate association-mapping. Association mapping identified one genome-wide-significant SNP for STI and several suggestive loci showed concordant associations across mapping methods. Within the current panel, marker coverage, and significance thresholds, most adaptation-index associations did not overlap previously reported yield loci; however, dDocent_Contig_39939_66, previously associated with seed yield in this panel, also showed cross-method suggestive associations with RPI and TOL. Comparative genomic analysis of three legume reference genomes supported two gene-linked candidate loci associated with STI: a cation/H⁺ antiporter and an importin subunit beta-1. The same analysis classified two of the strongest statistical signals, including the sole genome-wide-significant locus, as repetitive or transposable-element sequences rather than single-copy genes. These findings demonstrate that statistical association strength does not necessarily establish a coding-gene basis for loci identified using reference-free ddRAD markers. Within the current population size and marker coverage, environmental responsiveness and productivity appeared partially distinct but biologically connected components of environment-dependent yield performance. The results provide a genomic and phenotypic framework for prioritizing fenugreek germplasm for further evaluation while emphasizing the need for independent-population, multi-season, and functional validation of the identified candidate loci.

articles.title: Gynecological malignancy signal triage: A two-dimensional framework integrating US-derived FAERS data with comparative US–China GBD trajectories
articles.abstract: Background Cancer-related adverse-event reports are difficult to interpret because statistical disproportionality, stimulated reporting, and background disease burden are distinct phenomena. To address this, we formalized a two-dimensional prioritization framework that combines FAERS signal credibility with independent GBD burden context. Because the FAERS dataset is overwhelmingly of US origin, we utilized China exclusively as a prespecified macro-epidemiological GBD comparator, strictly avoiding cross-national pharmacovigilance extrapolations. Methods We analyzed FAERS reports (2004–2023) and female GBD 2023 estimates for China and the United States. Four disproportionality algorithms (ROR, PRR, IC, and EBGM) were evaluated for 150 high-frequency primary-suspect drug–event pairs (50 per cancer group). We report any-algorithm positivity and four-algorithm concordance alongside case-definition sensitivity analyses. GBD trends, age–period–cohort models, and exploratory projections to 2053 were integrated to provide population-level context, explicitly not as exposure denominators or for causal validation. Results FAERS cohorts yielded 19,717 cancer-associated report records. Among 150 high-frequency candidate pairs, 42 met all four algorithmic thresholds. The top-50 candidate screen captured approximately 72.8%–75.8% of primary-suspect records, serving as a variance-reduction step rather than a complete all-drug screen. Drugs like ranitidine and talc demonstrated marked disproportionality but also exhibited reporter and temporal features heavily compatible with stimulated reporting. Time-to-onset distributions reflected recorded administrative reporting intervals rather than biological carcinogenesis. GBD estimates revealed divergent China–US trajectories, notably a rising baseline for US uterine cancer. Conclusions The formalized F × G framework operates as a transparent triage tool, not a causal classifier. FAERS disproportionality generates hypotheses; GBD trajectories indicate potential public-health priority. All prioritized signals—particularly those involving consumer products or immunosuppressants—require formal causal evaluation in longitudinal exposure-denominator datasets.

articles.title: Identification of prognostic biomarkers for nasopharyngeal carcinoma through microRNA‑mRNA network analysis combined with screening of immune‑related genes
articles.abstract: Background Nasopharyngeal carcinoma (NPC) is a common head and neck cancer, and radiotherapy is its main treatment. Recurrence and metastasis are the main causes of treatment failure. Although immunotherapy can prolong patient survival, the molecular mechanisms underlying NPC development and progression remain unclear. MicroRNAs (miRNAs) and their target genes are abnormally expressed in many tumors and are closely involved in tumor development. Therefore, this study aimed to identify key miRNAs and immune-related target genes in NPC, construct miRNA–mRNA regulatory networks, and screen for and validate core immune genes to identify prognostic molecular biomarkers for NPC. Methods We downloaded NPC-related miRNA (GSE32960) and mRNA (GSE12452, GSE13597, GSE64634) microarray datasets from the Gene Expression Omnibus (GEO) and identified differentially expressed miRNAs (DEMs) and mRNAs (DEGs) using R. Target genes of DEMs were predicted with TargetScan, miRDB, and miRWalk, and then intersected with DEGs to identify core genes. A miRNA–mRNA regulatory network was constructed in Cytoscape. The core genes were further overlapped with immune-related gene sets, followed by functional enrichment analysis. A prognostic risk model was established using LASSO–Cox regression, and immune cell infiltration was evaluated with CIBERSORT. Model validation, immunohistochemical analysis, and drug–gene interaction analysis were also performed. In vitro, RT–qPCR was conducted in C666-1 and NP69 cell lines to verify the expression of key genes. Results We identified 213 potential target genes of key miRNAs. Three miRNAs (hsa-miR-30e-5p, hsa-miR-30a-5p, and hsa-miR-20a-5p) were associated with NPC prognosis, and 17 core immune-related genes were enriched in cytokine-mediated signaling, chemokine response, and JAK-STAT pathways. Five genes (CXCL11, SOCS1, ROBO1, LGR5, and RORB) showed promising diagnostic value for NPC; their expression was positively correlated (P < 0.05) with CD8 ⁺ T-cell, macrophage, and neutrophil infiltration. Drug-gene analysis predicted that 5-fluorouracil targeted LGR5 and aldesleukin targeted SOCS1. RT-qPCR demonstrated that SOCS1 was upregulated approximately 3.7-fold in NPC cells (P < 0.01). Conclusion This study identified potential novel key genes in nasopharyngeal carcinoma, providing new therapeutic targets for the treatment of this disease.

articles.title: Integrative genomic SEM analysis of shared genetic architecture and candidate genes for insulin resistance–related metabolic traits
articles.abstract: Insulin resistance is a complex metabolic state involving impaired insulin sensitivity, compensatory insulin secretion, abnormal lipid metabolism, and altered fat distribution. However, the shared genetic architecture underlying these correlated phenotypes remains incompletely defined. In this study, we applied Genomic Structural Equation Modeling to genome-wide association summary statistics of fasting insulin, insulin sensitivity index, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio to construct an insulin resistance-related latent genetic factor. SNP-level association analysis was then performed for the latent factor, followed by risk locus annotation, fine-mapping, transcriptome-wide association analysis, gene-level prioritization, enrichment analysis, and exploratory structural biology assessment of selected missense substitutions. The single-factor model showed acceptable but not optimal approximate fit and captured a biologically consistent genetic pattern, with positive loadings for fasting insulin, triglycerides, and waist-to-hip ratio and a negative loading for insulin sensitivity index. The latent factor showed detectable SNP heritability and revealed 3,067 genome-wide significant candidate SNPs, with Q_SNP retained as a complementary SNP-level heterogeneity diagnostic.. Functional annotation identified 100 genomic risk loci and 1,530 FDR-significant genes in MAGMA. Fine-mapping prioritized multiple candidate regions, including loci near PPARG, RSPO3, SLC38A11, SLC39A8, BCL2, GDF5, and SPATA5. TWAS and FOCUS further highlighted candidate genes involved in adipocyte biology, glucose–lipid metabolism, insulin secretion, and expression regulation, including PPARG, MLXIPL, TCF7L2, FAM13A, CCDC92, and SLC22A3. Enrichment analyses suggested that genetic signals associated with the insulin resistance-related latent factor were mainly linked to fat distribution, cardiometabolic traits, adipose tissue, mesenchymal cell lineages, and active regulatory genomic regions. In a separate exploratory analysis, AlphaFold3 modeling, ThermoMPNN prediction, and molecular dynamics simulations suggested structural perturbations for three ultra-rare missense substitutions in nominated candidate proteins: BCL2-W188G, GDF5-C400Y, and RSPO3-C129Y. These substitutions were selected using functional-impact annotations and modeling feasibility, were not GWAS lead or fine-mapped causal variants, and do not establish the mechanisms underlying the GWAS associations. These findings provide an integrated genetic and structural framework for understanding shared mechanisms underlying insulin resistance-related metabolic abnormalities, while emphasizing the need for further experimental validation.

articles.title: Interpretable EOG-based gaze classification using tree-based models: A SHAP and LIME analysis
articles.abstract: by Ayse Nur Ay Gul Electrooculography (EOG) is a low-cost biosignal modality for gaze-based human–computer interaction, but reliable validation and model interpretability remain important challenges for machine learning-based gaze classification. This study proposes an explainable EOG gaze classification framework using UNIOVI-EOG dataset. Horizontal and vertical EOG recordings from nine participants were converted into 100 ms non-overlapping windows, and only stable windows with at least 90% label purity were retained. Time-domain window features were extracted and evaluated using Decision Tree, Random Forest, XGBoost, and CatBoost classifiers under subject-wise five-fold cross-validation, ensuring that participants in the validation folds were not included in training. The final dataset contained 81,481 accepted windows across nine gaze classes. All models achieved very high subject-wise performance, with Random Forest providing the strongest overall results. The high performance was consistent with the controlled fixation protocol and the strong separability of horizontal and vertical EOG amplitude patterns, as supported by simple mean-amplitude baseline and leakage diagnostic analyses. Model interpretability was assessed using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) and Local Interpretable Model-Agnostic Explanations (LIME). The explanations showed that amplitude-related features, especially channel means, medians, quantiles, and absolute mean values, were the main contributors to classification decisions. SHAP–LIME rank correlation and permutation-based faithfulness analysis provided additional quantitative support for the explanations. These findings suggest that leakage-controlled, window-level, explainable machine learning can provide accurate and physiologically interpretable EOG gaze classification in controlled experimental settings.

articles.title: Lethal and sublethal influence of triflumezopyrim on life history traits and enzyme activities in the bean bug, Riptortus pedestris (Hemiptera: Alydidae)
articles.abstract: Riptortus pedestris (Fab.) is an important soybean pest in East Asia, where its piercing-sucking feeding behavior leads to soybean syndrome. Triflumezopyrim, a novel mesoionic insecticide, has been widely applied to control sap-sucking insects. However, its lethal and sublethal impacts on R. pedestris remain poorly understood. This study investigated the lethal and sublethal effects of triflumezopyrim on R. pedestris using bioassays, age-stage two-sex life table analyses, and enzyme activity measurements. Results demonstrated that triflumezopyrim exhibited strong toxicity (LC50 = 7.46 mg/L) and notable repellent activity against R. pedestris. Exposure of nymphs to sublethal concentrations (LC10 and LC30) significantly prolonged nymphal development and the adult preoviposition period, while reducing adult longevity, oviposition duration, and fecundity in the parental (F0) generation. In addition, LC30 exposure produced adverse transgenerational effects in the F1 generation, including extended adult preoviposition period, decreased male longevity, reduced oviposition duration, fecundity, net reproductive rate (R0), intrinsic rate of increase (r), and finite rate of increase (λ) of the population. Moreover, both LC10 and LC30 treatments led to substantial elevation in the activities of antioxidant (superoxide dismutase and peroxidase) and detoxification (multifunctional oxidase and glutathione S-transferase) enzymes. These findings indicate that triflumezopyrim exerts strong acute toxicity and pronounced sublethal inhibitory effects on R. pedestris, ultimately suppressing population growth potential. This study offers a scientific basis for the rational use of triflumezopyrim as well as the development of strategies for the management of this species.

articles.title: Light availability, not soil texture, correlates with shrub community structure in mesic forest gaps
articles.abstract: by Sam W. Anderson, Katherine A. McCulloh Woody shrubs are important components of temperate forest understories, contributing to forest structure, diversity, and succession. However, the extent to which variation in canopy openness and soil texture influence shrub occurrence, diversity, and composition remains unclear. Because woody tissues require comparatively high light availability and sandy soils may favor shrubs over trees, we hypothesized that shrub richness and cover would increase in canopy gaps and sandier microsites. To address this, we quantified soil texture, canopy gap structure, and recorded shrub abundance in twenty randomly stratified plots within sixteen different mesic forests in Wisconsin, USA. Using a mixed-effects modeling approach, we determined that shrub richness, Shannon diversity, and coverage increased significantly in more open canopy gaps, while soil sand content had no significant impact on these metrics. Canopy gaps also had a significant effect on the composition of shrub communities at the plot level. At the stand level, neither sandier nor more open-canopied forests had more diverse, dense shrub layers, though more heterogenous canopies had a weak negative correlation with shrub richness. Broadly, shrub abundance and cover increased in more open gaps, though individual species demonstrated significantly different preferences in terms of light availability and soil sand content. Our results demonstrate the importance of local light availability for shrub growth. However, species-specific responses to soil texture and light availability and the modeled importance of unmeasured site-level factors suggest that additional environmental and biotic factors are likely to impact this diverse temperate guild.

articles.title: A chemomechanical bifurcation landscape unifies sustained growth, length homeostasis, and regenerative collapse in axons
articles.abstract: Axonal growth machinery is largely shared across neurons, but axons exhibit strikingly different fates depending on developmental and environmental context: sustained elongation in peripheral neurons under permissive conditions, length homeostasis in cortical neurons after target innervation, and pathological collapse into dystrophic endbulbs in injured adult central nervous system (CNS) axons. These divergent outcomes have resisted explanation by length-sensing and biomechanical models that treat long-range transport and local force generation as separate problems. We unify these phenomena through a mechanochemical model that couples bidirectional motor transport and intracellular signaling to growth-cone balance of axonal tension, actomyosin contraction, and adhesion within a single feedback loop: The lengthening axon uses its own growing transport delay to establish self-limiting mechanical feedback, as the accumulating delay reshapes signaling waveforms to progressively elevate myosin contractility against actin-driven protrusion. Two physical parameters, the transport delay and the signaling feedback strength, organize axon fate into a unified state-space landscape spanning sustained growth, length homeostasis, and pathological collapse. Reduced feedback strength weakens this self-limiting mechanical feedback by simultaneously enhancing protrusion and suppressing contractility, providing a mechanistic interpretation of axon lengthening under partial reduction of retrograde transport. Bistability in the inhibitory regime explains why mature CNS tracts persist where nascent sprouts collapse, recasting regenerative failure as a state-dependent gate rather than a capacity limit. The framework predicts that partial rather than complete inhibition of retrograde transport could shift collapsed axons across the bifurcation into a growth-permissive regime, identifying a class of interventions complementary to existing capacity-restoration strategies for nerve injury.

articles.title: A sulfotyrosine motif in the human TrkB extracellular domain is required for activation by the agonist antibody ZEB85
articles.abstract: The brain-derived neurotrophic factor (BDNF)-tropomyosin receptor kinase B (TrkB) signaling axis is a key effector of synaptic plasticity and neuroprotection. While TrkB activation is a major target to prevent neural dysfunction, stimulation with exogenous BDNF administration has not proven tractable given the unfavorable physiochemical properties of BDNF. In addition, BDNF also activates a cell death pathway by binding to the neurotrophin receptor p75. The TrkB agonist antibody ZEB85 provides an alternative route to the selective activation of TrkB. To understand the ZEB85 mechanism of action, we mapped the binding site for ZEB85 to the TrkB extracellular juxtamembrane domain and found a sulfotyrosine modification at residue 400 crucial for ZEB85 interaction and activation of TrkB signaling. We determined the structures of ZEB85 and BDNF bound to their respective binding sites on human TrkB suggesting independent sites for each ligand, despite prior evidence of direct competition. Using structure-guided BDNF- and ZEB85-binding deficient TrkB mutants, we assessed their ability to sequester ligands from full-length TrkB in cultured human neurons. We found that the BDNF binding site extends into the juxtamembrane domain of TrkB but does not require the sulfotyrosine 400 to activate TrkB. Together with biophysical analysis and AlphaFold modeling, these results explain how BDNF can displace ZEB85 from TrkB through an overlapping epitope. Our findings reveal unique features of TrkB, not present in the related neurotrophin receptors TrkA and TrkC and suggest future directions to explore the role of sulfotyrosine in TrkB signaling.

articles.title: A symbiogenic merger enabled by oxygen initiated the evolution of eukaryotes
articles.abstract: Recently, extensive genetic information about archaeal hosts at the basis of eukaryogenesis has come to light. Characterization of these first eukaryotic common ancestor (FECA) related organisms allows improved understanding of the enigmatic FECA to last eukaryotic common ancestor (LECA) transition. However, these gene-centered discoveries have the unfortunate side effect of entrenching erroneous ideas about early eukaryotic evolution. This is apparent in the two-Domain vision of life, with eukaryotes seen as specialized Asgard archaea, while underestimating the contribution of the endosymbiont to eukaryogenesis. Establishment of the alpha-proteobacterium as the future mitochondrion is treated as one of many such endosymbiotic occurrences, ignoring its unique evolutionary position. I will marshal evidence for symbiogenic mechanisms involved in the FECA to LECA transition, with a key role for the endosymbiont’s electron transport chain and its acceptor molecular oxygen, especially in the incarnation of reactive oxygen species occurring in the host cytoplasm. We should overcome overestimating gene determinism, while not sufficiently allowing for effects of biological hierarchies, emergent properties, and chance. Many eukaryotic properties are best understood by envisaging the crucial uptake of the future mitochondrion as a merger instead of an acquisition. This merger is characterized by a new kind of elaborate cellular entity emerging as a result of rapid coevolution, replacing a scenario in which already complex pre-eukaryotes acquired endosymbionts, accompanied by important, but limited, changes. Successful mergers are rare because they are intrinsically more difficult, but synergistically open up completely new areas of possibilities, as illustrated by incredible eukaryotic success.

articles.title: Complexity functions of infinite sequences
articles.abstract: We address the inverse problem for complexity functions of infinite words, which asks which functions can occur as complexity functions of infinite words. We survey our recent advances on this problem and several of its ramifications. We describe an asymptotic solution to the inverse problem, realizing every function satisfying two necessary conditions as the complexity function of an infinite word up to asymptotic equivalence. We then turn to phenomena beyond asymptotic equivalence, presenting constructions of infinite words with seemingly contradictory behavior of the discrete derivatives of their complexity functions. These lead to a solution of a 1995 problem of Cassaigne and to applications in symbolic dynamics, including the question of convergence of Rauzy graphs, as well as to the growth and asymptotic invariants of algebraic structures.

articles.title: Computation and sampling for Schubert specializations
articles.abstract: We study a problem at the interface of enumerative algebraic geometry, algebraic combinatorics, and the statistical mechanics of vertex models with long-range interactions. We develop methods to explore the values S w ( 1 , … , 1 ) of Schubert polynomials (called principal specializations), which count reduced bumpless pipe dreams (RBPDs) with boundary permutation w ∈ S n . We exhibit counterexamples to the conjecture of Merzon and Smirnov that S w ( 1 n ) is maximized on layered permutations; the smallest such example we find is at n = 17. Despite the counterexamples, we present bounds that support a refined conjecture that the maximum of S w ( 1 n ) over all w ∈ S n grows at the same asymptotic rate as the maximum over layered permutations (found by Morales, Pak, and Panova). We implement and benchmark four recurrences for Schubert specializations: the descent formula of Macdonald, the transition formula of Lascoux–Schützenberger, the cotransition formula of Knutson, and the formula of Billey, Jockusch, and Stanley. We also explore typical random permutations drawn with probability proportional to S w ( 1 n ) , equivalently from uniformly random RBPDs. Our simulations reveal a permuton-like limit analogous to the Grothendieck setting studied by Morales, Panova, Petrov, and Yeliussizov. For sampling, we show that the standard monotone Coupling From The Past framework does not apply to RBPDs, leaving exact uniform sampling open. To bypass this, we develop an efficient Markov chain Monte Carlo sampler augmented with macroscopic “droop” updates that preserve connectivity and accelerate mixing. Our publicly available fast implementations reach n = 20 for exact computation of S w ( 1 n ) and n = 100 for Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling using a chain whose stationary distribution is uniform on RBPDs (run on a cluster).

articles.title: Correction for Bernabé-Rubio and Watt, Caspase-8-dependent autophagy regulates neutrophil infiltration in oral squamous cell carcinoma
Crowding limits relative bacterial surface accumulation with density-induced effective heating
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microswimmers near walls has been studied for decades. While hydrodynamics and single-cell kinematics are well-explored, the role of cell-cell interactions remains understudied. However, in realistic, crowded environments such as the human gut, these interactions can be just as crucial. Here, we demonstrate that they actively weaken bacterial surface accumulation. Analysis of entrapped cell tracks reveals that crowding enhances orientational fluctuations, which increase the effective rotational diffusion and facilitate wall escape. A minimal model shows that this collective effect is equivalent to raising the system’s effective temperature with density.

articles.title: Ddx3x deficiency in mice impairs corticofugal motor circuits and causes motor deficits that are attenuated by early-life exercise
articles.abstract: The X-linked RNA helicase DDX3X is a high-risk gene for autism spectrum disorder and intellectual disability primarily in females. Individuals with pathogenic variants in DDX3X have pervasive and often severe motor manifestations. Using mouse models, we studied the circuits underlying the motor phenotypes associated with Ddx3x deficiency and examined the feasibility of an early intervention to ameliorate motor trajectories. We show that Ddx3x controls both the development and later plasticity of motor circuits connecting the motor cortex with the pontine nuclei. Ddx3x haploinsufficiency during development affects the dendritic arborization of corticopontine neurons. Juvenile-onset Ddx3x loss in corticopontine neurons is sufficient to induce adult motor impairments overlapping with those caused by chemogenetic disruption of corticopontine circuits. Further, Ddx3x mutant mice engage corticopontine circuits in skilled motor tasks in a sex-dependent manner. Last, Ddx3x haploinsufficient female mice undergoing a juvenile motor intervention show long-lasting specific benefits in their adult motor function. Together, these findings establish Ddx3x as an essential regulator of corticopontine neuron development and function and provide an early motor intervention to ameliorate motor outcomes in a mouse model of DDX3X haploinsufficiency.

articles.title: Direct atomic-scale observation reveals rare earth element fractionation at mineral–water interfaces
articles.abstract: Clay minerals, ubiquitous across diverse geological systems, exert fundamental controls on critical geochemical processes, particularly through their adsorptive interactions with economically vital elements such as heavy rare earth elements (HREEs). The adsorption of HREEs onto clay surfaces is not only the key process that enriches these critical resources but also a potential archive for dating significant weathering events. However, the atomic-scale mechanisms governing the preferential adsorption and fractionation of rare earth elements (REEs) at mineral–water interfaces have remained poorly constrained. Here, employing in situ atomic-scale imaging via high-resolution atomic force microscopy, we systematically investigate the adsorption behaviors of light and heavy REEs (La, Y, Yb) onto key crystallographic planes—Si-basal, Al-basal, and edge terminations—of representative clay minerals (kaolinite, illite, mica) under environmentally relevant conditions (pH 4.8 to 6.4). We directly visualize and quantitatively reveal that Si-basal planes selectively enrich HREEs with pH-enhanced adsorption capacity, whereas Al-basal planes exhibit negligible REE adsorption below pH 5.8 but preferential HREE adsorption at pH 6.4. Integrating synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, we identify the adsorption mechanism of REE on Si-basal and Al-basal/edge planes as outer-sphere complexation and inner-sphere binding, respectively. Furthermore, we quantify the contributions of distinct planes via surface complexation modeling, revealing Si-dominated to Al- and edge-controlled adsorption with elevating pH. These atomic-scale findings not only resolve long-standing debates about clay mineral-mediated REE fractionation but also redefine fundamental paradigms of surface reactivity at silicate mineral–water interfaces, offering insights into the cycling and metallogeny of other critical metals in aqueous and sedimentary environments.

articles.title: Elucidating molecular regulatory rules of nanoparticle biological identity via standardized deep proteomics
articles.abstract: The biological identity of nanoparticles is often redefined upon exposure to physiological fluids through the formation of a protein corona (PC), However, the molecular rules linking synthetic design to biological fate remain elusive owing to the fragmented and inconsistent proteomics data. Here, leveraging a standardized deep proteomic database of 42 diverse nanomaterials, we reveal the general molecular selection rules that govern the PC formation. We demonstrate that the PC is not a product of random adsorption but is shaped by strict property-dependent recruitment. First, surface charge regulates cellular uptake, with anionic nanoparticles specifically recruiting adhesion proteins to promote Itgav-mediated endocytosis, thus forming a causal charge-corona-receptor chain. Second, PEGylation engineers immune evasion by selectively depleting specific complement and coagulation factors, rather than merely preventing protein adsorption. Third, nanoparticle geometry imposes structural constraints and selects proteins based on specific physicochemical features such as lysine content. Beyond mechanistic insights, we show that material-specific PCs can rebalance the serum proteome and enable the detection of low-abundance disease biomarkers. This work shifts the paradigm from empirical description toward rule-based prediction and provides a foundational framework for rationally engineering nanomedicines with predictable and programmable biological identities.

articles.title: Global bee bioregions mirror those of other taxa despite a uniquely bimodal latitudinal diversity gradient
articles.abstract: Bioregionalization, the partitioning of the globe into areas of biotic similarity, is one of nature’s most striking patterns, and highly congruent boundaries have been identified across plants, tetrapods, ants, and butterflies. However, these taxa also share a unimodal latitudinal diversity gradient (LDG), raising the question of whether bioregionalization and the LDG are mechanistically coupled or instead arise from largely independent processes acting on different timescales. Bees (Hymenoptera: Anthophila) provide a natural test, their diversity peaking at mid-latitudes rather than in the tropics. Using range estimates for 3,370 species and a phylogenetic beta-diversity framework, we recover 21 bee bioregions nested within at least six major realms (Australasia, Indomalaya-Oceania, Nearctic, Neotropics, Palearctic, and Sub-Sahara) that closely align with those of other taxa despite bees’ atypical diversity gradient. We propose that bioregionalization and species richness are decoupled because they arise from distinct processes: the former reflects historical dispersal and evolutionary history, the latter local diversification, extinction, and environmental filtering. Our analysis provides a global biogeographic framework for future bee research and highlights the processes shaping the world‘s major biogeographic boundaries.

articles.title: Hydration at the base of the mantle transition zone by ancient subductions in Asia
articles.abstract: Whether and how the subduction processes result in water enrichment at the base of the mantle transition zone (MTZ) remain elusive. The major orogenic belts of the Asian continent, including the Central Asian, Tethyan, and Alpine–Himalayan belts, which record extensive subduction processes, offer an ideal target to address the hydration of the MTZ and its relationship with subduction. Here, we map water content at the MTZ base by combining mineral physics constraints on hydrous pyrolite and global seismic observations of velocity structure and 660-km discontinuity topography. Our results indicate an average global water content of approximately 0.14 wt%, with pronounced hydration anomalies in parts of Asia. Linking these anomalies with reconstructions of past subduction events since 410 Ma reveals extensive water delivery to the MTZ, particularly beneath parts of the Mongol–Okhotsk suture zone, the Central Asian Orogenic Belt, and the Tethyan orogenic domain, where water content exceeds 0.5 wt%. These results connect ancient subduction history to present-day mantle hydration, offering insights into Earth’s deep water cycle.

articles.title: Intrinsic function of leptin receptor–regulated endothelial PD-L1
articles.abstract: Programmed cell death ligand-1 (PD-L1) is an immune checkpoint protein expressed in vascular endothelial cells (ECs). In contrast to cancer, our understanding of endothelial PD-L1 in relation to metabolic syndromes and its vascular complications is less studied. For example, its regulation and intrinsic function remain unclear. Here, we showed that endothelial PD-L1 is regulated by leptin receptor signaling in male mice. In particular, endothelial PD-L1 expression is affected by leptin resistance. A lack of leptin receptors leads to PD-L1 downregulation in vascular ECs via posttranslational degradation. To understand the fundamental roles of endothelial PD-L1, RNA interference and selective knockout are employed in human endothelium and animals, respectively. Silencing or deleting endothelial PD-L1 expression delays cell cycle progression and proliferation due to rat sarcoma (RAS)/mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) inactivation. In obesity, endothelial PD-L1 deficiency impairs the EC turnover and worsens the vascular function. Overall, we provide an insight into how endothelial PD-L1 contributes to vascular homeostasis, suggesting its pathophysiological importance in maintaining cellular turnover.

articles.title: Potential energy landscape networks of confined vortex matter
articles.abstract: Advances in nanoscale patterning of superconducting films [Y. L. Wang et al ., Nat. Nanotechnol. 13 , 560–565 (2018)] and the availability of submicron-sized superconducting single crystals with controlled geometry allow for the investigation of superconducting vortex matter under extreme confinement [A. K. Geim et al ., Nature 390 , 259–262 (1997)]. It has been observed in these systems that the interplay between sample geometry and vortex number results in the emergence of so-called “magic number” configurations which show unusually high stability against thermal fluctuations. However, a detailed, comprehensive theoretical study of the ground state and metastable states of confined vortex matter has not yet been developed. Here we show that the intricate properties of a system of vortices under extreme confinement can be characterized in detail by mapping the potential energy landscape of the system onto a network [J. P. K. Doye, Phys. Rev. Lett. 88 , 238701 (2002)] with nodes corresponding to local potential energy minima and edges to transition states between local minima. We apply these techniques to systems featuring repelling particles/vortices confined in small containers of various geometric shapes. We demonstrate that the ground state almost always belongs to a subset of system states within the deepest network core. We find that the emergence of magic number configurations in the ground state results in a drastic decrease in the complexity of the entire network. We use large-scale molecular dynamics simulations to study the size dependence of melting in different configurations. We find that as confinement effects increase, magic number configurations transition to states with lower symmetry.

articles.title: The ABCD hypothesis
articles.abstract: If α and β are cardinals, then the cardinal exponentiation α β is the set of all functions from α into β . The ABCD hypothesis is the statement that for all infinite cardinals α ≤ β and γ ≤ δ , | α β | ≤ | γ δ | if and only if α ≤ γ and β ≤ δ . The Axiom of Determinacy, AD, states that every two-player infinite game on ω has a winning strategy for one of the two players. Let Θ be the supremum of the ordinals onto which R surjects. This paper will show that if AD holds and V = L ( R ) , then the ABCD hypothesis holds below Θ .

articles.title: The efficiency of information gain by natural selection
articles.abstract: Natural selection enriches populations for genotypes that are well adapted to their environments, accumulating information about the selective conditions in the process. Therefore, selection can be viewed as a learning process through which populations acquire information about the environment. Motoo Kimura derived a relationship between the amount of information gained by selection and a measure of the inefficiency of the selective process, known as substitution load [M. Kimura, Genet. Res. 2, 127–140 (1961)]. Due to the gradual nature of selection and the ongoing mismatch of types to the environment, a lineage that is still acquiring information has lower mean fitness than a lineage that already has it. While this has been an influential insight, we find that Kimura’s model is inconsistent with selection experiments involving Escherichia coli . To address limitations in this model and develop a more robust measure for the efficiency of selection, we turn to computational learning theory. We show that the learning-theoretic concept of regret quantifies the inefficiency of selection as a learning process in terms of relative lineage fitness. We establish bounds on the efficiency of information gain in general settings, including frequency-dependent selection and arbitrary environmental change. We experimentally validate these bounds and demonstrate that our extended theory recovers Kimura’s fundamental insight. Finally, we show that selection is an asymptotically optimal algorithm for the basic problem faced by evolving populations and that it acquires information more efficiently than comparable processes in complex environments.

A case study in conflicts of interest
A commensally regulated immune rheostat fine-tunes skin barrier fitness
articles.abstract: At the skin’s surface, the epidermis must balance stem cell renewal with barrier maintenance to withstand environmental stress and shield against pathogens. In this study, we identify a microbial-immune-epithelial feedback mechanism that integrates environmental information into stem cell regulation in mice. Specifically, we show that Langerhans cells (LCs), an intraepithelial macrophage population, orchestrate this circuit by producing prostaglandin E 2 , which restrains stem cell proliferation, promotes epidermal differentiation, and maintains barrier integrity during homeostasis. Upon pathway disruption, stem cells become overactivated, hindering terminal differentiation and weakening barrier function. Upstream, LC activity is tuned by the local microbial environment in a rheostat-like fashion, coupling commensal sensing to stem cell dynamics. Our findings provide a general framework for how barrier tissues achieve adaptive homeostasis amid continual external fluctuations.

articles.title: Advance more drugs for China’s aquaculture
Altermagnetism revealed by polarized neutrons in MnF2
articles.abstract: Altermagnets are compensated magnets with symmetry-enforced spin split bands. Direct spectroscopic evidence for their existence has been reported in several materials. For example, inelastic neutron scattering (INS) has recently been used to witness a splitting of magnon bands in MnTe that is compatible with altermagnetism. Here, we present polarized INS results on MnF 2 showing that it is altermagnetic. Our data reveal a splitting coming from the long-range dipolar coupling. Furthermore, using a domain-biased sample, the data reveal a nonzero chirality in the neutron scattering cross section that reverses the sign between the two magnon modes. It is this feature that clearly demonstrates altermagnetism in MnF 2 . This finding highlights the potential for polarized INS to characterize altermagnets through its sensitivity to fine structure in magnon spectra.

articles.title: Chiral altermagnon in MnTe
articles.abstract: Altermagnetism has been recognized as a magnetic phase that bridges the properties of ferro- and antiferromagnetism. The momentum-dependent spin splitting observed in these materials reflects their distinctive symmetry characteristics, which also establish the conditions for chiral magnons to emerge. Here we provide direct experimental evidence for a chiral magnon in the altermagnetic candidate manganese telluride (MnTe) revealed by circular-dichroism resonant inelastic x-ray scattering. This mode, which we term chiral altermagnon, exhibits a distinct momentum dependence of its spin polarization consistent with the altermagnetic g -wave symmetry of MnTe. Our polarization-resolved data corroborate the existence of a discrete class of magnetic excitations, demonstrating how altermagnetic order shapes spin dynamics and paving the way for advances in spintronic and quantum technologies.

Data-driven discovery and rapid, direct synthesis of MXenes
articles.abstract: MXenes are a rapidly expanding family of two-dimensional transition metal carbides and nitrides, yet scalable synthesis routes remain limited and historical reports suggest a broader, largely unexplored chemical space. We used machine learning–assisted database mining to uncover hidden multilayer MXenes. Screening reveals 33 previously synthesized but unrecognized MXene candidates. Guided by these findings, we synthesized seven multilayer MXenes using a rapid, scalable self-propagating high-temperature method that requires no sustained external heating and completes within minutes. We further realized 11 previously unexplored rare earth–based MXenes (M = praseodymium, neodymium, samarium, gadolinium, terbium, holmium, and thulium). Experiments and modeling suggest semiconducting behavior and diverse magnetic states across this family. Together, these results expand the MXene family and demonstrate a data-driven strategy for accelerating materials discovery through sustainable methods.

articles.title: Genomic erosion across avifauna in a biodiversity hotspot sounds a conservation alarm
articles.abstract: Loss of biodiversity can have a hidden dimension—the cryptic erosion of genetic diversity even in the face of apparent species resilience. We quantified changes in genetic diversity by comparing historical and modern genomes of 62 songbird species from the Gaoligong Mountains, a biodiversity hotspot in southwestern China. We identified genomic loss averaging between 43 and 49%; and, unexpectedly, common species were disproportionately affected. We argue that this loss was driven primarily by habitat fragmentation (and mitigated by dispersal ability) and show that it exceeds prior estimates and conservation policy thresholds. Species identified as having lost diversity continue to be listed as “Least Concern” on the International Union for Conservation of Nature’s Red List of Threatened Species, exposing a blind spot in extinction risk monitoring. We call for genomic metrics to be rapidly integrated into global conservation frameworks.

articles.title: Immunity at scale
Intrinsic gestational timing governs human cerebellar development after preterm birth
articles.abstract: Intrinsic programs shape brain maturation; however, which of these programs are perturbed by prematurity as well as the molecular pathways involved remain unknown. The human cerebellum serves as a paradigm of extrauterine development—its accelerated growth and circuit formation align with the third trimester, a period disrupted by preterm delivery. Using multimodal datasets encompassing in vivo neuroimaging and neurodevelopmental outcomes with postmortem spatial-transcriptomic and histopathological profiling, we show that prematurity diverts the cerebellar developmental trajectory. Cerebellar growth and functional outcomes scaled with gestational age, despite modifying perinatal exposures. Spatially resolved developmental programs underlying macroscopic trajectories were marked by incomplete granule cell maturation and impaired Purkinje cell structural refinement, which indicate lineage-specific developmental asynchrony. Thus, prematurity constitutes biologically displaced maturation, in which infants of equivalent postmenstrual age occupy divergent developmental states.
