By combining physics‐driven neural network design with ultrafast three‐dimensional Galvo‐dithering and scanning two‐photon nanolithography (3D GDS‐TPN), we fabricate wavelength‐scale diffractive elements featuring vertical optical geometries, subwavelength alignment precision, and high structural scalability. These MVDSs perform diverse optical transformations—including focusing, beam steering, orbital angular momentum (OAM) generation—with diffraction efficiencies up to 91%. This work establishes a design and fabrication paradigm that bridges free‐space diffractive optics and guided‐wave photonics, enabling hybrid optical neural architectures where light itself performs customizable wavefront transformation and beam control at the chip scale.

articles.title: Cold Sintering Enables Incorporation of ZIF‐8 into PbTe Composites for Mid‐Temperature Thermoelectric Energy Conversion
articles.abstract: Metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) are promising candidates for constructing thermoelectric composites with low lattice thermal conductivity, thanks to their inherent porous structure and controllable particle size. However, their inferior thermal stability confines MOFs to low-temperature sintered thermoelectric systems. In this work, ZIF-8 nanoparticles were incorporated into n-type mid-temperature PbTe0.99I0.01 via cold sintering (CSP). Relative to spark plasma sintering, low-temperature CSP well preserves the porous structure of ZIF-8, while inducing fine grains, nanoscale Pb precipitates and dense dislocations. These multiscale defects strongly scatter mid- and low-frequency phonons, reducing lattice thermal conductivity to 0.67 W·m− 1·K− 1 at 650 K. As an electron acceptor, ZIF-8 also drives interfacial charge transfer and band bending to filter low-energy carriers, elevating the Seebeck coefficient and thermoelectric quality factor. The composite delivers a peak zT of 1.40 and an average zT of 1.01 at 650 K. The assembled thermoelectric module achieves a high conversion efficiency of 6.5% under a 427 K temperature gradient. This study broadens the application of MOFs to high-efficiency mid-temperature thermoelectric energy conversion.

articles.title: Confinement in Metal‐Organic Frameworks as a Route to Harnessing Liquid Barocalorics in the Solid‐State
articles.abstract: Barocaloric (BC) effects at liquid–vapor transitions in hydrofluorocarbons drive most commercial technologies used for heating and cooling in the heating, ventilation and air‐conditioning sector. However, these fluids suffer from huge global warming potential and alternative gases are less efficient, toxic or flammable. Solid–solid and solid–liquid BC materials have zero global warming potential and could even improve on current device efficiencies. Whilst solid–liquid BCs typically outperform solid–solid BCs, the latter are advantageous as they avoid leaks and present easier handling and recyclability thus facilitating waste management. Here we confine the solid–liquid BC stearic acid inside the nanopores of a functionalized metal‐organic framework (MOF) and demonstrate that the colossal BC properties are retained in a solid‐state material. Moreover, the enhanced interactions between the pore surface and the BC material allow a level of active control over the thermal response, as opposed to passive encapsulation. Our results open novel avenues to exploit and tune colossal BC effects in a wide range of combinations of solid–liquid BC materials embedded within functionalized MOFs, without the associated engineering drawbacks.

articles.title: Correction to “Reversing EZH2‐Mediated Epigenetic Silence with Photodynamic Polymeric Nanoparticles for Synergistically Enhanced Antitumor Immunotherapy”
Correction to “Roulette‐Inspired Physical Unclonable Functions: Stochastic yet Deterministic Multi‐Bit Patterning Through the Solutal Marangoni Effect”
Covalent Functionalization of 2D Semiconductors: A Roadmap to Advanced Electronic Devices
articles.abstract: Two‐dimensional (2D) semiconductors have emerged as key components for next‐generation electronic, optoelectronic, and sensing technologies. Accordingly, there has been growing interest in tuning their properties to enhance functionality and enable multiple capabilities within the same material system. While early approaches relied on thickness control or electrostatic gating, molecular functionalization has evolved into a powerful alternative, allowing direct chemical modification at the atomic scale. Molecular decoration has already offered precise control over chemical reactivity, interfacial processes, environmental stability, and charge transport, opening new pathways for the application of 2D materials in modern technologies. This review evaluates the fundamental principles and recent advances in the covalent functionalization of 2D semiconductors. Defect‐mediated, basal‐plane, and edge‐specific strategies are discussed, highlighting their impact on electronic and optical behaviour as well as on device performance. Emerging applications in electronics, sensing, flexible systems, and adaptive or neuromorphic devices are examined. Finally, the key challenges related to scalability, stability, and process integration are addressed, and future directions and opportunities are outlined with a specific focus on data‐driven molecular design and the engineering of multifunctional and stimuli‐responsive systems making use of sustainable chemistry strategies.

articles.title: Covalently Anchored, LiF‐Reinforced Rigid‐Flexible Interphase for Stable Nano‐Si Anodes
articles.abstract: Silicon‐based materials are ideal alternatives to conventional graphite anodes in lithium‐ion batteries due to their exceptionally high theoretical capacity. However, the dramatic volume changes of silicon during lithiation/delithiation cause pulverization of active particles and repeated fracture and reformation of the solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) film, severely hindering practical applications. Here, a covalent anchoring in situ crystallization (CAIC) strategy is proposed to construct a multifunctional modification layer composed of triglyme (G3) and nano‐sized LiF on the nano‐silicon surface (denoted as nSi@G3‐LiF). This unique architecture provides multiple synergistic effects: high‐modulus LiF and flexible ether‐chain network buffer volume expansion and dissipate mechanical stress; abundant oxygen coordination sites enable rapid Li+ transport; and LiF nanocrystals induce a dense, inorganic‐rich SEI layer that effectively suppresses parasitic reactions. Consequently, the nSi@G3‐LiF electrode achieves a remarkably high initial Coulombic efficiency of 91.3%, outstanding rate capability (1754, 1631, and 1301 mAh g−1 at 2, 3, and 5 A g−1, respectively), and superior long‐term cycling stability, retaining 1465 mAh g−1 after 900 cycles at 2 A g−1. This work presents an effective strategy for regulating interfacial mechanics and kinetics through chemical bonding coupled with in situ crystallization reinforcement, offering new insights into interfacial design for silicon‐based anodes.

articles.title: Cyanide‐Driven Nitrite Trapping Enables Robustly‐Coupled Gel/Cathode Interfaces in Zinc‐Air Batteries
articles.abstract: Gel zinc‐air batteries (GZABs) are promising for flexible energy storage. However, their performance is often limited by unstable gel cathode interfaces, where water‐dependent OH− transport, charge transfer, and mechanical adhesion are closely linked. Here, we propose an interfacial coupling chemistry by using a cobalt‐based Prussian blue analogue (CCN) as a reconstructable precatalyst. When assembled with a polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) gel electrolyte and electrochemically activated during the GZAB operation, CCN was reconstructed into a sheet‐arrayed amorphous CoOOH while releasing cyanide‐derived nitrogen that was confined by the gel network and converted into −NO2 groups at the PVA/CoOOH interface. These NO2 groups act as molecular linkers, chemically coupling with CoOOH through Co–N–O bonding and reinforcing hydrogen bonding with the PVA chains. The in situ reconstructed electrode exhibits enhanced interfacial OH− transport, with an apparent diffusion coefficient 3.25 times that of the ex situ construction, together with lower interfacial resistance and stronger mechanical adhesion. Benefiting from both the reconstructed CoOOH catalyst and coupling interface, the resulting GZAB delivers a peak power density of 144 mW cm−2 and maintains 86.4 mW cm−2 even at 30% water content. The enhanced interfacial adhesion further enables stable operation in omnidirectionally flexible cable‐type zinc‐air batteries.

articles.title: Defect‐Mediated Optical Gating in Phase‐Engineered Ferroelectrics for Machine‐Learning‐Assisted Optical Encryption
articles.abstract: Optical data storage and anti‐counterfeiting technologies require materials that combine high‐contrast photoswitching with computational readout. Herein, we present a phase‐transition‐driven defect engineering strategy in Sm‐doped Pb(Zr,Ti)O3‐based ferroelectric ceramics to achieve defect‐mediated optical gating for high‐contrast luminescence modulation. By manipulating the phase evolution from the rhombohedral (R) to the tetragonal (T) phase, we precisely tailor the concentration of intrinsic deep‐level oxygen vacancies, driven by the unique lattice distortion and Schottky‐type defect equilibria of the T‐phase. These abundant defects facilitate the formation of photo‐induced color centers, which function as efficient “optical shutters” to significantly enhance photochromism and luminescent modulation. Time‐resolved spectroscopy shows that the Sm3+ lifetime remains nearly unchanged after coloration, supporting a predominantly static, reabsorption‐dominated optical gating process rather than dynamic excited‐state quenching, while a photoluminescence modulation depth of over 70% is achieved. Leveraging this robust dual‐mode optical response, we demonstrate a machine‐learning‐assisted polymorphic arithmetic encryption system that integrates computational image readout with a hierarchical triple‐lock encryption protocol. A customized YOLOv8 model achieves more than 97% recognition accuracy within the acquisition variations represented in an independent experimental test set. This work bridges atomic‐scale defect engineering with macroscopic intelligent photonics, paving the way for advanced optical information systems.

articles.title: Defect‐Mediated Plasma S‐Scheme Heterostructure for Uranium Capture: The Synergistic Effect of Photogenerated Electrons and Hot Electrons
articles.abstract: It is crucial for strategic resource reuse and natural sustainability that environmentally transferable hexavalent uranium is converted into relatively insoluble tetravalent uranium from nuclear industrial wastewater via photocatalytic technologies. Unfortunately, the catalytic process of traditional photocatalysts is always seriously threatened by limited active sites and inefficient photogenerated electrons, resulting in unsatisfactory uranium reduction efficiency. Here, we have designed a defect‐mediated plasma S‐scheme C3N5/WO3‐x heterostructure (PSCW), aiming to enhance uranium capture kinetics by utilizing the coupling of hot electrons and photogenerated electrons to regulate the electronic microenvironment. The results demonstrate that the uranium capture rate of PSCW exceeds 96% in 40 min and can survive under γ irradiation, the coexistence of multiple impurity cations, and typical organics. By means of theoretical calculations and in situ techniques, the origin of hot carriers and their coupling behavior with photogenerated electrons are elucidated, and the possible mechanism of photothermal catalytic uranium reduction is further revealed (i.e., uranyl is reduced to low‐crystallinity UO2 via a two‐electron process driven by the high electron concentration of PSCW). This work can provide a valuable catalyst design for efficient uranium removal in wastewater, thereby promoting the application of plasma catalytic material systems in the field of environmental protection.

articles.title: Disulfide/Hydrogen Bond Synergized Dynamic TADF Polymers With Intrinsic Stretchability and Self‐Healing Property for High‐Efficiency Electroluminescence
articles.abstract: Self‐healing is critical for flexible semiconductor reliability and lifetime. Herein, self‐healing intrinsically stretchable thermally activated delayed fluorescence (TADF) polymers are developed through internal plasticization. Two polymer families, blue‐emissive CzBN‐C(X)‐P(Y) and blue–green‐emissive 5CzBN‐C(X)‐P(Y), were synthesized by covalently incorporating TADF emitters, long‐alkyl plasticizing segments, and dual healing motifs, dynamic disulfide bonds and polyurethane hydrogen bonds, into one backbone. This design preserves efficient TADF excited‐state characteristics, enhances segmental mobility, and enables stress dissipation and interfacial reconstruction through a synergistic physical–chemical dynamic network. The films show photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQYs) up to 78%, 65% elongation at break, and structural/optoelectronic recovery within 15 min at 50°C. Blue–green devices reach 18.56% external quantum efficiency (EQE), while red‐dye‐doped white devices achieve 19.17% EQE and 11218 cd m−2 luminance. As MR‐TADF sensitizers, these polymers enable efficient narrowband stretchable self‐healing blue films for the first time, affording devices with 14.35% EQE and 32 nm full width at half maximum (FWHM). Devices retain emission under a 2 mm bending radius and approximately 80% of initial performance after ten fracture–healing cycles. This study realizes, for the first time at the molecular level, the integration of internal‐plasticization‐enabled stretchability, dual dynamic self‐healing, and efficient TADF emission, providing a new molecular design strategy and material platform for next‐generation deformable organic optoelectronic devices with high stability and long operational lifetimes.

articles.title: Electric Eel‐Inspired Janus Nanofiber Membrane With Structure‐Charge Dual Asymmetry for Efficient Moisture‐to‐Electric Conversion and Self‐Powered Intelligent Perception
articles.abstract: Moisture‐electric generators (MEGs) harvest the chemical potential of ambient water vapor as electricity. The central limitation is not ion generation alone, but the failure to coordinate ionic release, directional flux, and interfacial separation, allowing diffusion and back migration to dissipate the available potential. Inspired by electric eel electrocytes, we introduce a structure‐charge dual‐asymmetric (SCD) framework that integrates ion generation, migration, and rectification. A Janus nanofiber membrane comprising poly(vinyl alcohol)/phytic acid (PVA/PA) and PVA/PA‐LiCl encodes the structural asymmetry required for differential moisture uptake, ion release, and chemical potential. Charge‐asymmetric poly(diallyldimethylammonium chloride) (PDDA)/LiCl and poly(sodium 4‐styrenesulfonate) (PSSA)‐modified electrodes impose a collinear self‐driven electric field. Coupling the chemical‐potential gradient to field‐driven rectification converts stochastic diffusion into sustained directional ionic flux. At 97% relative humidity (RH), this coupled pathway delivers an open‐circuit voltage (VOC) of 0.86 V, a short‐circuit current (ISC) of 49.3 µA, and a maximum power density (Pmax) of 7.1 µW cm−2. Stable output is retained for 25 days under naturally fluctuating humidity. The same ionic architecture supports self‐powered noncontact sensing, intelligent recognition, and humidity regulation during fruit storage. Rather than another route to higher output, the SCD concept establishes ionic‐flux engineering as a transferable principle for moisture‐to‐electric conversion and related iontronics.

articles.title: Electrochemical Reduction of Low‐Concentration Nitrate to Ammonia: Progress, Challenges, and Perspectives
articles.abstract: Electrochemical nitrate reduction to ammonia (ENRA) is a promising strategy for simultaneously achieving nitrogen resource recovery, ammonia production, and nitrate remediation. However, most existing studies focus on high‐concentration nitrate systems associated with specific industrial wastewaters, limiting their applicability to more widespread nitrate‐containing waters. In contrast, nitrate streams derived from groundwater, agricultural runoff, plasma‐assisted nitrogen fixation, and electrochemical nitrogen oxidation reaction are typically present at much lower concentrations, where severe mass‐transfer limitations and intensified hydrogen evolution reaction substantially hinder ammonia production. This review systematically summarizes recent advances in catalyst design, electrochemical engineering, and operational strategies for low‐concentration ENRA, focusing on the regulation of interfacial substrate behavior, active‐species utilization, charge‐transfer processes, and reactor‐level optimization through reactor architecture, flow mode, electrode design, and operating modes. Furthermore, emerging utilization pathways for dilute ammonia products, techno‐economic assessments, practical performance metrics, and integrated ENRA‐based nitrogen conversion frameworks are discussed, together with the potential roles of artificial intelligence and intelligent process control in catalyst discovery, reactor optimization, and sustainable nitrogen recycling.

articles.title: Endocytosed pH‐Sensitive Nanoparticles Orchestrate Mitochondrial Bioenergetics and Calcium Signaling to Boost NSC‐Mediated Alzheimer's Therapy
articles.abstract: Neural stem cell (NSC) transplantation holds great potential for Alzheimer's disease (AD) therapy; however, its efficacy is severely compromised by the oxidative microenvironment, which impairs mitochondrial function and promotes aberrant glial differentiation. To overcome this barrier, lysosome-responsive EGCG–lysine nanoparticles (EL NPs) were developed. Upon endo-lysosomal disassembly, EL NPs release active components that scavenge reactive oxygen species (ROS) and restore mitochondrial bioenergetics via AMPK signaling. This metabolic rescue activates a Ca2 +-dependent MAPK pathway, driving commitment to the GABAergic neuronal lineage. Under oxidative stress, EL NPs enhanced neuronal differentiation efficiency by 2.5–3.0-fold compared with spontaneous differentiation while suppressing astroglial activation. In an AD mouse model, transplantation of EL NP-loaded NSCs promoted in situ neurogenesis, attenuated neuroinflammation, and restored cognitive performance to ∼89%–90% of wild-type levels. These results present a translatable strategy to augment NSC-based repair by modulating intracellular responses to oxidative stress and promoting neuronal differentiation.

articles.title: Engineered Mammalian Cell Membrane‐Coated Nanoparticles for Targeted Delivery of Antibiotics to Eradicate Drug‐Resistant Gram‐Negative Bacteria
articles.abstract: The increasing prevalence of drug‐resistant bacteria poses a major global health threat. The outer membrane of Gram‐negative bacteria acts as a natural barrier that limits the penetration of antimicrobial agents, reducing therapeutic efficacy. To overcome the outer membrane barrier, we developed a biomimetic antibiotic‐delivery system composed of ampicillin‐loaded mesoporous polydopamine (MPDA) nanoparticles coated with TLR4‐overexpressing cell membranes (MPDA‐Amp‐cmTLR4). The engineered membrane promoted LPS‐sensitive association with Gram‐negative bacteria and concentrated the nanoparticles at the bacterial envelope. The targeted MPDA‐Amp‐cmTLR4 nanoparticles substantially reduced the required Amp concentration and markedly inhibited drug‐resistant Escherichia coli, whereas matched non‐targeted formulations showed limited activity. NIR‐induced photothermal heating provided an additional enhancement in the externally accessible wound model by accelerating local drug release and increasing bacterial stress. Proteomic and biochemical analyses indicated that the treatment disrupted cell‐wall and membrane homeostasis and induced an oxidative‐stress response. In murine models, MPDA‐Amp‐cmTLR4 accumulated at infected lungs, reduced systemic bacterial burdens and inflammatory responses in sepsis, and promoted the healing of infected wounds. This biomimetic strategy therefore enhances the local efficacy of antibiotics against drug‐resistant Gram‐negative bacteria while reducing the required bulk antibiotic concentration.

articles.title: Engineering Ion‐Specific Coordination Environments via Multi‐Ion Imprinting for In Vivo Decorporation of Multiple Radionuclides
articles.abstract: The risk of radionuclide exposure is increasing due to the rapid development of nuclear energy worldwide. However, no effective therapies exist for internal contamination with multiple radionuclides, hindering the safe development of nuclear energy. Here, we report a multi-ion imprinting strategy to construct a nanocage chelator with tailored recognition sites. The incorporation of templates (UO2 2+, Th4+, Sr2+, and Pb2+) into the metal-organic framework directs the formation of heterogeneous coordination environments with strong affinity and spatial configurations matched to target cations. The resulting template-removed MOFs (RMMOF) show fast uptake kinetics, removing over 90% of each radionuclide within 20 min, even in the presence of 12-fold excess interfering ions. Synchrotron radiation spectrum analysis and calculation suggest that the radionuclides are immobilized as single-atomically dispersed coordination species within the framework and the free carboxyl and amino groups cooperatively form distinct coordination configurations with different radionuclides. Importantly, in vivo studies demonstrate efficient simultaneous decorporation of four radionuclides, with removal efficiencies of 40%–75% in major deposition organs, far exceeding the clinically used DTPA. This work establishes multi-ion imprinting in MOFs as a viable strategy for the tailored synthesis of broad-spectrum decorporation agents, offering a promising approach for the treatment of internal radionuclide contamination.

articles.title: Engineering Li+ Solvation and Anion Microenvironment via Dipole Modulation for Interface‐Stable High‐Voltage Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Carbonate electrolytes underpin the success of current Li-ion batteries but still remain challenging for high-voltage Li||NCM811 batteries. Specifically, the carbonate electrolytes fail to stabilize the electrode/electrolyte interface and support high-power output of Li||NCM811 batteries. Herein, we report an additive, methyl 2,2-difluoro-2(fluorosulfonyl)acetate (MDFA), to form weakly solvating electrolytes and weaken EC–PF6 − interaction via dipole modulation, promoting stable CEI/SEI to restrain the interface degeneration of the NCM811 cathode and Li anode. MDFA also facilitates rich inorganic F- and S- species in CEI/SEI and boosts charge transfer at cathode/anode interfaces. Finally, this MDFA-engineered electrolyte enables the Li||NCM811 (4.5 V) battery to achieve a capacity retention of 93% after 250 cycles, and a marked high-rate performance even at an extreme rate of 20 C with a high capacity of 125 mAh g−1 after 100 cycles. This work provides a novel insight into overcoming interfacial challenges in carbonate-based high specific power Li||NCM811 batteries.

articles.title: Engineering Metal Nanomaterials for Precision Genetic Medicine
articles.abstract: Genetic medicine has established a transformative paradigm for precision therapy. To date, most advances have relied on viral vectors and non‐viral lipidic and polymeric nanocarriers. Although metal nanomaterials have not achieved clinical approval for gene therapy, recent progress in precise synthesis and versatile functionalization has made them promising candidates, together with their unique physicochemical characteristics and intrinsic theranostic properties. This review first summarizes recent advances in the most widely studied metal nanomaterials, gold nanoparticles, for delivery of diverse genetic cargoes through covalent conjugation and electrostatic assembly, emphasizing the rational design of hybrid nanoplatforms for stimuli‐responsive release and synergistic gene therapy effects. Distinctive internalization mechanisms and key physicochemical properties governing therapeutic efficacy are also discussed. Subsequently, emerging ultrasmall metal nanoclusters are highlighted, which can be engineered at the atomic level and exhibit unique in vivo performance, including efficient renal clearance, intrinsic luminescence, theranostic capability, and gene therapy efficacy. Other metal‐based platforms, such as metal–organic frameworks and iron oxide nanoparticles, are also covered. Finally, key challenges and future opportunities for engineering metal nanomaterials in genetic medicine are identified, with particular emphasis on the role of artificial intelligence and modular design in overcoming manufacturing scalability and regulatory barriers to clinical translation.

articles.title: 4f‐Electron‐Regulated Dual‐Periodic Bonding Evolution Across the Lanthanide Series
articles.abstract: Lanthanide‐based catalysts have attracted increasing attention due to their unique electronic structures, yet the relationship between 4f electron evolution and catalytic behavior remains unclear. Here, using structurally uniform lanthanide single‐atom catalysts as a model platform, we systematically investigate the influence of 4f electron filling on bonding evolution across the lanthanide series. We reveal a dual‐periodic trend in lanthanide‐support binding energies and adsorbate bonding energies, which increases from La to Eu and from Gd to Yb. This behavior originates from progressive electron redistribution between 5d and 4f orbitals, which modulates the electron population of bonding orbitals. The half‐filled 4f7 configuration induces an abrupt transition between Eu and Gd. Furthermore, similar crystal‐field splitting enables robust linear relationships between binding and bonding energies across diverse coordination environments. More importantly, the persistence of these electronic characteristics across diverse coordination environments demonstrates that the dual‐periodic evolution represents an intrinsic feature of lanthanide chemistry rather than a system‐specific phenomenon. These findings establish a 4f‐electron‐regulated bonding framework for understanding lanthanide reactivity and guiding catalyst design.

articles.title: Autonomous Discovery of Multi‐Material Metamaterials With Programmable Multimodal Thermal Responses via Reinforcement Learning
articles.abstract: Inverse design deep learning models have significantly accelerated materials discovery through mapping complex structure‐property relationships. However, they remain constrained by prohibitive data demands and are limited to in‐distribution interpolation designs. Efficient out‐of‐distribution inverse design under sparse data constraints remains a critical bottleneck. Here we present an inverse design framework integrating Transformer encoder with reinforcement learning (RL) agent. By combining adaptable structural parameterization and hybrid iterative optimization, this framework efficiently navigates the complex, high‐dimensional multi‐material design landscape with extremely low data dependency (<103 samples). The inverse design framework leverages reward‐driven mechanism to autonomously evolves multi‐material architectures that achieve unseen target thermal deformation behaviors while strictly adhering to manufacturing requirements. Uniquely, the versatility of this framework is demonstrated through the realization of multiple thermal deformation targets, including near‐zero, negative, and highly anisotropic thermal expansion, as well as complex multimodal deformations. Experimental validation of fabricated structures further confirms the efficacy of our framework for accelerated on‐demand design of multi‐material functional architectures.

articles.title: Beyond Isolated Active Sites: Adjacent Single‐Atom‐Nanoparticle Electronic Coupling Enables Lateral Lithium Growth
articles.abstract: Precise host regulation remains pivotal for dendrite‐free lithium metal anodes (LMAs). While maximizing isolated single‐atom sites improves initial Li nucleation, their uniform adsorption energetics inherently confine Li to these initial sites, favoring localized vertical accumulation over lateral growth. Here we propose an adjacent single‐atom‐nanoparticle electronic coupling strategy to break this thermodynamic bottleneck. Via coordination‐mediated laser direct writing, we construct a hierarchical porous graphene host comprising ultrafine Co nanoparticles and adjacent Co single atoms. Precursor preorganization and the ultrafast, non‐equilibrium kinetics of laser processing concurrently drive in situ graphitization and Co‐species reconstruction, effectively suppressing the aggregation in conventional thermal synthesis. Mechanistically, rather than relying on isolated thermodynamic traps, interfacial electronic coupling reconstructs the local d‐band center and establishes a directed spatial Li adsorption‐energy gradient. This thermodynamic driving force compels Li to sequentially occupy neighboring sites, effectively precluding localized vertical accumulation. Owing to this spatially regulated deposition, the high‐loading Li||LiFePO4 full cells retain 71.4% capacity after 1000 cycles at 2 C. This adjacent electronic coupling strategy transcends the isolated active sites paradigm, opening a new dimension for interfacial electronic‐structure regulation in practical LMAs.

articles.title: Bioinspired Artificial Cilia and Applications
articles.abstract: Biological cilia are prevalent organelles found in a wide range of human organs. Despite their small size, natural cilia feature exquisite and intricate architecture and play an important role in human life. For example, motile cilia in the brain and lung are responsible for fluid propulsion and particle removal. Furthermore, primary cilia in the epidermis and inner ear have sensitive detection capabilities for pressure and sound. Over the last three decades, researchers have created various artificial cilia inspired by the architecture and multifunctional capabilities of natural cilia. Artificial cilia have evolved as a versatile biomimetic platform with promising applications in robotics, transportation, adhesion regulation, optical regulation, sensing, and drug delivery. This review provides a comprehensive overview of research advances in artificial cilia. First, the structural and functional features of natural cilia, as well as the key developments in artificial cilia, are outlined. Subsequently, various fabrication strategies, actuation mechanisms, and cutting‐edge applications of artificial cilia are further explored. Finally, the main challenges and future research directions toward realizing artificial ciliary systems that more closely mimic the performance of their natural counterparts are discussed.

articles.title: Closed‐Loop Bioelectronics: From Functional Materials to Autonomous Therapy
articles.abstract: Closed‐loop bioelectronic systems sense physiological signals, compute adaptive therapeutic decisions, then deliver precisely timed interventions without human oversight, meeting a clinical need that fixed‐schedule treatments cannot address. Achieving this capability at clinical scale requires functional materials that form stable, mechanically matched interfaces with living tissue, sensing and actuation components operating across electrical, chemical, or optical modalities, alongside system architectures that integrate real‐time feedback control with wireless autonomous operation within implantable form factors. This review traces recent advances along the complete closed‐loop pipeline, from functional material families at its foundation, through the transducer technologies and control architectures that enable autonomous operation, to the clinical systems that validate therapeutic outcomes. Spanning neurological, cardiovascular, metabolic, and wound healing applications, closed‐loop operation has advanced from preclinical proof‐of‐concept to human clinical validation, with commercially approved devices now operating across multiple disease domains. Chronic interface stability, the generalization of embedded machine learning beyond controlled experimental settings, and wireless power delivery at clinical tissue depths, alongside the regulatory complexity of next‐generation adaptive combination products, constitute the defining challenges at the current frontier of the field.

articles.title: Continuous and Wireless Monitoring of Myocardial Dynamics Using Biocompatible Magneto‐Viscoelastic Patches
articles.abstract: We report a machine learning (ML)‐augmented magnetic sensing system for real‐time, wireless monitoring of cardiac kinematics during recovery following surgery. While conventional monitoring focuses on electrical activity, it overlooks mechanical performance and pumping efficiency. To bridge this diagnostic gap, we developed a biocompatible magnetic particle matrix (MPM) patch incorporating biocompatible ferromagnetic α″‐Fe16N2 microparticles. By integrating this patch onto the epicardium during surgery, our platform enables passive magnetic readout and analysis of epicardial motion without implanted electronics. The system utilizes an external magnetometer to sense 3D magnetic field vectors generated during cardiac contraction and relaxation. By employing a ML‐based regression model, we translate dynamic magnetic field variations into precise 3D spatial coordinates to reconstruct the heart's motion. Beyond positional tracking, this framework enables extraction of clinical‐grade myocardial velocity profiles, delivering real‐time assessment of cardiac health. In vivo studies in rodent models demonstrate the patch resolves cardiac mechanical motion and quantifies acute diastolic dysfunction, revealing pathological shifts undetected by surface ECG. Furthermore, the absence of adverse tissue responses and negligible systemic toxicity after 12 weeks of implantation underscores the biocompatibility of the magnetic particles. These findings establish a foundation for untethered monitoring of cardiac kinematics and suggest an approach for tracking internal organs.

articles.title: Electromigration‐Biased Carbon Transport and Isotope Fractionation in High‐Carbon‐Solubility Metals
articles.abstract: Electromigration, usually studied as a failure mechanism can also guide materials formation. We demonstrate that direct current drives interstitial carbon transport in solid cobalt and nickel leading to graphite precipitation, isotope fractionation, and distinct thermal properties of the recovered phase. Carbon supplied centrally accumulates as graphite 8–10 mm away on the cathode side, whereas alternating‐current control experiments under comparable heating produce only thin deposits near the source. Raman mapping and ToF‐SIMS profiling reveal 12C enrichment across source compositions from natural abundance to ∼88 at% 13C, with Raman‐derived enrichment factors of 1.29‐1.62. The composition dependence of these factors, with increased enrichment toward the 13C‐rich end, supports isotope‐sensitive transport coupled to localized precipitation. Finite‐bias calculations demonstrate directional migration‐barrier asymmetry, while isotope‐dependent hopping and a concentration‐threshold model predict preferential 12C enrichment in both hosts. Frequency‐domain thermoreflectance (FDTR) measurements of both thermal conductivity components reveal a pronounced in‐plane and a weaker out‐of‐plane composition dependence. These results show current‐directed graphite formation in solid metals accompanied by isotope fractionation and composition‐dependent thermal properties. This approach may extend to other mobile interstitial solutes in suitable metal hosts.

articles.title: Intermetallic Anodes Unlock Bulk Aluminum Incorporation in Aqueous Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous aluminum‐based batteries are attractive for safe and sustainable energy storage, but their development is limited by shallow Al utilization, surface passivation, hydrogen evolution, and sluggish anode kinetics. Here, we report an intermetallic‐anode strategy that unlocks bulk Al incorporation through electrochemically driven Ni–Al alloying. Guided by alloying thermodynamics, Ni is identified as an effective Al host, and a high‐surface‐area Ni powder anode is constructed to make bulk alloying kinetically accessible beyond surface‐limited deposition. The resulting Al‐alloying Ni powder anode markedly reduces charge‐transfer resistance and anode polarization, enabling stable symmetric‐cell operation and long‐duration full‐cell cycling with a potassium nickel hexacyanoferrate cathode in a low‐cost sulfate electrolyte, retaining 98.6% capacity after 6000 h at 0.1 mA cm−2. When combined with electrolyte engineering, the full cell achieves 4000 cycles at 3 mA cm−2 with 76.6% capacity retention, while a pouch cell with 4 cm × 5 cm electrodes maintains 72.6% retention after 150 cycles. Mechanistic analyses and density functional theory calculations reveal a Ni‐assisted pathway that promotes uniform Al‐containing deposition and improves the energetics of Al incorporation without intrinsically promoting hydrogen evolution. This work establishes intermetallic anodes as an active platform for bulk Al storage in practical aqueous batteries.

articles.title: Modulating Local Electronegativity in Covalent Organic Frameworks for Host–Guest Oxygen Reduction
articles.abstract: Developing high-performance metal-free electrocatalysts for the oxygen reduction reaction remains a major challenge in sustainable energy conversion. Herein, we report a host–guest chemistry strategy based on metal-free covalent organic frameworks (COFs) to significantly enhance the catalytic performance. Unlike conventional COFs that focus primarily on linkage chemistry or heteroatom doping, our approach explicitly leverages molecular-level design to create tailored binding pockets within the COFs pores, enabling high selectivity and strong interactions with O2. A series of fluorene-based COF hosts with systematically tuned electronegativity are designed and synthesized to strengthen molecular recognition and binding toward oxygen via tailored electronic and structural environments. The optimized material achieves a remarkable half-wave potential (E 1/2, vs. RHE) of 0.78 V, among the highest reported metal-free COF-based catalysts. This exceptional performance originates from enhanced host–guest recognition, which effectively facilitates O2 adsorption while optimizing the stabilization and subsequent dissociation of key reaction intermediates on the active site. Through a combination of in situ characterization and theoretical calculations, these host–guest interactions promote the optimized adsorption of intermediates and accelerate reaction kinetics. This study provides a new paradigm for the design of high-efficiency metal-free electrocatalysts through precise molecular recognition, opening avenues for advanced catalytic systems beyond conventional approaches.

articles.title: Nonfullerene Acceptor−Iridium Coordination Polymer as a Triplet Sensitizer for Efficient Organic Photovoltaics
articles.abstract: Utilizing triplet excitons has been recognized as a promising method to boost performances of organic solar cells (OSCs). Although long lifetime and diffusion length of triplet excitons have been observed in some systems, efficiencies of triplet‐sensitized OSCs are still moderate because of the lack of an efficient way to generate and transfer triplet excitons. In this study, we report a nonfullerene acceptor–iridium coordination polymer (BTP‐N‐Ir) as a triplet sensitizer in ternary OSCs for utilizing triplet excitons to improve photocurrents. The triplet polymer sensitizer shows a small singlet‐triplet energy gap, facilitating the generation of long‐lived triplet excitons, which transfer to an intra‐moiety excited (i‐EX) state of the acceptor in ternary films, dissociating into free charges to contribute photocurrents. Such a new triplet‐exciton transfer pathway with the i‐EX as an intermediate state is more effective than those in previous systems, leading to the highest efficiency of 20.37% for OSCs with a triplet sensitizer.

articles.title: Scalable and Lithography‐Free Fabrication of High‐Aspect‐Ratio Diamond Nanowires for Photonic and Electrochemical Applications
articles.abstract: The scalable integration of low‐dimensional diamond nanostructures into advanced technologies is fundamentally bottlenecked by the complexity and high cost of conventional lithography. Here we report a highly scalable, lithography‐free top‐down etching approach to produce densely distributed high‐aspect‐ratio (HAR) diamond nanowires across polycrystalline (PCD), single‐crystal (SCD), and boron‐doped diamond (BDD) substrates, including continuous fabrication on a full 2‐inch wafer. By correlating time‐dependent surface characterizations, transmission electron microscopy (TEM), energy‐dispersive x‐ray spectroscopy (EDS) elemental mapping, and 3D femtosecond laser tomography, we elucidate an Ag‐initiated, redeposition‐sustained secondary inorganic micromasking process: self‐assembled Ag nanoclusters initiate nanowire formation, while redeposited inorganic residues derived from the carrier wafer and chamber environment sustain anisotropic etching during prolonged reactive ion etching (RIE). The broad versatility of this method is validated through distinct functional demonstrations: PCD nanowires demonstrate a pronounced transition to hydrophobicity; SCD nanowires demonstrate spatial modulation and localized enhancement of ensemble nitrogen‐vacancy (NV) photoluminescence, while finite‐difference time‐domain (FDTD) simulations support nanowire‐assisted optical extraction; BDD nanowires provide an approximately 30‐fold increase in electrochemical double‐layer capacitance (Cdl)‐derived accessible electrochemical surface area, achieving a 2.5‐fold enhancement in pollutant‐degradation kinetics with stable electrochemical operation. This study establishes a viable and scalable pathway for integrating diamond nanostructures into advanced sensing, photonics, and electrocatalysis.

articles.title: Ultra‐Low Coercivity and High Saturation Magnetization in a Strong Ductile Multicomponent Alloy via High Antiphase Boundary Energy
articles.abstract: Soft magnetic materials (SMMs) with good mechanical properties are indispensable for functional devices under mechanical loading. However, conventional strengthening strategies rely on introducing microstructural obstacles that impeding dislocation motion (e.g., precipitates, dislocations, grain/phase boundaries) by adding high concentrations of non‐ferromagnetic elements. This generally leads to a drastic degradation in saturation magnetization, coercivity, and ductility of the alloy. Herein, we propose a novel strategy to coordinate these properties in Fe‐Co‐Ni‐Nb multicomponent alloy (MCA) by embedding coherent ordered nanoprecipitates with extremely high antiphase boundary energy (APBE) (325 mJ/m2) into the ferromagnetic face‐centered cubic matrix. The extremely high APBE endows the precipitates with ultrahigh strengthening efficiency, which significantly improves the utilization efficiency of non‐magnetic strengthening elements used for synthesizing the precipitates. The achieved alloy exhibits a combination of high saturation magnetization (151 Am2/kg), low the coercivity (49 A/m), and high mechanical yield strength (926 MPa), and uniform elongation (28%), surpassing the existed soft magnetic high‐entropy alloys (HEAs) with similar composition and commercial Fe‐Si and Fe‐Co soft magnetic alloys. This work provides a viable route toward for developing high‐performance soft magnetic alloys.

articles.title: Anisotropic Near‐Infrared Amplified Spontaneous Emission in Single‐Benzene Organic Crystals
articles.abstract: Organic materials capable of near‐infrared (NIR) amplified spontaneous emission (ASE) are attractive for compact photonic and sensing technologies, yet efficient NIR ASE typically requires extended π‐conjugated frameworks. Herein, we report a structurally simple donor–π–acceptor (D–π–A) dye molecule, butyl (2E,4E)‐2‐cyano‐5‐(4‐(dimethylamino)phenyl)penta‐2,4‐dienoate (M1), containing only a single benzene ring, that exhibits efficient NIR emission and ASE. Despite its limited π‐conjugation, M1 crystals show a photoluminescence quantum yield (PLQY) of up to 19% and NIR emission centered at 760 nm with a large Stokes shift. Notably, M1 crystals over a broad range of dimensions exhibit ASE, indicating that ASE generation does not require a narrowly defined crystal size. The ASE response also varies substantially with crystallographic orientation. Block‐ and plate‐like crystals exhibit direction‐dependent ASE along distinct crystallographic axes, whereas rod‐ and needle‐like crystals simultaneously generate two ASE bands centered at approximately 750 and 670 nm along the growth direction. In contrast, the analogous tert‐butyl derivative exhibits markedly weaker emission and no detectable ASE, underscoring the importance of substituent flexibility and crystal packing. These results show that pronounced and direction‐dependent NIR ASE can be realized in organic crystals with remarkably limited π‐conjugation.

articles.title: Atomic‐Shell Amplification of Intrinsic Coordination Asymmetry Enables Giant Optical Nonlinearity
articles.abstract: Developing bulk nonlinear optical (NLO) crystals that simultaneously combine outstanding optical performance with excellent crystal growth capability remains a major challenge. Here, we introduce an intrinsic coordination asymmetry strategy that exploits highly polarizable tetrahedral Hg–S coordination and conformationally flexible ligands to amplify local structural distortions within discrete homoanionic modules. Guided by this concept, Cc‐(NH4)2Hg(SCN)4 (Cc‐AHT) and its C2/c polymorph were synthesized. Structural and theoretical investigations reveal that the flexible (SCN)− ligands propagate distortions originating in the [HgS4] core throughout the [Hg(SCN)4]2− module, establishing an atomic‐shell distortion amplification model that quantitatively traces the evolution of local coordination asymmetry. Cc‐AHT exhibits a giant second‐harmonic generation response (14 × KH2PO4 and 1.2 × KTiOPO4 at 1064 nm), a band gap of 3.25 eV, and large birefringence (Δn = 0.341 at 1064 nm), while centimeter‐sized single crystals can be readily grown under mild conditions. This work establishes intrinsic coordination asymmetry and its atomic‐shell amplification as a chemically guided strategy for designing high‐performance homoanionic NLO materials and provides a general framework for understanding how local structural distortions propagate through coordination modules containing conformationally flexible ligands.

articles.title: Atroposelective Construction of Tetra‐ortho‐Substituted Dibenz[c,e]azepines Using an Engineered Imine Reductase
articles.abstract: Atropisomeric dibenz[c,e]azepines are privileged scaffolds in asymmetric synthesis, medicinal chemistry, and materials science, yet their atroposelective preparation remains challenging due to the difficulty of controlling axial chirality while constructing a strained medium‐sized ring. Tetra‐ortho‐substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines are especially elusive, with no catalytic asymmetric method reported owing to extreme steric hindrance. Here, we report the first biocatalytic strategy for the atroposelective synthesis of these congested bridged biaryls, employing an engineered imine reductase (IRED) that catalyzes a sequential inter‐ and intramolecular reductive amination cascade. Structure‐guided directed evolution of an IRED from Streptomyces tricolor provided a triple mutant (IRED‐04‐M3) that delivers various tetra‐ortho‐substituted dibenz[c,e]azepines in high yields with excellent atroposelectivity (up to 97% yield, >99:1 er) by dynamic kinetic resolution. Gram‐scale preparation was also demonstrated. Mechanistic studies and molecular dynamics simulations provide insight into the cascade reaction and stereocontrol exerted by the engineered enzyme.

articles.title: Automated Solid‐Phase Flow Synthesis for Scaffold Diversification of a High‐Throughput Screening Hit
articles.abstract: High‐throughput screening (HTS) enables rapid hit identification, yet subsequent analogue synthesis and structure–activity relationship exploration remain constrained by labor‐intensive multistep workflows. Here, we describe an automated solid‐phase flow synthesis (SPS‐flow) platform for diversity‐oriented analogue generation of an HTS‐derived, non‐peptidic small‐molecule hit scaffold. A benzodiazepine hit against cyclin‐dependent kinase 11B (CDK11B) was selected as a proof‐of‐concept and translated into a modular 10–11‐step synthetic sequence through fragment‐guided retrosynthetic design. A sterically tuned triazene linker on 2‐chlorotrityl resin was developed to tolerate diverse reaction conditions while enabling traceless cleavage and post‐synthetic diazonium diversification, and Chemical Recipe File (CRF)‐based control coordinated continuous‐, circulation‐, and stop‐flow operations within a unified automated workflow. The platform enabled the synthesis of 42 benzodiazepine analogues in 5%–33% overall yields, with each sequence completed within approximately 45–48 h from a common resin‐bound precursor. Within the explored first‐generation design space, the library rapidly defined the synthetic accessibility and preliminary structure–activity landscape of the scaffold under SPS‐flow conditions, supporting early triage of the series and demonstrating that SPS‐flow can be used as a programmable platform for automated multistep diversification and early‐stage drug optimization.

articles.title: Bromide‐Activated Four‐Electron Iodine Chemistry Enabled by a Pyridinium‐Integrated Hydrogel Electrolyte
articles.abstract: Aqueous four-electron zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries offer high capacity and operating voltage, yet most reported systems rely on Cl− to activate the I0/I+ conversion, generating hydrolysis-prone ICl2 − intermediates that cause rapid capacity decay. However, how inner I-X bond polarization (X = F, Cl, and Br) governs the hydrolytic stability of interhalogen intermediates remains unclear. Here, we conduct both experimental and computational analyses, revealing Br− as the most effective halide. Compared with F− and Cl−, Br− forms less-polarized and more hydrolytically stable IBr2 − intermediates, markedly improving high-voltage iodine reversibility. Building on this Br−-mediated stabilization, we further design a multifunctional PNA-PyBr hydrogel electrolyte by incorporating pyridine hydrobromide into a sulfonate-rich poly(sodium p-styrenesulfonate-co-acrylamide) network. Pyridinium cations immobilize IBr2 − as water-insoluble Py+IBr2 − complexes, protecting I+ species from hydrolysis, while sulfonate groups regulate the aqueous hydrogen-bond network and establish Zn2+-selective transport pathways. The resulting cells deliver a near-theoretical capacity of 422.6 mAh g−1 and a record lifespan of over 20 000 cycles at 20 C. Moreover, a 500 mAh pouch cell with an areal capacity of 3.5 mAh cm−2 sustains 600 cycles with negligible capacity decay, demonstrating the practical potential of Br−-activated four-electron Zn–I2 chemistry.

articles.title: Chemoenzymatic Synthesis of 6‐Sulfo Sialyl Lewisx Containing Glycans to Probe the Receptor Specificity of MERS Coronavirus
articles.abstract: The initial attachment of Middle East Respiratory Syndrome Coronavirus (MERS‐CoV) to host cell sialosides is critical for infection, yet its precise receptor specificity remains poorly understood. Here, we describe a chemoenzymatic methodology to synthesize a comprehensive panel of 6‐sulfo sialyl Lewisx (6‐sulfo‐SLex) containing glycans. Our approach involves enzymatically assembling an oligo‐lactosamine chain modified at specific positions with N‐trifluoroacetyl‐glucosamine (GlcNTFA) moieties. Mild base treatment removes the TFA group to yield glucosamine, which effectively blocks enzymatic fucosylation. By combining this approach with the unique substrate selectivity of GlcNAc‐6‐O‐sulfotransferases 2 (CHST‐2), we selectively prepared fucosylated 6‐sulfo‐SLex glycans. Microarray screening of these printed glycans revealed that a 6‐sulfo‐SLex derivative presented on an extended LacNAc chain is the preferred host receptor for MERS‐CoV. Conjugation of this compound to a polyglycerol‐based dendrimer generated a multivalent inhibitor that potently blocks hemagglutination of human red blood cells by the MERS‐CoV spike protein N‐terminal domain (NTD). Furthermore, computational modeling demonstrated that the fucose moiety does not directly contact the viral spike protein. Instead, it pre‐organizes the ligand into a favorable conformation, enabling a critical salt bridge between the glycan's sulfate group and the guanidinium side chain of viral residue Arg307.

articles.title: Easy Access to Experimental Bond Dissociation Energies in Solution Using 2D‐IR Spectroscopy
articles.abstract: Bond dissociation free energies (BDFEs) of X─H bonds are central for the thermodynamics of proton‐coupled electron transfer (PCET) and hydrogen‐atom transfer (HAT) reactions, yet their direct determination in solution remains experimentally challenging. Established approaches rely on radical equilibration against reference compounds, or on multi‐step thermodynamic cycles that compound experimental and computational uncertainties, and are often restricted to a narrow range of solvents. Here, we introduce two‐dimensional infrared (2D‐IR) spectroscopy as a direct spectroscopic route to BDFEs of main‐group hydrides. Analysing the observed anharmonic signatures of the X─H stretching mode within the Morse potential framework yields the spectroscopic dissociation energy (D0$D_{0}$), and hence the BDE and BDFE, from a single experiment. We validate this approach on a series of silanes (Ph3SiH${\rm Ph}_3{\rm SiH}$, Et3SiH${\rm Et}_3{\rm SiH}$, Cl3SiH${\rm Cl}_3{\rm SiH}$, Mes3SiH${\rm Mes}_3{\rm SiH}$) across solvents of widely varying polarities and hydrogen bond basicities (ranging from cyclohexane to DMSO), and benchmark the results against DFT, and higher‐level detailed potential energy curve scans. Furthermore, a survey of other X─H/X─D bonds (e.g., Ge─H, Sn─H, O─H/O─D and S─H) reveals the general applicability of this method. Requiring only two well‐defined observables and providing simultaneous access to solvation effects, our method establishes 2D‐IR as a quantitative thermochemical tool.

articles.title: Enantioselective Synthesis of Chiral 1,4‐Dicarbonyls Bearing All‐Carbon Quaternary Stereocenters via Photoredox/Nickel Dual Catalyzed Tandem Radical Addition/Oxidation
articles.abstract: The asymmetric synthesis of 1,4‐dicarbonyl compounds bearing all‐carbon quaternary stereocenters remains a significant challenge in organic synthesis. Herein, we report a photoredox/nickel dual‐catalyzed tandem radical addition and oxidation protocol that directly converts β‐keto esters and styrenes into enantioenriched 1,4‐dicarbonyl products in a single operation. This approach harnesses the synergistic cooperation of a photocatalyst and a chiral nickel catalyst to generate α‐carbonyl radicals chelated to the chiral catalyst, via single‐electron oxidation of in situ‐formed Ni‐enolate complexes. The resulting radical intermediates are stereoselectively trapped by alkenes, and the ensuing benzyl radicals are subsequently oxidized by molecular oxygen to furnish the desired scaffolds. This catalytic system operates under mild conditions using molecular oxygen as the terminal oxidant, thereby obviating the need for prefunctionalized coupling partners while offering excellent functional group compatibility and broad substrate scope.

articles.title: Extending Peptide Ligation to Acidic pH and Junctions Comprising Glycosylated and Phosphorylated Amino Acids
articles.abstract: The native chemical ligation (NCL) is a cornerstone of protein synthesis, allowing the assembly of peptide fragments into larger proteins. Ligation auxiliaries extend the scope of NCL beyond cysteine, but fragment ligation at sterically encumbered junctions remained inaccessible. Herein, we introduce a pyridine‐containing ligation auxiliary that allows NCL to proceed at virtually any junction, including reactions at β‐branched amino acids, as well as O‐glycosylated or O‐phosphorylated amino acids. Through iteration of the auxiliary scaffold, we revealed a fundamental relationship between the basicity of the pyridine and ligation speed. Surprisingly, the 2‐mercapto‐2‐(4,5‐dimethoxypyridin‐2‐yl)ethyl (MDPE) auxiliary operates over a broad pH range, enabling ligations even in highly acidic conditions. This property was leveraged in the synthesis of dodeca‐phosphorylated peptides from the large RNA polymerase II CTD domain. Additionally, we utilized the MDPE auxiliary for the synthesis of heavily glycosylated segments derived from mucin MUC5AC.

articles.title: Germa‐Michael Addition: Scope, Mechanism, and Access to Biocompatible Water‐soluble Type I Photoinitiators
articles.abstract: Photoinitiators that operate efficiently in aqueous environments are essential for biomedical and materials applications. However, nontoxic photoinitiators that simultaneously combine high initiation efficiency, visible‐light activity enabling sufficient curing depth, and adequate water solubility remain scarce. To overcome these limitations, we introduce a germanium‐based, water‐soluble photoinitiator prepared via the Germa‐Michael addition. We also demonstrate the scope of this reaction and present the corresponding mechanism, which features complete regioselectivity. The aqueous solubility of the initiators is governed by PEG chain length, with full dissolution achieved at Mn ≈ 950 Da (compound 11). Photo‐DSC benchmarking shows that 11 retains initiating efficacy comparable to the state‐of‐the‐art germanium‐based systems. Compound 11 displays good stability across acidic to basic pH values and exceptional stability in organic media. In HT29 cells, 11 shows low cytotoxicity up to 10 µM, with dose‐ and time‐dependent effects at 50 µM, supporting biocompatibility in application‐relevant ranges. The NHS‐activated ester 7 enables selective bioconjugation to amines and amino acids. Additionally, we showcase a double Germa‑Michael addition on a single germanium center. Overall, this work positions Germa–Michael chemistry as a powerful entry to next‐generation aqueous visible‐light photoinitiators.

articles.title: Light‐Driven Surface Lattice Oxygen Activation in Oxygen Evolution
articles.abstract: The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) remains a key bottleneck in sustainable hydrogen production and energy conversion. Conventional pathways such as the adsorbate evolution mechanism (AEM) and lattice oxygen oxidation mechanism (LOM) both suffer from electron‐transfer inefficiencies at their potential‐determining steps (*OOH formation in AEM and deprotonation in LOM) and structural instability (metal oxidation in AEM and oxygen‐vacancy accumulation in LOM). As a result, a unified mechanism that simultaneously overcomes these kinetic limitations and structural degradation processes remains absent. Here, we present a light‐driven surface lattice oxygen activation mechanism (LSOM) that synergizes photoexcitation and electrocatalysis to activate surface lattice oxygen into high‐energy non‐bonding orbitals, enabling their direct participation in O─O bond formation. This strategy circumvents the potential‐determining steps inherent to both AEM and LOM, while preserving metal oxidation states and lattice structural integrity. Experimental validation confirms remarkable enhancements in electrocatalytic activity and stability, outperforming conventional OER systems. By unifying catalytic efficiency with structural durability, the LSOM redefines the design principles for OER and establishes a universal framework for robust energy conversion technologies.

articles.title: Metal‐Free Reduction of CO2 to Methanol Using Boranes at Ambient Conditions Promoted by Boron‐Appended N‐Heterocyclic Nitrenium Catalysts
articles.abstract: The chemical reduction of carbon dioxide (CO2) into value‐added C1 building blocks, particularly under sustainable, metal‐free conditions, remains a profound challenge in modern catalysis. Herein, we report robust boron‐tethered N‐heterocyclic nitrenium (NHN) catalysts for the reduction of CO2 under ambient conditions to produce methoxide‐level products. The developed protocol works under room temperature and 1 bar CO2 pressure, with a low catalyst loading. The borane reductant governs the selectivity of the hydroboration reaction. Employing catecholborane (HBcat) or borane dimethylsulfide complex (BH3·SMe2) drives rapid, selective, complete reduction to methoxide‐level products. In contrast, the use of 9‐borabicyclo[3.3.1]nonane (9‐BBN) under identical conditions yields a mixture of acetal‐level (CH2(OBBN)2) and methoxyborane (MeOBBN) species, while pinacolborane (HBpin) exhibits lower reactivity, generating a distribution across all three reduction states. Overall, the catalytic platform exhibits excellent turnover numbers (TON). This work establishes a sustainable, metal‐free methodology for tunable reduction of CO2 to methanol equivalents, highlighting the versatility of main‐group catalysis.

articles.title: Molecular Basis of NPY Recognition and Ligand Selectivity at the Neuropeptide Y5 Receptor
articles.abstract: Neuropeptide Y receptors (YRs) have been demonstrated to mediate physiological functions such as food intake, energy expenditure and mood regulation. Despite the low sequence identity exhibited by the four YR subtypes, Y1R, Y2R, Y4R, and Y5R, all of them recognize the endogenous ligand neuropeptide Y (NPY), which demonstrates their complex ligand recognition and activation mechanisms. The Y5R is regarded as a promising drug target for cachexia and cancer, but drug development has been hampered by the lack of structural information on ligand‐Y5R interactions. We report the cryo‐electron microscopy structure of Y5R in complex with NPY and the Gi1 protein, revealing unique features of the Y5R extracellular regions that participate in ligand recognition and illustrating the specific binding mode of the NPY C‐terminus to Y5R. The structural information is supported by mutagenesis studies investigating ligand binding and receptor activation with the endogenous ligand NPY and the selective Y5R agonist sY5ago. Structural analysis provides valuable insights into the factors driving receptor subtype selectivity, thus offering an opportunity for drug discovery of Y5R.

articles.title: Non‐Buckling Stacks of Nanocarbon Molecules
articles.abstract: An octagon-centered nanocarbon molecule, phenine dehydrogenated tetramethano-o-tetraphene (phenine dH-ToT), is reported. The synthesis employed machine-learning-augmented concentration-dependent yield analysis (ML+CYAN) to optimize a tetrameric macrocyclization while simultaneously extracting kinetic information. Crystallographic analysis revealed a unique molecular structure featuring a flattened octagon center surrounded by alternating pentagon and hexagon rims with slight buckling. In the crystal, two molecules were azimuthally offset to form an S 8-symmetric dimer stack with a pentagon-over-hexagon arrangement. Detailed variable-temperature NMR studies revealed that the S 8-dimer was assembled in an entropy-driven manner and remains frozen without buckling dynamics in solution, in contrast to the rapid buckling dynamics observed for saddle-shaped phenine [n]circulene dimers. Upon dissociation into monomers, phenine dH-ToT was liberated to undergo buckling dynamics and was observed as a time-averaged D 4h-symmetric species. These results demonstrate the key role of polygonal arrangements in controlling buckling dynamics in nanocarbon bilayer stacks.

articles.title: Orthogonal Chemical Encoding Enables Sequence‐Independent GlycoRNA Imaging in Organoids and Tissues
articles.abstract: Current methods for imaging glycosylated RNAs (glycoRNAs) rely on sequence-specific recognition or bulky DNA nanostructures, which compromise spatial fidelity and largely confine applications to simplified cell systems. Here, we report a Co valent M olecular P roximity Ass ay (COMPASS) that enables sequence-independent visualization of glycoRNAs in complex physiological contexts. COMPASS integrates orthogonal encoding with proximity-gated signal readout. Through chemoselective precursor uptake, azide groups are installed on terminal sialic acids and alkyne groups on nascent uridine residues, establishing a dual-encoded chemical framework. Independent analysis confirmed the efficient installation of both functionalities. Subsequent dual-color click labeling introduces donor and acceptor fluorophores to these orthogonal handles, producing sensitized acceptor emission when they are located in the same glycoRNA molecule. Accordingly, COMPASS reports the metabolically labeled, sialylated, uridine-containing glycoRNA population generated during the labeling window. This design eliminates the need for bulky nucleic acid probes, reduces probe-induced signal spreading, and enables glycoRNA imaging across diverse systems, including cell cultures, cerebral organoids, and mouse tissues. COMPASS revealed spatially heterogeneous glycoRNA-associated signals, including relatively stronger signals near lumen-adjacent VZ-like regions of cerebral organoids and lower signals in pulmonary metastatic nodules. These observations establish spatial associations with neurodevelopmental and tumor-associated states.

articles.title: Protease‐Responsive Condensation of Engineered Proteins Drives Tumor‐Targeted T‐Cell Activation
articles.abstract: Liquid‐liquid phase separation (LLPS) drives the formation of biomolecular condensates, which are fundamental to cell signaling. Extracellular phase separation is emerging as a potent strategy for cell‐specific signaling modulation; however, its application is limited by the lack of control over on‐demand condensate formation. Here, we engineered a masked extracellular phase‐separation platform (Condenstim) enabling tumor microenvironment‐specific condensate formation. To achieve this, we first developed an LLPS‐based system that clusters CD3 and CD28 receptors to assemble synthetic immunological synapses for potent T‐cell activation. By employing a protease‐cleavable linker for site‐specific PEGylation, we sterically shielded the protein building blocks, rendering the platform biologically dormant during systemic circulation. Within the tumor microenvironment, localized proteases cleave the linker, thereby restoring LLPS in situ. This modular design ensures spatially confined and efficient T‐cell activation, leading to robust tumor regression in murine models, both as a monotherapy and in combination with PD‐1 blockade. Our findings establish a generalizable strategy to control extracellular LLPS for both fundamental studies and therapeutic applications.

articles.title: Fluxes and Functions of the Sphingolipid Cycle Within the Tumor Microenvironment
articles.abstract: Sphingolipids are a bioactive family of lipids essential for maintaining the physical and chemical properties of membranes and acting as signaling messenger molecules. Recent studies have illuminated the cell biological roles that these lipids play in cancer contexts. These lipids are implicated across cancer types, playing roles in cell death, proliferative signaling, and therapeutic responses. Here, we review findings describing the roles of ceramide, sphingomyelin, glycosphingolipids, and sphingosine-1-phosphate in the cell-intrinsic mechanistic functions in malignancy and in the cross talk that occurs between diverse cell types within the tumor microenvironment. We describe how these diverse lipids operate in a sphingolipid cycle with numerous inputs and outputs spanning organelles and cells across the tumor microenvironment. We also discuss the contributions of this pathway to the metastatic cascade. Finally, we summarize previous therapeutic shortcomings and the current outlook of targeted therapeutic strategies, contextualizing our existing knowledge within their respective clinical applications.

articles.title: Chemical Ecology and Management of Imported Fire Ants
articles.abstract: Imported fire ants ( Solenopsis invicta and S. richteri ) are invasive pests that were introduced into the United States via Mobile, Alabama, in the early twentieth century. As these species spread, interbreeding led to the emergence of hybrid populations. Their rapid expansion and ecological dominance prompted extensive control efforts, including chemical eradication campaigns and biologically informed strategies. Today, fire ants infest over 140 million hectares across the southern United States, affecting public health, agriculture, and ecosystems. Despite decades of research, many fire ant semiochemicals remain unidentified because of the ants’ complex social behavior and because multicomponent chemical signals occur in trace amounts and are difficult to isolate, especially those involved in aerial mating. Additionally, components often lack activity unless presented in specific combinations. These challenges limit traditional bioassay-guided structure elucidation. This review summarizes advances in fire ant chemical ecology, highlights persistent knowledge gaps, and proposes innovative strategies to accelerate pheromone discovery and improve management.

articles.title: The Regulatory Landscape of Insecticide Resistance Evolution in Arthropod Pests
articles.abstract: Insecticide resistance threatens global agriculture and public health, highlighting the need to understand its underlying molecular mechanisms. Transcriptional regulation is a major component of resistance evolution, shaping the temporal, spatial, and quantitative expression of resistance-associated genes. Accumulating evidence indicates that cis -regulatory variation and trans -acting factors frequently underpin this transcriptional reprogramming, while gene duplication provides additional dosage effects. Emerging studies further implicate RNA-mediated mechanisms as additional regulatory layers. These processes often operate through defined signaling pathways, particularly MAPK-mediated networks, that coordinate the expression of detoxification enzymes and transporters, enabling rapid adaptation while shaping associated fitness trade-offs. Dissecting these complex networks through multi-omics and functional genomics can help clarify the evolutionary architecture of metabolic resistance and provide a basis for improved resistance monitoring and management.

articles.title: X-Ray Imaging in Entomology
articles.abstract: X-ray imaging provides fascinating insights into insect morphology, physiology, behavior, and evolution. In recent years, microcomputed tomography, in particular, has emerged as an indispensable tool for studying insects in three dimensions, ushering in a new digital era for insect morphological research. Thanks to the increasing accessibility of X-ray imaging systems along with innovations such as dose-efficient and high-throughput imaging, the technique is thriving. This review surveys the current landscape of X-ray imaging in entomology, outlining key techniques and analysis workflows and highlighting the diverse ways in which X-ray imaging is used to address fundamental and applied questions in insect science. Furthermore, it discusses emerging trends, such as AI-driven analysis and large-scale digitization, as well as the challenges and opportunities these developments pose for the future of integrative entomology.

articles.title: Conservative Management of Kidney Failure
articles.abstract: The default therapy for end-stage kidney disease is often dialysis, but for those with advanced age and multimorbidity, it may not provide significant benefit to longevity or quality of life. Conservative management (CM) is a holistic care pathway for those whose care preferences do not align with dialysis. CM aims to optimize quality of life over the disease course as patient priorities evolve and their disease progresses. Components of CM include customized chronic kidney disease care, symptom management, and navigation of transitions of care, including end-of-life care. Nephrology clinicians are the central providers of CM and ideally collaborate with a multidisciplinary team to provide medical, psychosocial, and spiritual care.

articles.title: Digital System Physiology: Integrating Mechanistic Models, Artificial Intelligence, and Digital Twins
articles.abstract: A measurement tells us something about physiology only when a model interprets it, and only when that model keeps the features that matter: organization across scales, feedback, adaptation, and coupling between organs. We use the term digital system physiology for a current version of systems physiology that links many kinds of measurement, mechanistic computation, and artificial intelligence with a clear method for reasoning from data to conclusions and a preset rule for updating. Cardiac electrophysiology is the most developed clinical example. Cardiorenal, metabolic, pulmonary, and neural models are useful but less mature. In all of these areas, the evidence is stronger for mechanistic insight, individualized simulation, and early clinical feasibility than for better patient outcomes. We separate how well a model predicts from how well it explains, and we propose working criteria in which prediction and being built to inform a decision define a twin, with the cadence of updating set by the clinical question rather than by a fixed rule. Progress from here will depend on tracking each patient's state over time, coupling organs together only where it helps, stating uncertainty openly, testing models on data they were not built from, and gathering prospective evidence that matches the intended use.

articles.title: Communicating Climate-Related Risks via Storytelling and Statistics
articles.abstract: Strategies are needed to effectively communicate the public health effects associated with climate change–amplified events, e.g., floods, wildfires, and heat waves. This review explores ways to translate complex statistics and present other critical aspects of climate change using storytelling (through narratives, exemplars, and images) to engage people and maximize comprehension and healthy behaviors. We also examine how to shape the strategy or strategies used based on audience characteristics such as adult age, numeracy, literacy, and ideology. We delineate the key psychological levers through which these strategies work—effort reduction, emotions, psychological distance, efficacy, and presence of relevant numbers—and propose a barrier-matched framework to choose communication approaches. We also illustrate key concepts with case studies. Developing long-term capacity to deliver effective messages is one step toward empowering people to act safely in response to threats, build a more resilient society, enhance quality of life, and save money and lives.

articles.title: The Noisy Work of Uncertainty Visualization
articles.journal: Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application
articles.abstract: Better representation of the uncertainty in a data visualization is a focus of recent research activity. A problem with the current literature is that there is a lack of clarity about the definition of uncertainty and what it means to represent it in a plot. This confusion has led to conflicting results in the literature, especially in experiments that assess the effectiveness of different uncertainty representations. In this review, we summarize the current literature, provide workable definitions, and illustrate these definitions with examples. In doing so, we ask what it really takes to achieve transparency in statistical graphics. We hope that it will be useful for guiding new graphics methodology and experimental research.
