We address this gap by developing a lightweight general-purpose MLIAP for metal alloys spanning twelve elements (Al, Sc, Ti, V, Cu, Zn, Zr, Nb, Mo, Hf, Ta, W). Here, we utilize a step-wise active learning (AL) approach to develop a compact yet diverse dataset and model that generalizes well by interpolating from previously seen interactions. The resulting potentials transfer effectively to unseen, higher body-order alloys systems, requiring only unary and binary training data to capture ternary and quaternary systems. The model also transfers well to new elements via an alchemical extrapolation within the network, requiring only unary data for the new element and its alloys. These findings suggest that MLIAPs trained on targeted, diversity-driven datasets provide transferability at a relatively low computational cost, offering a practical path toward general-purpose, resource-efficient MLIAPs for materials modeling.

articles.title: Magnetism in a homometallic square-planar Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$$_4$Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$ metallacrown
articles.abstract: The well-established homometallic metallacrown Cu(II)[12-MC$_\text{Cu(II)N(Shi)}$-4]$^{2-}$, comprising four square-planarly arranged Cu(II) ions surrounding a slightly off-plane central Cu(II) ion, provides an excellent platform for investigating magnetism in exchange-coupled Cu(II) clusters both by experimental and ab initio numerical methods. In the present work, sterically bulky substituents are introduced into the salicylhydroxamate ligand to obtain a modified derivative, Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$[12-MC$_\text{Cu$({\mathrm{II})}$N(L)}$-4]$^{2-}$ (Cu$_4$Cu), thereby effectively suppressing intermolecular magnetic interactions and enabling a detailed investigation of its intrinsic ground-state spin structure and exchange interactions. Static magnetization reveals competing antiferromagnetic exchange interactions of $J_1=-8.1(2)$ THz ($-33.5(8)$ meV) between the central and the peripheral sites and $J_2=-4.40(12)$ THz ($-18.2(5)$ meV) between neighboring sites on the ring of the metallacrown, which are corroborated by ab initio broken symmetry-based density functional theory (DFT). These couplings yield an $S=1/2$ ground state for Cu$_4$Cu at low temperatures, for which X-band and high-frequency/high-field electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) precisely determine the $g$-factors $g_x = 2.028$, $g_y = 2.056$, and $g_z = 2.222$ close to axial anisotropy and in agreement with our DFT results. The ground-state spin-configuration is characterized by $d_{xy}$-character of the unoccupied states. Furthermore, our magnetization data evidence thermal transitions across a doublet-to-quartet gap of $Δ_{1/2\rightarrow3/2} = 4.8(4)$ THz which is also indicated by the emergence of an excited-state EPR signal.

articles.title: Multiscale evaluation of the elastic response of polycrystalline NiAl using molecular statics, EBSD-based finite element and analytical homogenization methods
articles.abstract: The presented work proposes a multiscale framework for the numerical and analytical determination of the elastic constants of the intermetallic nickel aluminide (NiAl) at the microscopic scale. Molecular dynamics (MD) calculations have been employed to evaluate the stiffness tensors of a single NiAl monocrystalline body with cubic Pm$\bar{3}$m symmetry. The atomistic results were transferred to the upper scale as an input to micromechanical models. Here, finite element modeling (FEM) and analytical homogenization methods were used to simulate the elastic behavior of polycrystalline NiAl, with special attention to grain anisotropy and its morphology. The microstructural features of the heterogeneous body were evaluated experimentally using electron backscatter diffraction (EBSD) and subsequently used to generate a 3D polycrystalline geometric model that preserves realistic distributions of grain orientations and grain sizes. The reconstructed NiAl polycrystal was subjected to uniaxial tensile test simulations using FEM to evaluate the effective Young's modulus ($E$) and Poisson's ratio ($ν$). The numerical results were confronted with the experimental values of $E$ and~$ν$. With these model assumptions, a very good agreement between numerical and experimental results was achieved. Finally, the experimental results were compared with classical analytical estimates. Among the analytical approaches, the Hashin-Shtrikman upper bound and self-consistent approximation reproduced the experimental Young's modulus with minor deviations.

articles.title: Uniaxial strain tuning of functional properties in antiferroelectric PbZrO3 membrane capacitors
articles.abstract: Lead zirconate (PbZrO3, PZO) is a prototypical antiferroelectric (AFE) system promising for applications such as energy storage and neuromorphic computing. However, in conventional thin-film architectures, its functional potential is often limited by substrate clamping. Although emerging freestanding membrane techniques offer an approach to release this clamping and enable dynamic strain engineering, a systematic understanding of how external strain modulates the switching between AFE and ferroelectric (FE) states is missing. In this study, we investigate the uniaxial strain effects on PZO membrane capacitors transferred onto flexible substrates via a gold-bonding method. We demonstrate that in-plane dynamic strain modulates the AFE-FE switching and functional properties. Corroborated by atomistic simulations, we reveal that the strain-dependent evolution arises from the superposition of the intrinsic strain dependence of specific domain orientation variants and extrinsic strain-induced redistribution of the relative population of different domain variants. These findings provide a predictive understanding of uniaxial strain tuning of AFE-FE switching in PZO, and pave the way for exploiting the functional potential of freestanding antiferroelectric membranes.

articles.title: Cell cycle-coupled CK1δ turnover, autoinhibition, and activity
articles.abstract: Casein kinase 1δ (CK1δ) is a ubiquitously expressed kinase involved in diverse cellular processes, including cell-cycle regulation. CK1δ activity is attenuated by (auto)phosphorylation. However, inhibitory phosphorylation is efficiently opposed by cellular phosphatases as CK1δ accumulates in its hypophosphorylated, active state. CK1δ is a target of the nuclear ubiquitin ligase APC/C-CDH1, yet the kinase is apparently stable. Thus, the physiological relevance of CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation, autoinhibition, and regulated turnover has remained unclear. Previously, we showed that CK1δ is dynamically regulated in a manner that is dependent on kinase activity, subcellular localization, and interaction with its binding partners, such as PER2 (Serrano et al., 2026). Here, we show that CK1δ activity and abundance are additionally coordinated in a cell cycle-dependent manner. During G1, assembled CK1δ kinase is stable while free active kinase is degraded. In S phase, unassembled CK1δ seems to be no longer degraded, likely to support functions in DNA damage signaling. Upon mitotic entry, the downregulation of phosphatases promotes CK1δ (auto)phosphorylation and consequent autoinhibition, thereby preserving a pool of kinase to rapidly re-establish the post-mitotic steady state.

articles.title: Loose coupling between Ca2+ channels and release sensors as a synaptic correlate of higher-order brain function
articles.abstract: In the mature neocortex, functionally distinct areas are built by the same archetypes of neurons, but depending on the area, these neurons and their synapses are engaged in very different functions, ranging from lower-order processing of sensory information to higher-order associations and cognitive functions. We found significant differences in the functional presynaptic nanoarchitectures of the same types of pyramidal neuron synapses, depending on whether they are located in the prefrontal cortex (PFC) or in the primary somatosensory cortex (S1) of mice. Mature synapses in PFC operated with loose microdomain coupling, as opposed to tight nanodomain coupling in S1. These differences were associated with significant differences in synaptic timing, efficacy, and plasticity between areas. Our data suggest that the mature neocortex uses tuning of synaptic topographies to specialize seemingly identical types of neurons for their required function. They suggest that microdomain coupling in pyramidal neuron synapses could be a presynaptic structure-function correlate of higher-order neocortical functions.

articles.title: Out-of-balance growth enables cost-free synthesis of the flagellum and other proteins in a single bacterium
articles.abstract: The cost of expressing unnecessary genes on growth has been explained at the population level through balanced growth assumptions. However, due to the high degree of stochasticity in growth and gene regulation, it remains unclear how classical growth laws derived from bulk measurements manifest at the level of individual cells. For example, flagellar gene expression, one of the most energy-intensive processes in Escherichia coli, is typically associated with reduced growth rates in bulk measurements. By contrast, we find at the single-cell level that a strikingly opposite behavior coexists: flagellar gene activity is associated with an increase in growth rate. We show that this apparent contradiction, reminiscent of Simpson’s paradox, results from examining in each cell instantaneous growth and gene expression without indiscriminately aggregating the single-cell data like in bulk measurements. We attribute this unrecognized behavior to out-of-balance growth boosts that temporarily offset the burden of flagellum production, likely driven by a surplus of growth factors inherited across cell division. Furthermore, we show that this non-intuitive relationship between growth and gene expression at the single-cell level is general, as we observe similar effects with synthetic systems driving the expression of fluorescent proteins downstream of constitutive promoters. Finally, we use a computational model to show that the inheritance of parental growth factors can explain the apparent contradiction and constitutes a general mechanism for mitigating the short-term cost of nonessential and biosynthetically demanding genes in the single cell.

articles.title: Plasticity associated with adoption of social roles in clown anemonefish
articles.abstract: Central questions of animal behavior are how individual phenotypes shape and how individual phenotypes are shaped by dominance hierarchies. Using clownfish (Amphiprion percula) as a model system, we investigated how individuals strategically modify their phenotype during hierarchy formation. We tested the overarching hypothesis that interactions among size- and age-matched rivals will lead to the emergence of social roles (dominant, subordinate, solitary), accompanied by divergence in four aspects of individual phenotypes: growth, feeding behavior, agonistic behaviors (aggression, submission), and gene expression. To test this, we created 30 replicates of juvenile clownfish, each comprising a size-matched pair housed together, and a solitary size-matched individual housed separately. Our results show that an individual’s social context shapes its growth trajectory through coordinated changes in feeding behavior, agonistic behaviors, and gene expression. Individuals emerging as dominant within pairs grew twice as much compared to those emerging as subordinates, while subordinate and solitary individuals showed comparable growth. Initially, paired individuals consumed more food per capita than solitary individuals, but this difference declined as size hierarchies became established. Agonistic behaviors also decreased over time among paired individuals as size differences emerged. Transcriptomic analyses revealed upregulation of conserved vertebrate growth pathways and ossification-related genes, and downregulation of satiety-associated genes, in dominant individuals compared to subordinates and solitaries. Here, we identify associations between changes in gene expression, growth, and feeding behavior regulation that reinforce social role differentiation during dominance hierarchy formation in clownfish. Our findings lay the foundation for a broader framework to explore the mechanisms underpinning strategic growth in social vertebrates.

articles.title: Structural insights into peptidoglycan hydrolysis by the FtsEX system in Escherichia coli during cell division
articles.abstract: Bacterial cell division relies on precise peptidoglycan (PG) remodeling, a process orchestrated by the FtsEX complex. Comprised of FtsE and FtsX, this complex collaborates with EnvC, a periplasmic lytic enzyme activator, to regulate septal PG hydrolysis by amidases like AmiB. While recent structural investigations, particularly of Pseudomonas aeruginosa FtsEX (PaeFtsEX), have shed light on complex interactions and proposed activation mechanisms, the structural intricacies governing PG degradation by the FtsEX complex and EnvC in Escherichia coli cytokinesis remain unexplored. In this study, we present a comprehensive biochemical and structural analysis of E. coli FtsEX complexes, unveiling a key role for ATP in complex stabilization that extends across bacterial species. Upon EnvC binding, ATPase activity markedly increases. High-resolution structures of EcoFtsEX, both in the presence and absence of EnvC, reveal a symmetrical conformation of EcoFtsEX capable of accommodating the inherent asymmetry of EnvC, mediated by flexible loops within the periplasmic domain. Our negative-staining imaging showcases an elongated EcoFtsEX/EnvC/AmiB complex reminiscent of the PaeFtsEX system. These findings collectively provide intricate insights into the regulation of PG cleavage by FtsEX in E. coli—a pivotal model system used in pilot genetic studies, suggesting a conserved mechanism for precise hydrolase activation in bacteria.

articles.title: Ultrasound neuromodulation hypotheses on the directionality of effects and community resource
articles.abstract: Low-intensity transcranial ultrasound stimulation (TUS) is a promising non-invasive technique for brain stimulation and focal neuromodulation. Research with humans and animal models has raised the possibility that TUS can be biased towards enhancing or suppressing neural function. Here, we first collate a set of hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects and conduct an initial meta-analysis on available healthy human participant TUS studies reporting stimulation parameters and outcomes (n=47 studies, 52 experiments). In initial exploratory analyses with univariate tests, we find that parameters, such as the intensity and continuity of stimulation (duty cycle, DC) show statistical trends towards likely TUS neural enhancement or suppression of function. Machine-learning analyses were limited by the currently small sample size. Given that human TUS sample sizes are expected to increase, predictability on the directionality of TUS effects could improve if a database is available. Therefore, we establish an inTUS database and resource for the systematic reporting of TUS parameters and outcomes to assist in greater precision in TUS use for brain stimulation and neuromodulation. The paper concludes with a selective review of human clinical TUS studies illustrating how hypotheses on the directionality of TUS effects could be developed for empirical testing in the intended clinical application, not limited to the examples provided.

articles.title: A Two-Water-Assisted Deacylation Pathway in Class C β-Lactamase ACC-1 Revealed by High-Resolution Crystallography and QM/MM Calculations
articles.abstract: β-Lactam antibiotics are among the most widely prescribed antibacterial agents, yet their clinical efficacy is increasingly compromised by β-lactamase-mediated resistance. Class C β-lactamase ACC-1 hydrolyzes third-generation cephalosporins such as cefotaxime through a covalent acyl-enzyme intermediate, but the molecular basis of deacylation remains unresolved. Here, we report high-resolution synchrotron and room-temperature X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) crystal structures of the cefotaxime-acylated ACC-1. These structures reveal a previously unrecognized two-water configuration near the acyl center, comprising the previously proposed deacylating water, Wat1, and an additional ordered water molecule, Wat2, positioned at a Bürgi–Dunitz angle suitable for nucleophilic attack. Quantum mechanics/molecular mechanics (QM/MM) calculations identify a previously unrecognized two-water-assisted deacylation pathway in which the substrate C4-carboxylate and Wat1 cooperatively activate Wat2 as the nucleophilic deacylating water. This pathway exhibits a substantially lower activation free-energy barrier than the alternative substrate-assisted and Tyr150–Lys67 general-base pathways examined. Together, these findings revise the deacylation mechanism of class C ACC-1 β-lactamase by revealing how an ordered water network and the substrate C4 carboxylate can cooperate to promote acyl-enzyme hydrolysis. This atomic-level mechanism provides a foundation for rational design strategies aimed at developing β-lactam antibiotics and β-lactamase inhibitors that resist or disrupt enzymatic hydrolysis.

articles.title: Carboxylation of Bio-Based 2-Furoic Acid with CO2 to 2,5-Furandicarboxylic Acid over CuAlO x Catalysts
articles.abstract: Direct C–H carboxylation with CO2 as a renewable C1 source stands out as an atom-economical strategy for CO2 utilization. However, the low reactivity of C–H bond and intrinsic inertness of CO2 limit carboxylation efficiency. This work presents a cooperative CuAlOx-Cs2CO3 catalytic system for the C–H carboxylation of 2-furoic acid (FA) with CO2 to produce 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid (2,5-FDCA), a key bio-based monomer for polyethylene furanoate (PEF). By integrating a hydrotalcite-derived Cu2AlOx catalyst into a Cs2CO3-promoted system, the 2,5-FDCA yield increases from 13% to 91% at 190 °C under 2 MPa CO2 with 1.33 equiv Cs2CO3, with a reduction of 61 kJ·mol–1 in apparent activation energy. The high Cu-normalized apparent activity (33.2 mmolFA gCu–1 h–1) with 96.8% selectivity to 2,5-FDCA is achieved. Mechanistic and theoretical analyses reveal that Cu2AlOx promotes the activation of both FA and CO2. The interaction of Cu2AlOx with the carboxylate group of FA elongates the C5-H bond and facilitates Cs2CO3-promoted deprotonation, while Cu2AlOx activates CO2 mainly via bidentate carbonate species that enhance the electrophilicity of the carbon center, thereby lowering the C–C coupling barrier. The resulting 2,5-FDCA is a viable monomer for producing PEF with rigid furan-based backbones, underscoring its potential for engineering plastic applications. This synergistic strategy offers an atom-economical route to bio-based 2,5-FDCA and provides mechanistic insights into substrate and CO2 activation in direct C–H carboxylation.

articles.title: Effects of Zeolite Framework on Direct Reduction of Esters to Ethers Using H2 on Pt-Zeolite Catalysts
articles.abstract: The direct reduction of esters to ethers using H2 represents a fundamental selectivity challenge for heterogeneous catalysis and offers a method to increase the hydrothermal stability of chemicals and fuels derived from renewable resources. Prior studies revealed that ethers derive from a series of reactions that involve in situ formation of hemiacetals by hydrogen transfer on metal nanoparticles, followed by diffusive transport to Brønsted acid sites that cleave the carbonyl C–O bond. The competing hydrogenolysis pathway proceeds by a similar bifunctional mechanism; however, hydrolysis and transesterification occur by direct reactions of esters solely at Brønsted acid sites. Here, we find that rates and selectivities reflect the intrinsic reactivity at individual Brønsted acid sites, which depends upon the topology of the aluminosilicate support. Pt-Faujasite (FAU) provides ether formation rates at least an order of magnitude greater than smaller pore zeolites that possess similar Pt loadings and Si/Al ratios (e.g., mordenite framework inverted (MFI), beta (BEA), and ferrierite (FER)). Correlations between formation rates and activation energies for ether formation with heats of adsorption of propyl acetate across Pt-zeolites and Pt-AlMCM41 suggest that dispersive interactions among the zeolite pore wall, surrounding molecules (e.g., propyl acetate), and transition states contribute to differences in performance among these catalysts. These effects appear responsible for Pt-FER providing the highest ether selectivities observed (∼50%), although the specific structural features responsible for this behavior remain uncertain and may reflect framework-specific confinement and transport effects. However, ether selectivities also appear sensitive to other zeolite properties, including channel dimensionality, which may influence diffusive transport between Pt and Brønsted acid sites. These findings illustrate that the topology of the aluminosilicate support impacts rates and selectivities for ester reduction by orders of magnitude: these differences reflect contributions of inter-function transport reminiscent of other bifunctional catalysts for hydrotreating reactions but also evidence from comparisons to titration calorimetry that the local solvation of reactive intermediates at Brønsted acid sites influences catalysis.

articles.title: Electronic Control of Mechanistic Divergence in Iron-Catalyzed Olefin Carboamidation to β- and γ-Lactams
articles.abstract: Regiodivergent synthetic strategies employing common precursors provide a powerful means of accessing structurally distinct molecular scaffolds. Herein, we report an electronically controlled, regiodivergent iron-catalyzed intramolecular olefin carboamidation of styrenyl dioxazolones that selectively affords either β- or γ-lactams using a range of carbon nucleophiles, including electron-rich arenes, allylsilanes, and propargylsilanes, thereby providing access to arylated, allylated, and allenylated products, respectively. Combined Hammett analysis, experimental mechanistic studies, and density functional theory (DFT) calculations support the involvement of a common azabicyclo[2.1.0]pentanone intermediate and reveal two electronically differentiated pathways: 1) strain-releasing SN2-type aziridine ring-opening promoted by electron-withdrawing substituents to deliver five-membered γ-lactams and 2) solvent-assisted aziridine ring-opening promoted by electron-donating substituents to generate a benzylic carbocation intermediate, followed by SN1-type trapping with a carbon nucleophile to furnish four-membered β-lactams.

articles.title: Facet-Dependent Regulation of Reactive Oxygen Species Generation and Utilization Governs Biomass Oxidation
articles.abstract: Reactive oxygen species (ROS) are key intermediates in radical-mediated heterogeneous oxidation, yet the relationship between ROS generation and their effective utilization remains poorly understood. Here, we demonstrate that crystal facets can differently influence ROS generation and utilization during biomass-derived alcohol/aldehyde oxidation. Using CuO catalysts, predominantly exposing either the (001) or (111) facet as model systems, we show that the CuO(001) facet preferentially promotes hydroxyl radical (·OH) generation through efficient tert-butyl hydroperoxide activation, whereas the CuO(111) facet promotes efficient interfacial utilization of surface-associated ·OH during the hydrogen-abstraction step. Despite producing fewer EPR-detectable radicals, CuO(111) exhibits higher catalytic performance for the base-free oxidation of 5-hydroxymethylfurfural to 2,5-furandicarboxylic acid, achieving quantitative HMF conversion and an FDCA yield of 85.7% under mild conditions (80 °C, 4 h). Time-resolved kinetic analysis, radical trapping experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and density functional theory calculations reveal that facet-dependent adsorption configurations regulate oxidant activation and subsequent hydrogen abstraction, thereby determining whether generated ROS undergo productive interfacial reactions or non-productive accumulation. This work provides mechanistic insights into the relationship between ROS generation, ROS utilization, and catalytic performance, highlighting the importance of considering the productive participation of generated ROS in catalyst evaluation.

articles.title: Synergistic-Tandem Active Sites Engineered in Pd-Doped Mo5N6 Nanosheets for Efficient CO2 Photoreduction to Acetic Acid
articles.abstract: CO2 photoreduction into multicarbon products such as acetic acid represents a promising strategy for addressing the greenhouse effect and energy shortages. However, the process is limited by kinetically sluggish C–C coupling and inefficient proton-coupled electron transfer (PCET). Herein, we construct Nv-Pdδ+ tandem active sites in Mo5N6 nanosheets via low-valent Pdδ+ (2 < δ < 4) doping, which simultaneously introduces abundant stable nitrogen vacancies (Nv) and adjacent Pdδ+ centers. Combined experimental and theoretical analyses reveal that the Nv sites promote CO2 activation and reduce the energy barrier for *CO dimerization, while the neighboring Pdδ+ sites efficiently drive water splitting to supply H*, thereby facilitating the hydrogenation of key *OCCO intermediates. Accordingly, the optimized Pd0.5-Mo5N6 achieves a high acetic acid selectivity of 90.1% with an evolution rate of 33.24 μmol·g–1·h–1 under solar irradiation. This work establishes a tandem active-site design strategy for efficient and durable photocatalytic synthesis of multicarbon products from CO2.

articles.title: Toward the High-Yield Generation of Vanillic Acid from Lignin by Selective C–C Cleavage over CuO Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: The selective cleavage of C–C bonds in lignin for scalable production of phenolic biochemicals constitutes a major obstacle, owing to lignin’s inherent structural complexity, the poor selectivity of existing catalysts, and the complicated separation process. Herein, we report a strategy to overcome this by improving the lignin side-chain C–C selective cleavage using a CuO nanoparticles (CuO NPs) catalyst through a one-pot oxidation process under mild conditions. The CuO NPs (<10 nm) were prepared by super-slow in situ precipitation of Cu2+ on GO. Morphology analysis revealed the presence of both CuO NPs and single Cu atoms, which exhibited an average size of 8 nm. Under mild conditions (140 °C, 1 atm), the CuO NPs/GO catalyst facilitated the selective cleavage of lignin Cα–Cβ side chains, resulting in over 95% lignin conversion and 10.8 wt % pure vanillic acid (VA), a record efficiency for isolated VA production. The high selectivity could be attributed to the presence of CuO NPs on the GO support. DFT simulations suggest that the CuO NPs decrease the formation energy barrier of active [O] species significantly, resulting in selective oxidation of the double bond in the lignin-derived intermediate, enol ether. By elucidating the key factors governing bond selectivity, our findings provide a foundation for the rational design of C–C bond oxidation catalysts in biomass valorization. The economic analysis based on a daily lignin feedstock of 500 tons demonstrates an estimated gross margin of ∼20%.

articles.title: Decoupled Water Electrolysis with an Air-Stable Zwitterionic Azo Mediator
articles.abstract: Decoupled water electrolysis (DWE) separates H2 and O2 evolution, improving safety and flexibility under intermittent renewable electricity, but requires durable, oxygen-tolerant redox mediators. Here we evaluate 4,4′-azo-bis(1-pyridinium-3-propane-sulfonate) (ABPS), a zwitterionic azo molecule, as an electron-coupled proton buffer for acidic DWE. Its azo/hydrazo core supports reversible two-electron/two-proton chemistry at 0.81 V vs RHE, while zwitterionic substituents provide high aqueous solubility and suppress crossover through low-cost sulfonated poly(ether ether ketone) membranes. Reduced H2ABPS shows no detectable oxidation after 90 days in air or during >5 h of continuous pure-O2 bubbling. Symmetric flow-cell cycling over 1000 h yields a capacity-fade rate below 1% year–1. With commercial catalysts at room temperature, decoupled flow cells reach 1.2 A cm–2 and operate for >200 h at 500 mA cm–2 with near-quantitative Faradaic efficiencies while producing high-purity H2 and O2. These results establish zwitterionic azo chemistry as an oxygen-tolerant, durable platform for high-rate decoupled hydrogen production.

articles.title: Microphase-Engineered Homologous Ion-Exchange Layers for High-Current-Density Bipolar Membrane Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Bipolar membranes (BPMs) maintain separated acidic and alkaline environments via water dissociation at the junction, but high-current-density operation remains challenging because rapid hydrated H+/OH– migration away from the junction must be coupled with sufficient water replenishment toward it. A transport imbalance between these opposing processes causes interfacial dehydration and limits long-term operation. Here, we develop microphase-engineered homologous ion-exchange layers to balance this coupled transport. These layers are fabricated from homologous multiblock poly(biphenyl alkylene) ionomers sharing a common backbone and block architecture, promoting interlayer compatibility and interconnected ionic domains. The hydrated pathways accelerate water replenishment and ion transport, thereby maintaining a stably hydrated junction. The resulting BPM enables pure-water electrolysis at 2.11 V at 1000 mA cm–2 and sustains high-purity hydrogen production for over 1100 h at 500 mA cm–2. This work establishes molecularly engineered ion-exchange layers as an effective approach for improving mass transport in high-current-density BPM systems.

articles.title: A Hyaluronic Acid-Stabilized Zinc-Loaded Probiotic Mitigates Nanoplastic Toxicity across the Microbiota–Gut–Brain Axis
articles.abstract: Nanoplastics are emerging stressors that perturb host physiology across the gut–immune–brain continuum, yet scalable interventions remain limited. Here, we engineer ZG@EcN@HA, a biohybrid living system created by vacuum-assisted intracellular loading of zinc gluconate into Escherichia coli Nissle 1917 (EcN) followed by an outer hyaluronic acid (HA) shell. This architecture preserves probiotic culturability under gastric challenge and supports sustained zinc availability in intestinal conditions. In zebrafish chronically exposed to polystyrene nanoplastics, we observe reproducible neurobehavioral impairment coupled with inflammatory activation, redox imbalance, barrier stress, neurotransmitter dysregulation, and multiorgan histopathology. ZG@EcN@HA yields the most coherent rescue compared with single-component controls, restoring behavioral outputs and realigning immune–redox–neurochemical readouts. ASV-based profiling shows recovery of microbial diversity and a shift toward a control-like community structure, including reduced dominance of inflammation-linked taxa. Intestinal transcriptomics and integrative correlation analyses further support normalization of barrier/metabolic programs and attenuation of innate inflammatory signaling. Together, the data identify a materials-enabled strategy for microbiota–gut–brain protection against chronic nanoplastic stress.

articles.title: Automated Perovskite Film Fabrication with High-Resolution Data Acquisition and Machine Learning Analysis
articles.abstract: Lead halide perovskite solar cells have emerged as promising candidates for next-generation photovoltaics; nevertheless, fabrication of the perovskite photoactive layer remains highly intricate with film formation strongly modulated by various processing and environmental factors. Here, we report an environment-controlled, robot-assisted platform for automated thin-film fabrication designed to quantify and visualize perovskite crystallization in situ. Beyond precise control of each processing step, the system captures dynamic phenomena spanning subsecond color evolution and millisecond antisolvent droplet behavior while simultaneously recording slower environmental parameters (temperature, humidity/moisture, and concentrations of oxygen and volatile organic compounds). For optoelectronic assessment, we implemented time-resolved microwave conductivity (TRMC) measurements together with photoluminescence intensity quantification by using a complementary automated evaluation system. By combining machine-learning regression with SHAP (Shapley additive explanations) analysis, we identify the environmental parameters that most impact film properties and propose a feedback strategy to refine data and extract precise effects of process factors. A comparative study of a two-cation perovskite, (FAPbI3)0.87(MAPbBr3)0.13, and a three-cation perovskite, FA0.85MA0.10Cs0.05PbI3, further reveals markedly different sensitivities to environmental factors (FA, formamidinium; MA, methylammonium), in particular, temperature and resultant phase transition kinetics during thermal annealing. Based on the ML analysis and feedback, we tuned the antisolvent droplet velocity and obtained the maximized power conversion efficiency of 24.4%. Notably, this manual device fabrication was consistent with the results obtained by the automated system. This work establishes a practical route to stable, quantitative, and mechanistically informed investigation of solution-processed photovoltaic films.

articles.title: Band-like Transport with Hall Mobility >70 cm2 V–1 s–1 in Stoichiometric Perovskite Crystals via Ion Confinement and Strain Relaxation
articles.abstract: Despite substantial progress in optoelectronic applications, lead–halide perovskites remain underperforming in field-effect transistors (FETs) due to multiphase instability, ion migration, and grain boundary scattering. Here, a dual-ion co-incorporation strategy was applied to CsxFA1–xPbI3–yBry single crystals. By systematically mapping a phase stability diagram, we pinpoint an optimal stoichiometry of Cs0.1FA0.9PbI2.7Br0.3 that integrates phase stability engineering with atomic-level ion confinement. Structural analysis reveals that 10% Cs+/Br– co-incorporation induces strain-relaxed lattice contraction (−1.23% along the a-axis relative to FAPbI3) and reinforces Pb–I bonds via octahedral distortion. This yields superior crystallinity (FWHM = 0.04°) and reduced I– migration, thereby enabling the investigation of FET and gated Hall effect carrier mobilities as functions of temperature. Consequently, champion two-terminal FET devices exhibit an electron mobility of 25.1 cm2 V–1 s–1 at room temperature, which increases to 126 cm2 V–1 s–1 at 120 K. Furthermore, high-resolution four-terminal measurements on a single crystal quantify and correct for contact-resistance effects, validating the relationship: Hall mobility (μHall) > linear regime mobility (μlin) > saturation regime mobility (μsat) with values of 89, 79.2, and 71.6 cm2 V–1 s–1, respectively. These findings collectively elucidate intrinsic band-like electron transport behavior in lead–halide perovskite single crystals, distinguishing it from hopping transport in organic semiconductors. By achieving a defect-minimized lattice, this compositional engineering paradigm overcomes the mobility bottleneck in perovskite FETs, facilitating the transition from photoelectronic applications to FET integration.

articles.title: Centrosymmetry Breaking of Cobalt–Vanadium-Layered Double Hydroxide Nanosheets via Nitrogen Doping for Enhanced Piezocatalytic Tumor Therapy
articles.abstract: Piezocatalysis has emerged as a promising tumor therapeutic strategy because it enables oxygen-independent generation of multiple reactive oxygen species (ROS) with deep tissue penetration. However, the piezocatalytic efficiency of piezoelectric nanomaterials remains constrained by limited lattice distortion, low carrier separation efficiency, and insufficient catalytic active sites. Herein, we report the centrosymmetry breaking of cobalt–vanadium-layered double hydroxide (CoV-LDH) nanosheets via nitrogen doping for efficient ultrasound (US)-mediated piezocatalytic tumor therapy. Owing to the nitrogen doping-induced disruption of the centrosymmetric structure and lattice distortion in CoV-LDH, nitrogen-doped CoV-LDH (N-CoV-LDH) achieves an ultrahigh piezoelectric coefficient of 89.4 pm·V–1, which is superior to that of previously reported piezocatalytic nanomaterials. Moreover, nitrogen doping introduces an unsaturated coordination environment, significantly promoting the adsorption and activation of O2 (Eads = −2.63 eV) and H2O (Eads = −2.37 eV), thereby enhancing piezocatalytic redox reaction kinetics (k > 1.1 × 103 min–1·g–1). Consequently, under low-power US stimulation (0.15 W·cm–2), N-CoV-LDH nanosheets exhibit markedly enhanced ROS generation efficiency, including that of hydroxyl radicals (·OH), superoxide anions (·O2–), and singlet oxygen (1O2). This robust piezocatalytic ROS generation induces tumor cell apoptosis and immunogenic cell death, thereby activating an antitumor immune response characterized by dendritic cell maturation, M1 macrophage polarization, and T cell activation. Ultimately, N-CoV-LDH-mediated piezocatalytic therapy achieves suppression rates of 97.78% for primary tumors and 87.67% for metastatic tumors, establishing an efficient therapeutic paradigm for suppressing tumor metastasis and recurrence.

articles.title: Copper-Catalyzed Covalent Nanostructure Synthesis on Atomically Flat Highly Oriented Pyrolytic Graphite (HOPG)
articles.abstract: On-surface Ullmann-type coupling has been widely employed for constructing atomically precise carbon-based nanostructures, yet its implementation remains largely restricted to metal substrates, where strong molecule–substrate interactions perturb intrinsic electronic properties and hinder further device integration. Extending on-surface reaction to chemically inert surfaces such as highly oriented pyrolytic graphite (HOPG) is fundamentally challenged by the competition between reaction activation and molecule desorption under ultrahigh vacuum (UHV) conditions. Here, we demonstrate classical Ullmann coupling on HOPG catalyzed by exogenous copper (Cu) atoms. Two brominated precursors, 2,4,6-tris(4-bromophenyl)-1,3,5-triazine (pTBPT) and 5,10,15,20-tetra(4-bromophenyl) porphine (TBrPP), are employed to investigate how exogenous Cu regulates the critical competition between molecular desorption and reaction activation. For pTBPT, scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) reveals the formation of uniform and well-ordered oligomeric structures at 350 °C, whereas in the absence of Cu, molecules desorb without reaction. Synchrotron radiation X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (SR-XPS) and density functional theory (DFT) calculations further indicate that Cu atoms simultaneously promote molecular anchoring and reduce the activation barrier for dehalogenative coupling. As a complementary system, STM and XPS analysis of TBrPP reveals a critical competition between molecular desorption and dehalogenative coupling. While HR-XPS reveals in situ metalation at room temperature, STM imaging confirms that complete molecular desorption occurs at 200 °C, preventing subsequent dehalogenative coupling. These findings provide mechanistic insights into how transition metal mediates the interplay between surface reaction and desorption, while offering a strategy for the fabrication of structurally defined covalent nanostructures on electronically decoupled platforms.

articles.title: Direct Imaging of Energy Dissipation in Surface Acoustic Waves
articles.abstract: Unraveling the spatial distribution and energy dissipation of high-frequency surface acoustic waves (SAWs) is essential for advancing nanoacoustic architectures and probing low-dimensional wave–matter interactions. However, visualizing these dynamics at the subwavelength scale remains challenging due to the optical diffraction limit and severe topographic artifacts, such as surface defects and roughness, in scanning probe measurements. Here, we establish scanning thermal microscopy (SThM) as a robust metrological paradigm to map nanoscale energy dissipation and resolve complex acoustic wavefields through their localized thermal signatures. Leveraging this platform, we demonstrate how microgeometries sculpt the acoustic energy landscape and enable quantitative extraction of wave scattering parameters. Furthermore, by interrogating the h-BN/LiNbO3 van der Waals (vdW) interface, we capture localized temperature signatures of interfacial energy exchange. We observe anomalous nonlinear thermal scaling at the 2D heterointerface, consistent with the intrinsic nonlinear damping of the 2D heterostructure. This work highlights the capability of SThM to probe acoustic energy dissipation, establishing a diagnostic framework for subwavelength acoustic wavefields and heterogeneously integrated devices.

articles.title: Dopant Engineered Y-Doped Hafnia-Zirconia Nanolaminates with 0.26 nm Equivalent Oxide Thickness for Dynamic Random Access Memory Capacitors
articles.abstract: Y-doped Hf0.5Zr0.5O2 demonstrated feasible field-induced ferroelectric properties for capacitor dielectrics in dynamic random access memory (DRAM) by stepwise cycling, which enabled low-voltage charge boosting. However, practical implementation remains limited by high cycling stress and leakage current density (J) degradation. This study reported a Y-doped ZrO2/HfO2/ZrO2 nanolaminate with middle-inserted and top-inserted Y2O3 layers, enabling low-voltage charge boosting with substantially decreased stepwise cycling stress. This effect arose from a more uniform distribution of oxygen-vacancy-dopant complexes, thereby decreasing the energy barrier for the tetragonal-to-polar orthorhombic phase transition. The middle-inserted Y2O3 layer underwent substitutional diffusion, stabilized the tetragonal phase and suppressed J by acceptor doping. In contrast, the top-inserted Y2O3 layer displayed limited bulk diffusion, resulting in minimal lattice strain and phase change, but further suppressed J. Consequently, a 5.2 nm-thick film achieved an ultralow equivalent oxide thickness of ∼0.26 nm while satisfying the DRAM J criterion (J < 10–7 A cm–2 at ±0.8 V), outperforming all previously reported DRAM dielectrics.

articles.title: Facile Polyiodides Conversion Enabled by Facet Engineering for Durable Zinc–Iodine Batteries
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc–iodine (Zn–I2) batteries are highly promising for grid-scale energy storage, yet their practical viability is severely plagued by the polyiodides shuttle effect and sluggish liquid–solid conversion kinetics, which fundamentally arise from the contradictory energetic demands between soluble intermediate confinement and solid-product desorption. Herein, we rationally construct a dual-facet spinel cobalt oxide to precisely decouple these competing interfacial behaviors. By regulating the proportional exposure of strongly coordinating (100) and weakly coordinating (111) facets, a tailored surface microenvironment is constructed that effectively circumvents the inherent thermodynamic trade-off, breaking the single adsorption limitation intrinsic to uniform catalysts. In situ iodine L3-edge X-ray absorption spectroscopy and three-dimensional synchrotron-based nanocomputed tomography reveal that this specific facet modulation substantially reduces the activation barrier for rate-determining polyiodides oxidation, facilitating spatially uniform solid-iodine deposition. Driven by these structural advantages, the assembled Zn–I2 batteries with c/o-Co3O4 deliver a high specific capacity of 161.1 mAh g–1 at 16 A g–1 and an ultralow capacity decay rate of 0.00055% per cycle after 50,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. Furthermore, the batteries also exhibit a broad operational temperature ranging from −30 to 60 °C, highlighting the strong potential for practical applications. This work provides a perspective on facet engineering for achieving wide-temperature-tolerant aqueous iodine storage.

articles.title: Molecular Crowding Programs Trifluoroacetate-Solvation Nanoclusters for Stable Aqueous Zinc Metal Chemistry
articles.abstract: Aqueous zinc metal batteries offer a safe and cost-effective platform for electrochemical energy storage, yet their practical operation remains limited by water-driven parasitic reactions and spatially heterogeneous Zn deposition. Here, we report a molecule-crowding strategy that programs zinc/sodium trifluoroacetate (Zn(TFA)2/NaTFA) aqueous electrolytes into an anion-rich nanoclustered solvation environment. The balanced affinity of TFA– toward Zn2+ and H2O promotes Zn2+–TFA– association and drives the evolution from water-rich local coordination toward abundant contact ion pairs, ion aggregates, and interconnected multi-ion nanoclusters. Spectroscopic characterization, X-ray scattering, and molecular dynamics simulations collectively reveal reconstructed Zn2+ coordination, extended ion-associated correlations, and reorganization of the water hydrogen-bonding environment, accompanied by reduced water activity. The nanocluster electrolyte suppresses hydrogen evolution and Zn corrosion and promotes more uniform Zn deposition. The optimized nanocluster electrolyte sustains Zn||Zn cycling for over 2100 h, enables Zn||Cu cells to operate for more than 3000 h with an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.4%, and affords Zn||Na2V6O16·3H2O full cells with 82.4% capacity retention after 30,000 cycles at 10 A g–1. These results show that balanced anion interactions and molecular crowding regulate ion association and the water hydrogen-bonding environment, contributing to improved Zn reversibility and cycling stability.

articles.title: Oxygen-Promoted Dehydrogenation on Size-Selected Cu–Pd Pentamer Clusters for Low-Temperature Hydrogen Release from Cyclic Hydrocarbons
articles.abstract: Despite extensive studies on cycloalkane and cycloalkene dehydrogenation for liquid organic hydrogen carrier applications, the mechanisms governing selective H2 release under mild conditions remain poorly understood. Here, subnanometer CuxPdy pentamer clusters supported on ZrO2 represent a highly active and selective class of low-temperature dehydrogenation catalysts. Pd5 exhibits the highest benzene and molecular H2 formation rates from dehydrogenation of cyclohexene, followed by Cu2Pd3 and Cu3Pd2, whereas Cu5 is inactive. All active catalysts favored H2 over H2O as the hydrogen-containing product and completely suppressed combustion pathways, with no detectable CO2 formation. Oxygen-lean conditions further favored H2 formation across all active catalysts, with H2 selectivity exceeding 99% for Pd5. Kinetic analysis of Cu3Pd2 reveals positive fractional apparent orders in both C6H10 and O2 and an effective apparent activation energy of approximately 66 kJ·mol–1, while reactant composition and temperature systematically control H2/H2O branching. In situ XPS and in situ GIWAXS reveal that catalytic activity and cluster stability arise from the interplay of atomic composition, electronic structure, metal–oxygen interactions, and the chemical environment, with Cu exhibiting a composition-sensitive redox response and Pd-containing clusters accommodating oxygen while retaining electronically active Pd-derived states near the Fermi level. DFT/MLIP free-energy calculations identify kinetically accessible O-assisted first C–H activation pathways involving H transfer to cluster-bound O, with barriers strongly dependent on cluster composition and O configuration. These findings establish an ensemble-based structure–activity framework for controlling dehydrogenation pathways and provide design principles for catalysts that efficiently promote selective hydrogen release suitable for hydrogen carrier applications.

articles.title: Sulfur-Induced Local Structure Reconstruction and Weak Na–Anion Interactions Enable Fast Na+ Transport in x Na2S-TaCl5 Electrolytes
articles.abstract: Amorphous solid electrolytes offer opportunities for fast ion transport, yet the structural origins governing their performance remain difficult to resolve due to the absence of long-range order. While mixed-anion strategies have recently emerged to improve ion transport in sodium halide electrolytes, how sulfur incorporation modifies the local structure and Na+ transport remains poorly understood. Here, we develop a series of xNa2S-TaCl5 mixed anion solid electrolytes to elucidate the impact of sulfur on the structure and Na+ transport. Structural analyses reveal that sulfur incorporation reconstructs the connectivity of Ta-centered polyhedra while progressively disrupting the long-range crystalline ordering to form an amorphous framework. More importantly, neutron pair distribution function analysis reveals the sulfur-induced reconstruction of the local Ta-centered structure, with the emergence of coexisting edge-sharing- and corner-sharing-like motifs from the isolated polyhedra in crystalline NaTaCl6. Simulations further show that sulfur shifts the local polyhedral connectivity toward a larger proportion of edge-sharing configurations relative to the O-containing analogue. Matched-composition machine-learning molecular dynamics (MLMD) comparing O- and S-containing amorphous models suggest that sulfur weakens Na-anion binding, shortens Na–anion residence times, and lowers the barrier for Na+ migration relative to the O analogue. As a result, the optimized composition achieves a high room-temperature ionic conductivity of 3.25 mS cm–1 with a low activation energy of 0.28 eV. When evaluated in all-solid-state sodium batteries with an uncoated NaNi1/3Mn1/3Fe1/3O2 cathode, the cell delivers a discharge capacity of 112 mAh g–1 after 100 cycles (82.6% retention) with a high average Coulombic efficiency of 99.8%, demonstrating stable interfacial compatibility with uncoated layered oxide cathodes.

articles.title: Temporal Dosing Tunes Glutathione Gradient across Liver-Blood-Tumor Axes to Boost the Chemotherapeutic Potency of Prodrug Nanoassemblies
articles.abstract: Redox-responsive prodrug nanodelivery systems hold immense promise in cancer therapy, offering advantages of improved pharmacokinetics, enhanced tumor selectivity, and increased safety. However, compared with standard therapeutic formulations, prodrug nanodelivery systems fail to yield superior antitumor efficacy at equivalent doses, attributable to inadequate drug activation and intratumoral accumulation. Herein, the three-in-one drug-release module, comprising an α-disulfide bond, an ethylene glycol moiety, and a short carbon chain, was covalently linked to paclitaxel (PTX) to construct three prodrug nanoassemblies (PSBA10 NPs, PSBA12 NPs, PSBA14 NPs). Notably, PSBA10 NPs, which possessed the shortest carbon chain, exhibited hypersensitive redox-responsive drug release and potentiated antitumor efficacy. Although PSBA10 NPs exhibited better safety than paclitaxel solution (Taxol) at equivalent doses, superior efficacy remained unattainable. Interestingly, a temporal-dose-regulated glutathione (GSH) gradient across the liver-blood-tumor axis increased the intratumoral accumulation of PSBA10 NPs by approximately 3-fold, resulting in pronounced antitumor efficacy superior to Taxol. This transient depletion of GSH in the liver and blood reduced the cleavage of disulfide bonds in the systemic circulation, enhancing tumor accumulation and selective activation of PSBA10 NPs. Our study highlighted a tumor treatment model based on the synergistic strategy of structural optimization and GSH gradient regulation across the liver-blood-tumor axis to boost the efficacy of chemotherapy.

articles.title: Topology-Programmed Peptide Architectures Orchestrate Durable Tumor Targeting and Cascade Antitumor Immunity
articles.abstract: Peptide supramolecular systems offer recognition and biocompatibility for precision theranostics, yet their in vivo performance is limited by insufficient structural stability, poor retention, and loss of accessible recognition interfaces under physiological perturbations. Herein, a topology-programmed supramolecular assembly strategy was developed to stabilize adaptive peptide architectures through confinement-guided organization. A β-sheet-based peptide EH, with PD-L1 (programmed death-ligand 1) targeting, favorable assembly behavior, and hydrophobic anchoring potential, was screened from an amphiphilic peptide library and integrated with immunoactivating SeAD quantum dots into PLGA (poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid)) microspheres featuring an interconnected hydrophobic channel network. This network guides channel-confined EH assembly through hydrophobic anchoring and β-sheet reinforcement, enabling ordered nanofiber alignment while preserving local conformational flexibility and exposed recognition motifs. This topology-programmed assembly converts dynamic peptide fibers into a structurally stabilized supramolecular interface, leading to prolonged tumor retention and sustained local immune checkpoint blockade. Meanwhile, ultrasound-activated SeAD induces immunogenic cell death and systemic antitumor immunity. By coupling confinement-stabilized peptide recognition with sonodynamic immune activation, EHSeAD@MS achieves durable local tumor intervention, immune microenvironment remodeling, and suppression of distant and metastatic lesions. It establishes a molecular design principle for balancing structural integrity and adaptive recognition in peptide supramolecules, providing a strategy for long-lasting peptide-based cancer immunotherapy.

articles.title: When Transition Metal Dichalcogenides Twist: Opportunities for Spintronics and Quantum Technologies
articles.abstract: Moiré superlattices form quantum-active interfaces in which geometric reconstruction of stacked two-dimensional (2D) materials generates emergent quantum phases that are not present in the parent materials. These engineered interfaces give rise to a wide range of quantum phenomena, including strongly correlated electronic states, flat-band formation, topological phases of matter, and spin–valley locking, all of which can be tuned in situ through the twist angle. Twisted hetero/homostructures of 2D transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) exhibit an unprecedented degree of control over electronic and spin degrees of freedom, driving rapid advances in the emerging field of twistronics and opening pathways toward next-generation spintronic device applications. In this Review, we examine the fundamental concepts, applications, and prospects of twisted 2D TMDs. We outline the evolution from three-dimensional (3D) to 2D materials and the concept of twistronics, then highlight the emergent structural and magnetic properties of twisted 2D TMDs and their heterostructures. Finally, we discuss the remaining challenges and future directions toward applications in spintronic and quantum technologies.

articles.title: First-principles calculations of hydrogen trapping energy at mixed, edge, and binary-junction dislocation cores in bcc iron
Generation of structural defects in epitaxial corundum thin films and mitigation strategies
Hydrogen trapping at γ′ and γ″ precipitates in nickel and its alloys
Impact of magnetism on grain boundary solute segregation spectra in Ni polycrystals from multiscale simulations
Interface reconstruction induced exceptional coarsening resistance of in situ formed V-phase nanoprecipitates in Al-Cu-Mg-Ag-Sc alloys
Adaptive Ferroic Bi‐Sb Hybrid Iodides for Multi‐Modal Energy Harvesting and Phototronics
articles.abstract: Organic–inorganic hybrid halides offer a versatile platform for programmable multimodal functionalities, through structural softness and lattice‐charge coupling, despite the challenge of balancing the competing ferroic order, carrier transport, and thermal stability requirements. We present a composition‐driven lattice engineering strategy in a 1D iodide series based on 1,6‐diaminohexane (HDA), comprising orthorhombic non‐centrosymmetric phases of HDABiI5 (HBI) and HDASbI5 (HSI) together with a lower‐symmetry non‐centrosymmetric monoclinic phase of HDABi0.5Sb0.5I5 (HBSI) identified by its birefringent response, allowing systematic control of symmetry, lattice dynamics, and coupled transport phenomena. Through variable‐temperature crystallography and 1H NMR, multi‐perturbation Raman spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, photophysical measurements, and electronic structure calculations, we demonstrate a progression from a rigid Bi‐dominated lattice exhibiting strong piezoelectric and ferroelectric coupling to a softer Sb‐rich framework with enhanced anharmonicity, pyroelectricity, and photonic activity, while HBSI combines efficient thermal robustness and phonon transport. Density functional theory calculations show that Bi/Sb substitution tunes the electronic structure from indirect to direct bandgap, modulates oscillator strength, spontaneous polarization, pressure‐dependent electronic properties, thermoelectric and piezoelectric responses, while preserving low iodine‐vacancy formation energies. A trilayer HBI‐HSI‐HBSI architecture couples piezoelectric, triboelectric, pyroelectric, thermoelectric, ferroelectric, and photonic effects, showing 5.1‐fold synergistic enhancement in current generation through interfacial polarization and multimodal coupling.

articles.title: Bifunctional Additive Enabled Thermoresponsive Electrolytes With Dual‐Mode Manipulation Toward Safe Lithium Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Thermal safety issues arising from electrolyte instability at elevated temperatures pose a critical challenge for lithium (Li) metal batteries (LMBs). Thermoresponsive electrolytes offer a promising solution, yet battery systems with high-rate capability and reliable thermal protection have not been realized. Herein, we introduce a bifunctional LiNO3 additive into a high-volume-fraction vinylene carbonate-based thermoresponsive electrolyte (HVCE-N) to enhance the performance of LMBs at room and elevated temperatures. Notably, the introduction of the LiNO3 additive modifies the solvation structure of Li+ and forms a Li3N/LiN x O y solid electrolyte interface with high ionic conductivity. Under thermal shock, HVCE-N undergoes a rapid liquid-to-solid phase transition upon free radical polymerization to form a polymer network. More importantly, LiNO3 can regulate the free radical concentration to control the degree of polymerization, thereby preserving high ion transport capability even after phase transition. As a result, a Li||NCM811 cell based on HVCE-N exhibits high-rate performance from 1C to 10C, and stable cycling at 100°C. When subjected to a thermal shock of 200°C, HVCE-N suppresses thermal runaway for Li||NCM811 pouch cell. This electrolyte design offers a new strategy to develop highly safe LMBs with high-rate performance.

articles.title: Chloride‐Mediated Activation of Aluminum‐Alloyed Liquid Metal Anodes for Stretchable Asymmetric Energy Storage
articles.abstract: Gallium-based liquid metals are attractive anodes for stretchable energy storage because they operate dendrite-free, yet their bulk faradaic capacity remains locked behind a native oxide shell that conventional electrolytes cannot remove. Here, this passivation problem is resolved through the co-design of an aluminum-alloyed gallium–indium (AlGaIn) anode and a chloride-rich water-in-ionic-liquid (WIL) electrolyte, and the indium-assisted electrochemical activation mechanism connecting them is identified. Al alloying converts the native oxide into a hydroxyl-rich mixed Al–Ga–O shell susceptible to [GaCl4]−-mediated etching, while the In(III) ions preferentially reduced into metallic patches that seed reversible Ga alloying/dealloying within the WIL. Potential-resolved ex situ XPS indicates that in conventional TFSI-based electrolytes, the electrode passivates beneath a TFSI-derived interphase, whereas in the WIL, a chloride-dominated electrode–electrolyte interphase forms instead. The activated anode gains 60% capacity during activation and retains ∼100% capacity over 1600 cycles at 500 mA g− 1. Paired with a sonochemically derived GaOOH nanosheet cathode in a stretchable asymmetric cell, the asymmetric full cell delivers a maximum of 66.28 mWh cm−3 normalized to the active-electrode volume, and 90% capacity retention over 4000 cycles. The halide-mediated oxide-displacement principle established here provides a generalizable electrolyte-design strategy for oxide-passivated liquid-metal and post-lithium anodes.

articles.title: Descriptor‐Guided Stabilization of Reconstructed Active Phases for High‐Activity and Durable CO2‐to‐Formate Conversion
articles.abstract: Sn oxides are promising CO2RR electrocatalysts for formate production, but their high activity is difficult to sustain because cathodic reconstruction can over‐reduce active oxide‐derived surfaces to metallic Sn. This dynamic evolution makes it challenging to identify and stabilize the true working‐state active phase. Here, we construct a descriptor‐guided framework that links dynamic Sn‐oxide reconstruction with electronic‐structure evolution and formate‐producing activity to identify and stabilize the favorable working‐state active phase. Electronic‐structure analysis shows that the optimal SnxOy/Sn surface stabilizes the *OCHO intermediate through coupled charge‐polarization redistribution and Sn 5s/5p orbital modulation. To quantify this effect, we develop a TD descriptor integrating Bader charge, Sn 5p coupling, and Sn 5s lone‐pair activation, which exhibits a volcano‐type correlation with the limiting free energy, with the minimum at TD = 0.67 corresponding to the most favorable reconstructed SnxOy/Sn surface. Guided by this descriptor, amorphous SnO2 is designed to stabilize the favorable SnxOy/Sn working state and suppress deep reduction, achieving an HCOO− partial current density of 438.0 mA cm−2 at −1.8 V vs. RHE, 1.8 times that of commercial SnO2. This work provides a descriptor‐guided strategy for stabilizing reconstructed active phases in CO2RR.

articles.title: Homogenizing Fullerene Contacts by Supramolecular Host–Guest Assembly for Stable Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Fullerene and its derivatives are widely adopted as electron transport layers (ETLs) in high‐performance perovskite solar cells (PSCs). However, fullerene materials are prone to aggregation and rearrangement under environmental stress, which acts as one of the critical factors restricting the long‐term operational stability of devices. Here, we report a host–guest supramolecular assembly strategy using rigid triptycene (TPC) molecules to stabilize fullerene‐based ETLs. The [6,6]‐phenyl‐C61‐butyric acid methyl ester (PCBM)–TPC host–guest interaction enables the spatial isolation and noncovalent immobilization of PCBM cages, which suppresses the thermal‐driven aggregation, crystallization, and morphological variation of PCBM layers. The resulting inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency of 26.83%, with 96.0% efficiency retention after 1000 h of 85°C thermal aging and 92.3% retention after 1000 h of 85°C photothermal maximum power point tracking. This work offers a supramolecular solution for high‐stability optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Molecularly Induced Carrier‐Polarity Regulation Enables Efficient Methylammonium‐Free Wide‐Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Methylammonium (MA)‐free wide‐bandgap (WBG) perovskites are attractive top‐cell absorbers for tandem photovoltaics. However, defect‐related donor‐state contributions can shift the perovskite Fermi level away from the valence‐band maximum (VBM), creating an unfavorable energetic mismatch with the hole‐selective Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite contact and contributing to voltage and fill‐factor losses in perovskite solar cells with an inverted structure. Here, we introduce 4‐(piperidin‐4‐yl)benzoic acid hydrochloride (PBAC) as a spatially organized molecular additive that regulates the carrier polarity of MA‐free WBG perovskites while passivating defects. PBAC shifts the Fermi level toward the VBM and reduces the Fermi‐level offset at the Poly‐4PACZ/perovskite interface. This carrier‐polarity regulation improves energetic compatibility at the hole‐selective contact, facilitating hole extraction and suppressing interfacial recombination. Defect passivation and strain relaxation further inhibit halide migration and stabilize the mixed‐halide lattice. As a result, MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells with bandgaps of 1.66 and 1.77 eV achieve power conversion efficiencies (PCEs) of 24.66% and 20.74%, respectively. The unencapsulated PBAC‐treated 1.66 eV device retains 86% of its initial PCE after 1000 h of continuous AM 1.5G operation in ambient air. These results establish molecularly induced carrier‐polarity regulation as an effective strategy for reducing interfacial losses in MA‐free WBG perovskite solar cells.

articles.title: Redirecting Bond Cleavage in Sacrificial Prelithiation via Dual‐Side Separator Engineering for Anode‐Free Lithium Batteries
articles.abstract: Anode‐free lithium metal batteries (AFLMBs) promise extreme gravimetric and volumetric energy densities but suffer from irreversible active lithium loss, sluggish desolvation kinetics, and dendritic proliferation. Herein, we report a catalyst‐induced bond‐cleavage redirection concept to unlock efficient sacrificial prelithiation, implemented via a dual‐side functionalized separator. On the cathode side, a 5 µm MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co coating redirects Li2C2O4 decomposition from high‐barrier Li–O cleavage to preferential C─C bond scission. Theoretical calculations and operando characterizations confirm this mechanistic shift, lowering the delithiation potential to 3.79 V at 60°C with a 99.5% Li+ utilization rate. To safeguard the liberated lithium inventory against depletion, the anode side integrates a PSSLi‐PFPE bilayer. This coating accelerates Li+ desolvation and drives the in‐situ construction of a LiF‐rich solid electrolyte interphase, enabling Li symmetric cells cycling for over 1700 h (1.0 mAh cm−2, DOD = 80.7%). Bridging fundamental bond kinetics with practical engineering, the assembled 1.0 Ah anode‐free pouch cell (NCM811||MoC1‐x/NC‐0.3Co‐LCO/PE/PSSLi‐PFPE||Cu) achieves gravimetric and volumetric energy densities of 458.6 Wh kg−1 and 1005.2 Wh L−1, a power output of 989.1 W kg−1, retaining 80.1% capacity after 100 cycles. This non‐invasive separator strategy provides a unified framework connecting bond kinetics to practical cell manufacturing, charting a feasible avenue for high‐energy AFLMBs.

articles.title: 1D Plasticity in Semiconductor Crystals
articles.abstract: The exceptional plasticity recently found in inorganic semiconductors can be classified into two types: the three‐dimensional (3D) orientation‐insensitive deformability in polycrystals, and the two‐dimensional (2D) anisotropic case in layered crystals. It is thus highly anticipated that one‐dimensional (1D) plasticity should also exist but it has not been found yet. Here this work reports the excellent 1D plasticity in tin selenide (SnSe) semiconductor crystals. In in‐plane directions, the bending strain is as large as ∼22.7% for the zig‐zag‐aligned specimen (plasticity) while as small as ∼1.4% for the armchair‐aligned one (brittleness). Such 1D plasticity is ascribed to the coherent and stronger bond topology along b‐axis that allows for multiple deformation mechanisms including layer segments, interlayer slip, bridging, lattice distortion, and dislocations. This bonding topology enables that the 1D plasticity is also observed in isostructural SnS and GeSe crystals. High‐performance shape‐conformable thermoelectric generators are then successfully developed using materials with 1D plasticity. This work enriches the diagram for plasticity and thus provides a new direction for the design and discovery of ductile semiconductors.

articles.title: 2D Halide Perovskite Single Crystals Constructed by Aromatic Diammonium for High Sensitivity and Low Detection Limit X‐Ray Detectors
articles.abstract: 2D perovskites exhibit remarkable features such as strong X‐ray absorption, high resistivity, and low ion migration, endowing them with high competitiveness in X‐ray detection. Although numerous 2D perovskites (RP, DJ, and ACI phases) have drawn substantial attention, their widespread application is still restricted by excessively large interlayer spacing and limited structural stability. In this study, an aromatic diamine 2AMPY (2‐aminomethylpyridine) is designed to enhance structural rigidity and reduce interlayer spacing of the 2D perovskites by modulating the tailored hydrogen bonding interactions and the embedding depth of organic cations within the inorganic octahedral frameworks. Moreover, high quality centimeter‐sized 2D perovskites (2AMPY)PbX4 (X = Cl, Br, I) single crystals (SCs) are successfully grown via a solution method. Among them, (2AMPY)PbBr4 SCs display the shortest interlayer spacing and therefore the highest carrier mobility‐lifetime product. As a result, detectors fabricated using these SCs achieve high sensitivity (13306 µC Gy−1 cm−2), ultralow detection limit (1.69 nGy s−1), superior stability, and high‐resolution x‐ray imaging. These detectors exhibit superior performance among the reported 2D perovskite X‐ray detectors. In conclusion, this work establishes a new strategy for constructing novel 2D perovskite using aromatic diammonium cations, providing a promising solution for the development of X‐ray detection technology.

articles.title: 3D Cuprous Iodide Cluster‐Covalent Organic Framework for Ultrasensitive and Highly Selective Trace HF Detection at Room Temperature
articles.abstract: Hydrofluoric acid (HF) poses a serious and irreversible threat to human health necessitating the development of highly sensitive and selective detection materials. Herein, a three‐dimensional cuprous iodide cluster‐based covalent organic framework (CuI‐MCOF), with diamond topology has been successfully prepared, which shows an ultrafast and highly sensitive response to HF gas. At room temperature, CuI‐MCOF displays an exceptional response of 7188% toward 100 ppm HF, with remarkably rapid response/recovery times of 3 s/2 s at 4 ppm. Notably, the sensor achieves an ultralow detection limit of 21 ppb, outperforming previously reported HF sensors. Moreover, it demonstrates outstanding selectivity and anti‐interference performance, maintaining stable responses to 4 ppm HF even in the presence of 16 interfering gases (100 ppm each). Experiments combined with density‐functional theory calculations reveal that the imine‐linker N atoms serve as reversible HF adsorption–desorption sites, while the electron‐rich CuI clusters enhance dipole interactions and facilitate charge transfer. Leveraging these properties, an on‐chip miniaturized perceptron system integrated with evaluation algorithms is developed for anti‐interference HF discrimination, spatiotemporal distribution estimation, and leakage source prediction. This work provides a new strategy for designing high‐performance HF sensors and expands the application of cluster‐based COFs in gas sensing.

articles.title: A Multiferroic Morphotropic Phase Boundary
articles.abstract: Bismuth ferrite (BiFeO3) thin films possess large ferroelectric polarization and antiferromagnetic order, yet their magnetoelectric coupling is limited by weak intrinsic magnetization. Here, a multiferroic morphotropic phase boundary (MPB) is demonstrated wherein the crystal structure, polarization, and magnetic order simultaneously evolve across a chemically induced phase boundary in strain-engineered (1−x)BiFeO3-(x)BaTiO3 thin films. Between 0.1 < x < 0.2, the crystal structure evolves from a monoclinic phase to a newly stabilized tetragonal phase through an intermediate mixed-phase region. This structural transition is accompanied by concurrent changes in magnetic order, resulting in dramatically enhanced functional responses as compared with those of BiFeO3. Specifically, films with x = 0.2 exhibit larger electromechanical strains (≈ 0.3%, about three-times larger than BiFeO3) and a significantly enhanced magnetoelectric-coupling coefficient (αME ≈ 416 mV cm−1 Oe−1, nearly 1000- and 19-times larger than bulk and thin-film BiFeO3, respectively). These enhancements diminish beyond the MPB (x > 0.2) and arise from polarization rotation and evolving spin configurations driven by the near degeneracy of competing ferroic states at the multiferroic MPB. These results establish a rare multiferroic MPB where both the polar and magnetic order evolve simultaneously, providing a promising strategy for designing materials with strongly coupled ferroic order parameters.

articles.title: A Poly(lactic Acid)‐Porphyrin‐Cobalt Vaccine Adjuvant System Elicits Protein‐ or Peptide‐Specific Humoral and Cellular Immunity
articles.abstract: There is growing interest in vaccine adjuvant systems that are scalable, adaptable, and capable of stimulating humoral and cellular immune responses with recombinant protein or synthetic peptide immunogens. In this study, we introduced a “plug‐and‐play” nanoadjuvant system consisting of poly(lactic acid)‐porphyrin‐cobalt ion co‐formulated with immunostimulatory saponin QS‐21 (PPCoQ). PPCoQ facilitated subunit vaccine assembly by coordinating antigens' polyhistidine tags with immobilized cobalt (Co2+) within a porphyrin‐modified poly(lactic acid). Using the receptor‐binding domain (RBD) of severe acute respiratory syndrome coronavirus 2 (SARS‐CoV‐2) as a model antigen, the resulting nanovaccine, PPCoQ‐RBD, induced high levels of anti‐RBD antibodies in transgenic mice expressing human ACE2. Following viral challenge, immunized mice achieved a 99.7% clearance rate of the SARS‐CoV‐2 Omicron variant, demonstrating strong humoral and cellular immune responses. Additionally, PPCoQ‐RBD was compatible with nebulization‐based inhalation, which enhanced mucosal immunity, increased IgA antibody titers, and promoted the formation of abundant tissue‐resident memory T cells. A model T cell epitope (OVA) was formulated to evaluate cellular responses, generating PPCoQ‐OVA, which significantly inhibited B16‐OVA tumor growth. The PPCoQ vaccine adjuvant system is easy to produce and supports efficient antigen loading, lymph node targeting, lysosomal escape, and biocompatibility, and has broad prospects for application and clinical translation.

articles.title: A Synergistic Hydrogel Strategy for the Treatment of Candida Vaginitis Through Pathogen Clearance and Microecosystem Restoration
articles.abstract: Microbial infections often disrupt the delicate balance of host commensal microbiota, leading to dysbiosis and recurrent infections, yet current therapies lack the capacity to simultaneously eradicate pathogens and restore ecological homeostasis. Here, we report a synergistic therapeutic strategy for Candida vaginitis that integrates targeted pathogen clearance with vaginal microecosystem restoration. We engineer a vaginal microenvironment‐degradable hydrogel, HCS/FUC@LabPC, which self‐assembles from highly deacetylated high molecular‐weight chitosan oligosaccharide (HCS) and fucoidan (FUC) to encapsulate Lactobacillus (Lab) coated with procyanidine (PC). Within the vaginal microenvironment, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases HCS, which efficiently eliminates Candida albicans (C. albicans) by disrupting cell wall integrity and interfering MAPK related signaling. FUC and PC further contribute to microenvironmental remodeling through their intrinsic anti‐inflammatory and antioxidant activities. This remodeling facilitates stable colonization of Lab, which subsequently reinforces barrier integrity through competitive exclusion and metabolic modulation. In murine models, this approach effectively disrupts the infection–dysbiosis–recurrence vicious cycle, supporting an integrated therapeutic strategy that combines pathogen clearance, microenvironmental remodeling, and microecosystem restoration.

articles.title: A Textile‐Based, Battery‐Free, Electrochromic Platform for Visual Epidermal Sweat Biosensing
articles.abstract: Noninvasive wearable sweat sensors are promising for personalized health management, yet their widespread adoption is hindered by complex multi‐component architectures, reliance on rigid batteries, and a lack of intuitive visual feedback. Herein, we propose a sweat‐powered metabolism‐to‐visual transduction mechanism that utilizes sweat as both an energy source and a detection target. A fabric‐based sweat electricity harvester is fabricated, which harnesses sweat energy to yield a stable power output, enabling battery‐free sensing operation. Coupled enzymatic sensing electrode–electrochromic display system translates sweat glucose concentration into directly perceptible color change. To overcome the subjective errors inherent in traditional colorimetry, a neural network‐based smartphone application is employed to provide precise quantitative visual readouts, achieving highly accurate estimation of sweat glucose (R2 = 0.997) comparable to commercial assay kits in on‐body evaluation on human subjects. By successfully decoupling wearable sensors from rigid power sources while fusing self‐powered electrochromic displays with AI‐assisted digital readouts, this lightweight textile platform establishes an on‐demand strategy for user‐friendly, and intelligent metabolic monitoring.

articles.title: AR/PARP Dual‐Targeting Bioactive Photosensitizer for Photo‐Immunotherapy of Prostate Cancer
articles.abstract: Prostate cancer poses a severe threat to men's health worldwide, and conventional therapeutic modalities are associated with various limitations. Photodynamic therapy (PDT) offers distinctive advantages such as minimal invasiveness, mild side effects and repeatable treatment. However, the therapeutic efficacy of PDT is limited by two critical factors: the single functional property of traditional photosensitizers and the pathological tumor microenvironment. Accordingly, molecular targeting photosensitizers have been developed to address these drawbacks. Notably, long‐term administration of single‐target agents entails a high risk of drug resistance. Accordingly, based on two key targets closely implicated in the DNA repair pathways of prostate cancer cells, the androgen receptor (AR), and poly(ADP‐ribose) polymerase (PARP), we proposed an AR/PARP dual‐targeting photosensitizer strategy and synthesized a quinoxalinone‐based photosensitizer QTEO, which can simultaneously target AR and PARP and exert a synergistic effect with photodynamic activity to induce DNA damage in cancer cells. The resulting damaged DNA fragments can further activate the innate immune pathways of the organism through a coordinated cascade of reactions. This promising strategy concurrently overcomes the limited functionality of conventional photosensitizers, the potential drug resistance induced by single‐target agents, and the complex pharmacokinetic issues associated with multidrug combination therapy, ultimately enabling molecular‐targeting photo‐immunotherapy for prostate cancer.

articles.title: An "AND" Logic Gate S‐Scheme Nanozyme for Magneto‐Pyroelectric Dynamic Therapy Integrated With Lactate–Urate Immunometabolic Remodeling in Glioblastoma
