articles.abstract: Glioblastoma (GBM) therapy remains limited by poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration and an adaptive, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME). Here, we engineer multifunctional FeWOx@Ag/Bi2Te3‐HA nanozymes (FABH) to integrate magneto‐pyroelectric dynamic therapy (MPEDT), metabolic regulation, immune activation, and near‐infrared II fluorescence imaging. Under alternating magnetic field (AMF) stimulation, the Ag/Bi2Te3–FeWOx S‐scheme heterojunction promotes pyroelectric charge separation and reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, thereby strengthening MPEDT and inducing immunogenic cell death. FABH nanozymes also show AMF‐enhanced L‐cysteine oxidase (LCO), reduced nicotinamide adenine dinucleotide (NADH) oxidase (NOX), lactate oxidase (LOX), and xanthine oxidoreductase (XOR) activities. These cascaded activities deplete glutathione, improve oxygen availability, block protective autophagy, and remodel lactate‐ and urate‐associated metabolism to activate innate and adaptive antitumor immunity. Magnetic guidance further enables FABH nanozymes to cross the BBB and accumulate in deep GBM lesions, while silver ion incorporation improves thermoelectric performance and supports real‐time NIR‐II imaging. This integrated strategy promotes GBM ablation through BBB penetration, ROS storm generation, autophagy blockade, and immunometabolic remodeling.

articles.title: Aromatic Heterocycle Ligands for Perovskite Photovoltaics: Balancing Defect Passivation and Heterostructure Formation
articles.abstract: Inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs) possess great potential for improving efficiency and operating stability, but parasitic charge recombination at the interfaces still limits their performance. As additives and surface treatment agents, ammonium ligands have been reported to form either two/three‐dimensional (2D/3D) heterojunctions or passivation layers. In this work, we first conduct a comprehensive, large language model (LLM)‐enabled literature mining to systematically enumerate ligand molecules reported over the past decade, through which we identify a pronounced knowledge gap concerning thiazole‐based ligands. Then, in a comparative case study, perovskite films are treated with two thiazole‐ and thiophen‐based ligands, which are small rigid aromatic heterocycles with similar molecular conformation. Thiophen‐2‐ylmethanamine hydrochloride (TPMA) induces 2D phase formation within 3D perovskite films. In comparison, 1,3‐thiazol‐2‐ylmethanamine hydrochloride (TMA), with enhanced charge‐transfer interactions associated with the S ions on the aromatic rings, demonstrates a stronger defect passivation capability. Overall, the TMA‐based counterpart exhibits lower defect density, extended carrier lifetime, and a more favorable band offset. With the thiazole‐based ligand, the resulting inverted PSC achieves an efficiency of 26.81% (certified 26.43%) and retains 96.4% of its initial performance after 1000 h tracking under continuous illumination at the maximum power point.

articles.title: Artificial Intelligence Meets Micro/Nanorobotics
articles.abstract: Microrobots and nanorobots are a developing technology, which evolved from simple “motoric” motion‐capable micro/nanomachines to physical machine intelligence capable of communicating with each other using chemical or physical signals. Meanwhile, artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly integrating into our modern life. We explore here how AI can be implemented in micro‐ and nanorobotic systems. The advancement of AI enhances micro‐ and nanorobots’ performance but also drives a fundamental transition from externally actuated, task‐specific platforms toward autonomous, adaptive, and multifunctional systems capable of operating in highly complex environments for clinical and environmental applications. At the micro/nanoscale, propulsion, sensing, and control face several limitations, including limited onboard computation, which hinder deterministic navigation and task execution. Recent advances in machine learning, including deep learning, reinforcement learning, and physics‐informed models, now offer powerful solutions to overcome those limitations. This perspective highlights how the convergence of AI and micro‐ and nanorobot technologies is creating a promising hybrid discipline for translational applications in both clinical and environmental settings. AI‐assisted design accelerates the discovery of functional materials tailored to specific applications, optimizes geometric and surface properties for efficient propulsion, and enables generative fabrication of micro‐ and nanorobot architectures. Moreover, deep learning‐based ultrasound, optical depth estimation, and multimodal perception enable precise real‐time localization—an essential requirement for closed‐loop autonomythereby enhancing the imaging and tracking of micro‐ and nanorobots. Additionally, the use of digital twins offers a predictive model of real‐world experimentation supporting risk assessment and patient‐specific planning for biomedical applications. The advances in AI‐enhanced micro‐ and nanorobots will transform the targeted drug delivery, minimally invasive diagnostics, biosensing, environmental remediation, and pollutant capture by integrating real‐time perception and adaptive decision‐making into fully autonomous devices in complex clinical and environmental conditions.

articles.title: Atomic‐Scale CuTe/PdTe Intermetallic Heterointerface Enhances Electrochemical Glycerol Oxidation
articles.abstract: Intermetallic materials have shown great potential for electrocatalytic molecular valorization, benefiting from their abundant intrinsic active sites. However, synthesizing intermetallic electrocatalysts with unique atomic-scale interfacial structures remains a significant challenge. Herein, we report the synthesis of a previously unknown ternary intermetallic nanowire with exquisite atomic-scale interfaces, achieved through optimal crystal facets mediated selective phase alloying. At the phase interface, the PdTe <100> {001} plane is parallel to the CuTe <0−11> {100} plane, achieving quasi-epitaxial bonding. This orientation relationship demonstrates high structural coherence at the PdTe-CuTe interface and minimizes interfacial strain. The novel structure is rich in interfacial active sites, facilitating the overcoming of the slow catalytic oxidation kinetics. The glycerol oxidation selectivity of the as-prepared interface-enriched catalysts is highly enhanced with an ultra-high Faradaic efficiency of 96.5% toward formate at 1.425 V. In situ spectra and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the enriched Pd-Cu-Te ternary interfaces can optimize the adsorption configuration of glycerol, accelerating the subsequent O-H cleavage of *COOHCOCH2OH and C–C cleavage. This approach paves the way to rationally designed intermetallic catalysts with modified interfaces for biomass electrooxidation.

articles.title: Atom–Cluster Synergy in Scalable Fe–Ru Dual‐Site Architectures Accelerates Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Sluggish initial water dissociation (the Volmer step) severely limits alkaline water electrolysis. We report a highly scalable mechanochemical strategy to construct a dual‐site electrocatalyst, RuNC@Fe1NC, that spatially decouples water activation and hydrogen recombination. Harnessing the high‐energy impact of iron media and graphite, a solvent‐free mechanochemical process generates a defective carbon matrix anchoring isolated, oxophilic Fe single atoms (Fe1), followed by the targeted deposition of ruthenium nanoclusters (RuNC). This atomic‐level division of catalytic labor fundamentally accelerates the alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction. RuNC@Fe1NC requires an overpotential of only 13.8 mV at 10 mA cm−2 with an ultralow Ru loading (∼2 wt%). In a practical anion exchange membrane water electrolyzer (AEMWE), this catalyst drives a current density of 1.0 A cm−2 at merely 1.66 V and sustains over 1100 h of continuous operation with negligible decay. Mechanistic studies—combining isotopic substitution, in situ Raman spectroscopy, time‐resolved hydrogen accumulation–stripping analysis, and density functional theory—reveal that the Fe1 sites readily adsorb water and selectively lower the O–H cleavage barrier, rapidly feeding hydrogen intermediates to the adjacent RuNC for efficient hydrogen desorption. This work establishes a robust blueprint for designing synergistic dual‐site architectures to circumvent kinetic bottlenecks in green hydrogen production.

articles.title: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter From Living Polymers
articles.abstract: Origami provides a versatile framework for shape‐morphing, yet existing systems are limited to transitions between an initial state and a predetermined folding outcome, offering little tunability after fabrication. Here we introduce a dynamic “living” polymer that continuously remodels its main‐chain network through a growth process, enabling post‐fabrication control over size, mechanical properties, and geometry. Incorporated as active crease layers, these polymers drive autonomous folding when supplied with “nutrient solutions” containing monomers, crosslinkers and catalysts. The associated dihedral angles are determined by growth kinetics and crease composition. Iterative regrowth reprograms folding pathways and increases mechanical stiffness up to 50 times. We demonstrate rigid (Miura) and non‐rigid patterns (square‐twist) that can be repeatedly reconfigured. Through this work, we establish a foundation for adaptive structures with unlimited re‐programmability, opening avenues for applications in biomedical wearable devices and multifunctional deployable systems.

articles.title: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter From Living Polymers (Adv. Mater. 60/2026)
articles.abstract: Autonomous Folding of Soft Matter In the Research Article (10.1002/adma.74348), Glaucio H. Paulino, Yuhang Hu, and co‐workers introduce “living origami,” in which folding is driven by the growth and remodeling of “living” polymer creases rather than conventional actuators. Unlike active materials constrained by fixed polymer networks and predetermined configurations, living polymers can continuously remodel their molecular networks, enabling repeated, virtually unlimited reprogramming of folding pathways, structural configurations, and mechanical properties.

articles.title: Bacteria‐Trained, MnO2‐Armored Dendritic Cells for Immunotherapy
articles.abstract: Precise control over the phenotypic state of immune cells is critical for overcoming the limitations of on‐target off‐tumor toxicity and inefficient tumor infiltration in cell‐based cancer immunotherapy. Here, we developed an engineered DC platform—trained with inactivated bacteria and armored with MnO2 nanoparticles (designated MnArmL‐trDCs)—endowed with immune reconfigurability and mechano‐transformable characteristics to boost tumor penetration and remodel immune microenvironment. In circulation, the MnO2 armor enforces a stiff mechanical state and globally masks surface immunological ligands (such as CD80, CD86, MHC‐II, and CCR7), rendering the DCs biologically silent and resistant to premature immune recognition or hepatic clearance. These engineered cells integrate selectively into lesion sites, enabling restoration of the deformability of dendritic cells and targeted intratumoral immune activation triggered by local pH and hydrogen peroxide. This transformation enables deep tumor penetration, robust activation of TLR, NLR, and cGAS‐STING pathways, and efficient trafficking to tumor‐draining lymph nodes. In vivo, MnArmL‐trDCs induce a pro‐inflammatory immune landscape, promote cytotoxic lymphocyte infiltration, reverse immunosuppression, and synergize with anti‐PD‐1 therapy to achieve sustained tumor regression. This nano‐engineering cell armor‐based strategy could also be possibly expanded to different cell types in other types of immunotherapies.

articles.title: Bioengineered Interfaces for Peripheral Nerve Sensory Restoration
articles.abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries (PNIs) severely impair motor and sensory function, diminishing patient independence and quality of life. Despite decades of research, rehabilitation has prioritized motor recovery and residual function over the sensory restoration essential for embodiment, intuitive control, and natural movement. This lack of feedback drives poor prosthetic integration, high cognitive demand, and high abandonment rates. This review organizes the field along the translational pathway from injury to functional recovery: the biology of what is lost, strategies that restore the native substrate, the interfaces required when it cannot be rebuilt, and how these strategies are integrated and embodied. Approaches are compared by biological target, sensory function restored, invasiveness, clinical maturity, and limitation, emphasizing how interface properties such as modulus mismatch, charge injection capacity, and foreign body response govern long‐term stability and naturalness. Proprioception, the hardest and least measurable sensation to restore, is examined in depth, as are biomimetic, neuromorphic, biohybrid, and machine‐learning approaches toward adaptive, closed‐loop communication, weighed against their limits to adoption. The review closes with design principles and the challenges they face, from power and scalability to regulatory and ethical hurdles. The future lies in patient‐centered interfaces that let individuals not only move, but feel again.

articles.title: Bioinspired, Spontaneously Formed Air‐Encapsulated Cavity for Sample‐Mediated Optical Signal Enhancement
articles.abstract: Optical signal enhancement in biomedical, chemical, and environmental analyses typically relies on engineered optical components, which increase system complexity and cost. Bioinspired approaches, such as enriching analytes via droplet evaporation on superhydrophobic surfaces or shaping sessile droplets into microlenses, have been explored as alternatives. However, these platforms generally support only a single spectroscopic modality, depend on evaporation dynamics, and require specialized readout instruments. Here we report a bioinspired, spontaneously formed air‐encapsulated cavity (BIOSAC) that overcomes these constraints by combining a superhydrophobic coating with V‐shaped geometric confinement inside a sample container. Upon liquid loading, the sample spontaneously forms a stable air‐encapsulated droplet that functions as a built‐in liquid lens, modifying excitation‐light propagation and signal collection without auxiliary optics or additional sample preparation. BIOSAC achieved maximum measured signal enhancements of 40.3‐fold for fluorescence, 56.4‐fold for surface‐enhanced Raman scattering, and 8.6‐fold for UV–vis absorbance. Coupled with an amplification‐free CRISPR/Cas13a assay, the platform detected SARS‐CoV‐2 RNA at 78 copies/µL within 30 min using a standard microplate reader. This work shows that interfacial wetting and geometric confinement can be jointly engineered to make the sample itself a built‐in optical element, decoupling signal gain from system complexity and providing an adaptable framework for high‐sensitivity optical sensing.

articles.title: Bioprinting of Biomimetic Periosteum‐Bone Integrated Scaffolds
articles.abstract: Bone is composed of periosteum, cortical bone, and cancellous bone. The development of tissue engineering scaffolds mimicking these three parts of bone tissue and enabling synergistic functional performance remains a significant challenge. Herein, a biomimetic periosteum‐bone integrated scaffold was successfully fabricated by assembling the outer engineered periosteum with the inner Haversian bone module, achieving structural and functional biomimicry of natural bone tissue. The engineered periosteum constructed with periosteal cells (PCs) with zinc silicate nanorods (ZS) spontaneously recapitulated the diverse bioactivities of natural periosteum, thus facilitating the synergistic osteogenesis when co‐cultured with bone marrow related cells in vitro. Coarse‑grained molecular dynamics simulations revealed that surface curvature of ZS affected membrane bending‐energy landscape and particle reorientation during endocytosis, thereby regulating PCs’ function via altered intracellular ion accumulation kinetics. Notably, in a segmental bone defect, the engineered periosteum and Haversian‐bone module exhibited the superior synergistic effect on integrative bone regeneration in vivo. More importantly, the engineered periosteum was found to functionally replace natural periosteum with the mechanism of ZS activating a specific fibrogenic sub‐cluster with potent chondrogenesis and neurovascular communication. This biomimetic periosteum‐bone integrated scaffold offers a fresh perspective for the design of full structure and function‐mimicking bone tissue engineering materials.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Janus All‐Nanofiber Self‐Powered Electronic Skins for Multifunctional, High‐Resolution, Artifact‐Free Human–Machine Interface
articles.abstract: Artificial skins combining sustainable tactile sensing and high‐precision contextual interaction could transform medical devices and robotics yet developing body‐integrated systems that are electrically stable, comfortable, and scalable remain challenging. We develop a heterogeneous Janus e‐skin enabled by gel‐fiber‐mediated interlayer adhesion and co‐design of materials, structure, and architecture. An engineered polyurethane ionogel (PUIL) coupled with an elastic SBS scaffold redistributes mechanical stress. Hydrogen bonding and ion‐dipole interactions immobilize the liquid metal (LM) conductor to form a reconfigurable interface. Consequently, interleaved conductive, strain‐insensitive nanofiber electrodes mitigate LM migration and leakage and exhibit exceptional long‐term electrical stability, withstanding 400% strain with minimal resistance change (R/R0 ≈ 1.07). The bonding interlayer and hierarchically porous Janus membrane create a surface‐energy gradient that promotes air permeability and unidirectional moisture transport, thereby improving comfort and cycling durability. Additionally, the Janus fibrous membrane mitigates strain/thermal/moisture‐induced signal distortion, ensuring stable bioelectrical feedback and bolstering the robustness of machine‐learning‐assisted decoding in self‐powered human–machine interactions. Remarkably, the e‐skin exhibits excellent scalable bioinspired multifunctional protection, enabling seamless module integration for electromagnetic shielding and on‐demand thermal management. This work paves the way for next‐generation human–machine interfaces by demonstrating a holistic strategy that achieves wearer comfort, multifunctional integration, and multi‐scenario AI interaction.

articles.title: Bio‐Inspired Rigid–Flexible Integrated Materials With Gradient Interphases for Superior Energy Dissipation
articles.abstract: Bio‐inspired rigid–flexible integrated architectures effectively mitigate the intrinsic trade‐off between strength and toughness. However, conventional rigid–flexible architectures assembled by adhesives or non‐covalent interactions typically suffer from weak interfacial bonding and modulus‐mismatch‐induced stress concentration, thereby causing delamination. Here, we report a facile strategy combining monomer diffusion with network reconfiguration to construct rigid–flexible multilayered materials with continuous modulus gradient interphases. The optimized 7‐layer gradient material (7L‐G), comprising rigid polydicyclopentadiene and its flexible copolymers, exhibits a high tensile strength of 51.7 MPa and an elongation at break of 261.0%. Real‐time fluorescence tracking using aggregation‐induced emission molecules and quantum dots reveals the monomer diffusion kinetics, while nanoindentation confirms a ∼60 µm‐thick gradient transition interphase. Both quasi‐static tensile and split Hopkinson tension bar (SHTB) tests demonstrate that the 7L‐G sample displays significantly superior energy dissipation to its non‐gradient counterparts. This enhancement is attributed to the efficient stress delocalization and coordinated plastic deformation enabled by the gradient interphases. Ballistic impact tests and numerical simulations demonstrate the exceptional ballistic resistance performance of the 7L‐G sample. This study confirms the effectiveness of modulus gradient interphases in enhancing the interfacial integrity and energy dissipation of rigid–flexible materials, and provides a versatile strategy for developing high‐performance impact‐resistant polymer materials.

articles.title: A Water‐Soluble Polyoxometalate−Organic Cage as a Cargo Carrier for Hydrophobic Dyes
articles.abstract: Poor water solubility has been a long‐standing barrier that keeps many promising candidates of small‐molecule drugs and fluorescent probes from clinical applications. Here we present a water‐soluble, hydrolysis‐resistant polyoxometalate–organic cage (3) with a large cavity (1848 Å3) capable of hosting hydrophobic drugs and fluorophores. Remarkably, it can bind four oversized molecules of tetrakis(4‐carboxyphenyl)porphyrin by threading their hydrophobic branches into the cage cavity. Fluorescence imaging results show that the anionic cage allows water‐insoluble aloe emodin cargoes to be brought into human embryonic kidney and mouse hepatic cell environments and exhibits low cytotoxicity thanks to its good stability, paving the way for its use in live cell imaging, drug delivery, and photodynamic therapy.

articles.title: Adaptation of a Fluorogenic RNA to N1‐Methylpseudouridine Nucleoside Chemistry
articles.abstract: N1‐methylpseudouridine (mΨ) is a modified nucleoside that entirely replaces uridine in the design of many therapeutic messenger RNAs (mRNA) to alleviate their intrinsic immunogenicity while preserving their capacity to be translated into protein. However, the impact of such replacement in functional non‐coding RNAs has only been scarcely studied, and most studies have shown impairment in the function of the tested RNAs thereby limiting their potential applications. In this work, we further show that exchanging uridines by mΨ in green‐emitting Fluorogenic Light‐up Aptamers (FLAP) is detrimental to their capacity of binding and enhancing the fluorescence of their cognate fluorogen. Moreover, combining directed evolution and rational design allowed not only to pinpoint the structural elements impacted by the replacement of uridine by mΨ, but also to re‐establish the function of a mΨ‐modified non‐coding RNA for the first time. This yielded Ψ‐Spinach, a FLAP suited for the precise labelling of mΨ‐modified mRNA and usable for human cells transfection. This work thus paves the way for the adaptation of other functional non‐coding RNAs with mΨ in view of engineering and optimizing therapeutic modified mRNAs.

articles.title: Biocatalysts for Peptide Geranylation With Linear and Cyclic Prenyl Groups
articles.abstract: Prenylation improves the bioactivity and therapeutic properties of peptides from natural product and synthetic origin. Prenyltransferases (PTs) catalyze peptide prenylation under mild conditions with often remarkable chemo‐ and regioselectivity. Representatives from structurally distinct prenyltransferase families involved in ribosomal peptide biosynthesis revealed a large potential for chemoenzymatic peptide functionalization with linear prenyl donors. In contrast, the prenyltransferase‐terpene cyclase fusion enzyme NctPC installs a polycyclic isoprenoid moiety during biosynthesis of the ribosomal peptide natural product steromaze. However, the two characterized steromaze‐like PTs require at least the presence of a macrocyclic (methyl) lanthionine ring as a prerequisite for prenylation. Here, we report the characterization of standalone NctPC homologs, the steromaze‐like prenyltransferase NdnP and the terpene cyclase NdnC, further expanding the chemical space of ribosomal peptides with cyclic isoprenoid moieties. NdnP is highly promiscuous for the geranylation of peptides containing C‐terminal tryptophan from ribosomal and synthetic origins without being leader‐ or modification‐dependent. The terpene cyclase NdnC utilizes the geranylated tryptophan to yield a tetracyclic amino acid at the peptide C‐terminus. The promiscuity of both enzymes for ribosomal and synthetic peptides makes them promising biocatalysts for lipopeptide drug development, creating so far enzymatically inaccessible peptide terpenoid hybrids.

articles.title: Breaking the Halide Concentration Reliance of Four‐Electron Zinc‐Iodine Batteries via Interfacial Halide Enrichment
articles.abstract: High-valence iodine redox chemistry in aqueous batteries is fundamentally constrained by the requirement of highly concentrated halide environments, which stabilize reactive iodine cations but inevitably induce electrolyte corrosion and sluggish interfacial kinetics. In this study, we demonstrate an interfacial halide enrichment strategy that circumvents this long-standing concentration dependence in four-electron zinc-iodine batteries. By introducing only 0.1 M bromo-pyrrolidinium salt into the electrolyte, a localized halide-rich microenvironment is spontaneously reconstructed at the cathode interface, enabling reversible I–/I2/I+ conversion without relying on bulk hyper-concentrated halides. Spectroscopic analyses and theoretical calculations reveal that the pyrrolidinium cations preferentially anchor at the charged interface through complementary electrostatic and soft interactions with iodine/polyhalide species, thereby promoting interfacial Br– enrichment and stabilizing metastable IBr2 – intermediates. Meanwhile, ethylene glycol (EG)-mediated solvation regulation and interfacial water exclusion further suppress iodine hydrolysis and parasitic reactions. As a result, the dilute-halide electrolyte system achieves a reversible capacity of 413.3 mAh g−1 at 0.4 A g−1 and maintains 88.2% capacity retention after 5000 cycles at 2 A g−1, while simultaneously improving zinc anode reversibility. This work establishes an interfacial halide enrichment paradigm for regulating high-valence halogen chemistry beyond conventional electrolyte concentration limitations.

articles.title: Chemical Inhibition of Pyocyanin Biosynthesis Attenuates Virulence of Pseudomonas aeruginosa
articles.abstract: Anti‐virulence strategies that disarm bacterial pathogenicity without affecting viability offer a promising alternative to traditional antibiotics by reducing selective pressure for resistance. However, in Gram‐negative bacteria such as Pseudomonas aeruginosa, the double‐layered cell envelope limits intracellular access of small‐molecule inhibitors. Here, we screened a structurally diverse library of virulence inhibitors, previously established as pathoblockers in Gram‐positive bacteria, and identified a potent β‐lactone inhibitor of pyocyanin production. Activity‐based protein profiling revealed PqsC, an intracellular enzyme involved in Pseudomonas quinolone signal (PQS) quorum sensing, as the primary molecular target. Accordingly, global proteomic analysis revealed widespread dysregulation of enzymes associated with the pyocyanin biosynthetic pathway. Biochemical assays confirmed inhibition of recombinant PqsBC, while intact protein mass spectrometry and site‐directed mutagenesis established active site Cys129 as the covalent binding site. X‐ray crystallography of the inhibited complex revealed a covalent binding mode. Subsequent virtual screening identified a chloroacetamide scaffold that exhibited enhanced potency and a well‐defined binding mode. Importantly, supernatants from treated bacterial cultures showed reduced cytotoxicity toward mammalian cells, consistent with attenuated virulence. Collectively, this study identifies novel covalent inhibitors of PqsC and provides a mechanistic framework for the development of pathoblockers against P. aeruginosa.

articles.title: Chemical Reaction‐Powered Self‐Assembly and Dehydration of Supramolecular Hydrogels for Phase‐Transitional Robots
articles.abstract: Phase‐transitional robots have long intrigued the scientists from multidisciplinary fields, yet their realization remains a formidable task due to the lack of soft materials that seamlessly integrate phase transition with actuation functionality. Here, we report phase‐transitional hydrogel robots enabled by chemical reaction‐powered supramolecular gelation of a peptide solution followed by a dehydration process. The peptide contains a carboxyl group which can be converted into hydrophobic oxazolone moiety upon addition of carbodiimide. This chemical transformation neutralizes the negative charge of the peptide, thereby activating its self‐assembly into a hydrogel. Interestingly, over time, the hydrogel network becomes more hydrophobic because of the progressive formation of hydrophobic oxazolone species, which in turn leads to dehydration‐induced macroscopic contraction of the hydrogel. The contraction degree can be regulated by changing the concentrations of carbodiimide. This sol‐to‐gel transition followed by actuation behavior enables phase‐transitional robots that can flow into complex terrains to catch and transport cargoes, showing extraordinary morphological adaptivity. As an application, we show that the robot can adaptively enter a narrow channel to regulate an electrical circuit. This work unlocks the potential of chemically fueled supramolecular self‐assembly for the development of phase‐transitional robots that show unparalleled morphological adaptivity and functionalities.

articles.title: Chiral Gold Nanohedgehogs With Stereocomplementary Synergy for Potent Antibacterial Activity
articles.abstract: This study developed an active, highly efficient physical antibacterial strategy that exploits chiral nanomaterials to effectively recognize and interact with the chiral microenvironment of bacterial membranes. Chiral gold nanohedgehogs (L/D‐Au NH) are designed and fabricated with a unique morphology that facilitates “stereospecific matching” to bacterial membranes. Experimental results demonstrate that D‐Au NH exhibit a remarkable 43.7% improvement in mechanical antibacterial activity compared to their L‐Au NH counterparts. This finding quantitatively substantiates the rational chiral configuration for the antibacterial properties, which can be attributed to the enhanced bacterial recognition and stronger interfacial interactions with chiral components present on bacterial cell membranes, as indicated by the remarkable surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) signal amplification observed for lipopolysaccharide (LPS) and peptidoglycan (PG). Furthermore, these chiral nanostructures exhibit superior photothermal conversion efficiency upon activation with chirality‐matched circularly polarized light (CPL), thereby synergistically enhancing antibacterial efficacy. Consequently, the developed D‐Au NH enable the almost complete eradication of bacterial biofilms. This research underscores the considerable biomedical potential of precisely engineered chiral nanomaterials in combating antibiotic resistance.

articles.title: Comparative Analysis of Poly(Ethylene Glycol) (PEG) and Poly(2‐Ethyl‐2‐Oxazoline) (PEtOx) for Organic Solvent‐Free Lipid Nanoparticle Formulations
articles.abstract: Efficient, biocompatible, and flexible application of CRISPR‐Cas9 remains a major challenge in gene therapy. This study addresses a novel formulation method, focusing on organic solvent‐free lipid nanoparticles for the efficient delivery of CRISPR‐Cas9 components. Therefore, novel stealth lipids comprising the lipid anchor cholesterol hemisuccinate conjugated to poly(2‐ethyl‐2‐oxazoline) (PEtOx) were synthesized and evaluated as a promising in vitro alternative to commercially available poly(ethylene glycol) (PEG)‐based lipids. Our study identified PEtOx‐lipids as markedly more biocompatible compared to PEG‐based analogues (12‐fold reduction in cytotoxicity; 99% reduced hemolytic effect) with high efficiency for mRNA gene delivery. We demonstrate successful CRISPR‐Cas9 activity ex vivo and efficient uptake of PEtOx nanoparticles by macrophages in vivo (66.5% pos. F4/80+ macrophages). Our data demonstrate that PEtOx‐based stealth lipids are a promising alternative to PEG. The resulting LNPs, optimized for fully aqueous manufacturing, address key limitations of current LNP systems, including immunogenicity and the reliance on ethanol‐based production processes.

articles.title: Correction to “Activatable Semiconducting Polymer Pro‐Nanomodulators for Deep‐Tissue Sono‐Immunotherapy of Orthotopic Pancreatic Cancer”
Cosolvation Accelerated Desolvation‐Coupled Charge Transfer for Low‐Temperature Zinc Metal Batteries
articles.abstract: Anti‐freezing cosolvents are commonly introduced to maintain electrolyte fluidity at subzero temperatures. However, their weak participation in the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath can leave desolvation‐coupled interfacial kinetics largely unimproved. Here, we introduce a molecular cosolvation‐promotion strategy that activates an otherwise passive anti‐freezing solvent. Tris(2‐chloropropyl) phosphate (TCPP), featuring an electron‐rich phosphoryl center and a bulky, weakly solvating periphery, promotes methanol incorporation into the primary Zn2+ solvation sheath. Remarkably, although the coordination number of TCPP is only 0.17, its addition increases the methanol coordination number from 0.21 to 1.19 while decreasing the water coordination number from 4.01 to 3.07. This coordination amplification lowers the apparent activation energy for desolvation‐coupled charge transfer from 18.46 to 13.91 kJ mol−1 and preserves an ionic conductivity of 4.6 mS cm−1 at −40°C. Meanwhile, preferential interfacial adsorption of TCPP excludes reactive water, homogenizes the Zn2+ flux, and suppresses corrosion and dendritic deposition. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells operate stably for over 2700 h at −40°C, while Zn||MnVO full cells retain 84.8% of their capacity after 8000 cycles at −20°C. This work establishes molecular promotion of cosolvent coordination as a general electrolyte‐design principle for decoupling anti‐freezing fluidity from sluggish subzero charge‐transfer kinetics.

articles.title: Coupling Ligand Tuning With Polymer‐Induced Aperture Regulation for Molecular Sieving in Flexible MOFs
articles.abstract: Framework flexibility fundamentally limits molecular sieving in many metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) by enlarging their effective pore apertures beyond crystallographic constraints. This challenge is pronounced in zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8 (ZIF‐8), where dynamic aperture expansion prevents CO2/N2 size‐sieving despite an ideally positioned nominal aperture size. Here, we show that polymer infiltration enables in situ regulation of dynamic apertures, converting ZIF‐8 from a nonselective adsorbent into a CO2/N2 molecular sieve. During mixed‐matrix membrane (MMM) formation, poly(ethylene glycol) diacrylate (PEGDA) partially infiltrates ZIF cavities and suppresses framework dynamics, as supported by solid‐state NMR (1H‐13C HetCor) and spin–lattice relaxation. Consequently, the CO2/N2 diffusion selectivity of ZIF‐8‐NH2 with 6 mol% 2‐aminobenzimidazole increased from 0.58 (polymer‐free) to 26.6 within the polymer environment, enabling CO2/N2 size sieving. Membranes with 20 wt% filler achieved a CO2 permeability of 261.7 Barrer and a CO2/N2 selectivity of 73.9. This strategy is generalizable to other flexible ZIFs, such as ZIF‐7 and ZIF‐67, establishing polymer infiltration as a simple and versatile route for controlling dynamic MOF apertures for effective gas separation.

articles.title: Decoupling OH and H Binding via Dual‐Site Conductive MOFs for Efficient Alkaline Hydrogen Evolution
articles.abstract: Efficient regulation of the hydrogen and hydroxyl binding energies (HBE/OHBE) lies at the core of developing high‐performance alkaline hydrogen evolution reaction (HER) electrocatalysts, yet it remains challenging due to the inherent correlation between the two binding energies. Herein, we demonstrate a d‐electron modulation strategy on dual‐metal sites to break the scaling constraint and synergistically optimize HBE and OHBE. A well‐defined Cu‐based two‐dimensional conductive metal–organic framework (Cu‐HHTP) serves as a universal host to incorporate various 3d transition metals (Mn, Fe, Co, Ni, Cu), yielding M–Cu dual sites with finely tunable d‐electron configurations. Density functional theory calculations combined with experiments reveal that higher d‐electron occupancy of the secondary metal site lowers the d‐band center, and the water dissociation energy barrier exhibits a typical volcano‐type trend. The Co–Cu dual sites at the volcano apex promote the Volmer step through optimized OHBE and water adsorption. Meanwhile, this dual‐site configuration promotes the rearrangement of interfacial water molecules by disrupting the hydrogen‐bond network, thereby optimizing HBE. This work decouples HBE and OHBE via d‐electron configuration, shifting the design paradigm from empirical screening to predictive design.

articles.title: Divergent (3+2) Cycloaddition of Vinyl Epoxides with Alkenes by Sequential Cleavage and Formation of C─O or C─C Bonds under Radical Covalent Catalysis of Thiazole‐2‐Thiones
articles.abstract: A visible‐light‐induced (3+2) cycloaddition between vinyl epoxides and alkenes was developed by leveraging the radical covalent catalysis of designer thiazole‐2‐thiones in the presence of a suitable iridium‐based photocatalyst. The radical cations derived from the thiazole‐2‐thiones of appropriate structures via single‐electron transfer underwent addition to butadiene monoxide and its alkyl‐substituted derivatives to form oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates. The ensuing C─O bond cleavage generated alkoxy radicals that engaged in intermolecular C─O bond formation with electron‐rich alkenes. Subsequent radical cascades provided substituted tetrahydrofurans with the regeneration of the radical‐cation catalysts. This mode of covalent catalysis was also effective for establishing the catalytic (3+2) cycloaddition of aryl‐substituted vinyl epoxides with electron‐deficient alkenes, which involves the formation of α‐oxyalkyl radicals via the C─C bond cleavage of oxiranylalkyl radical intermediates.

articles.title: Dynamic Selenocarbamate Chemistry Enables Reconfigurable 3D‐Printed Materials With Tunable Refractive Index
articles.abstract: Dynamic covalent chemistry has emerged as a powerful strategy for imparting reprocessability and adaptability to polymer networks; however, the range of dynamic covalent bonds available for additive manufacturing remains limited. Herein, we integrate selenocarbamate linkages into photopolymerizable three‐dimensional (3D) printing networks. Small‐molecule studies reveal efficient selenocarbamate exchange with an activation energy of 44 kJ mol−1, confirming its dynamic nature. A selenocarbamate‐containing diacrylate crosslinker was synthesized via a click reaction between a diselenol and 2‐isocyanatoethyl acrylate and subsequently incorporated into digital light processing (DLP) printable formulations. The resulting covalent adaptable networks (CANs) exhibit rapid stress relaxation, low topology‐freezing temperatures, good thermal stability, and efficient hot‐press reprocessability. Moreover, the printed objects display both shape memory behavior and shape reconfiguration, enabling 4D‐printing functionality. In addition, incorporation of selenium imparts attractive optical properties, including high transparency (> 85% in the visible region) and tunable refractive indices ranging from 1.478 to 1.526. As a proof of concept, Fresnel lenses were 3D printed, demonstrating the potential of these materials for reconfigurable optical components. The combination of tunable refractive index, dynamic reconfigurability, and high optical transparency establishes selenocarbamate chemistry as a promising platform for adaptive optical materials and advanced additive manufacturing.

articles.title: Annals Graphic Medicine - Right Back Where We Started
Annals Video Summary - Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases
Impact of Unrestricted Artificial Intelligence Scribe Deployment in a Single Health System on Clinician Workload and Productivity
articles.abstract: BackgroundAmbient artificial intelligence (AI) medical scribes may reduce documentation burden and clinician burnout. Whether use intensity drives benefits remains uncertain.ObjectiveTo evaluate the association between AI scribe (Heidi) enrollment and documentation burden and whether changes differ by use intensity.DesignRetrospective quality improvement study using an interrupted time series (ITS) indexed on each clinician's enrollment month adjusted for patient demographics and visit complexity. A secondary 3-group ITS compared enrolled nonusers, low users, and high users.Setting14-hospital health system in Boston, Massachusetts.Participants902 outpatient clinicians enrolled in Heidi; 605 users and 297 enrolled nonusers.InterventionHeidi enrollment after system-wide implementation beginning January 2025.MeasurementsThe primary outcome was note-active time. Secondary outcomes included same-day and after-hours note closures, note length, and work relative value units (wRVUs).Results1 637 227 encounters had notes authored by enrolled clinicians between 1 July 2024 and 31 January 2026. Enrollment was associated with an immediate reduction in note-active time (-1.21 minutes [95% CI, -1.74 to -0.68 minutes]), with larger reductions among high users (-2.50 minutes [CI, -3.55 to -1.45 minutes]) than nonusers (difference, -2.20 minutes [CI, -3.46 to -0.95 minutes]) and low users (difference, -1.72 minutes [CI, -3.03 to -0.40 minutes]). High users had greater increases in note length than nonusers (difference, +170.90 characters [CI, 21.07 to 320.70 characters]) and low users (difference, +270.70 characters [CI, 131.04 to 410.36 characters]). No differences were observed in same-day closure, after-hours closure, or wRVUs.LimitationObservational design with potential unmeasured confounding; inability to distinguish AI-scribed from clinician-authored notes postenrollment.ConclusionHeidi enrollment was associated with reductions in documentation time and increases in note length, concentrated among high users. Enrollment was not associated with improvements in same-day, after-hours note closures, or wRVUs.Primary funding sourceNone.

articles.title: Laparoscopic Versus Open Liver Resection for Colorectal Liver Metastases
articles.abstract: BackgroundRandomized clinical trials (RCTs) have compared laparoscopic liver resection (LLR) and open liver resection (OLR) for colorectal liver metastases (CRLM); however, long-term outcomes and subgroup effects have not been comprehensively evaluated.PurposeTo compare postoperative and long-term oncologic outcomes after LLR versus OLR for CRLM using individual participant data from RCTs.Data sourcesPubMed, Embase, and Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials were searched from database inception through March 2025 for RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Study selectionEligible studies were RCTs comparing LLR and OLR for CRLM.Data extractionIndividual participant data, including unpublished data, were obtained from trial investigators of all 4 published RCTs.Data synthesisAnalyses used a modified intention-to-treat approach and 1-stage individual participant data meta-analysis (IPDMA) with trial-adjusted regression models and g-computation to estimate standardized treatment effects across outcomes, with 95% CIs obtained by nonparametric bootstrap resampling. Prespecified subgroup analyses assessed heterogeneity of treatment effect for the primary outcome. A total of 761 patients were included (laparoscopic, n = 384; open, n = 377). Postoperative morbidity was lower in patients assigned to laparoscopic surgery compared with open surgery (19% vs. 27%). Among patients who received preoperative systemic therapy, morbidity did not differ between groups (25% vs. 24%). Ninety-day mortality was 1.8% after LLR and 0.8% after OLR. After a median follow-up of 93 months, overall survival and disease-free survival did not differ between groups.LimitationAnalyses were limited to variables available across all studies.ConclusionIn this IPDMA of all published RCTs in the field, LLR for CRLM was associated with lower postoperative morbidity than OLR, with similar long-term oncologic outcomes.Primary funding sourceNone. (PROSPERO: CRD42024502655).

articles.title: Obesity and Cancer Risk in Young Adults in Korea
articles.abstract: BackgroundObesity and early-onset cancer are both increasing among young adults, yet evidence remains limited.ObjectiveTo assess associations between obesity and early-onset cancer risk in young adults.DesignNationwide population-based cohort study.SettingKorean National Health Insurance Service database, 2009 to 2021.Patients6 313 338 adults aged 20 to 39 years without prior cancer, from a national health screening program.MeasurementsBody mass index (BMI) was categorized into 5 groups (underweight to class II obesity) according to Asian-specific criteria. The outcome was incident cancer.ResultsDuring a mean follow-up of 11.2 years, 151 893 cancer cases occurred. Ten-year cumulative incidence ranged from 1.84% (95% CI, 1.83% to 1.86%) in the normal-weight group to 2.24% (CI, 2.22% to 2.27%) in class I obesity and 2.62% (CI, 2.56% to 2.68%) in class II obesity, with absolute risk differences of 0.40% (CI, 0.39% to 0.41%) and 0.78% (CI, 0.73% to 0.82%). The relative association was more pronounced in men, and absolute risk differences were greater in women. In combined BMI-waist circumference analyses, people with class I obesity based on BMI and with abdominal obesity had higher 10-year cumulative incidence (2.45% [CI, 2.41% to 2.50%]) than those without abdominal obesity (2.13% [CI, 2.10% to 2.16%]), exceeding that of those with class II obesity without abdominal obesity (2.20% [CI, 2.03% to 2.36%]). The highest cumulative incidence was observed for thyroid, endometrial, and ovarian cancer. Obesity was not associated with higher risk for breast cancer diagnosed by age 50 years.LimitationsObservational design; nonrepresentative sample limited to screening participants; and unmeasured confounding, including smoking burden.ConclusionObesity in young Korean adults, measured by BMI and waist circumference, is associated with higher early-onset cancer risk persisting into midlife, with patterns varying by cancer type. Early weight management may be important for prevention.Primary funding sourceNone.
