articles.title: TFXcan reveals transcription factor programs driving GWAS loci
articles.abstract: Adeluwa et al. developed TFXcan, a framework that predicts personalized transcription factor binding from genotype data across ∼700 transcription-factor-tissue pairs. Applied to PrCa risk, TFXcan identified specific transcription factors and coordinated programs of transcription factors that drive the disease at risk loci.

articles.title: Mesothelin-induced lysosomal biogenesis sustains neutrophil longevity to drive brain metastasis
articles.abstract: Tumor-associated neutrophil (TAN) enrichment is a defining feature and driving force of brain metastases (BrMs), a leading cause of death in solid tumors. Yet, the mechanisms governing TAN enrichment in BrM remains undefined. Herein, we demonstrate that BrM cell-derived shed soluble mesothelin (sMSLN) critically prolongs neutrophil survival to facilitate tumor cell colonization and outgrowth in the brain. Specifically, sMSLN binds to toll-like receptor 4 (TLR4) on neutrophil to activate the JAK2-STAT3 pathway. This activation promotes lysosomal biogenesis and function, reducing cellular reactive oxygen species (ROS) and inhibiting neutrophil apoptosis. Neutrophil depletion or TLR4-STAT3 blockade abrogates sMSLN-induced BrM progression. Targeting MSLN with Anetumab effectively reduces TAN enrichment, and combining this with TLR4 inhibition synergistically suppresses lung cancer BrM. Our findings establish a critical role for tumor cell-derived sMSLN in sustaining neutrophil longevity and driving BrM, highlighting the sMSLN-TLR4 axis as a promising therapeutic target for brain metastatic tumors.

articles.title: Neuroprotectant development from small molecule inhibitors of CHOP/ATF4 expression
articles.abstract: Glaucoma is a neurodegenerative disease that is in urgent need of neuroprotective therapies. We previously revealed the critical role of neuronal endoplasmic reticulum (ER) stress induced by optic nerve injury in glaucomatous neurodegeneration. We also demonstrated that modulation of the ATF4-CHOP branch of ER stress provides significant neuroprotection. Here, we present multiple new chemical series identified by high-throughput screening that inhibit ER stress-induced C/EBP homologous protein (CHOP) expression. We perform a structure-activity relationship analysis of one "hit" compound and establish two analogs with potent activities on inhibiting the expression of CHOP and activating transcription factor 4 (ATF4). We further demonstrate their neuroprotective efficacy in two optic neuropathy models; in both models, they increase survival of retinal ganglion cell somata and axons and preserve visual function. Together, this proof-of-concept evidence establishes the new ER stress modulators as promising candidates for further drug development to provide neuroprotective therapy for glaucoma and other optic neuropathies, and potentially for diverse CNS axonopathies.

articles.title: One factor, two safeguards: RUNX1 divides its labor across the regulatory genome
articles.abstract: Fritz et al.1 use acute RUNX1 degradation to reveal how mammary epithelial cells maintain their state. RUNX1 links enhancer-centered control of epithelial identity with promoter-centered control of DNA-damage responsiveness.

articles.title: PhIP-Seq reveals geography- and disease-associated human herpesvirus antibody repertoires and distinct EBV response modules
articles.abstract: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) has been implicated in immune-mediated inflammatory diseases, but herpesvirus-directed humoral responses across populations and disease states remain incompletely defined. We profiled antibodies to all nine human herpesviruses by PhIP-Seq in 908 serum samples from 848 individuals in Madagascar and Germany. Cohorts showed distinct reactivity patterns, including cross-virus associations between homologous alphaherpesvirus envelope glycoproteins. German cohorts recognized a broader range of latent and lytic EBV proteins than Malagasy controls, with increased reactivity in primary sclerosing cholangitis. Proteome-wide profiling detected reactivity to 60 of 79 EBV proteins; 29 contained at least one peptide recognized in >5% of participants. Co-occurrence analyses identified an EBNA2-EBNA3A/B/C module and BFRF3-EBNA1 and BZLF1-BMRF1 pairs in German cohorts. Peptide ELISA showed individual-level concordance with PhIP-Seq for EBNA1. These findings reveal geography- and disease-associated herpesvirus antibody repertoires incompletely captured by single-antigen serology.

articles.title: Species-specific gene programs define divergent antiviral responses in Marburg virus reservoir bats and humans
articles.abstract: Bats tolerate viruses that cause severe disease in humans. Egyptian rousette bats, the natural reservoirs of Marburg virus (MARV), sustain asymptomatic infection, whereas humans develop severe and fatal disease. To define the basis of this divergence, we establish a comparative framework using primary and immortalized Egyptian rousette and human cells exposed to double-stranded RNA and interferon (IFN). Bat cells upregulate antiviral effectors while limiting inflammatory amplifiers, a pattern further supported by analysis of independent in vivo MARV infection datasets. In contrast, human cells activate antiviral programs and immune hyperactivation in response to MARV. Integrating transcriptomic and proteomic analyses, we identify species-specific immune programs encompassing differential IFN-stimulated gene regulation, apoptotic control, and cytokine signaling. Our findings establish an integrative framework for understanding species-specific antiviral responses associated with MARV reservoir biology, identify pathways linked to immunopathogenesis in humans, and provide a foundation for future studies of host responses to filovirus infection.

articles.title: The compositional encoding of hand-eye coordinated movements for single neurons in the posterior parietal cortex
articles.abstract: Human posterior parietal cortex (PPC) is known to play a role in hand-eye (H-E) coordination, yet the underlying encoding mechanisms remain uncertain. We recorded 412 single neurons across 11 sessions from motor cortex (MC; n = 251) and PPC (n = 161) in a single human participant performing an H-E coordinated center-out task. While MC neurons showed negligible modulation by eye movements, 79% of PPC neurons had neural representations that were additively separable into independent hand- and eye-movement tuning curves. Due to this separability, representations could be separated and additively recomposed while maintaining structural similarity. Consequently, compositional decoders trained solely on single-effector movements could match the performance of decoders trained on coordinated H-E movements (hand: 66% vs. 69%; eye: 34% vs. 36%). These results show that, during simple center-out tasks, MC hand-movement codes are unaffected by eye movements and that compositionality can be used to modularly decode H-E coordinated movements in PPC.

articles.title: An in vivo T cell engager platform induces deep plasma cell depletion in autoimmune dry eye
articles.abstract: Ling et al. develop T-IDLESTCE, a T cell-targeted integration-deficient lentiviral vector that programs endogenous T cells to secrete TCEs in situ. TCE-secreting T cells infiltrate disease-relevant tissues, drive deep plasma cell depletion, and promote sustained ocular improvement in an autoimmune dry eye model.

articles.title: Escape from flatland: Strained-ring linchpins for 3D heterocyclic scaffolds in drug discovery
articles.abstract: Strained rings offer an escape from flat chemical space, enabling access to three-dimensional bridged heterocycles. This perspective examines two complementary strategies—introducing heteroatoms through reaction partners or embedding them within strained precursors—and links precursor design and activation mode to topology, stereochemistry, and substituent orientation. It highlights how heteroatom identity and placement tune molecular properties and outlines advances in stereocontrol, precursor accessibility, and medicinal-chemistry validation needed to make strain-release synthesis a practical tool for drug discovery.

articles.title: Photoinduced Charge Separation via Symmetry-Breaking
articles.abstract: Photoinduced symmetry-breaking charge separation (SB-CS) is a fundamental process in molecular photophysics that underpins energy and charge transport in reaction centers and organic, supramolecular, and hybrid materials. Despite extensive investigations across diverse systems, SB-CS is often described in system-specific terms, obscuring the underlying unifying principles. In this Review, we establish a coherent framework demonstrating that SB-CS can be understood within a multidimensional parameter space defined by electronic coupling, energetic driving force, and nuclear reorganization. We critically analyze how the interplay between locally excited and charge-transfer states governs charge separation and recombination dynamics, highlighting the existence of an optimal intermediate coupling regime that enables efficient symmetry-breaking while suppressing nonproductive decay pathways. By integrating insights from solution, solid-state, and single-molecule measurements, we show that environmental fluctuations and structural heterogeneity play a central role in driving charge localization rather than merely acting as spectators or perturbations. Importantly, we distinguish universal physical principles from system-specific manifestations, allowing the formulation of transferable design rules for achieving efficient and long-lived charge-separated states. Finally, we outline emerging directions toward predictive, data-driven models that link molecular structure to SB-CS dynamics, providing a foundation for the rational design of next-generation optoelectronic and energy-conversion materials.

articles.title: Ultrafast Nonlinear Vibrational Spectroscopy of Aqueous Solutions at Surfaces and in Heterogeneous Environments
articles.abstract: Water and aqueous electrolytes at surfaces, interfaces, and in confinement behave differently from the bulk, yet linear spectroscopy rarely combines the chemical specificity, surface selectivity, and temporal resolution needed to resolve electric double-layer formation, specific-ion adsorption, and hydration at interfaces and under nanoconfinement. This review assesses how ultrafast nonlinear vibrational spectroscopy, comprising two-dimensional infrared spectroscopy, vibrational sum-frequency generation (SFG), and time-resolved SFG, probes the hydrogen-bond network and the dynamics of interfacial water and electrolytes on femtosecond-to-picosecond timescales. We first establish vibrational benchmarks for bulk water and simple electrolytes, then treat soft aqueous boundaries, including air–water, hydrophobic and hydrophilic, lipid, surfactant, and nucleic acid interfaces. We next examine solid–liquid and electrochemical systems, spanning metal oxides, minerals, and field-induced effects, before turning to water and proton dynamics in nanoconfined geometries and complex architectures. Throughout, experimental results are set against theoretical and computational frameworks, from polarizable force fields to machine-learning potentials. Our aim is to identify which molecular-level features of interfacial water are now firmly established, where the prevailing mean-field description of the electric double layer breaks down, and which experiments would resolve the outstanding discrepancies.

articles.title: Bifunctional Electrocatalysts
Cation Radius Engineering of d10 Metal Hybrid Halides toward Coordination Modulation for Giant Optical Anisotropy
articles.abstract: Birefringent crystals are core materials for polarization modulation in optical devices, yet commercial crystals generally suffer from low birefringence values. In this work, three hybrid halide crystals, (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, and (C5H5NS)HgCl2, were successfully prepared by combining 4-mercaptopyridine unit with d10 metal chlorides to further modulate the metal coordination environments. For (C5H5NS)2ZnCl2 and (C5H5NS)2CdCl2, two π-conjugated units directly coordinate to one metal-centered tetrahedron, which further assembles into a one-dimensional structure via hydrogen-bond interactions. For (C5H5NS)HgCl2, two π-conjugated units coordinate to two metal-centered tetrahedra, forming the isolated (C5H5NS)2Hg2Cl4 dimer, and the complete crystal framework is stacked by intermolecular forces. The birefringence of the three compounds exhibits diversity with the variation of d10 metal ions. Notably, (C5H5NS)2CdCl2 sets records among cadmium-based hybrid halides with metal−halogen−organic functional groups. Structural analyses and theoretical calculations demonstrate that the birefringence of the three crystals is jointly contributed by the organic part and inorganic composition. This study verifies that modifying the coordination environment by tuning the ionic radii of metal center ions is an effective strategy for birefringence modulation and advances the research on hybrid halides for birefringent crystal applications.

articles.title: Dynamic Poly(disulfide) Interphase Enhances Ductility and Toughness of Covalent Adaptable Network Composite without Loss of Stiffness
articles.abstract: Covalent adaptable networks (CANs) offer recyclability and reprocessability, yet bond-exchange dynamics can reduce mechanical strength and toughness. Although the composite formation of CAN provides benefits in both aspectsstrengthening the CAN and adding recyclability to the compositeit still faces a stiffness−ductility trade-off that limits material usefulness. Here, we demonstrate a CAN composite design in which silica nanoparticle incorporation, combined with interfacial chemical structure, enhances ductility and toughness in a highly crosslinked matrix without compromising the high elastic modulus. Introducing poly(disulfide) dynamic covalent bonding chains into the network and at the filler interface significantly increases ductility, toughness, and stress at break. Together with a comparison to composites with permanent interfacial bonding, these results underscore the important role of interfacial chemistry. Based on these comparative experiments, the observed toughness enhancement is proposed to arise from energy dissipation via reorganization at the interphase through stress-activated disulfide exchange and network topological rearrangement. The resulting stress-responsive viscoelasticity enables stable deformation and allows CAN-based composites to overcome the stiffness−ductility trade-off.

articles.title: Heteroanionic Tuning of Cooperative Ta Off-Centering in Quasi-One-Dimensional CsTaS3− x Cl x Semiconductors
articles.abstract: The structural behavior of CsTaS3 was investigated alongside that of the new heteroanionic compound CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, synthesized via the reaction of Ta and S in a CsCl flux. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that both compounds are isostructural, crystallizing in the centrosymmetric hexagonal space group P63/mmc with split Ta positions along the face-sharing octahedral chain direction. Pair distribution function analysis of both compounds, supported by STEM imaging of CsTaS3, identifies the local intrachain displacement motif as cooperative Ta sliding rather than alternating Ta−Ta dimerization. While X-ray absorption near-edge spectroscopy (XANES) confirms the decrease of the average oxidation state in CsTaS2.16Cl0.84, the same structural distortion persists, albeit now with a reduced magnitude. Both materials are semiconducting, and Cl incorporation increases the band gap from ∼1.00 eV in CsTaS3 to ∼1.12 eV in the heteroanionic phase. Single-crystal detectors fabricated from CsTaS2.16Cl0.84 exhibit high resistivity, which effectively suppresses dark current and enhances signal-to-noise performance. These devices deliver an X-ray sensitivity of 7470 μC Gyair−1 cm−2, demonstrating efficient charge generation and collection under irradiation.

articles.title: Interplay of Synthesis, Structure and Thermoelectric Properties in Two Families of Silicide Zintl Phases Grown in Magnesium-Rich Flux
articles.abstract: Large crystals of metal silicide Zintl phases with general formula (Ca/Eu/Mg)2Si were grown from reactions of silicon with varying amounts of europium and calcium in magnesium/zinc flux. The Eu/Ca reactant ratio determined the structure type of the products. Calcium-rich reactions yielded Ca1−xEuxMgSi (0 < x < 0.7) compounds adopting the orthorhombic TiNiSi structure type in space group Pnma. Increasing europium content led to the prevalence of Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (0 < y < 3.4) products with the hexagonal Ho5Ni19P12 structure type in space group P6̅2m. Single crystal X-ray diffraction studies indicate mixing of Zn on one Mg site in the hexagonal structures; thus, the formula can be expressed as Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12. Magnetic susceptibility data indicate europium is divalent in all of the compounds, with low-temperature magnetic ordering transitions. Density of states calculations show a pseudogap at the Fermi level for both structures, indicating semimetallic character; transport measurements indicate p-type behavior. Ca/Eu mixing and higher ratios of Eu2+ suppress lattice thermal conductivity in both structure types. In Ca1−xEuxMgSi, Eu-substitution lowers resistivity but yields minimal Seebeck enhancement; in Eu8−yCayMg16Si12 (Eu8−yCayMg16−αZnαSi12), Ca-substitution increases resistivity and markedly improves the Seebeck coefficient, with Eu7.59Ca0.41Mg15.62Zn0.36Si12 reaching S ≈ 150 μV K−1 at 300 K.

articles.title: Nonclassical Dihydrogen Bond-Directed Assembly of o -Carborane-Based Molecules into Macroscopic Architectures with Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: Hierarchical architectures are ubiquitous in nature; however, the bottom-up construction of multilevel chiral macroscopic assemblies from small organic molecules remains highly challenging. Herein, we report an unprecedented assembly strategy for constructing hierarchically organized particles (HOPs) through the co-assembly of achiral o-carborane-based molecules (C-1 and C-2) with chiral (R/S)-limonene. Intriguingly, C-1-(S)-limonene forms microscale cocoon-like superstructures, whereas C-1-(R)-limonene undergoes self-assembly into fibrous architectures that ultimately evolve into random aggregates at the micrometer scale. In contrast, C-2-(R/S)-limonene assembles into bowtie-shaped microarchitectures. Graph Theory (GT) analysis reveals structural complexity indices (CIs) of 5.5 and 54 for the C-1-(S)-limonene- and C-2-(S)-limonene-based HOPs, respectively, indicating significantly higher architectural complexity for the latter. These assemblies exhibit distinct circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) properties: C-1-(S)-limonene displays intense CPL emission at 504 nm with a high luminescence dissymmetry factor (glum) of +0.006, whereas C-2-(S)-limonene exhibits CPL emission at 560 nm with a glum value of +0.002. These results demonstrate that chirality signals are transferred across multiple length scales from the molecular level to macroscopic architectures. The observed structural divergence originates from the synergistic effects of nonclassical dihydrogen bonding (Bδ+−Hδ−···Hδ+−Cδ−) between achiral o-carborane derivatives and chiral limonene, together with molecular polarity and elasticity effects. This study establishes a paradigm for fabricating chiral o-carborane-based hierarchical aggregates with programmable architectures and tailored chiroptical properties.

articles.title: Progressive Fluorination-Controlled Steric Effects in Low-Dimensional Bismuth Bromides
articles.abstract: Although fluorination introduces tunable lattice rigidity and steric matching that influence molecular dynamics, the use of progressive fluorination as an effective method for structure−property tuning remains limited. Here, we report structural, thermal, dielectric, vibrational, and optical investigations of two members of zero-dimensional (0D) hybrid bismuth bromides with the general formula A3BiBr6, where A denotes 2,2-difluoroethylammonium and 2,2,2-trifluoroethylammonium cations. Differential scanning calorimetry reveals that the difluorinated compound undergoes a first-order phase transition at 184.3/177.5 K (heating/cooling), similar to the monofluorinated analogue, whereas its trifluorinated counterpart exhibits no structural phase transitions within the studied temperature range. A single-crystal X-ray diffraction study shows that the trifluorinated compound adopts trigonal symmetry (space group P3̅). In contrast, the difluorinated analogue crystallizes in the orthorhombic space group Pnnm at room temperature and transforms upon cooling into a monoclinic phase described by the P21/n space group. Temperature-dependent infrared and Raman spectroscopies indicate that the phase transition mechanism is governed by order−disorder processes. The noncovalent interaction calculations support that the F···F intermolecular interactions originate from sterically constrained packing rather than attractive interactions, contributing to dense crystal arrangement. Optical studies reveal that band gap energies correlate with octahedral deformation and level of fluorination. The difluorinated compound exhibits orange luminescence of excitonic origin, which is still observable at room temperature. The presented data demonstrate that degree of fluorination is a versatile design strategy for tuning dipolar degrees of freedom, intermolecular interactions, the strength of organic−inorganic coupling, and optical properties in hybrid halides.

articles.title: Reductive Electrodeposition of Cationic Polymer Networks for Conformal Permselective Interphases
articles.abstract: The integration of ultrathin and conformal interphases onto electrodes can lead to advanced electrochemical systems with control over the near-surface nanoenvironment impacting the double layer, electrode stability, reagent access, and solvation. However, the precise fabrication of nanometric interphases with tailored thickness and composition without blocking active surface sites is challenging, especially on porous application-relevant electrodes. Here, we report the reductive and self-limiting electrodeposition of polymer networks (EPoN) as a versatile and tunable method to uniformly coat non-planar and porous electrodes with physically adhered ultrathin functional polymer networks. The deposition chemistry is based on cathodically mediated methylpyridinium crosslinking and achieves the fabrication of polymer thin films on oxidation-sensitive catalytic metals. Our reductive EPoN process follows a self-limiting growth mechanism, yielding uniform and defect-correcting coatings with tunable nanometric thickness and charge density. The polymer network interphase is permselective, retaining molecular access to the functional surface, but modulates its permeation and activity based on charge and size, as demonstrated with a positively charged nanometric interphase as a functional barrier for regulating the hydrogen evolution reaction on copper. Our reductive EPoN strategy establishes a robust platform to tailor catalytic interphases for precise control over the electrochemical nanoenvironment.

articles.title: Structure-Directing Agents of Chaordic Materials Using High-Entropy Alloying
articles.abstract: For nearly a century, alloy design has been guided by the Hume-Rothery rules, which describe the conditions required for solid solution formation and have traditionally constrained the compositional space available to materials scientists. The emergence of high-entropy alloys fundamentally altered this paradigm by demonstrating that configurational entropy can stabilize compositions that would otherwise be thermodynamically unfavorable. Since their discovery, high-entropy concepts have expanded beyond metallic systems into ceramics, including oxides, carbides, silicides, nitrides, and borides, creating new opportunities to access unconventional chemistries and local atomic environments. This review examines how high-entropy alloying can be used to transcend classical alloying limitations and stabilize elements in coordination environments that are inaccessible in conventional materials. Particular emphasis is placed on high-entropy borides, where ordered boron frameworks provide a structural scaffold that accommodates chemically disparate elements while preserving phase stability. Recent examples, including Pt- and Si-containing high-entropy diborides, demonstrate how entropy stabilization enables the incorporation of elements that do not form stable binary diborides (MB2), resulting in unique electronic structures, bonding environments, and functional properties. More broadly, these systems illustrate how the interplay between disorder and local order can be leveraged to design next-generation materials beyond the boundaries imposed by traditional alloying rules.

articles.title: Symmetry-Broken Co3O4 via Site-Selective Pd Substitution for Bifunctional Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Spinel oxides generally show subpar activity for electrochemical water splitting because of low electronic conductivity, suboptimal adsorption energies, and poor operational stability. To overcome these limitations, Pd2+ is introduced to induce lattice strain in a metastable Co3O4 phase featuring off-centered cobalt and oxygen atoms. While pristine Co3O4 typically crystallizes in the centrosymmetric Fd3̅m space group, 1.2 at % Pd transforms it to the dominant non-centrosymmetric F4̅3m space group. This unconventional lattice contains two non-equivalent tetrahedral sites and one octahedral site. Pd2+ preferentially substitutes the Co1 atom at the (0, 0, 0) 4a tetrahedral position, with a relative stabilization of −1.02 eV. Pd2+-induced enhancement of the density of states near the Fermi level tunes the d-band center, while Co-to-Pd charge redistribution activates the otherwise less active tetrahedral site alongside the intrinsically active octahedral site, thereby enhancing alkaline water electrolysis. For oxygen and hydrogen evolution, this bifunctional catalyst delivers mass activities of 60.6 and 31.0 A/g and turnover frequencies of 0.32 and 0.28 H2 s−1 at 300 and 250 mV overpotentials, respectively. In a two-electrode configuration, it reaches 50 mA/cm2 at an iR-uncorrected cell voltage of 1.85 V, while at 200 mA/cm2, it produces 25.4 mL/h H2 at a cell voltage of 2.31 V.

articles.title: The AtomicLimits Database: Towards Artificial Intelligence as a Research Assistant for Atomic Layer Deposition and Etching
articles.abstract: The AtomicLimits ALD/ALE database is a community resource that catalogues atomic layer deposition (ALD) and atomic layer etching (ALE) processes reported in the literature. While widely used, it currently captures only a small fraction of the available information, with limited process information per entry, and relies on manual curation. As ALD/ALE process development grows in demand and complexity, with many interdependent parameters and increasingly sophisticated chemistries such as for multicomponent films, decades of experimental and simulation knowledge remain locked across publications, supplementary files, and lab notebooks. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML) and large language models (LLMs), offer a path to unlock this knowledge for data-driven analysis and process design, but realizing this potential depends on structured, machine-readable data. In this perspective, we propose a framework to evolve AtomicLimits into an AI-ready knowledge infrastructure that integrates literature-extracted, experimental, and simulation data through a community-defined schema, a structured template that specifies which data fields to capture and how to organize them. We outline the AI capabilities this enables, from structured querying to autonomous experimentation, and discuss the coordinated community effort required to realize this vision for the atomic-scale processing field.

articles.title: Unraveling the Correlation between Crystallite Orientation in Conjugated Polymer Thin Film and Charge Transport Properties
articles.abstract: Despite great progress in tailoring the molecular structures of donor−acceptor (D−A) copolymers, the ability to precisely tailor their solid-state chain packing and establish a comprehensive structure−property relationship remains a grand challenge. Here, three diketopyrrolopyrrole (DPP)-based copolymers adjusting alkyl side chains with various lengths are developed to control their aggregation behavior in different solvents and the corresponding crystallite orientation in thin films, establishing the structure−charge -transport −property relationship and elucidating the underlying mechanism. Specifically, DPPs with longer side chains exhibit weaker solution aggregation, favoring the formation of a face-on orientation in as-cast films, where the face-on to edge-on orientation can be further achieved by strengthening their solution aggregation via changing the solvent from chloroform to chlorobenzene and xylene. Remarkably, by using a floating-film transfer method, the initially face-on crystallites in as-cast DPP films can be transformed into narrower distributed edge-on crystallites, resulting in the charge mobility being nearly tenfold higher than that of the corresponding as-cast sample. This study highlights how molecular engineering and processing strategies collaboratively guide the aggregation and packing of DPPs in the solution and solid state, offering key insights into the structure−processing−property relationship of D−A copolymers for high-performance optoelectronic devices.

articles.title: Unravelling the Role of Stacking Disorder on the Optoelectronic Properties of Zn3P2
articles.abstract: Zinc phosphide (Zn3P2) is a promising photovoltaic absorber for thin-film and flexible solar cells due to its earth-abundant composition and favourable optoelectronic properties. Recent advances in epitaxy have enabled the growth of high-quality Zn3P2 thin films despite the challenges posed by its incompatible lattice parameter and thermal expansion coefficient. However, Zn3P2 remains prone to intrinsic extended defects, such as rotated domains, that can limit device performance. Here, using (scanning) transmission electron microscopy, we identify a class of extended defects that appear as planar faults described by displacement vectors lying in the (001) plane. Within a pseudo-cubic description of Zn3P2, we establish a direct correspondence between planar faults and rotated domains, showing that both arise from the flexible ordering of vacant sites in the Zn sublattice. First-principles calculations reveal an extremely low planar-defect formation energy of 2.5 mJ m−2, demonstrating that these defects form at essentially negligible energetic cost, in excellent agreement with their high experimentally observed occurrence. Additional density functional theory calculations show that the studied intrinsic planar defects neither introduce mid-gap electronic states nor significantly perturb the local electrostatic potential, indicating that they are electronically benign. Our results suggest that any connection between the observed planar defects and a reduction in device performance must therefore involve indirect mechanisms, such as strain effects or interactions with other defects.

articles.title: A Scalable Workflow for Extracting Species Interactions From Ecological Literature Using Large Language Models
articles.abstract: The contemporary ecological crisis calls for integration and synthesis of vast amounts of mostly scattered and often hard‐to‐extract ecological information that is dispersed across hundreds of thousands of scientific papers. Recent advancements in natural language processing (NLP) and the emergence of large language models (LLMs) offer a novel and promising approach to this persistent challenge. Here, we present a replicable and adaptable workflow that automates the extraction of a broad range of biological interactions among species from scientific literature using LLMs. We provide a demonstration of this workflow by performing a large‐scale data extraction directly from a corpus of 83,910 scientific articles using OpenAI GPT‐4o. Our approach successfully extracted a network of 144,402 interactions between 36,471 taxa. Performance analysis shows that the model exhibits a precision of 89.5% with a recall of 70.0%, demonstrating that a general‐purpose LLM can perform complex ecological information extraction at scale for analysis and synthesis. Results depend on quality filtering choices and inherit biases present in the underlying literature, emphasizing the need for validation and quality control. Standardized outputs can be browsed, queried, or joined with existing interaction repositories and taxonomic backbones, facilitating downstream reuse and interoperability. Our case study shows that LLMs are capable of carrying out complex extraction tasks on key ecological data on a very large scale, paving the way for a multitude of potential applications in ecology and beyond.

articles.title: Chloroplast Genome Characterization and Phylogenetic Implications of Reyesia and Salpiglossis (Salpiglossideae, Solanaceae)
articles.abstract: Solanaceae represents one of the most economically significant families among flowering plants. Genomic research within the family has primarily concentrated on some crop genera, such as Solanum L., Nicotiana L., and Capsicum L., whereas early‐diverging clades remain comparatively understudied. This study presents the complete chloroplast (cp) genomes of two species belonging to the tribe Salpiglossideae (subfamily Cestroideae), Reyesia chilensis Clos and Salpiglossis sinuata Ruiz & Pav, and performs comprehensive comparative analyses across representative Solanaceae plastomes, focusing on genome structure, gene content, repeats, codon usage, nucleotide polymorphism (Pi), and phylogenetic relationships. The cp genomes of R. chilensis and S. sinuata have lengths of 156,969 and 156,262 bp, respectively, and both exhibit the characteristic quadripartite structure. Their genome organization and gene composition were highly conserved. The plastome of R. chilensis encoded 112 unique genes (111 in S. sinuata), including 79 protein‐coding genes, 29 transfer RNA‐coding genes (28 in S. sinuata), and four ribosomal RNA‐coding genes. Comparative analyses revealed only minor sequence divergence between the two plastomes, with highly similar codon usage bias and repeat sequence composition. Phylogenetic analyses supported R. chilensis and S. sinuata as a clade representing Salpiglossideae, sister to Benthamiella patagonica Speg. (Benthamielleae), together forming an early‐diverging branch within the Solanaceae. Nucleotide polymorphism analyses revealed a mean nucleotide diversity (Pi) of 0.013 within the shared genes, whereas intergenic spacers exhibited a higher sequence polymorphism (average Pi = 0.028). Several hypervariable segments were identified as promising markers for Solanaceae species delimitation and phylogenetic inference. This work contributes critical genomic datasets and further clarifies the phylogenetic comprehension across the family.

articles.title: Ecosystem Health Assessment of Hulun Lake Using an eDNA Metabarcoding‐Based Phytoplankton Index of Biotic Integrity
articles.abstract: Hulun Lake, one of the largest freshwater lakes in China, is currently experiencing significant water quality deterioration. Therefore, water quality assessment is of paramount importance, as it not only provides critical insights into the current pollution status of lakes but also offers a scientific basis for effective lake management and ecological restoration. Using environmental DNA‐metabarcoding data from 13 sampling sites in Hulun Lake in June 2023, our study explored the spatial variation of α‐diversity, the community composition, and phytoplankton index of biotic integrity (P‐IBI). A total of 431 phytoplankton species were identified across 10 phyla, 191 families, and 335 genera, with Chlorophyta and Bacillariophyta predominating. Biodiversity was higher in the northern and southern regions, except for the site XHK, but lower in the central region. P‐IBI scores exhibited clear spatial variation, with relatively high scores in the central and northern regions, except for the site XHK, indicating comparatively favorable ecological conditions. In contrast, lower P‐IBI scores were observed in the southern region, except for DNHWZ and GZ, suggesting relatively greater ecological degradation. The P‐IBI scores were significantly negatively correlated with Water Quality Index (WQI) values, indicating that higher biotic integrity was generally associated with better physicochemical water quality. RDA and Spearman rank correlation analyses revealed that ammonia nitrogen (NH3–N) and total organic carbon (TOC) were positively correlated with P‐IBI, whereas temperature (T) and total nitrogen (TN) showed negative correlations with P‐IBI, indicating that spatial variation in P‐IBI was closely associated with nutrient status and organic carbon availability. Lake management should integrate both P‐IBI and WQI‐based assessment approaches, providing a scientifically robust basis for the identification of environmental pressures and the diagnosis of ecological health.

articles.title: Experience Improves Spatial Foraging Performance in a Complex Environment in Heliconius Butterflies
articles.abstract: Heliconius butterflies rely on spatial memory to maintain trapline foraging routes, repeatedly visiting pollen resources along memorized paths. Increased foraging performance resulting from learning the spatial distribution of resources is thought to have driven the evolution of this specialized behavior. Here, we experimentally test whether prior experience in a spatially complex environment influences relative foraging performance in the pollen‐feeding butterfly Heliconius erato, a species with well‐documented behavioral, ecological and neuroanatomical specializations for spatial learning. We reared freshly eclosed adults in either an open cage or a cage that was matched for resource distribution but structurally divided to increase the spatial complexity experienced by the butterflies. We then tested them individually in a controlled foraging assay under familiar and unfamiliar environments. Butterflies reared in the spatially complex environment efficiently reached the feeder regardless of familiarity with the environment, whereas butterflies reared in the open environment showed strong context dependence, performing well only in the open cage. These results indicate that prior experience of a spatially complex environment supports greater foraging efficiency in Heliconius butterflies, highlighting environmental structure as a likely determinant of the ecological value of spatial learning in this group, with potential consequences for foraging behavior in natural environments.

articles.title: Lost and Found: Western Honey Bee (Apis mellifera) Matrix Metalloproteinase 1
articles.abstract: The quality of reference genomes is of utmost importance as they and the therein annotated genes and proteins serve as basis for many downstream applications. Although the current Western honey bee (Apis mellifera) genome assembly (Amel_HAv3.1) represents a significant improvement over previous versions (Amel_4.0, Amel_4.5), it nevertheless lacks certain protein‐coding genes present in those earlier assemblies. One of these “lost and found” genes is locus 409868 of Amel_4.0 and Amel_4.5 which is missing due to an approximately 160 kb assembly gap on chromosome 10 in Amel_HAv3.1. Here we show that the A. mellifera genome indeed harbours locus 409868 encoding matrix metalloproteinase 1 (mmp1) and that it is expressed in at least four different mRNA isoforms in honey bee workers. Orthologues from other insect species have essential tissue and organ remodelling functions during development and gene knockdowns at specific developmental time points are lethal. As adult honey bee workers show in addition an elaborate age‐based division of labour with drastic major morphological and physiological changes requiring extensive tissue and organ remodelling, leaving out mmp1 because of a missing gene in the reference genome, may mean leaving out a potential key player in development.

articles.title: Network Indices and Diversity Follow Distinct Patterns for Bee–Plant Networks Along a Neotropical Elevational Gradient
articles.abstract: A critical goal of ecology is to quantify mutualistic network structure across all ecosystems and organisms, as these networks often represent essential ecosystem services and therefore network metrics are often used as conservation targets. Some major gaps still exist, one of which is Neotropical bees, a group expected to contribute exceptional insight to ecological network theory, owing to the extreme diversity of mutualistic interactions characteristic of the Neotropics, as well as the unique global distribution patterns of bees. Elevational gradients are a useful tool for quantifying change in network structure, with results having direct implications for predicting resilience in ecosystem service provisioning. In this study, we compared mutualistic network properties of 28 Neotropical bee–plant networks, along an elevational gradient from 200 to 1500 m elevation. Bee species richness peaked at mid‐elevation while network specialization and modularity decreased with increasing elevation. Connectance and nestedness showed a statistically significant increase by elevation. Combining indicator analysis and the number of bee species collected from only one elevational band, the majority of bee species, 101 of 157 (64%), showed association with specific altitudes, and each elevational band harbored a unique assemblage of bee species, with 95% of beta‐diversity explained by species replacement. The highest elevation band studied represents the top elevation of these short tropical mountains, emphasizing an urgent conservation need for these bee communities throughout the tropical realms as temperatures rise. Our finding of high specialization in lowland mutualistic networks of the tropics suggests that previously documented patterns of higher generalism toward lower latitudes may not have included bee–plant networks from Neotropical lowland and mainland ecosystems; resolving this debate will have important implications for conservation and restoration action.

articles.title: Seasonal Dietary Composition of the Mountain Bongo (Tragelaphus eurycerus ssp. isaaci) at the Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy
articles.abstract: The mountain bongo (Tragelaphus eurycerus ssp. isaaci) represents a rare and critically endangered subspecies endemic to the Afromontane forests of Kenya. This study investigated the seasonal dietary composition of the mountain bongo at the Mount Kenya Wildlife Conservancy and the Mawingu Mountain Bongo Sanctuary. We conducted a two‐year observational study on the reintroduced wild population, employing random focal animal sampling at 30‐min intervals during active feeding periods from 06:00 to 11:00 and 16:00 to 19:00. Following each sampling session, we allocated 10 min to collect plant samples for subsequent identification. The data collected included the plant species consumed, the time spent on each species and the specific plant parts browsed. A total of 80 plant species, representing 43 families, were identified as components of the mountain bongo's diet, encompassing trees, shrubs, herbs, grasses, ferns, creepers, climbers and rhizomes. Seasonal variations exhibited minimal effects on herb or shrub consumption; however, conditions during the wet season were significantly correlated with a reduced likelihood of tree consumption. Seasonal dietary shifts, with reduced tree consumption during the wet season, underscore the importance of conserving a mosaic of vegetation types to ensure year‐round forage availability for mountain bongos.

articles.title: Surplus Killing of Magellanic Penguins Spheniscus magellanicus by Puma Puma concolor) in Islote Lobos National Park, Northern Patagonia
articles.abstract: Surplus killing (SK) by large carnivores may generate high‐intensity mortality events in colonial seabirds. Here, we document repeated predation events involving Magellanic penguins (Spheniscus magellanicus) and pumas (Puma concolor) in Islote Lobos National Park (ILNP, Río Negro, Argentina). During the 2024–2025 breeding season, only four adult penguins with cervical injuries and no signs of consumption were recorded, precluding their interpretation as SK. In contrast, during the 2025–2026 breeding season, multiple high‐intensity mortality events were recorded at La Pastosa and Isla de los Pájaros, two islets harboring reproductive penguin colonies in the ILNP. Across all documented 2025–2026 events, at least 961 penguins were found dead, including 887 adults and 74 chicks. Carcasses exhibited cervical bite injuries and little or no evidence of consumption, while fresh puma tracks, feces, and direct observations of an adult individual within the colonies strongly supported puma predation. During the four consecutive breeding seasons prior to these events, population monitoring did not record mortality episodes of comparable magnitude and suggested stable population dynamics within the ILNP colonies. The mortality recorded during the 2025–2026 breeding season represented a minimum direct mortality of 3.52% of the local breeding adult population. These records represent the northernmost confirmed case of SK involving Magellanic penguins and pumas, extending the documented geographic range of this interaction by more than 1000 km northwards. They also suggest that repeated SK events may represent an important source of additive mortality for local penguin colonies. Our findings highlight the ecological importance of episodic terrestrial–marine trophic interactions and the need for continued demographic monitoring in coastal breeding systems.

articles.title: Correction: Stacked direct-current triboelectric nanogenerators based on volume discharge and in situ superposition for enhanced volume power density
articles.abstract: Correction for ‘Stacked direct-current triboelectric nanogenerators based on volume discharge and in situ superposition for enhanced volume power density’ by Ruijie Tang et al. , Energy Environ. Sci. , 2026, https://doi.org/10.1039/d6ee04690h.

articles.title: Methylcyclohexane-assisted polypropylene upcycling over PtRu/Al 2 O 3 via tandem dehydrogenation–hydrogenolysis
articles.abstract: Polymer–solvent interactions influence polypropylene chain conformation and catalytic performance. Among the solvents tested, methylcyclohexane enhances polypropylene conversion, favouring naphtha-range liquids over gaseous products.

articles.title: Re-thinking gas diffusion electrodes: microporous layer free architectures for robust zero-gap CO 2 electrolysis
articles.abstract: Microporous-layer-free cathodes deliver high-rate, durable CO 2 electrolysis, challenging conventional electrode design principles and simplifying device architecture.

articles.title: Molecular Modulation of Phenyl-Bridged Diphenanthroline Anodes toward Ultralong-Cycling Sodium–Organic Batteries
Simultaneous Bulk Zr4+ Doping and In-Situ Li2ZrO3 Interfacial Coating Enable Robust Single-Crystal LiNi0.88Co0.07Mn0.05O2 Cathodes for High-Voltage Lithium-Ion Batteries
Structural Engineering of Gel Electrolytes for Decoupled Suppression of Side Reactions in Aqueous Zinc Batteries
Medicinal plants in a changing climate: evolutionary genomics for resilience and conservation
articles.abstract: Medicinal plants face growing threats from climate change, habitat fragmentation, selective harvesting, and other human-induced pressures that may diminish genetic diversity and weaken evolutionary resilience. Recent studies in population genomics and landscape genomics indicate that resilience is influenced not just by diversity across a species, but also by how adaptive variation is distributed among populations and its connection to environmental gradients. In medicinal plants, factors such as geographic isolation, precipitation, temperature, salinity, and demographic history have been linked to population differentiation and potential adaptive loci. Genomic methods can thus shift conservation from outlining neutral diversity to pinpointing populations and alleles that may be significant for upcoming climates. Simultaneously, transcriptomic, metabolomic, and epigenetic research shows that genetic adaptation is enhanced by phenotypic plasticity and environmental modulation of stress and specialized metabolism pathways. Nevertheless, direct evidence linking adaptive genomic variation to fitness in wild medicinal plant populations is still scarce, and numerous at-risk taxa are deficient in genomic resources. In this study, we integrate recent findings that connect genetic variability, regional adaptation, molecular stress responses, and conservation strategies for medicinal plants. We emphasize landscape genomics and genomic vulnerability as tangible connections between evolutionary ecology and conservation, stressing the importance of incorporating adaptive variation, epigenetic plasticity, demographic history, ecological interactions, and habitat preservation. Future research should emphasize non-model medicinal species, wider geographic sampling, temporal genomic tracking, and field validation of potential adaptive loci.

articles.title: Higher priming effect induced by stem than leaf and root litter
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Plant litter input can affect soil organic carbon (SOC) decomposition, that is the priming effect. Variation in experimental conditions, litter characteristics and soil properties among individual studies has led to inconsistent reports of priming effects. We aimed to synthesize global patterns and drivers of the litter‐induced priming effect. Using meta‐analysis, we synthesized 621 observations from 118 publications and performed multiple statistical approaches, including mixed‐effects meta‐regressions and variation partitioning analysis. We showed that plant litter input stimulated SOC decomposition by an average of 42% globally, indicating an overall positive priming effect. Compared with leaf and root litter, stem litter, which had lower nitrogen (N) content, induced a greater priming effect, particularly in N‐rich cropland soils. Microbial biomass C also increased by an average of 45% following litter addition, with a greater increase under stem litter than under other litter types, consistent with the microbial N‐mining hypothesis. Experimental conditions, including incubation duration and litter addition rate, were more important in explaining priming induced by leaf and stem litter, whereas litter characteristics and soil properties, such as C:N ratio and pH, were more important in explaining root litter‐induced priming, potentially reflecting the relatively high recalcitrance of root litter. Furthermore, the effects of soil properties on the priming effect depended on litter characteristics, with particularly strong interactions observed for root litter, highlighting that root litter‐induced priming is jointly regulated by litter quality and the soil properties. We emphasize the importance of the specificity of litter type in regulating the priming effect. Future studies should comprehensively investigate litter characteristics and their interactions with experimental conditions and soil properties using long‐term experiments to improve global predictions of SOC decomposition via the priming effect. articles.title: Saline versus alkaline stresses in paddy soils drive divergent microbial nutrient limitations despite shared carbon constraints
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Soil salinization and alkalization often suppress microbial functional activity, triggering negative feedback loops in microbial metabolism, degrading nutrients and agricultural productivity. However, the impacts of saline versus alkaline soils on microbial metabolism remain unclear. We compared reclaimed coastal saline (S 1) and Songnen alkaline (A 1) paddy soils with their corresponding non-saline controls (S 0 and A 0) using models of ecoenzymatic stoichiometry, aggregate fractionation, amplicon sequencing and high-throughput qPCR to quantify microbial carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) limitation and their abiotic and biotic drivers. Our findings revealed that saline and alkaline stresses consistently intensified microbial C limitation by 24.79% and 90.43%, respectively, relative to their corresponding CK soils. However, the two regional soil systems showed divergent nutrient limitation patterns associated with contrasting physicochemical and microbial conditions. Saline soils exhibited acute microbial N limitation (VTN/P limitation = −6.51), which was associated with lower N availability, including 53.29% lower DTN than in alkaline soils, macroaggregate-associated N depletion, and bacterial-associated network reorganization. Microbial functional profiles further indicated greater genetic potential for denitrification and lower genetic potential for dissimilatory nitrate reduction to ammonium, with A 1 soils having 25.12% lower nirK/S abundance and 49.68% higher napA abundance than S 1 soils. In contrast, alkaline soils exhibited stronger microbial P limitation (VTN/P limitation = 9.73), which was associated with reduced P bioavailability, including 56.68% lower AP than in saline soils, greater P sequestration in silt+clay fractions, and fungal-associated network reorganization. This pattern was accompanied by stronger suppression of genes associated with organic P mineralization and inorganic P solubilization, with phnK and gcd + pqqC abundances being 28.27% and 25.19% lower than in S 1 soils, respectively. These results show that divergent microbial nutrient limitations arise from coupled soil physicochemical constraints, microbial community reassembly, network reorganization and functional gene responses, rather than from ion-specific chemistry alone. These results highlight organic matter restoration as a common priority, but indicate divergent N/P fertilization strategies for saline and alkaline soils. These insights provide a fundamental framework for targeted remediation of saline and alkaline soils and facilitate sustainable agricultural practices by integrating both universal and salt-type-specific methodological approaches. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 土壤盐渍化和碱化通常会抑制微生物功能活性，引发微生物代谢的负反馈效应，进而导致土壤养分状况恶化和农业生产力下降。然而，盐胁迫与碱胁迫对土壤微生物代谢的影响及其差异仍不明确。 本研究以滨海盐土(S1)和松嫩平原碱土(A1)改良稻田及其对应的非盐碱对照土壤(S0和A0)为研究对象，综合运用生态酶化学计量学模型、土壤团聚体分级、扩增子测序和高通量荧光定量PCR等方法，定量评估土壤微生物碳(C)、氮(N)和磷(P)限制特征，并解析其非生物和生物驱动因素。 研究结果表明，与各自对照土壤相比，盐胁迫和碱胁迫均显著加剧了微生物碳限制，增幅分别为24.79%和90.43%。然而，由于土壤理化性质和微生物特征存在差异，两类土壤系统表现出截然不同的养分限制模式。滨海盐土表现出强烈的微生物氮限制(VTN/P limitation = −6.51)，这与较低的氮素有效性密切相关，具体表现为溶解性总氮(DTN)含量较碱土降低53.29%、大团聚体中氮素亏缺以及细菌相关网络重组。微生物功能特征进一步表明，盐土中反硝化过程的遗传潜力较高，而硝酸盐异化还原成铵(DNRA)的遗传潜力较低。其中，与S1土壤相比，A1土壤中nirK/S基因丰度降低25.12%，而napA基因丰度增加49.68%。相比之下，碱土表现出更强的微生物磷限制(VTN/P limitation = 9.73)，这与磷生物有效性降低密切相关，具体表现为有效磷(AP)含量较盐土降低56.68%、粉砂和黏粒组分中磷固定增强以及真菌相关网络重组。同时，碱土中参与有机磷矿化和无机磷溶解的功能基因受到更强抑制，其中phnK和gcd + pqqC基因丰度分别较S1土壤降低28.27%和25.19%。这些结果表明，盐土与碱土中不同的微生物养分限制模式并非仅由特定盐离子的化学性质决定，而是土壤理化条件约束、微生物群落重组、网络结构重构及功能基因响应共同作用的结果。 本研究强调，有机质恢复是盐土和碱土改良的共同优先措施，但两类土壤应采取差异化的氮、磷养分管理策略。研究结果为结合共性改良措施与盐分类型特异性调控途径，实现盐土和碱土的精准修复及农业可持续利用提供了重要的理论依据。

articles.title: Five Decades of Citizen Science Reveal Erosion of Hotspots of Multifaceted Plant Diversity
articles.abstract: Biodiversity includes taxonomic, phylogenetic, and functional diversity but the changes in these facets at regional scales remain unclear and often context dependent. Using 2.5 million citizen science observations of 1957 vascular plant species across 53 years in SW‐Germany, we assessed changes in seven biodiversity metrics. Rather than a general decline, we found different facets exhibited different trends in both direction and magnitude of change. Phylogenetic and taxonomic diversity change were mostly negatively correlated, and change in functional diversity was independent from the others. We identified the role of climate and human activity influencing the change in taxonomic and functional diversity, while phylogenetic diversity was also affected by geodiversity. Crucially, we detected consistent erosion of biodiversity hotspots across all facets, while areas with low initial diversity tended to gain species. These findings highlight the need to consider multiple biodiversity facets and local context dependency to better understand biodiversity change at regional scales.

articles.title: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Tools
articles.abstract: To the Editor The Viewpoint article by Drs Singh and Mello provides a balanced discussion of advertising in artificial intelligence (AI)–powered clinical decision support (CDS). It is worth highlighting that the authors state that AI-powered CDS often is free. Did we not say the same about drug company–sponsored lunches and so-called “free” pens and other giveaways in the 1990s? Some will recall when drug companies sponsored lunches for faculty and trainees, gave away pens and other branded items, and sometimes accompanied physicians on rounds. For those who trained more recently, please know that this practice was widely accepted; however, we eventually learned that there is, in fact, no free lunch. Now, we must learn there is no free CDS. Singh and Mello note that while “some products operate on a subscription model, others such as OpenEvidence use advertising revenue to offer access without charge.” It is surprising and disappointing that clinicians may think they are receiving CDS for free. Perhaps they have forgotten—or may have never learned—that drug company advertisements influence prescribing behavior when they appear alongside information intended to educate physicians and support clinical practice. Clearly the drug companies themselves have not forgotten. Twenty years ago, the International Federation of Pharmaceutical Manufacturers and Associations revised its code of ethics and barred gifts or money that could influence prescribing behavior. CDS companies that embed pharmaceutical advertisements in their products should end this practice and, if they do not, the pharmaceutical industry should do so. Better yet, clinicians should recognize they have other options without industry advertisements and should choose such CDS tools.

articles.title: AI-Powered Clinical Decision Support Tools—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We appreciate the thoughtful letters in response to our Viewpoint. We agree with Dr Ziegelstein that the simplest solution to the ethical quandaries of advertising in AI-powered CDS tools would be for the AI-powered CDS companies that use advertisements and/or the pharmaceutical companies that partner with them to end this practice altogether. However, this is unlikely to happen, given that advertising is a potentially more lucrative revenue source than other options such as subscriptions. Ziegelstein’s suggestion that clinicians recognize they have other options and choose CDS tools that do not embed advertisements seems more realistic, particularly if their organizational employers nudge them in this direction. Historically, once Epocrates (a free drug information app) began supporting ads at the point of care, its credibility with its physician users eroded and other services such as UpToDate ultimately won out.

articles.title: Blood Pressure Targets in Critically Ill Children
articles.abstract: “Do I need to treat this blood pressure?” is one of the most common questions to pass through the minds of acute care pediatricians during a typical day in the hospital. Blood pressure generally increases with somatic growth, reflecting developmental changes in stroke volume, vascular structure and function, and neurohumoral regulation. As a result of interindividual variation across the developmental stages of childhood, there is a wide range of acceptable blood pressure values. There is also long-standing ambiguity about what should be considered the limits of acceptable blood pressure, particularly among hospitalized children. Age-based reference values offer a starting point, although the threshold used to identify an unusually low blood pressure may differ from the pressure needed to maintain adequate organ perfusion. This uncertainty can create substantial tension when a clinician faces the decision whether to manage potentially low blood pressure in a child. Treatments for potentially low blood pressure can also vary widely, from temporary stimulation to administration of vasopressor and inotropic medications through a central vascular catheter. The clinical question of whether to manage low blood pressure is driven by concern that withholding treatment could cause harm that is hard to measure.

articles.title: Cost-Effectiveness of Fecal Immunochemical Testing—Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank Dr Huynh and colleagues for their thoughtful comments on our economic evaluation of HPSA-FIT co-testing. Rather than modeling a program developed de novo, we evaluated the incremental value of integrating HPSA testing into an established colorectal cancer screening program. Accordingly, infrastructure development costs were not included in our analysis; however, this should not be interpreted as suggesting implementation requires only minimal investment. Health system readiness varies considerably across countries, but we regard such heterogeneity as support for a staged implementation strategy rather than a limitation: countries with established FIT programs can readily add HPSA testing to existing stool-based testing pathways, whereas those with less mature systems may need to strengthen registries, laboratory networks, referral pathways, and treatment capacity.

articles.title: Fixed Pupils: Neurologic Finality vs Poetic Repair
articles.abstract: In “Holding Hope,” the poem’s crux is not simply the devastating neurologic sign of “fixed pupils,” but also the way this medical phrase is transformed in the ear of the shocked sibling of a mortally wounded patient into the impossible mercy of healing: “[t]hey fixed his pupils.” The clinical distancing inherent in a bedside case presentation, reflexively performed before a disbelieving family member, is translated by a kind of poetic mishearing from incomprehensible loss into hopeful repair. The patient’s sibling seems to only grasp fragments of reality, while the physicians only offer partial truths. Even the clinician-speaker of the poem struggles with what can be held medically vs emotionally, the gasping lines and broken-up stanzas structurally reflecting the patient’s wounded brain and body and the heartbreak of both family member and physician. Yet poetry here does not really restore hope like some kind of harmless magic bullet, nor does it heal the lethal real-world gunshot wounds; more painfully, perhaps, it tries to reconcile brutal finality with the disconsolate wish it were not so. Thus the poem ultimately becomes an “antipresentation” of sorts, in which medical facts are melded with human truths, words can have double meanings, and what can be held is both the obligatory, dire prognosis and its denial. The insistence on what poetry can hear, and what no case presentation could ever convey, is reiterated in the poem’s final lines, expressed in the importunate paradox of the patient’s sibling’s repeated words: “…you heard/‘They fixed his pupils.’”

articles.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence
articles.abstract: To the Editor A recent Perspective proposed a federal licensure framework for autonomous clinical artificial intelligence (AI) modeled on physician credentialing. We disagree with the analogy. Medical licensure regulates a professional actor with fiduciary duties, moral agency, personal accountability, and the ability to refuse unsafe action. A software product has none of these. It is deployed by identifiable commercial and institutional actors. Granting it professional standing does not create accountability; it obscures it.

articles.title: Licensure Framework for Autonomous Clinical Artificial Intelligence—In Reply
articles.abstract: In Reply We thank the correspondents for their Letters to the Editor, which converge on 1 concern—that autonomous clinical AI is not a person—and we agree. Our proposal never attributes moral agency to software, and licensure does not require it. Drs Ferguson and Telemi and Dr Jiang argue that a product cannot be a practitioner. But we do not license software as a moral actor; we authorize a defined clinical function and attach accountability to identifiable human parties. Developers bear primary responsibility and deploying institutions secondary responsibility precisely because the model cannot. Licensure here is a mechanism for ongoing, outcome-based authorization, not a claim of personhood.

Silicon shifts plant stoichiometry: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Si could regulate plant C and P stoichiometry with potential ecological implications. By mobilising P and improving NUE, Si may help mitigate nutrient constraints on biomass production and shape plant performance. Furthermore, reduced plant C:P ratios translate into P‐rich and high‐quality litter, which may in turn alter litter decomposition and soil nutrient cycling. Abstract Silicon (Si) is increasingly linked to shifts in plant carbon (C), nitrogen (N) and phosphorus (P) stoichiometry. However, reported responses vary widely across records. A quantitative synthesis is therefore needed to understand the overall direction and magnitude of these responses. We conducted a meta‐analysis of 168 records to quantify responses of plant C, N and P stoichiometry and nutrient use efficiency (NUE) to Si addition. Overall, Si addition reduced C concentration by 2.3% and C:P by 5% and increased P concentration by 8% and NUE by 14%. Plant N concentrations and C:N ratios showed no significant response. Reductions in C and C:P and increases in NUE were stronger in Poaceae, whereas the P increase was larger in non‐Poaceae. The Si‐C relationship was nonlinear and differed between families, and the P increase occurred only in substrate‐grown plants, not in hydroponics. This suggests no single mechanism accounted for the stoichiometric responses across plant families. Synthesis. Si could regulate plant C and P stoichiometry with potential ecological implications. By mobilising P and improving NUE, Si may help mitigate nutrient constraints on biomass production and shape plant performance. Furthermore, reduced plant C:P ratios translate into P‐rich and high‐quality litter, which may in turn alter litter decomposition and soil nutrient cycling.

articles.title: The Genomic Complexity of Invasion: Cryptic Lineages, Founder Effects and Sex Determination in Armoured Catfish
articles.abstract: Genetic biocontrol approaches offer promising tools for managing invasive species. However, their success depends on species identity, demographic history and the genomic architecture of sex determination, which remain poorly resolved for many non‐model taxa. We integrated high‐quality genome assembly, whole‐genome resequencing and population genomics to evaluate biocontrol feasibility in invasive suckermouth armoured catfish (Loricariidae) in Texas. Mitochondrial phylogenies and genome‐wide SNPs revealed cryptic diversity, with distinct lineages from at least two genera (Hypostomus and Pterygoplichthys) exhibiting strong drainage‐level genetic differentiation. Effective population size estimates were exceptionally low, consistent with founder effects and moderate inbreeding. Genome‐wide association analyses detected no large‐effect loci for sex in either genus, despite high statistical power in Hypostomus, suggesting that sex determination is polygenic and/or environmentally influenced. These results identify key biological constraints for sex‐ratio‐based biocontrol and underscore the importance of genomic assessments prior to management interventions. More broadly, our study highlights how integrating genomic resources, demographic inference and evolutionary context can guide invasive species control strategies.
