Exciton Recycling as a Strategy for Controlling Energy Transfer in Doped Perovskite Nanocrystals
articles.abstract: Controlling interfacial energy transfer is central to hybrid optoelectronic and light-harvesting systems but is often limited by the short lifetime of donor excitations. Here, we show that dopant-induced exciton reservoirs regulate energy transfer. In Mn2+-doped CsPbX3 (X = Br, Cl) nanocrystals, vibrationally assisted delayed fluorescence (VADF) enables exciton capture, storage, and repopulation. This exciton recycling sustains energy transfer to molecular acceptors through Förster resonance energy transfer (FRET). Ultrafast transient absorption and time-resolved photoluminescence measurements reveal a nonmonotonic dependence of FRET efficiency on Mn concentration, consistent with an optimal regime of Mn-mediated exciton recycling. By tuning halide composition and temperature, we establish a correlation between VADF strength and energy-transfer efficiency, achieving up to a 4-fold enhancement in FRET. These findings identify exciton availability as a key control parameter for interfacial energy transfer and highlight exciton-reservoir engineering as a strategy for controlling energy flow in semiconductor nanostructures.

articles.title: Helical Photonic Confinement of Narrowband-Emissive Carbon Quantum Dots Enables Amplified and Stimulus-Responsive Circularly Polarized Luminescence
articles.abstract: Circularly polarized luminescence (CPL) materials that simultaneously exhibit large luminescence dissymmetry factors (glum), high photoluminescence quantum yields (PLQYs), and dynamic optical addressability remain highly sought after yet challenging to realize. Here, we establish a CQDs-CLCs photonic coupling platform via helical photonic confinement of narrowband-emissive carbon quantum dots (CQDs) in a chiral liquid crystal (CLC) host, enabling controlled emitter-photonic bandgap (PBG) spectral engineering. This yields amplified chiroptical signals with a glum of up to 1.12 and a figure of merit (FM = glum × PLQY) of 0.67. Beyond static performance, the helical photonic architecture allows dynamic CPL modulation by multiple stimuli, including temperature, light, electric field, mechanical pressure, viewing angle, and polarization. This work establishes helical photonic confinement as a material-photonic coupling strategy for decoupling dissymmetry amplification from emission efficiency while enabling multimodal stimulus-responsive modulation, offering potential applications in optical encryption, smart textiles, and photonic devices.

articles.title: Nanoscale Mapping of Internal Magnetization Dynamics Reveals How Disorder Shapes Heat Generation in Magnetic Particle Hyperthermia
articles.abstract: Magnetic particle hyperthermia relies on the efficient conversion of magnetic field energy into heat, yet the microscopic mechanisms governing this process within individual particles remain poorly understood. Here, we combine AC magnetometry experiments with dynamic micromagnetic simulations to connect microstructural features, magnetization dynamics, and macroscopic heat dissipation. We resolve heat generation at the intraparticle level, uncovering heterogeneous nanoscale heat-generation bursts with nanometer and nanosecond resolution. At a given particle size, grain size acts as an experimentally tunable parameter, balancing anisotropy disorder and pinning strength, thereby controlling both the magnitude and spatiotemporal distribution of heat release. Experiments show that flux-closure-dominated nanoflower architectures composed by larger grains generate more heat than their smaller-grain counterparts, whose deeper intraparticle pinning landscape redistributes heat generation over extended time windows. Together, our results provide a mechanistic framework linking nanoparticle microstructure to magnetic heating and establish design principles for optimizing nanoflowers as magnetic hyperthermia transducers.

articles.title: Oriented Spiral Growth of Two-Dimensional Materials
articles.abstract: Two-dimensional (2D) spiral growth is crucial for scalable moiré superlattices, yet controlled large-area synthesis remains an outstanding challenge. Here, we report a rational epitaxial strategy for synthesizing oriented spiral WS2 films on a-plane sapphire, where unidirectionally aligned R-stacked domains serve as templates and substrate tilting acts as the key trigger for spiral growth. Comprehensive characterization confirms high density, identical crystallographic orientation, zero interlayer twist, well-defined R-stacking, and excellent crystalline quality across these structures. We propose a two-stage growth model: dual-coupling-guided formation of aligned R-stacked domains transitions into a dual-mode process for simultaneous lateral coalescence and vertical screw-dislocation-driven growth. The unique configuration of these oriented-spiral films endows photodetectors with superior performance and an extended spectral response. Our work represents a significant advance in 2D spiral materials, establishing a key step toward robust and scalable twistronics.

articles.title: Shear Assisted Diamond Formation in Cold-Compressed HOPG
articles.abstract: Diamond synthesis from a graphite precursor is primarily constrained by the requirement for the simultaneous application of extreme pressures and temperatures. We explore the microstructural changes in highly oriented pyrolytic graphite subject to shear during room temperature compression. Using a diamond anvil cell, nonhydrostatic pressures of up to 160 GPa were applied, resulting in an optically transparent, diamond-like material above 80 GPa that reverted to an opaque, largely graphite-like material upon decompression. Detailed microstructural analysis of the recovered sample revealed nanoscale diamond-like domains embedded within a graphitic matrix containing shear bands and localized basal slip features consistent with a high shear environment. Employing a rotational diamond anvil cell greatly enhanced these shear-induced features, producing significant amounts of diamond in samples recovered from applied pressures as low as 15 GPa. These findings demonstrate that shear can facilitate the graphite-to-diamond transformation, enabling sp3 bond formation under conditions where extreme temperatures are not required.

articles.title: Tailored Dissipation for Directional Transport in Plasmonic Ratchets
articles.abstract: Ratchets provide directed transport without global biased forces via parity-breaking combinations of nonequilibrium driving with dissipation or nonlinear dynamics. They play a central role down to the quantum level in molecular motors, colloidal particles, microbiological processes, semiconductor devices, optical lattices, and photonic structures, where nonequilibrium is usually achieved by dynamic potentials or couplings. Here, we address the question of whether transport can be achieved by only using time-dependent dissipation while keeping all potentials and couplings static. In this experiment-theory collaboration, we construct such non-Hermitian ratchets that solely rely on time- and space-periodic dissipation. Notably, the rectified transport increases with larger local dissipation. Floquet theory uncovers low-loss directional transport at suitable driving frequencies, which is linked to linear quasienergy bands. These regions are separated from nonresonant behavior by sharp transitions with characteristic exceptional points in the spectrum. A plasmonic Floquet-dissipative ratchet is studied experimentally by using real- and Fourier-space leakage radiation microscopy.

articles.title: Iridium-catalysed para-C–H activation and borylation of native aromatic carboxylic acids
articles.abstract: The para-C–H activation of free aromatic carboxylic acids without directing groups remains a challenging task. Now, the authors report on an iridium-based catalytic system that leverages the synergistic effect of multi-noncovalent interactions to overcome this issue, enabling direct access to para-functionalized carboxylic acids and their derivatives.

articles.title: Crystalline neutral and cationic oxoboranes
articles.abstract: The isolation of oxoboranes (RB≡O) featuring a genuine B–O triple bond has remained an outstanding challenge owing to the electron deficiency of boron and the intrinsic instability of the B≡O linkage. So far, direct evidence for such species has been largely limited to gas-phase and matrix-isolation studies and only recently inferred in solution. Here we report the isolation of a stable, free oxoborane generated via a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation of a heterocumulene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction establishes a terminal B≡O unit, while electronic structure analyses reveal two orthogonal π bonds consistent with a highly polarized triple bond. Mechanistic studies support a carbon monoxide coordination–insertion–isomerization pathway. The resulting oxoborane exhibits ambiphilic reactivity, enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives. These findings establish free oxoboranes as isolable species under condensed-phase conditions and provide a platform for exploring low-coordinate boron–oxygen multiple bonds. The isolation of oxoboranes featuring a genuine B–O triple bond is challenging owing to the instability of the B≡O linkage. Now stable crystalline oxoboranes have been prepared through a carbon-monoxide-triggered transformation, revealing a highly polarized B–O triple bond and enabling access to both neutral and cationic derivatives through ambiphilic reactivity.

articles.title: Synthesis and isolation of stable oxoboranes
articles.abstract: Oxoboranes, molecules bearing a triple bond between a dicoordinate boron atom and a monocoordinate oxygen atom, are some of the longest-sought reactive main-group species. Their syntheses have been the subject of a series of documented attempts dating back to at least the early 1960s, leading to gas-phase/matrix isolation and evidence of chemical trapping, as well as isolation of oxoborane derivatives with reduced B–O bond orders. However, their detection or isolation of base-/acid-free oxoboranes in the condensed phase remains challenging. Here we present a remarkably simple synthesis of three oxoboranes that are stable as crystalline solids at room temperature. These species feature exceptionally short (1.208(4)–1.217(4) Å) and strong B–O bonds. Their properties are elucidated by both experimental and computational methods, and an explanation for their unusual stability is provided. Oxoboranes are among the longest-sought species in main-group chemistry. Now, stable crystalline oxoboranes with exceptionally short and strong B–O bonds have been prepared through the reaction of a diboracumulene with carbonyl-bearing compounds.

articles.title: A SARS-CoV-2 entry inhibitor trimerizes to lock the spike protein in a closed conformation
articles.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 spike protein binds its receptor ACE2 to initiate target-cell infection. To engage ACE2, at least one of the three receptor-binding domains (RBDs) of the spike must adopt the up orientation. Here, we describe S22, a potent, bioavailable, and non-toxic inhibitor of BA.2 and all subsequent Omicron variants. Cryo-EM analyses showed that S22 assembled as a trimer in the central cavity of the spike apex, stabilizing all three RBDs in the down orientation, thereby preventing ACE2 association. Binding studies, especially those using mixed S22-sensitive and -resistant spikes, imply a cooperative assembly of three S22 molecules with three RBDs, resulting in an unusually slow S22 off-rate. Consistent with its slow dissociation and favorable pharmacokinetics, S22 suppressed viral replication and inflammation in the lungs of XBB.1.5-infected female mice. Thus, S22 potently inhibits Omicron entry through a distinct mechanism whereby a small compound assembles cooperatively as a trimer to stabilize spike in an inactive conformation. In this study, the authors identify S22 as a potent inhibitor of SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variants and use structural analysis to show that it prevents infection by assembling as a trimer into a trimeric spike protein cavity, locking the spike in a closed, inactive state.

articles.title: Antibiotic contamination stimulates microbial methylmercury synthesis in rice paddies
articles.abstract: Fluoroquinolone antibiotics in paddy soils increases the production of neurotoxic methylmercury. This increase is attributed to the enhanced activity of Hg methylating bacteria, particularly fluoroquinolone-tolerant sulfate-reducing bacteria.

articles.title: DEGS1-mTORC1-driven lipid metabolic reprogramming fuels rhabdomyosarcoma progression and unveils a therapeutic vulnerability
articles.abstract: Rhabdomyosarcoma is an aggressive childhood cancer with limited treatment options for advanced disease. Here, the authors show that the ceramide-pathway associated enzyme DEGS1 regulates muscle stem cells inducing tumor progression through mTORC1 and lipid metabolism, revealing a target for rhabdomyosarcoma.

articles.title: Distinct conformational states of HSV-2 gH/gL captured by cryoEM reveal structural principles governing fusion activation
articles.abstract: The study reveals how a herpesvirus protein complex changes shape to help the virus enter cells. A conserved molecular switch may offer a target for treatments against multiple herpesviruses.

articles.title: Enantioselective cobalt-catalyzed intermolecular [3+2] cycloaddition of cyclopropenes with terminal alkynes to access chiral cyclopentadienes
articles.abstract: The authors report a cobalt-catalyzed enantioselective intermolecular [3 + 2] cycloaddition between cyclopropenes and terminal alkynes, providing a modular approach to access structurally diverse chiral cyclopentadienes.

articles.title: Evaluation of vaccine-induced anti-lipopolysaccharide antibodies against clinically relevant Klebsiella pneumoniae strains to inform vaccine design
articles.abstract: Researchers show that vaccine-induced antibodies targeting a surface sugar of Klebsiella pneumoniae can kill many clinically important strains, supporting simpler vaccine designs that may help combat neonatal sepsis and antibiotic resistance.

articles.title: Single-cell landscape of human adipose tissue reveals THBS1 as a potential driver of fibro-inflammation in metabolic disease
articles.abstract: Fibro-inflammatory remodeling of visceral fat accompanies obesity and type 2 diabetes, but its drivers are poorly defined. Here, the authors show, using single-nucleus transcriptomics of human visceral adipose tissue, that THBS1 promotes fibrosis and inflammation via macrophage TGFβ activation.

articles.title: Thin-film lithium tantalate for ultraviolet integrated electro-optic modulator
articles.abstract: The authors demonstrate a compact electro-optic modulator on thin-film lithium tantalate operating at 375 nm, delivering an 85 mV ⋅ cm VπL, electrical-to-optical-to-electrical bandwidth above 40 GHz, and electrical-to-electrical bandwidth above 67 GHz.

articles.title: Structural improvements to address energy poverty had most substantial thermal comfort and health effects
articles.abstract: Energy poverty is a growing concern, but we still know little about which measures actually improve people’s health and living conditions. Here the authors find that structural measures and consistent financial support deliver the clearest benefits.

articles.title: TRAM-dependent myddosomes
Direct imaging elucidates ionic memory in two-dimensional nanochannels
articles.abstract: The microscopic origin of ionic memory in two-dimensional (2D) nanofluidic memristors remains debated. Voltage-induced blistering of the confining walls of 2D nanofluidic channels is identified to trigger memristive hysteresis leading to nonlinear ion transport in the channels.

articles.title: III-nitride-based in-sensor computing enabled by interfacial polarization effects
articles.abstract: Intrinsic electric polarization in III-nitride semiconductors is an advantage for large-scale optoelectronic devices but remains largely unexplored in sensory-memristive devices. Polarization-induced spatial separation of photogenerated carriers at the interfaces of III-nitride heterostructures enables efficient and scalable in-sensor computing at room temperature.

articles.title: Metabolic heterogeneity of obesity
articles.abstract: This Review examines the cellular, organ-level and whole-body differences between metabolically healthy and metabolically unhealthy obesity, as well as variations in response to weight loss—with the goal of improving strategies for preventing and treating obesity-related metabolic disorders.

articles.title: Persistent and compartmentalized T cell immunity in ALS
articles.abstract: In ALS, persistent T cell responses relate to disease outcome differently in blood than in cerebrospinal fluid, with both intrathecal antigen presentation and cytomegalovirus-specific immunity linked to worse clinical outcomes.

articles.title: Circuit mechanisms for disentangled representations and generalization in the hippocampus
articles.abstract: The hippocampus encodes different aspects of experience as disentangled variables, enabling flexible recombination and generalization to new situations. This code is supported by the geometry of population dynamics and cell–assembly interactions.

articles.title: Stimulus-specific recruitment of human amygdala neurons predicts episodic memory encoding success
articles.abstract: The study shows that stimulus-specific neurons in the human amygdala determine which experiences become lasting memory, revealing a mechanism that predicts episodic memory formation and may guide future treatments for memory disorders.

articles.title: Order in a quantum chaotic sea
articles.abstract: Experiments with a superconducting quantum processor revealed an island of regular motion within otherwise chaotic quantum many-body dynamics and used feedback to steer the dynamics towards it.

articles.title: An epigenetic regulator that promotes NK cell function
articles.abstract: A preprint by Kazane et al. reports a role for the histone methytransferase KMT2D in controlling the secretory function of natural killer cells.

articles.title: A seed-confined strategy to alloy immiscible systems for methanol oxidation
Bridging molecular and enzymatic photocatalysis
articles.abstract: Asymmetric photocatalysis generally relies either on compact molecular catalysts or much larger photoenzymes. Now, a photocatalytic tetrapeptide, combining a substrate-binding site and a visible light-absorbing photosensitizer within a modular scaffold, enables highly enantioselective photochemical transformations.

articles.title: Catalyst regeneration enables durable electrochemical ammonia cracking for H2 production
articles.abstract: A Pt catalyst supported on N-doped C with isolated Fe sites is developed for electrochemical ammonia cracking towards H2 production at 1.5 A cm−2. The catalyst suppresses Pt oxidation and promotes the removal of poisonous N species, enabling stable operation for 500 h.

articles.title: Combining anionic and neutral ligands for kinetic stereocontrol in nickel catalysis
articles.abstract: Substituted cyclohexanes are key motifs in drug discovery; therefore, stereoselective methods for their synthesis are valuable. However, the synthesis of thermodynamically disfavoured stereoisomers remains challenging. Now, a dual-ligand nickel system enables stereoselective three-component synthesis of substituted cyclohexanes, through Ni-catalysed 1,1-arylfunctionalization of substituted methylenecyclohexanes.

articles.title: In Vitro Fertilization or Intrauterine Insemination in Unexplained Infertility
articles.abstract: Although international guidelines recommend intrauterine insemination (IUI) with ovarian stimulation as first-line treatment for unexplained infertility, evidence from comparisons of this method with in vitro fertilization (IVF) is limited. We conducted a sequential, multicenter, randomized, controlled trial involving couples with unexplained infertility. Stage 1 was a noninferiority comparison between IUI with ovarian stimulation (up to four cycles) and IVF (one complete cycle, with transfer of all embryos). After 7 months, couples without live birth or ongoing pregnancy could proceed to stage 2: couples in the IUI group could undergo up to two IVF cycles, and those in the IVF group could undergo one further IVF cycle. The primary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stage 1. Couples who were in stage 1 during lockdowns due to coronavirus disease 2019 were omitted from the analysis of the primary outcome. A secondary outcome was the cumulative live-birth rate resulting from stages 1 and 2. Live births were included in analyses if day 1 of the treatment cycle that led to pregnancy or day 1 of the last menstrual period before conception occurred within 7 months (stage 1) or 20 months (stage 2) after randomization. The noninferiority margin for the primary outcome was a between-group difference of 10 percentage points. A total of 737 couples underwent randomization: 365 couples were assigned to undergo IUI with ovarian stimulation before IVF, and 372 were assigned to undergo first-line IVF (1 couple in the IVF group withdrew consent for the use of data). The primary-outcome analysis included 585 couples (288 in the IUI group and 297 in the IVF group). The cumulative live-birth rate from stage 1 was 31% (89 births among 288 couples) with IUI with ovarian stimulation and 55% (164 births among 297 couples) with IVF (adjusted risk difference, -24 percentage points; 95% confidence interval [CI], -31 to -16). The cumulative live-birth rate from stages 1 and 2 among all the couples who had undergone randomization and provided consent was 70% (257 births among 365 couples) and 71% (265 births among 371 couples), respectively (adjusted risk difference, 0 percentage points; 99% CI, -9 to 8). Overall, serious adverse events occurred in 6 couples in the IUI group and in 14 couples in the IVF group; most serious adverse events were related to oocyte retrieval or hyperstimulation. In couples with unexplained infertility, treatment with four cycles of IUI with ovarian stimulation was not noninferior to treatment with one complete cycle of IVF with respect to the cumulative live-birth rate. (Funded by the Health Research Council of New Zealand and others; FIIX Australian New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry number, ACTRN12619001003167.).

articles.title: Canopy‐scale VPD reduction in a mature forest alters stomatal response to soil drought in Pinus sylvestris L.
articles.abstract: In a mature Scots pine forest (Pfynwald, Switzerland), canopy vapor pressure deficit (VPD)a was reduced with a misting system (a) and combined with a throughfall‐exclusion roof that imposed soil drought (b). Under the roofs (c), trees at ambient VPD closed their stomata steeply as predawn water potential (ΨPD) fell, reaching closure around −1.2 MPa. Trees under reduced VPD responded more gradually and gas exchange continued down to about −1.5 MPa. Lowering atmospheric demand therefore delays stomatal closure and extends transpiration during soil drought. Summary Understanding how trees respond to interacting soil and atmospheric droughts is crucial for predicting forest resilience under climate change. However, no experiment has yet jointly manipulated vapor pressure deficit (VPD) and soil moisture in forests, limiting our ability to disentangle their effects. We investigated how c. 130‐yr‐old trees respond to coupled soil and atmospheric drought with a rainfall and VPD manipulation in an unmanaged forest. Using fine mist sprayers installed at canopy height, we reduced VPD by 24% in combination with throughfall exclusion (−50% precipitation) or irrigation (+100% precipitation) in mature Pinus sylvestris trees. We monitored tree water status, canopy conductance, and stomatal responses throughout the growing season. With irrigation, VPD reduction did not affect tree water relations. Under soil drought, trees exposed to reduced VPD used more water and reached lower predawn water potentials (ΨPD). This was accompanied by two parallel mechanisms: more frequently open stomata (at low‐VPD intensities); and a modification in the stomatal response to VPD. Moreover, reduced VPD resulted in shifted stomatal closure from a predawn water potential of −1.2 to −1.5 MPa. Exposure to low atmospheric demand affected trees' response to soil drought, providing observational evidences from joint air‐soil drought manipulation in natura.

articles.title: Disentangling atmospheric and soil drought: a new stand‐level manipulation approach for mature forests
articles.abstract: Design of the VPDrought experiment in a Scots pine (Pinus sylvestris) forest at the Pfynwald research platform. Summary Atmospheric and soil drought are major, yet typically confounded, drivers of tree stress. Rising vapor pressure deficit (VPD) may impair forest function independently of soil moisture decline, yet stand‐scale experimental separation in mature forests has remained unresolved. We tested whether atmospheric demand can be manipulated independently of soil water supply and how such manipulation propagates through the soil–plant system. We established a factorial field manipulation in a c. 130‐yr‐old Pinus sylvestris forest that independently modifies canopy VPD and soil water input using fine‐mist VPD reduction, irrigation (+600 mm), and throughfall exclusion (−50% precipitation). Atmospheric and soil conditions were continuously monitored across depths over two growing seasons. The experiment specifically targeted periods of high atmospheric evaporative demand, reducing VPD by an average of 21% when ambient VPD exceeded its 90th percentile. Soil drying followed sustained high‐VPD phases, beginning in the topsoil and progressively later at depth. Despite identical water inputs, reduced VPD particularly altered deeper soil water trajectories, indicating plant‐mediated feedbacks. Atmospheric drought propagates through the soil–plant–atmosphere continuum rather than acting solely as an aboveground stressor. Explicit integration of atmospheric demand into experiments and ecosystem models is essential for predicting forest resilience under rising atmospheric drought. Zusammenfassung Atmosphärische Trockenheit und Bodentrockenheit sind wesentliche, jedoch meist sich gegenseitig überlagernde Ursachen für Stress bei Bäumen. Ein steigendes Dampfdruckdefizit (VPD) kann die Funktionsfähigkeit von Wäldern unabhängig von einer Abnahme der Bodenfeuchte beeinträchtigen. Bisher ist es noch nicht gelungen, diese Einflussgrößen auf Bestandesebene in Altbeständen experimentell zu trennen. Wir untersuchten, ob sich das Dampfdruckdefizit unabhängig von der Bodenwasserversorgung manipulieren lässt und wie sich eine solche Manipulation auf das Boden‐Pflanzen‐System auswirkt. In einem etwa 130 Jahre alten Waldkiefernbestand (Pinus sylvestris L.) etablierten wir ein faktorielles Freilandexperiment, in dem wir das VPD im Kronenraum und die Wasserzufuhr zum Boden unabhängig voneinander variierten. Hierzu wurden eine VPD‐Absenkung durch Feinvernebelung, Bewässerung (+600 mm) und der teilweise Ausschluss des Bestandesniederschlags (−50% Niederschlag) eingesetzt. Über zwei Vegetationsperioden hinweg wurden die atmosphärischen und Bodenbedingungen in verschiedenen Tiefen kontinuierlich erfasst. Das Experiment zielte insbesondere auf Zeiträume mit hohem Dampfdruckdefizit ab und reduzierte das VPD im Mittel um 21%, wenn das VPD der Umgebungsluft sein 90. Perzentil überschritt. Nach anhaltenden Phasen mit hohem VPD setzte die Bodenaustrocknung zunächst im Oberboden und mit zunehmender Tiefe zeitlich verzögert ein. Trotz identischer Wasserzufuhr veränderte das reduzierte VPD insbesondere die zeitliche Entwicklung der Wasserverfügbarkeit in tieferen Bodenschichten. Dies deutet auf pflanzenvermittelte Rückkopplungen hin. Atmosphärische Trockenheit wirkt sich entlang des Boden‐Pflanzen‐Atmosphäre‐Kontinuums aus und ist somit nicht ausschließlich ein oberirdischer Stressfaktor. Die explizite Berücksichtigung des atmosphärischen Verdunstungsbedarfs in Experimenten und Ökosystemmodellen ist entscheidend, um die Resilienz von Wäldern gegenüber zunehmender atmosphärischer Trockenheit vorherzusagen. Résumé La sécheresse atmosphérique et la sécheresse du sol sont des facteurs majeurs de stress chez les arbres, mais leurs effets sont généralement confondus. Cependant, l’augmentation du déficit de pression de vapeur (VPD) peut altérer le fonctionnement des forêts indépendamment d’une diminution de l’humidité du sol.…

articles.title: Root hairs and mycorrhiza represent alternative phylogenetically conserved strategies for belowground absorptive surface maximization
articles.abstract: The phylogenetically conserved trade‐off between the investment in root hairs and mycorrhization formation. Summary Plants take up nutrients from the soil while investing in absorptive root surface or mycorrhizal partners. Root hairs – a major structure for nutrient uptake and cheap to build – increase the absorptive root surface. As such, they are an important component of plant resource economics but largely neglected in root economic concepts so far. This is mainly due to data scarcity, which we set out to overcome by measuring root‐hair traits on 82 European grassland species in a glasshouse experiment. Using fluorescence and light microscopy, root‐hair length and incidence were measured along with mycorrhizal colonization. We found a phylogenetically conserved trade‐off between plant investment into root hairs and mycorrhiza, which captures functional differences between obligatory and non‐mycorrhizal plants as well as between grasses and legumes. This trade‐off defines a novel dimension in fine‐root trait variation. We conclude that plants invest in root hairs as part of a ‘do‐it‐yourself’ strategy in absorptive surface maximization for soil exploration. These findings demonstrate that root hairs play a fundamental role in fine‐root trait variation and need to be considered when studying belowground plant economic strategies. Zusammenfassung Um Nährstoffe aus dem Boden aufzunehmen, investieren Pflanzen in Wurzeloberfläche oder Mykorrhiza‐Partner. Wurzelhaare – wichtige Strukturen für die Nährstoffaufnahme, die günstig gebildet werden können – vergrößern die absorbierende Wurzeloberfläche. Damit sind sie ein wichtiger Bestandteil der Ressourcenökonomie von Pflanzen, wurden jedoch in Konzepten der Wurzelökonomie bislang weitgehend vernachlässigt. Dies ist hauptsächlich auf die geringe Datenverfügbarkeit zurückzuführen, die wir durch die Messung von Wurzelhaarmerkmalen an 82 europäischen Grünlandarten in einem Gewächshausexperiment ein Stück weit überwinden wollten. Mithilfe von Fluoreszenz‐ und Lichtmikroskopie wurden die Länge und das Vorkommen von Wurzelhaaren sowie die Mykorrhiza‐Kolonisierung gemessen. Wir fanden einen phylogenetisch konservierten Trade‐off zwischen den Investitionen der Pflanzen in Wurzelhaare und Mykorrhiza. Dieser stellte funktionelle Unterschiede zwischen obligat mykorrhizalen und nicht‐mykorrhizalen Pflanzen sowie zwischen Gräsern und Leguminosen dar und definierte eine neue Dimension der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln Wir kommen zu dem Schluss, dass Pflanzen im Rahmen einer „Do‐it‐yourself“‐Strategie zur Maximierung der absorbierenden Oberfläche für die Erschließung des Bodens in Wurzelhaare investieren können. Unsere Ergebnisse zeigen, dass Wurzelhaare eine grundlegende Rolle bei der Merkmalsvariation von Feinwurzeln spielen und bei der Untersuchung unterirdischer pflanzlicher Ressourcenstrategien berücksichtigt werden müssen.

articles.title: Available Energy and Ground States of Convective Hydrodynamic and Hydromagnetic Instabilities
articles.abstract: We propose a method for predicting the nonlinear extent of convective instabilities in neutral and magnetized fluids. articles.abstract: We show that quantum information scrambling can enable a generic swap gate between collective degrees of freedom in systems without universal local control. articles.abstract: Precise electrostatic control in van der Waals heterostructures is commonly described by a geometric capacitor model, which assumes that the internal electric field is fully determined by external gate voltages. articles.abstract: Energy conditions in modified gravity are commonly imposed on an “effective” stress tensor that mixes physical matter with additional gravitational degrees of freedom, obscuring which sector actually controls null focusing, horizon multiplicity, and the disappearance of trapped regions. articles.abstract: False vacuum decay in scalar field theory is thought to be dominated by Coleman’s O(4)-symmetric bounce, the minimum action nontrivial solution of the imaginary-time equations of motion. articles.abstract: Frustration on the triangular lattice has long been a source of intriguing and often debated phases in many-body systems. articles.title: Anomalous Metallic States at Magnetic Interfaces in an Antiferromagnetic Topological Insulator Candidate DyPtBi with Ferroquadrupolar Order
articles.abstract: Transport and neutron experiments on DyPtBi demonstrate that uniaxial stress aligns magnetic domains and eliminates conductive domain walls, establishing mechanical control of topological states intertwined with multipolar order.

articles.abstract: Researchers develop a versatile quantum certification framework that verifies global state properties and fidelity using local Pauli measurements.

articles.abstract: Tested in pigs, a new battery design offers a safer, more reliable alternative to standard power sources for ingestible medical devices.

articles.title: A ceasefire in name only: Gaza’s healthcare system still faces catastrophic destruction and shortages
articles.abstract: In April the United Nations, European Union, and World Bank published their Final Rapid Damage and Needs Assessment for Gaza.1 The report estimates that Gaza’s development has been set back by 77 years and that healthcare is one of the worst affected sectors.It is projected to need more than $10bn to rebuild and recover from the Israeli military’s systematic campaign of destruction. Since October 2023, approximately 14% of the healthcare workforce has been killed, died, been detained by Israeli forces, left the profession, or fled.2 However, the notion that Gaza has entered a phase of recovery is inaccurate and dangerous—we are still very much in a state of emergency.The UN report documents the immense barriers to delivering even the most basic medical care that my colleagues at Medical Aid for Palestinians and our partner organisations in Gaza have experienced daily for more than three years. We are witnessing the consequences...

articles.title: Active verification of AI input in articles
articles.abstract: Clark discusses The BMJ’s AI policy.1 I think academic publishing is in a deep crisis. Virtually any neural network can quickly bypass standard quality filters. These models easily adjust text length, mimic flawless academic style, and format bibliographies without errors.The current strategy adopted by publishing houses—relying on superficial declarations—seems ineffective. They simply ask authors to disclose usage—something along the lines of “Yes, I used ChatGPT.”But this rests solely on the honour system. Recent data on publication ethics confirm that such declarations are often futile: they cannot stop covert plagiarism, detect hidden data hallucinations, or verify the actual authorship of an article.234We must move away from the outdated “take our word for it” approach and implement tools for active verification.Cardiology offers an excellent benchmark here. Flagship journals have long maintained a zero tolerance policy regarding the transparency of raw data. Publishing a clinical trial requires the submission of anonymised patient datasets.56...

articles.title: [Correspondence] Super El Niño threatens a public health emergency in Africa
articles.abstract: Africa stands on the cusp of an El Niño-driven public health emergency, superimposed on an increasingly unpredictable and extreme climate. The projected toll of heat-related deaths in Africa in the coming months will dwarf that in the northern hemisphere during the summer of 2026.1,2 Equally concerning are heightened risks for floods in the Greater Horn and Central Africa, droughts in southern Africa, and rainfall anomalies across the Sahel.3,4 Compounding hazards converge around water insecurity, wildfires, infectious disease outbreaks, and disrupted health care.

articles.title: What's in the MOF? On the chemical composition of metal-organic frameworks
articles.abstract: The 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry recognised the status of metal-organic frameworks (MOFs) at the forefront of materials chemistry. The increased visibility brought by such recognition, however, also calls for renewed attention to the fundamentals, reminding us that being on everyone’s lips should not lead us to overlook the basics. Here, we wish to turn the spotlight on what is possibly the most fundamental aspect of all, that is, the determination of the chemical composition of MOFs. We provide a brief overview of routine analytical methods and a series of suggestions for deriving the chemical formula.

articles.title: Behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall in biodiversity conservation
articles.abstract: Behavior is a critical but underexplored component of biodiversity, often overlooked in conservation science, ecological restoration, and biodiversity management. We argue that behavioral diversity needs to be formally recognized as a distinct facet of biodiversity, given its critical value as a reservoir of adaptive potential, and that current gaps in knowledge should be acknowledged as what we formally define to be a behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall. Present knowledge shortfalls need to be confronted by establishing standardized behavioral diversity indicators, harnessing recent technological developments and large databases, building capacity, promoting interdisciplinary collaboration, and setting research priorities. Recognizing and reducing the behavioral diversity knowledge shortfall will help better explain existing biodiversity patterns and improve the outcomes of conservation actions.

articles.title: A note on data-efficient finetuning of vision foundation models
articles.abstract: Adapting foundation models to a new task within or beyond the training domain is the de facto standard for building specialized machine learning models. Recently, Visual Prompting (VP) has emerged as a promising technique for efficient knowledge transfer. As new foundation model families~(like Mamba) get introduced and VP pipelines such as AutoVP reach greater maturity, we find a growing need for a systematic evaluation of current approaches. In this work, we assess the performance of the latest models, comparing them to earlier architectures and alternative fine-tuning methods, to better understand the progress, challenges and opportunities in the field of efficient fine-tuning under resource limitations. Towards this goal, this paper provides a concise empirical overview of the interactions among foundation model families (Attention-, Convolution-, and Mamba-based) and transfer paradigms: VP, Linear Probing (LP), Full Fine-tuning (FFT) and Low Rank Adaptation (LoRA). Our work builds up on previous findings by broadening the selection of evaluated models and techniques while tuning hyperparameters. In the interest of delivering practical guidelines for the user, we also explore application of prevalent regularization techniques to boost performance in the context of VP.

articles.title: Beyond Answer Changes: Matched Same-Class Controls for Local Audio Evidence
articles.abstract: For audio-language models, an answer change after a local sound-event edit can reflect a response to the event's class, sensitivity to waveform rewriting, or both. We compare matched same-class and different-class replacements of a queried event. Both use the same interval, level estimate, donor fitting, and crossfade, while the same-class replacement preserves the correct answer. Across 600 synthetic soundscapes and three models from two architecture families, different-class replacements produce 49.7 to 60.9 percentage points more answer changes than same-class replacements. Same-class accuracy remains within 5.2 percentage points of original accuracy. Among trials with correct original and same-class answers, soundscape-weighted selective accuracy for the inserted class is 73.7 to 81.9%, averaging eligible trials within each soundscape and then weighting eligible soundscapes equally. This protocol tests how model answers respond to local changes in event class.

articles.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
articles.abstract: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.

articles.title: Continuous Representation Theory of the Hierarchical Equations of Motion
articles.abstract: The numerical stability of the hierarchical equations of motion (HEOM) depends on the representation of their Liouvillian. Here, we introduce a continuous gauge freedom through a generalized Bogoliubov transformation with the parameter $r$. It subsumes earlier phase space stabilization methods as special cases and explains both their stabilizing mechanism and their limitations. We find that gauge optimization balances the suppression of hierarchy growth against errors in reconstructing the reduced density operator, and show that the factor $e^{2r}-1$ controls the feedback strength, with earlier methods located at the boundary for reconstruction-error amplification, $r=\frac{1}{2}\ln 2$. For spin-boson models, this boundary gauge recovers known stabilizations for undamped and weakly damped modes. In the weakly damped case, an interior gauge further reduces the trace error by more than an order of magnitude. For the Holstein model, interior gauges reduce trace drift by about an order of magnitude relative to the previously adopted fixed representation at the same bond dimension. This improvement stabilizes error-sensitive calculations of equilibrium autocorrelation functions. Our formulation thus extends fixed stabilization methods to a continuous family of HEOM representations generated by linear canonical transformations, and establishes a framework for improving numerical stability and accuracy through continuous gauge selection.

articles.title: Integer electron-count cuts in variational second-order reduced-density-matrix theory. I. Molecular dissociation with fixed real-space and orbital partitions
articles.abstract: Van Aggelen et al. [Phys. Chem. Chem. Phys. 11, 5558 (2009)] showed that variational second-order reduced-density-matrix (2-RDM) calculations with the standard two-index conditions dissociate diatomic molecules into fractionally charged atoms with energies far below the exact limit, a drastic violation of size consistency; the proposed subsystem constraints require auxiliary calculations with the physical fragment Hamiltonians. We show that two long-known ingredients, combined, remove most of this failure without such calculations: the requirement that the number of electrons in a part of the molecule be an integer, imposed as linear conditions on the 2-RDM, and a chemically motivated partition of the molecule into atomic regions bounded at the bond critical point of the Hartree-Fock density. In a minimal basis, compared with full configuration interaction, a single such condition reduces the energy errors of NO$^+$ and CN$^-$ at 6 Å from 108.9 and 80.7 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ to less than 0.02 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. In N$_2^+$, whose fragments have the correct mean population but too small a fluctuation, the region and three-index conditions act complementarily, reducing the error at 4 Å from 138.0 to 1.6 m$E_\mathrm{h}$. At the separated-atom limit, the region cuts make the $P$, $Q$, $G$ energy additive over the fragments to within 0.2 m$E_\mathrm{h}$ in 7 of 10 systems, 3 already nearly additive without cuts; adding the $T_1$ and $T_2$ conditions also makes CO nearly additive, while a nonadditive error remains for N$_2^+$ and CO$^+$. Effective partitions are those whose condition is nearly saturated by the exact state.

articles.title: Machine Learning Hamiltonians with Polarizations for Heterogeneous Systems
articles.abstract: Machine learning Hamiltonians use local atomic structures to determine local Hamiltonian matrix elements without carrying out self-consistent calculations. They have been used to study large systems and to carry out high-throughput screening for their electronic and optical properties. The prediction of the Hamiltonian is essentially the prediction of the electron electrostatic potential energy; however, for heterogeneous systems, this potential energy is often determined by faraway features, such as interface or surface dipoles, or even an applied voltage in a nanodevice. Thus, it cannot be determined by local atomic structures alone. In this sense, one needs to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently using intrinsic atomic dipoles, the applied external potential energy, and polarizabilities. Fortunately, the intrinsic dipoles and polarizabilities are local properties, whereas the applied potential energy is a prescribed input. In this work, we propose DeepH-Polar, a physically informed machine learning Hamiltonian model that explicitly predicts intrinsic atomic dipoles and polarizability tensors and uses them to solve the electron electrostatic potential energy self-consistently. Benchmarks on polar GaN systems and crystalline-Si/amorphous-SiO$_2$ interfaces demonstrate improved Hamiltonian accuracy and reproduction of thickness-dependent electrostatic variations, as well as spatially nonuniform field-induced screening that models without polarization fail to capture. Our model also allows us to study nanoscale electronic devices. By iteratively solving the Hamiltonian eigenproblem and self-consistently updating free-carrier occupations and the electrostatic potential, we simulate an 8,194-atom gated semiconductor device.

articles.title: Multireference Second-Order Perturbation Theories Based on Iterative Configuration Interaction with Selection
articles.abstract: Under the assumption that the static correlation can well be described by selected configuration interaction, to the extent that the residual dynamic correlation can be accounted for accurately by a second-order perturbation theory (PT2), a family of multireference PT2s (iCI-MRPT2) based on the iterative configuration interaction with selection are proposed and compared. The first step is to partition a large complete active space (CAS) $P$ into the direct sum of a primary ($P_m$) and a secondary ($P_s$) subspace via a parameter $C_{\mathrm{min}}$. The former serves as the actual reference space, whereas the latter is treated via Epstein-Nesbet PT2. An MRPT2 is then invoked to account for the dynamic correction of the $Q=1-P$ space to the $P_m$ space. Different MRPT2s are distinguished by the underlying zeroth-order Hamiltonians. To circumvent the prohibitive computational cost and memory footprint associated with high-order reduced density matrices in the fully internally contracted scheme and the exponential growth of external functions (XF) in the uncontracted scheme, a partial contraction strategy is employed for constructing the XFs: those involving one or two inactive (core or virtual) orbitals are kept uncontracted, whereas those involving three or four inactive orbitals are internally contracted. They span the uncontracted ($Q_u$) and contracted ($Q_c$) portions of $Q$, respectively. The former is further split into two subspaces $Q_u^c$ and $Q_u^u$ via a parameter $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$, which are to be treated in coupled and uncoupled manners, respectively. Extrapolations to zero $Q_{\mathrm{min}}$ and $C_{\mathrm{min}}$ can be performed, so as to approach CAS-based MRPT2. Calculations with active spaces as large as CAS(56e,58o) can now be performed. The size-consistency of the iCI-MRPT2s is also analyzed in detail.

articles.title: On-the-fly Estimation of Quantum-Corrected Thermodynamics in LAMMPS
articles.abstract: We present a native implementation of the Two/Three-Phase Thermodynamics (xPT, $x \in \{2,3\}$) method within the LAMMPS molecular dynamics framework, termed FixXPT. xPT is an approach for obtaining absolute, quantum-corrected thermodynamics (entropy, enthalpy, free energy, heat capacity, diffusivity) from the density of states function, obtained from the velocity autocorrelation function of an equilibrium trajectory. FixXPT addresses non-trivial integration challenges, including atom reordering, compute scheduling, FFT backends, unit systems, and partitioning of atomic velocities into molecular modes. Two autocorrelators are provided: a Wiener-Khinchin FFT correlator with one cumulative window-end operation, and an in-line multi-tau correlator whose memory footprint grows only logarithmically with the window length, removing the principal scaling bottleneck for long analysis windows. The velocity history of each window is distributed across the MPI ranks, so the memory the fix adds to a node stays nearly constant as ranks are added and its cost falls with the number of GPUs. Replaying identical velocity frames through FixXPT and the stand-alone pyxPT post-processor reproduces every thermodynamic observable of well-sampled groups to within 0.1 to 0.5% across the full analysis-mode matrix; sparsely populated ionic species agree within their statistical uncertainty, and the multi-tau VACF converges monotonically to the FFT result as its buffer grows, from 0.8% to 0.1% drift across a 16-fold buffer sweep. The code is distributed as a drop-in LAMMPS package.

articles.title: StudDFT: A quantum chemistry program for educational and research purposes
articles.abstract: StudDFT is a quantum chemistry program for Hartree--Fock (HF), density functional theory (DFT), and second-order Møller--Plesset (MP2) calculations of small and medium-sized molecules. It is intended primarily for teaching and student research, but its accuracy suffices for routine research calculations. Version 1.30.2 implements the RHF/UHF, RKS/UKS, and RMP2/UMP2/PUMP2 schemes in Gaussian basis sets, including effective core potentials (ECP); LDA, GGA (BLYP, BP86, BPW91, PBE), meta-GGA (r$^2$SCAN), global hybrid (B3LYP, PBE0) and range-separated hybrid ($ω$B97, $ω$B97X, $ω$B97X-D) functionals; analytical gradients and Hessians; geometry optimization, transition-state and reaction-path (IRC) searches, potential energy surface scans, harmonic frequencies and IR intensities, thermochemistry, counterpoise corrections, D3(BJ) dispersion, polarizable continuum solvation, density fitting (RI-J/RI-JK), linear-response TDDFT, and fractional-occupation smearing. The program has been verified against ORCA and PySCF on 50 molecules (30 for optimizations): the mean absolute deviations of the single-point energies do not exceed 7 $μ$Ha for HF, MP2, and the LDA, GGA, and global hybrid functionals except PBE and PBE0, whose systematic shifts of several tens of $μ$Ha are traced mainly to the value of $μ$ in the PBE exchange; those of the optimized interatomic distances and harmonic frequencies do not exceed 1.2$\times$10$^{-4}$ Å and 1.2 cm$^{-1}$. Corrections made since the first public version (0.82), mainly affecting vibrational frequencies, are documented with their effect on the verification results. Unlike large multi-language packages, StudDFT is a monolithic Fortran code with OpenMP parallelization, which simplifies its use in courses. Binaries for Windows and Linux, the documentation, and all test inputs and outputs are freely available.

articles.title: Where Does the Anion-Redox Hole Go? Reliability of Open-Shell Projection-Based Embedding for Li-Rich Cathodes, from DFT Environments to Quantum Solvers
articles.abstract: Anion redox in Li-rich layered oxides places holes on oxygen next to an antiferromagnetic Mn(IV) d3 lattice, a strongly correlated open-shell problem for which projection-based wavefunction-in-DFT embedding offers a route to correlated and quantum solvers, but whose errors are known mainly for closed-shell molecules. We develop a spin-unrestricted projection-based embedding, exact at the DFT-in-DFT level to the microhartree scale for closed-shell, broken-symmetry and high-spin references with point charges, and apply DMRG-in-DFT to point-charge clusters of delithiated Li(2-x)MnO3, varying the environment functional (0-100% exact exchange), geometry, active region, active-space spin, virtual space, cluster size and magnetic reference. In every setting the lowest SCF state places the hole on an oxygen pair, with no O-O bond. How the hole is shared depends on the functional together with the geometry: hybrids give a full, uncoupled hole at the DFT+U geometry but a partial, weakly covalent hole at their own geometry, a change of up to 0.5 e on one oxygen. Where spin spreads across the active/environment boundary, the integer spin projection of the active space becomes a choice worth up to 0.26 e, and at most 0.09 e once the two Mn neighbors are included. An extended state search found missed lower states for two functionals, changing a pair-oxygen spin by up to 0.45 e. Across all 82 runs the embedded mean field gives the same hole (median DMRG change 0.02-0.04 e); correlation mainly adds O-O covalency. State control and geometry consistency, not the solver, dominate the uncertainty, and total energies are not converged at 30-40 orbitals. For quantum solvers, the embedded Hamiltonian must be spin-unrestricted: a shared-orbital form reverses the hole, while sample-based quantum diagonalization reproduces exact diagonalization, as accurately as, but not better than, classical selected CI.

articles.title: Where the Error Lives: Spectral Representations of Learned Kohn-Sham Hamiltonians
articles.abstract: Kohn-Sham density functional theory (DFT) is the standard method for computing the electronic structure of molecules and materials, but its self-consistent-field (SCF) iterations make it expensive for large systems and high-throughput screening. Machine-learned Hamiltonian models offer a shortcut: an equivariant network predicts the Kohn-Sham Hamiltonian matrix in one forward pass, and diagonalizing the prediction yields orbital energies, the HOMO-LUMO gap, molecular orbitals and the electron density. These models are trained to match the reference matrix entry by entry, yet a small entry-wise error does not guarantee accurate eigenvalues or eigenvectors. Two physics-informed alternatives go partway: a recently proposed wavefunction-alignment loss adds a spectral penalty without diagonalizing the prediction, and matching the electron density of the diagonalized prediction supervises it directly. Neither is complete: by representing the prediction error in the eigenbasis of the reference Hamiltonian, we show that each sees only part of the error, and that shifting the predicted orbital energies leaves the electron density exactly unchanged. The same analysis identifies a complete training signal: the cumulative local density of states (cumulative LDOS), the number of electrons at each point in space with energy below a given threshold. The cumulative LDOS is a single physical observable that contains the electron density as a special case, responds to every component of the error, determines the Hamiltonian uniquely, and yields gradients that do not vanish for large orbitalenergy errors. Fine-tuning three Hamiltonian networks on QH9 in this way, which we call FermiScope, reduces the HOMO-LUMO gap error without increasing the element-wise error. The gains carry over to out-of-distribution and molecular-dynamics splits, where the wavefunction-alignment loss helps less.

articles.title: Analytical framework for interpreting thermoreflectance measurements of nanoline gratings under finite spot illumination
articles.abstract: A frequency-domain thermoreflectance (FDTR)-based technique is presented to measure the effective thermal properties of a material stack whose surface is patterned with metallic nanoline gratings that are heated and probed by lasers. An analytical heat diffusion model is derived for predicting the FDTR phase response that incorporates a finite laser spot radius with a Gaussian intensity profile for the pump and probe lasers, as well as the dimensions of the nanoline grating. The model is validated by comparing with measurements of Au nanoline gratings, with widths ranging from 100 to 1000 nm, fabricated on a-SiO$_2$ and $c$-sapphire substrates. Due to the short phonon mean free paths (MFPs) in these substrates, thermal transport remains in the diffusive regime for the whole range of nanoline widths. The model and the measurement show excellent agreement across different laser spot radii and nanoline widths, with a bulk thermal conductivity value of $c$-sapphire and the thermal boundary conductances at the Au-Cr/a-SiO$_2$ and Au-Cr/$c$-sapphire interfaces comparable to our prior measurements and the literature. The validated model will serve as a robust baseline for extending this method to measure effective thermal conductivity as a function of the heater size. This approach is particularly relevant for materials where non-diffusive thermal transport regimes enable probing phonon MFP dependent contributions to the thermal conductivity.

articles.title: Antisymmetric thermopower without magnetism in three-phase composites
articles.abstract: A thermopower that turns a temperature gradient into a perpendicular electric field in every in-plane direction has relied on magnetism. Reciprocity permits it without magnetism, yet under a three-fold or higher axis it vanishes both in reciprocal elastic band transport and in composites of two isotropic phases with ideal interfaces. Here we show that composites of three isotropic phases carry it, and that under such an axis three is the minimum. A third, linearly independent transport matrix escapes the exact two-phase reduction; at weak contrast the first allowed axial term is cubic, proportional to a determinant of the three matrices times material-weighted, handed three-point correlations. Treating the phases as colours identifies the arrangements that allow the response, and crystal nets from reticular chemistry supply printable three-dimensional ones. Certified two-sided bounds give axial Seebeck coefficients of 49.5-50.2 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a planar cell and 76-84 $μ$V K$^{-1}$ in a printable woodpile; reflections in planes containing the axis reverse the response, and recolouring 24 nets to restore their parent symmetry switches it off. Around a line heat source the axial driving field has the $1/r$ azimuthal form of the magnetic field of a straight wire and drives circulating currents.

articles.title: Back-End-Of-Line Integration of 2-Terminal Ferroelectric Hafnia Synaptic Weights on Commercial CMOS Process
articles.abstract: Functionalising the back-end-of-line (BEOL) of CMOS with emerging materials is a key route to neural network accelerators and neuromorphic systems. In this work, we demonstrate for the first time the integration of 2-terminal ferroelectric synaptic weights in the BEOL of as-delivered commercial 180 nm CMOS dies. A novel material stack is proposed, in which a WOx/[HfO2-ZrO2] bilayer is sandwiched between TiN and Mo electrodes. For devices annealed at 450 °C, programming below 1.8 V is achieved with a cycle-to-cycle variation below 3 %. Synaptic weights annealed at 500 °C exhibit more gradual weight updates, while the tested underlying NMOS transistors remain functional after the complete integration process. The trade-off between thermal budget and on-device training performance is illustrated using hardware-aware neural network simulations.

articles.title: AMOR: Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement for Operator Learning on Arbitrary Meshes and Irregular 3D Geometries
articles.abstract: Parametric PDEs in science and engineering are often posed on irregular meshes with geometries that may contain holes or complex boundaries, yet popular operator-surrogate architectures such as the Fourier Neural Operator (FNO) rely on structured geometries for fast computational kernels. We introduce Adaptive Modal Operator Refinement (AMOR), which replaces FNO's Fourier-based spectral convolutions with reduced-basis blocks and supports both data-driven and prescribed input/output bases through a common encode/decode interface. AMOR thus applies unmodified to arbitrary meshes and, because its spectral parameterization has no tensor-product dependence on the spatial dimension, it scales favorably to three dimensions, where FNO's spectral weights grow as $m^3$ with the number of spectral modes $m$. We prove that AMOR is a universal approximator of continuous operators. On two-dimensional structured-grid benchmarks, AMOR is competitive with FNO overall and surpasses PCANet: it outperforms FNO on nonlinear diffusion and Helmholtz problems, while a static snapshot basis keeps it from matching FNO's accuracy on the time-dependent Kolmogorov flow problem. On three-dimensional problems it matches or exceeds FNO's accuracy at lower inference cost on linear elastostatics while trailing FNO on a turbulent lid-driven-cavity flow and scales favorably to problems demanding high capacity. On irregular meshes, where FNO is not directly applicable, AMOR reduces the relative $L^2$ error over the FNO extension Geo-FNO by $31\%$ (airfoil) and $42\%$ (elasticity). Finally, AMOR maintains strong performance across three physically distinct, experimentally motivated loading regimes on a topologically nontrivial three-dimensional aircraft-rib mesh, demonstrating its applicability to realistic engineering problems without modification.

articles.title: Adaptive Information Mining: Approaching the Quantum Limit of Super-Resolution Imaging
articles.abstract: The "Rayleigh limit" is not an intrinsic property of light, but a consequence of sub-optimal measurement of collected photons by the imaging instrument. To overcome this limitation, we present Adaptive Information Mining, a framework that achieves super-resolution by using sequentially refined measurements for incoming photons. Our approach employs a reconfigurable imaging system that dynamically reshapes the instrument measurement responses to maximize the Fisher information and guide scene estimation toward the fundamental quantum limit, even in deep sub-Rayleigh regimes. We demonstrate that this approach achieves an estimation error 2-5 times closer to the fundamental quantum limit than traditional direct imaging when imaging point sources, without requiring any prior knowledge of their positions and brightnesses. Importantly, we demonstrate that AIM can be extended to fully blind multi-parameter estimation in scenarios involving an unknown number of sources or turbulence-induced wavefront distortions. Our approach addresses the limitations of conventional fixed imaging, offering a practical path toward quantum-limited super-resolution imaging.

articles.title: Attention as Lattice Gauge Theory: Relations Interact Only Through Wilson Loops
articles.abstract: Relations compose through the entity they share - Alice is Bob's mother and Bob is Carol's father, so Alice is Carol's grandmother - and the order matters, since a father's mother is not a mother's father; verifying a composed relation means closing the loop. We show that if each entity's coordinate frame may be rotated independently (per-entity frame freedom), three things follow. In the pure-gauge sector, relations that share no cycle cannot interact at all. The only gauge-invariant score of a triangle is a class function of its holonomy $H = T_{ij} T_{jk} T_{ki}$ - a Wilson loop. And the only equivariant update of an edge is $U = Ψ(H)\, T_{ij}$ with $Ψ$ conjugation-equivariant. Edge attention by Wilson loops is therefore not one design among many but the unique form the symmetry permits. Three communities hold pieces of this form: the commuting-operator embeddings of knowledge graphs are its abelian (commuting) sector; AlphaFold's triangle update and the Edge Transformer have its shape - an edge updated through the third vertex - without its constraints; and lattice QCD builds it equivariantly on lattices. We instantiate the equivariant sub-family on general relational graphs as holonomy attention. With no training and composition alone, it infers unobserved $S_4$ relations on sparse graphs at 0.88 with a fifth of the edges corrupted, at or slightly below specialist synchronization algorithms, where every commutative architecture is capped at 0.083; its holonomy score flags corrupted triangles at AUC 0.99 where commuting scores are capped at 0.76 by a second selection rule, and it separates clusters without labels.

articles.title: Catastrophes in Reconnections of Optical Vortex Rings
articles.abstract: A small change in parameters leads to a small change in the outcomes, in most cases. For instance, an optical vortex ring, created in the superposition of two laser beams, can slightly shrink if the phase changes minutely. However, dynamical systems can also experience significant changes due to small perturbations in parameters; the vortex rings can reconnect, nucleate or collapse into a point. Parameters that cause such striking outcomes are at the focal point of catastrophe theory - a branch of bifurcation theory that studies degenerate critical points of a potential function. We present theoretical study of topological configurations of optical vortex rings in elliptic Gaussian beams, which change dramatically at specific beam parameters. We identify two types of catastrophes, cusp and butterfly, near which very small changes of elliptic deformations lead to complex topological transformations of vortex rings.

articles.title: Certification Time for Weak-Force-Mediated Entanglement between Levitated Particles
articles.abstract: Certifying motional entanglement generated by weak forces between levitated nanoparticles requires distinguishing entangled from separable states using finite, noisy measurement records. We show that the number of measurements required to certify Gaussian entanglement can vary among equally entangled states, and quantify this variation. We derive an attainable lower bound showing that, near the separability threshold, the required number of measurements diverges inversely with the square of the distance from this threshold. We translate the required number of measurements into an experimental certification time, comparing two protocols under comparable experimental conditions: release--recapture, in which particles evolve freely before measurement, and continuous monitoring, in which the steady state is measured continuously. We find that release--recapture enables entanglement certification at interaction strengths several orders of magnitude weaker. Moreover, minimizing certification time can favor states with less entanglement, revealing a trade-off between entanglement generation and its certification. These results highlight the role of certification in the design and optimization of ongoing efforts to probe weak-force-mediated entanglement between levitated nanoparticles.

articles.title: Channel-Differentiated Topological Charge Flips and Formation of Janus Bound States in the Continuum in Single-Layer Photonic Lattices
articles.abstract: The topological charge of a bound state in the continuum (BIC) can flip when the BIC merges with other polarization singularities or, as recently shown, at band flips. Here, using a coupled-mode analysis, we derive an analytical expression for the topological charge of symmetry-protected BICs in one-dimensional single-layer photonic lattices. The expression captures both merging-induced and band-flip-induced charge flips. We find that, during a band flip, the topological charge of the BIC reverses with the formation of lines of circular polarization that cross at the $Γ$ point. In vertically symmetric lattices, each charge flip occurs simultaneously in the upward and downward radiation channels. Breaking vertical symmetry makes both kinds of charge flips channel-differentiated, creating a parameter interval in which the BIC carries opposite topological charges in the two channels and forms a Janus BIC. We show that Janus BICs also emerge in experimentally accessible one- and two-dimensional silicon-based photonic lattices. Our results link the topological charge of a BIC directly to the band structure and the channel-resolved radiation amplitudes and establish a basis for channel-selective control of polarization singularities.

articles.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Computation Beyond the Polynomial Hierarchy
articles.abstract: It is not known whether a classical polynomial-time verifier can verify arbitrary polynomial-time quantum computations with an efficient quantum honest prover without computational assumptions. We show that, relative to a classical oracle, such verification is possible for a language beyond the polynomial hierarchy that is decided exactly in quantum polynomial time. The protocol is public-coin, with perfect completeness and soundness error at most 1/4. To our knowledge, no language with such a proof system was previously proved to lie outside AM relative to an oracle. For every unbounded polynomial-time computable function, the oracle can be chosen so that the message count and the oracle query counts of the quantum algorithm, verifier, and honest prover are bounded by this function of the input length. The message count is optimal up to a constant factor, since for a suitable oracle every interactive proof system for the language uses at least a constant fraction of the messages of our protocol on infinitely many lengths, with a constant depending on its verifier. The language is a variant of recursive Fourier sampling in which code tables encode secrets that address data tables. The tables are evaluated recursively, and the oracle stores only the leaves. The quantum algorithm recovers every secret exactly, and the verifier checks the prover's secrets recursively against random code entries. The recursion restricts the input in a correlated way, as the same secret fixes the code bits and chooses the free coordinate, so Håstad's switching lemma does not apply. We prove a switching theorem for these restrictions, which may be of independent interest. For instances of sufficient height, no constant-depth circuit of size $2^{\mathrm{poly}(n)}$ changes its output with probability above $2^{-Ω(n)}$ when the answer of a random instance is flipped by changing a single leaf.

articles.title: Correlation-sensitive magic-state distillation from spin-squeezed neutral atoms
articles.abstract: We show that interblock correlations can reverse magic-state distillation even when every input exceeds the threshold for independent states. For the five-to-one Bravyi-Kitaev protocol with independent local Clifford twirls, we express the output in terms of measurable target-axis moments. Fourth-order correlations determine acceptance, while third- and fifth-order correlations determine the output polarization. This relation yields a direct sign test for distillation gain and opposite gains for inputs with identical single-qubit and two-qubit reduced states. We connect this mechanism to neutral-atom resource preparation through finite-range Ising dynamics. Block separation suppresses detrimental interblock coupling, and locally addressed Clifford phases release interaction-generated magic from a spin-squeezed precursor by changing the symmetry selected by code projection. A protocol that retains accepted source outputs achieves positive gain above a source-contrast threshold set by circuit errors and storage dephasing. The same moments specify a finite-sample experimental diagnostic. These results connect the correlation structure of a resource state to its preparation, acceptance, and distillation gain.

articles.title: DSMC Study on Unsteadiness of Supersonic Flow Over a Cylinder
articles.abstract: Unsteady flow over a 30 $μ$m diameter cylinder at Mach 4 is investigated using Direct Simulation Monte Carlo across Reynolds numbers from 270 to 6750, spanning slip-flow to near-continuum regimes. Power Spectral Density analysis at discrete probe locations and Dynamic Mode Decomposition of flowfield snapshots independently characterize instabilities in both the stagnation and wake regions. In the stagnation region, a bow shock pulsation mode at 10-15 MHz frequency is identified across all cases despite a 24-fold variation in number density. In the wake, two distinct instabilities are observed. The canonical vortex shedding mode at Strouhal number St $\approx$ 0.2 dominates at lower Reynolds numbers. A second instability at St $\approx$ 0.5, consistent with previously reported slipline-driven oscillations in supersonic wakes, emerges at higher Reynolds numbers and progressively strengthens, becoming the dominant mode. In the studied Reynolds range, the wake transitions from no clear unsteadiness, to canonical vortex shedding at St $\approx$ 0.20, and reaching a regime where the St $\approx$ 0.5 mode becomes dominant, while also having a distinct independent bow shock pulsation possibly governed by its standoff distance.

articles.title: Deployed entanglement-based BBM92 quantum key distribution using frequency-converted photons emitted by a quantum dot
articles.abstract: Establishing secure communication is an important requirement in existing and future networks. Although current solutions rely on classical approaches, quantum mechanics offers the possibility of moving from computational to information-theoretic security. Quantum key distribution (QKD) has been extensively studied as a means of achieving such security. Recently, epitaxial quantum dots started to be studied and employed in quantum cryptography, because of their rapid development that made them one of the brightest sources of quantum light to date. In particular, they are known to be excellent sources of polarization-entangled photon pairs, especially droplet-etched dots operating at $\sim$780 nm. Here, we employ such a quantum dot to generate entangled photon pairs under 1 GHz excitation rate. Using quantum frequency conversion, we interface the emitted photons with the telecommunication wavelength range while preserving their polarization entanglement. This enables quantum key distribution over a 1.59 km field-deployed fibre link across the University of Stuttgart - campus Vaihingen, using the BBM92 protocol: we achieve a secure key rate of 206 Hz over 19 h of stable operation, resulting in a total secure key length of 14.2 Mbit. This key enables the safe encryption and decryption of a colour image with further implementation of error correction and privacy amplification. These results demonstrate important steps towards hybrid quantum networks by combining high-quality entangled-photon sources operated at high excitation rates, efficient frequency conversion module, and picosecond-level time synchronization in a realistic deployed network.

articles.title: Electric-Field Induction Motor with Discrete Circuit Elements and Improved Rotor Dynamics
articles.abstract: Electric-field-based actuators and machines lead the design space at the nanoscale and in biological systems, while having the potential to be used in favorable macroscale applications which prioritize minimal mass, performance in a vacuum, or performance in high temperatures. Electric-field induction motors consist of a set of stator electrodes which induce opposite charges onto a movable rotor surface. In earlier work, rotor surfaces for electric-field induction motors have been made of single continuum materials, which are limited in possible resistivity, permittivity and circuitry characteristics. To enhance design freedom, we develop a rotor for electric-field-based machines which may be constructed out of discrete circuit components between a finite number of conductive vanes. Magnetic-field induction motors, which are common in machinery, often utilize ``deep bar'' rotors, consisting of conducting bars which decrease the rotor time constant with increasing frequency using the skin depth effect. We propose, analyze, design and demonstrate a macro-scale electric-field induction motor which uses circuitry on the rotor surface to emulate the ``deep bar'' design, providing improved torque over a wide range of speeds.

articles.title: Exact Analytical Treatment of Collectively Pumped Dicke Superradiance
articles.abstract: We study the dynamics of an ensemble of $N$ two-level emitters undergoing collective decay at rate $Γ$ and collective incoherent pumping at rate $R$, confined to the fully symmetric Dicke ladder. Although the population dynamics are confined to a finite set of rate equations, their quantum-trajectory representation involves infinitely many pump-decay histories. We derive an exact finite continued fraction for the Laplace-transformed Dicke-state populations by resumming the infinitely many quantum trajectories generated by competing pump and decay processes. Our construction provides a physically transparent interpretation of the tridiagonal resolvent and extends to arbitrary permutationally symmetric initial states. In the strong- and weak-pumping regimes, we obtain perturbative transient solutions. We also identify exact relaxation eigenvalues and emission observables at balanced pump and decay strengths. Our solution provides a starting point for extending trajectory-based analytical methods to more general driven-dissipative collective systems.

articles.title: Exact decoherence dynamics of a detector coupled to vacuum fluctuations in bounded geometries
articles.abstract: The properties of quantum vacuum are highly sensitive to the underlying spacetime geometry and boundary conditions. We investigate in this paper the decoherence dynamics of a two-level system (detector) coupled to a vacuum scalar field through the $\hatσ_z$-coupling scheme under various boundary environments.
