Zamtocabtagene autoleucel, a tandem CD20–CD19-directed CAR T-cell therapy, for second line treatment of large B-cell lymphoma in patients ineligible for transplantation (DALY 2-EU): primary analysis of an open-label, multicentre, randomised phase 2 study
articles.abstract: BackgroundAnti-CD19 CAR T-cell therapy is the standard second-line treatment for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma. However, there is no evidence from randomised controlled trials in patients ineligible for transplantation. To address this gap, we compared zamtocabtagene autoleucel (zamto-cel), a CAR T-cell therapy directed at CD20 and CD19, with rituximab-gemcitabine-oxaliplatin (R-GemOx) chemoimmunotherapy in patients ineligible for transplantation with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma.MethodsDALY 2-EU is an open-label, multicentre, randomised, phase 2 trial conducted at 45 centres across 12 countries in Europe. Eligible patients were adults (aged ≥18 years) with second-line relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma confirmed histologically who were ineligible for transplantation and had received first-line chemoimmunotherapy containing a combination of an anthracycline-based regimen and an anti-CD20 monoclonal antibody, with Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status score of 2 or less. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1) to zamto-cel (single intravenous infusion of 2·5 × 106 fresh (ie, non-cryopreserved) CAR T-cells per kg, capped at 100 kg, produced in a closed automated system) or R-GemOx (rituximab [375 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1], gemcitabine [1000 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2], and oxaliplatin [100 mg/m2 intravenously on day 1 or 2] administered for up to eight 14-day cycles). Randomisation was done with an interactive web response system and stratified by age, gender, lactate dehydrogenase, International Prognostic Index, histology, time to relapse after the start of first-line therapy, and country. The primary endpoint was event-free survival assessed by a masked independent review committee and compared all patients randomly assigned to the zamto-cel and R-GemOx groups using a one-sided log-rank test. Safety was assessed in all patients who received study treatment. This ongoing trial is registered with ClinicalTrials.gov (NCT04844866).FindingsBetween Oct 14, 2021, and Jul 16, 2024, 219 patients were screened and 160 were randomly assigned to zamto-cel (n=82) and R-GemOx (n=78). The median age was 74·0 years (IQR 70·5-77·0). Patients were predominantly male (100 [63%] of 160 were men and 60 [38%] women) and White (91 [57%]), with race not reported for 64 (40%). Median vein-to-vein time for zamto-cel was 15 days (IQR 15-16). With a median follow-up of 17·0 months (IQR 9·0-22·8), event-free survival was longer in the zamto-cel group than in the R-GemOx group (6·21 months [95% CI 3·84-13·77] vs 2·53 months [1·97-3·35]; HR 0·39 [95% CI 0·27-0·58]; pInterpretationThe risk-benefit ratio observed in the DALY 2-EU study supports consideration of zamto-cel as a second-line standard treatment option for patients with relapsed or refractory large B-cell lymphoma who are ineligible for transplantation.FundingMiltenyi Biomedicine.

articles.title: A Density-Matrix Formulation of Vibrational Circular Dichroism Spectra for Møller-Plesset and Configuration Interaction Methods
articles.abstract: We reformulate the overlap of wave-function derivatives that defines the atomic axial tensors (AATs) and velocity-gauge atomic polar tensors (VG-APTs) used to compute vibrational circular dichroism (VCD) rotatory strengths. In place of our earlier determinant-level derivatives, the new approach expresses these tensors as contractions involving molecular-orbital derivative integrals, perturbed and unperturbed one- and two-electron density matrices, and dot products of the perturbed correlated wave-function amplitudes. Following the elegant treatment of the diagonal Born-Oppenheimer correction by Gauss and co-workers, the formulation holds for any real, normalized CI-like wave function. The two-electron density contribution vanishes exactly, because one perturbation is real (nuclear) and the other imaginary (magnetic field or momentum); this removes multiple terms from our earlier AAT and VG-APT expressions for second-order Møller-Plesset perturbation theory (MP2) and configuration interaction singles and doubles (CISD). We also present a simplified form of the origin-independent length-gauge [LG(OI)] rotatory strength that avoids the singular-value decomposition of the outer product of the length-gauge APT and VG-APT vectors for each mode, and that clarifies how the LG(OI) and velocity-gauge rotatory strengths are related. Applying the density-based AATs and VG-APTs to ($P$)-hydrogen peroxide, (\textit{S})-methyloxirane, and (\textit{S})-3-chloro-1-butyne, we find that discrepancies among the gauges arise chiefly from basis-set incompleteness in the VG-APT. The charge-sum rule serves as a useful measure of that incompleteness, independent of the correlation method.

articles.title: An Ab Initio Quantum-Chemistry-Based Three-Temperature Approach for Non-Equilibrium Hypersonic Flows: Application to Homogeneous 0-D Chemical Systems
articles.abstract: This work presents an ab initio quantum-chemistry-based one-bin, three-temperature (1-bin 3T) model for non-equilibrium thermochemistry of homogeneous chemical systems in their electronic ground state, derived using the multi-group maximum-entropy principle. The proposed framework captures both vibrational and rotational non-equilibrium effects, thereby enabling an accurate representation of thermochemical behavior in high-temperature gases. To account for departures from equilibrium dissociation, a non-equilibrium correction factor derived from ro-vibrational State-to-State (StS) analysis is incorporated into the population distribution. Because this correction is constructed from the quasi-steady-state (QSS) distribution, the resulting model is valid only for systems and conditions under which the QSS assumption holds. The proposed 1-bin 3T model is validated across a broad range of zero-dimensional test cases through comparisons with high-fidelity StS simulations and Direct Molecular Simulations (DMS). The results demonstrate excellent agreement between the reduced-order model and high-fidelity approaches for both dissociating and recombining environments. Overall, the 1-bin 3T model shows strong potential as an efficient and accurate framework for modeling non-equilibrium thermochemical behavior, while keeping computational costs orders of magnitude lower than the high fidelity ro-vibrational StS simulations.

articles.title: Lanthanide Crystal Field Theory in the J-Mixing Regime: $f^n$ Configurations
articles.abstract: The low-energy sector of the lanthanide $f^n$ shell is to first approximation governed by the interplay of three interactions: Coulomb repulsion, spin-same-orbit coupling and the ligand crystal field potential. To rationalize the energy landscape in different chemical environments, it is desirable to extract the phenomenological crystal field parameters from experimental data; however, in practice, high-dimensional fitting procedures complicate their routine determination. Here, we present a computational extraction procedure based on real tensorial sets and the $U(7)$ canonical chain that, unlike existing operator equivalent methods, takes all $J$ multiplets of the lowest-energy $LS$ term into account, ensuring meaningful results even in the presence of considerable $J$-mixing. Two series of lanthanide compounds, [Ln(III)(C$_8$H$_8$)$_2$]$^-$} and doped Ln(III):Y$_2$O$_3$} (Ln $\in$ {Ce, Pr, Nd, Sm, Eu}) serve as examples for high- ($D_{8h}$) and low-symmetry ($C_2$) scenarios. Consequences for the generalisation toward actinides are briefly discussed.

articles.title: Preparing State-Selected Molecular Beams with high Efficiency using Quantum Cascade Lasers
articles.abstract: We demonstrate the ro-vibrational state-selective preparation of CO molecules ($v$ = 0, J = 0 $\rightarrow$ $v$ = 1, J = 1) in an internally cold molecular beam using a continuous-wave, narrow-linewidth distributed feedback type quantum cascade laser, with an output wavelength of 4.65 $μ$m. Using a modulation-free wavelength stabilization scheme, we show that population transfer to near saturation levels can be obtained with sufficient long term stability, as needed for state-resolved scattering experiments. We show preliminary results of CO molecules prepared in the $v$ = 1 state, scattering from a clean Cu(100) surface. This study showcases the promise of QCL based excitation for state-selected molecular beam based scattering experiments, especially involving transitions in the mid-infrared domain ($λ$ > 4.5 $μ$m) which are otherwise difficult to access using conventional sources.

articles.title: Pulsed Laser Deposition of Ferroelectric SrTiO3 Shells Enables Polarization-Controlled Charge Separation in TiO2 Photoanode
articles.abstract: Ferroelectric polarization offers a powerful route to govern the interfacial charge separation in photoelectrodes; however, chemically converted ferroelectric shells lack sub-nanometer thickness control, coherent strain retention, and chemically clean interfaces. Here, we use pulsed laser deposition to fabricate stoichiometric SrTiO3 shells on hydrothermally grown TiO2 nanorod arrays, achieving atomically defined core-shell architectures while preserving the one-dimensional transport geometry. The photocurrent density followed a volcano-shaped dependence on shell thickness and reached 1.9 mA cm-2 at 1.23 V versus RHE under AM 1.5G illumination for the optimized 15-mins sample, exceeding the established hydrothermal benchmark. High-resolution transmission electron microscopy and X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy revealed a tetragonally distorted, oxygen-stoichiometric shell, identifying coherent interfacial strain rather than defect dipoles as the origin of the ferroelectric order. Kelvin probe force microscopy directly imaged a polarization-induced built-in electric field whose magnitude scaled with charge-transfer efficiency and photocurrent density. Together, these complementary structural, chemical, electrostatic, and device-level measurements established a quantitative strain-polarization-built-in field-charge separation relationship. This work transforms ferroelectric photoanode engineering from empirical optimization into an atomically controllable and predictive materials strategy for high-efficiency solar water-splitting devices. This approach is readily extendable to visible-light absorbers and complex ferroelectric heterostructures.

articles.title: RPAx Instabilities from Ground- and Excited-State References
articles.abstract: Random-phase approximation with exchange (RPAx) calculations based on ground- or excited-state references can yield complex excitation energies, causing the corresponding RPAx correlation energy to become complex as well. In this work, we investigate the origin of these complex energies using \ce{H2} in the 6-31G basis set as a minimal model. For the ground-state restricted Hartree-Fock reference, complex roots emerge at the well-known triplet instability associated with the appearance of a lower-lying unrestricted, symmetry-broken solution. For excited-state references, we identify two distinct mechanisms leading to complex excitation energies. The first is similarly associated with symmetry breaking. The second arises when a positive-energy excitation becomes degenerate with the positive-energy de-excitation associated with a negative-energy transition. Finally, we demonstrate the practical implications of these findings for spin-flip Bethe-Salpeter equation calculations of cyclobutadiene and state-specific core-ionization calculations for selected systems. These examples show that, in the absence of the relevant instabilities, methods sharing the generalized eigenvalue structure of RPAx can be applied to excited-state references without resorting to the Tamm-Dancoff or core-valence separation approximations, while retaining real excitation energies.

articles.title: State-specific perturbation theory for configuration interaction singles: Theoretical analysis, benchmarks, and improvement with size-intensive level shifts
articles.abstract: We recently proposed a state-specific second-order perturbation theory based on the configuration interaction singles (CIS) state, termed CIS(2). Here, we clarify its theoretical connections, assess the accuracy of its excitation energies in greater detail, and develop size-intensive level shifts to improve both accuracy and convergence of its amplitude equations. We first derive the MP2 structure of its working equations and show that our previously introduced Hybrid partition recovers CIS(D) when the ground-state Fock operator is used and the residual Fock action on the CIS reference is neglected. For this partition, an expanded benchmark shows that using the CIS-state Fock operator improves Rydberg and especially charge-transfer accuracy relative to CIS(D), while slightly worsening valence accuracy. We analyze how the hole and particle densities contribute to these changes in excitation energy, which differ among the classes. We then introduce size-intensive level shifts that preserve the ground-state correlation contribution of noninteracting fragments while leaving the ground-state MP2 energy unchanged. With appropriately calibrated parameters, these shifts improve overall accuracy and substantially accelerate convergence without increasing the formal scaling of the amplitude solve. Different optimal parameters for valence and Rydberg states reveal the limitations of a common parameter. The analysis further shows that shifting the contracted-triples block contributes markedly to the excitation-energy correction in addition to accelerating convergence.

articles.title: Subpercent accuracy in molecular electric quadrupole coupling: nuclear-size and relativistic effects in RaF
articles.abstract: We report a benchmark study of the electric-quadrupole hyperfine interaction in the electronic ground state of the RaF molecule, including finite-nuclear-size effects. The calculations include relativistic effects using the Dirac-Coulomb-Breit Hamiltonian and electron correlation up to perturbative quadruple excitations within the coupled cluster framework. At the achieved level of accuracy, penetration of the electronic density into the finite nuclear quadrupole distribution produces a non-negligible correction to the usual electric field gradient (EFG) description at the center of the nucleus and must be considered. At a fixed rms charge radius, the EFG is much less sensitive to the shape of the monopole nuclear charge distribution: electron wavefunctions computed using the Gaussian and Fermi nuclear charge models yield nearly identical EFGs. The recommended effective EFG parameter for the $X\,{}^{2}Σ_{1/2}$ electronic ground state is $\langle q\rangle_0=-5.178(21)$ a.u., with an estimated uncertainty reduced by an order of magnitude compared to previous studies. Combined with future measurements of electric-quadrupole hyperfine coupling constants in RaF, this result can be used to determine the nuclear quadrupole moments of Ra isotopes with record precision.

articles.title: Why Emission Spectral Profile of Diverse Fluoro-phores Look Alike with Thick Polymer Overlayers?
articles.abstract: Fluorescence from fluorophore-polymer overlayers reflects an interplay between molecular photo-physics and thickness dependent optical propagation. Combining spectrally resolved single mole-cule measurements, transition dipole moment orientation analysis and ensemble fluorescence, we show that structurally and photophysically distinct fluorophores can exhibit similar red shifted emission profiles under thick polymer overlayers even without additional reflecting surface. This similarity indicates a common optical transfer function imposed by the overlayer rather than a pure-ly fluorophore specific molecular response. Although local molecular interactions, excited state dy-namics and vibronic coupling govern intrinsic emission, the overlayer modifies detected spectra through refractive index contrast, dielectric boundary reflections, cavity effects and collection ge-ometry. Vibronic energy spacing distributions remain largely preserved as thickness changes, whereas spectral positions and relative intensities vary systematically. Thus, polymer thickness pri-marily reshapes detected spectrum through optical propagation and outcoupling while retaining vi-brational modes. Time dependent density functional theory identifies candidate Franck-Condon and Herzberg-Teller active dye modes contributing to spectral fluctuations and dipole reorientation.

articles.title: Correction: Sequentially induced motor neurons from human fibroblasts facilitate locomotor recovery in a rodent spinal cord injury model
Genetic canalization of nutrient resorption in the widespread grass Phragmites australis under salt stress
articles.abstract: Nutrient resorption is a key plant strategy for nutrient conservation, yet whether it responds plastically to non-nutrient stressors such as salinity remains unresolved. Using a common garden experiment with 110 genotypes of the cosmopolitan grass Phragmites australis, we first established that the imposed salinity treatment induced strong multilevel stress responses: above-ground biomass declined by >60%, sodium accumulated three- to fivefold across all leaf stages, and 484 metabolites showed significant differential accumulation, including canonical markers of osmotic and oxidative stress. Against this backdrop of confirmed stress, we found that nutrient resorption efficiency (NuRE) remained largely unaffected by salinity. Instead, NuRE was strongly correlated with phylogeographic lineage, ecotype, and latitude of origin, demonstrating evolutionary canalization rather than short-term acclimation. Element-specific regulatory patterns were also evident: while phosphorus resorption followed concentration-dependent control regardless of stress, nitrogen control was disrupted under salinity, and potassium resorption showed no such dependence. Our findings reveal that intraspecific variation in nutrient resorption is predominantly shaped by historical adaptation and geographic context, not by plasticity to salinity. This genetic canalization of a key functional trait implies that predictions of nutrient cycling under global change must account for the phylogeographic composition of plant populations.

articles.title: Heterogeneous responses to embryonic critical period perturbations within the Drosophila larval locomotor circuit
articles.abstract: As developing neural circuits become functional, they undergo a phase of heightened plasticity that facilitates network tuning in response to intrinsic and/or extrinsic stimuli. These developmental windows are termed critical periods (CPs) because perturbations during but not outside the CP can lead to lasting changes, such as the formation of sub-optimal or unstable networks. How separate but connected elements within a network might respond differently to a CP perturbation is not well understood. To study this, we used the locomotor network of the Drosophila larva as a model and heat stress as a CP stimulus that has ecological relevance. When embryos experienced heat stress, the subsequent development of their locomotor network was changed, creating larvae with reduced crawling speed and decreased network stability. Developing body wall muscles and central neurons are sensitive to heat stress perturbations during distinct, consecutive phases of embryogenesis. Within the CNS, transient embryonic CP perturbation leads to increased synaptic drive from premotor interneurons to motoneurons, which in turn adopt reduced excitability. In contrast, the peripheral neuromuscular junction maintains normal synaptic transmission, despite significant structural changes. Thus, connected elements respond differentially to a CP perturbation, suggesting a sequence, or hierarchy of network adjustment during the CP.

articles.title: Improved cryo-EM reconstruction of sub-50 kDa complexes using 2D template matching
articles.abstract: Visualizing the structures of small proteins and complexes has been a longstanding challenge in single-particle cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM). Some of these targets have been successfully resolved by binding to antibody fragments (Fabs) or fusing with external scaffolds to increase their size. Recent advances in conventional single-particle techniques have enabled the determination of an increasing number of structures smaller than 100 kDa, achieving resolutions relevant to drug research. Compared to X-ray crystallography, cryo-EM preserves the near-native states of biomolecules, can resolve structural heterogeneity, and has the potential to apply to a wide range of targets. In this work, we demonstrate that the alignment and reconstruction of small macromolecular complexes can be improved using high-resolution structures as priors, combined with 2D template matching. Using this method, we reconstructed a previously intractable ∼43 kDa protein kinase and improved the density of its ligand-binding site. Our theoretical analysis predicts that this method can further extend single-particle cryo-EM to important drug-binding complexes well below 50 kDa.

articles.title: Mid-zone hepatocytes trade proliferation for survival via Atf4-Chop axis in early acute liver injury
articles.abstract: Hepatocytes undergo extensive proliferation to facilitate liver repair after injury, yet early adaptive changes prior to proliferation remain unclear. Using a mouse model of acetaminophen (APAP)-induced liver injury, we show that hepatocytes undergo transient proliferation suppression that is most pronounced in mid-zone hepatocytes, consistent with zonal APAP metabolism. Although spatial transcriptomics (ST) alone could not independently confirm zonal proliferative restraint, ST analysis identified a unique mid-zone stress-response program centered on the Atf4-Chop axis. By integrating Cut&Run with immunohistochemistry and functional studies, we found that the Atf4-Chop axis suppresses proliferation via the cell-cycle inhibitor Btg2. Together, our findings support a model in which mid-zone hepatocytes transiently prioritize stress adaptation over proliferation, thereby preserving regenerative capacity for subsequent liver repair.

articles.title: Open source laser-scanning photostimulation for neuroscience with Zapit
articles.abstract: Optogenetic tools are indispensable for understanding the causal neural mechanisms underlying animal behavior, providing millisecond-precision control over genetically defined neural populations. Random-access laser-scanning optogenetics is a powerful and underutilized method for transiently manipulating cortical activity in mice. Despite the utility of this technique, no general-purpose open-source implementation currently exists, and potential users need expertise across optics, real-time hardware control, and programming. This represents a major barrier to adoption, particularly for newly established research groups. Here we present ‘Zapit’, the first open-source general-purpose platform for random-access laser-scanning optogenetic experiments in head-fixed mice. Zapit is fully documented, has a user-friendly GUI, works in stereotaxic coordinates, and comes with easy-to-build hardware options that extend functionality beyond any published system. We validate Zapit’s performance through electrophysiological recordings and cortical photoinhibition in behaving mice. Zapit is a novel and innovative tool with the potential to democratize laser-scanning optogenetics and significantly increase uptake throughout the scientific community.

articles.title: SARS-CoV-2 main protease inhibition through dimerization promotion by peptidomimetic inhibitors and disruption by ebselen
articles.abstract: The SARS-CoV-2 main protease (Mpro) is a key antiviral target that equilibrates between an active dimer and inactive monomer, making the dimerization interface a promising therapeutic vulnerability. This study investigates Mpro monomer-dimer equilibrium and conformational changes induced by inhibitor binding using 13C labeling with native mass spectrometry and hydrogen/deuterium exchange mass spectrometry (HDX-MS). We evaluated how peptidomimetic inhibitors (PF-07321332, PF-00835231, GC376, boceprevir) and non-peptidomimetic inhibitors (carmofur, ebselen, MR6-31-2, AT7519, pelitinib) influence Mpro dimerization and subunit exchange. Key findings revealed divergent mechanisms: peptidomimetic inhibitors significantly shifted the equilibrium towards the dimeric state, suppressing subunit exchange dynamics and rigidifying the dimer interface; in contrast, ebselen impaired dimer formation and increased interface flexibility. Notably, tandem mass spectrometry identified a novel covalent binding site for ebselen at C300. Molecular dynamics simulations and mutational analyses demonstrated that this C300 modification allosterically alters the hydrogen bond network of the dimer interface, directly contributing to ebselen-mediated dimer disruption and enzymatic inhibition. Overall, this study clarifies distinct inhibitory modes between peptidomimetics and ebselen, highlighting the therapeutic potential of targeting allosteric sites at the dimer interface for designing next-generation Mpro inhibitors.

articles.title: Small brown planthopper infestation enhances it reproduction and insecticide tolerance by manipulating glucose distribution and levels in rice
articles.abstract: The evolutionary arms race between plants and insects involves not only direct defense and counter-defense but also sophisticated resource manipulation. However, how herbivorous insects respond to host nutritional signals to modulate their fitness traits remains unclear. This study investigates how the small brown planthopper (SBPH, Laodelphax striatellus) manipulates host plant carbohydrate allocation, and to elucidate the molecular mechanisms by which the acquired glucose enhances SBPH fecundity and insecticide tolerance. Using molecular, pharmacological, and biochemical approaches, we found that SBPH infestation induced systemic carbohydrate reallocation in rice, elevating whole-plant glucose levels by promoting aerial accumulation while depleting root reserves. Host-derived glucose enhanced SBPH fecundity by activating the target of rapamycin (TOR) pathway, upregulating juvenile hormone (JH) signaling, and increasing vitellogenin production. For imidacloprid tolerance, glucose boosted glutathione S-transferase (GST) activity via two synergistic mechanisms: by upregulating glutamate cysteine ligase (GCL) to increase glutathione synthesis, and transcriptionally via the glucose-TOR-JH axis to induce LsGSTe1 (SBPH epsilon class GST) and LsGSTo1 (SBPH omega class GST) expression. Our findings establish host-derived glucose as a central signaling molecule that SBPH utilizes to modulate conserved pathways for simultaneous optimization of reproduction and insecticide resistance. This reveals a multifaceted nutrient-responsive mechanism in insect pests and identifies the glucose-TOR-JH axis as critical molecular targets for developing nutrient-based pest control strategies, such as disrupting insect nutrient-sensing pathways or modulating host carbohydrate metabolism.

articles.title: The transcription factor BCL11A restores differentiation potential to aged oligodendrocyte progenitor cells
articles.abstract: In young animals, oligodendrocyte progenitor cells (OPCs) in the CNS efficiently differentiate into myelinating oligodendrocytes (OLs), whereas ageing reduces this capacity, impairing remyelination following demyelinating injury and adaptive myelination involved in learning. To identify factors that restore resilience in aged OPCs, we developed gSWITCH (https://altoslabs.shinyapps.io/gSWITCH/, https://github.com/Tanay-math/gSWITCH), a computational pipeline that captures dynamic gene-expression patterns to identify ‘switch’ genes during lineage progression and ordered biological transitions, including time-series experiments. gSWITCH identified OPC-characteristic switch genes, which we compared between young and aged OPCs to determine whether their regulation is altered with ageing. This revealed several transcription factors with reduced expression in aged OPCs. Transcription-factor binding-site enrichment highlighted Bcl11a as a potential master-regulator of multiple switch genes. Bcl11a inhibition reduced OPC differentiation into OLs, whereas its overexpression in aged OPCs significantly enhanced OL differentiation without affecting proliferation. In aged mice subjected to demyelination injury in spinal cord white matter, Bcl11a overexpression increased OPC differentiation within lesions. We found that Bcl11a has undergone pervasive purifying selection throughout vertebrate evolution, preserving its amino acid sequence by eliminating deleterious mutations. Our study shows that reversing the age-related decline of this evolutionarily conserved factor in aged OPCs restores their impaired capacity for differentiation.

articles.title: Data-Driven Investigation of Asymmetric Photo-Organocatalyzed Alkylation of Indoles
articles.abstract: Enantioselective dual catalysis represents a powerful strategy for the preparation of functionally dense optically active compounds. Photocatalysis, paired with organocatalysis, undeniably represents a popular choice that takes advantage of radical and polar reactivity for crafting challenging bonds. Despite the interest in this methodology, the detailed analysis of the effects governing selectivity between the two catalytic cycles has not been extensively studied. Herein, we report a data-driven mechanistic study campaign to disclose the factors that influence the enantioselectivity of a photo-organocatalytic alkylation of indoles. Data science tools were used to generate a virtual library of potential substrates, thus ensuring the selection of a statistically diverse training set. Subsequent multivariate linear regression (MLR) analysis led to the identification of substrate electronic features as the key factor affecting the stereochemical outcome. Moreover, comprehensive mechanistic experiments unveiled the key role of the in situ generated oxindole intermediate that connects the two catalytic cycles in determining the observed selectivity. These findings lay the foundation for developing asymmetric dual catalytic transformations of synthetic relevance and provide a general platform for interrogating other complex catalytic systems.

articles.title: Photoredox-Mediated Three-Component Carboamination of Reverse Exo -Glycals: Modular Access to C 4-Quaternary Furanosides and Spironucleosides
articles.abstract: Quaternary stereocenters on densely functionalized furanoside frameworks are challenging to construct with high chemo-, regio-, and stereocontrol, especially in the presence of nitrogen-containing motifs and multiple downstream diversification handles. Here, we disclose a sequence-programmed three-component radical carboamination of reverse exo-glycals that provides modular access to C4-quaternary furanosides through a distinct radical retrosynthetic logic. In this photoredox process, an N-centered radical adds to an electron-rich reverse exo-glycal to form a pseudo-anomeric radical, which is then intercepted by a Giese acceptor, enabling concomitant C–N and C–C bond formation in a single step. The protocol accommodates diverse N-radical precursors and electron-deficient alkenes, is further extendable to distinct pyranose- and furanose-derived reverse exo-glycals, supports late-stage glyco-functionalization of structurally complex molecules, and furnishes a spiro-glycosyl donor on preparative scale. Subsequent Vorbrüggen glycosylation enables divergent entry to structurally distinct spironucleosides. Preliminary biological profiling of these compounds reveals a modest antiviral signal against influenza A (PR8) at 50 μM, supporting the utility of this platform for probing underexplored spironucleoside chemical space. Mechanistic experiments support the proposed photoredox-mediated radical relay, while DFT studies provide a plausible basis for the contrasting reactivity of representative N-radical precursors. Collectively, this work offers a concise and programmable strategy for the synthesis of quaternary-center furanosides and their downstream spirocyclic derivatives from readily available carbohydrate feedstocks.

articles.title: Quantum Chemical Insight into Species Competition in Electrochemical Upgrading of Bio-Oil
articles.abstract: Bio-oil derived from lignocellulosic biomass represents an alternative to fossil fuels as an energy source and chemical feedstock. Fast pyrolysis of lignocellulosic biomass yields a rich mixture of oxygenated organic species with low energy density and low stability, which can be electrochemically upgraded to increase energy density and stability and produce value-added chemicals. Here, we focus on electrocatalytic hydrotreatment of furfural (FF) and 4-propylphenol (4-PP), two constituents of raw bio-oil. In a binary mixture, the presence of FF has been shown to inhibit the reduction of 4-PP. The underlying mechanisms of these competing reactions are probed using density functional theory (DFT) and experimental electrochemical deposition techniques. The binding energies of FF and 4-PP, as well as their respective reduction products and associated reaction thermodynamics, are examined comparatively on multiple facets of single-crystal platinum and ruthenium catalysts. FF is shown to bind competitively compared to 4-PP, particularly on Pt(111) and Ru(0001), and hydrogenation products such as tetrahydrofurfuryl alcohol (THFA) and 4-propylcyclohexanol (4-PCOL) were found to bind less strongly to the surfaces than the reactants. FF reduction side products, including dimers furoin (FUI) and hydrofuroin (HF), were also found to bind competitively with 4-PP. No thermodynamic barriers were observed for FF hydrogenation to THFA, whereas 4-PCOL formation is favored on Pt facets, and propylcyclohexane (PC) formation is favored on Ru. The presence of barriers to 4-PP hydrogenation indicates that FF hydrogenation is thermodynamically favored on Pt and Ru. Further, limiting potential calculations suggest that the FF reduction pathways are generally favorable around 0 V vs. RHE. In contrast, the 4-PP reduction pathways require a more cathodic bias, achieved at potentials less than -0.1 V vs. RHE. The adsorption behavior of FF-derived reduction products on polycrystalline Pt is experimentally validated using a Quartz Crystal Microbalance (QCM). Such experiments yield estimates of aqueous-phase free energies of adsorption, which are compared with computational results that are correlated to the aqueous phase. Overall, the DFT model results suggest that the observed inhibition of 4-PP by FF is due to competitive adsorption and favorable FF reaction thermodynamics.

articles.title: Alicyclic Lewis Bases Enable 100 °C-Processed α-FAPbI3 Inverted Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Formamidinium lead iodide (α-FAPbI3) perovskite, despite its ideal bandgap, requires high-temperature (≥150 °C) annealing for the δ-to-α phase transformation, hindering its application in low-temperature processed inverted perovskite solar cells (PSCs), particularly on flexible substrates. Herein, we demonstrate that the alicyclic Lewis base caprolactam (CPL) effectively drives the complete δ-to-α phase transformation of FAPbI3 at a reduced temperature of 100 °C. Experiments and theoretical calculations reveal that CPL lowers the phase transition energy barrier and retards crystallization kinetics via strong Pb2+ coordination and controlled desorption. This strategy yields highly crystalline, fully phase-converted α-FAPbI3 films with improved morphology, reduced defect densities, and enhanced optoelectronic properties. Consequently, CPL-modified inverted PSCs achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.64% with good operational stability. The low-temperature processability also enables high-performance flexible PSCs with a PCE of 23.73%. This work presents an additive engineering approach for realizing efficient and stable α-FAPbI3 PSCs through low-temperature manufacturing.

articles.title: Dual Functions of Halogen-Bonding Molecules for Stabilizing Ultra-wide Bandgap Perovskite Solar Cells
articles.abstract: Ultra-wide-bandgap (UWBG) metal halide perovskite solar cells are essential for multi-junction solar cells with higher power conversion efficiency (PCE) potentials. In this work, we report the dual functions of 5-iodoisophthalic acid (I-BDC) to suppress phase segregation and uncoordinated Pb2+ related defects to enhance UWBG perovskite cell performance and stability. An I-BDC incorporated 1.95 eV perovskite film exhibited stable photoluminescence after 120 min of illumination. The best I-BDC cell achieved a certified reverse scan PCE of 16.5%, the highest for 1.95 eV perovskite cells to date. These UWBG perovskite solar cells are the most stable reported to date, with one encapsulated device retaining 90% of its initial PCE after 500 h of maximum power point tracking at ∼40 °C and another retaining 95% of its initial PCE after 206 thermal cycles (–40 ↔ 85 °C), passing the International Electrotechnical Commission (IEC) 61215 testing protocols at the cell level.

articles.title: Making 1000 Wh/kg LiNiO2 Cathode Nearly Strain-Free by Complex-Concentrated Doping
articles.abstract: High-energy batteries require cathodes with greater capacity and specific energy. Ni-rich-layered oxides approach the performance limit of LiNiO2 (LNO), yet its practical use is hindered by severe chemomechanical degradation. Near 4.2 V, the H2-H3/H4 transition drives substantial c-axis contraction, volume shrinkage, O1 formation, oxygen loss, and rapid capacity decay. Here, we show that only 5% cobalt-free complex concentrated doping stabilizes LNO without sacrificing energy density. The modified LNO reduces c-axis strain from 7.4 to 2.1%, exhibits near-zero-strain behavior, and delivers 258 mAh•g–1 and 973 Wh•kg–1. In pouch cells, it retains 80% capacity after 1800 cycles and shows markedly improved thermal stability. These results demonstrate that complex-concentrated doping at low dopant loading can suppress strain and phase transformations at the full-Ni limit, providing a broadly applicable strategy for stabilizing high-energy intercalation electrodes while preserving their intrinsic capacity and specific energy during prolonged electrochemical cycling.

articles.title: rGO-MXene 2D Interfacial Engineering for Enhanced Efficiency and Stability of Perovskite Solar Cells and Modules
articles.abstract: In this work, we report an innovative interface engineering strategy combining bidirectional chemical anchoring and electronic bridging via a 2D reduced graphene oxide (rGO) and MXene conductive network. This hierarchical 2D structure suppresses the aggregation and stacking of single-layer MXene nanosheets while mutually compensating for individual charge transport limitations. Specifically, the abundant functional groups passivate interfacial defects (Pb2+ and I–) and bond with the PCBM layer via coordination, hydrogen bonding and π–π interactions. This synergistic architecture lowers the electron energy offset. Consequently, PSCs incorporating the rGO-MXene interlayer achieve a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 25.96% (certified 25.05%) and retain 96.43% of initial efficiency after 1000 h in ambient air. Furthermore, 10 × 10 cm2 large-area PSM yields a high PCE of 20.25%, maintaining 96.05% of initial efficiency under maximum power point tracking for 963 h.

articles.title: Phase Homogenization via Decoupled Nucleation and Growth for High-Efficiency Quasi-Two-Dimensional Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes
articles.abstract: Quasi-two-dimensional (quasi-2D) perovskites with multiquantum-well structures hold great potential for light-emitting diodes (LEDs) due to their cascaded energy funnels, yet their performance is hampered by defect-rich low-n phases and disordered crystallization. Here, we present a phase-homogenization strategy that combines a self-adaptive solvent by doping ethyl acetate (EA) with dimethyl phosphonate (DPP), which simultaneously modulates the polarity and evaporation kinetics of EA, guiding the crystal growth and phase distribution of quasi-2D perovskites. The strong coordination of DPP with Pb2+ also passivates deep-level traps, thereby drastically reducing nonradiative low-n-phase recombination. We further use the bridging molecules to enhance perovskite/transport layer interfaces by incorporating sodium 4-amino-1-naphthalenesulfonate tetrahydrate (SANT) into the PEDOT/PSS hole transport layer, which weakens PEDOT–PSS electrostatic attraction, enhancing conductivity while reducing acid-induced corrosion of the ITO electrode and perovskite film. SANT also templates perovskite nucleation via its functional groups, promoting ordered crystallite growth. Overall, the resulting green-emitting quasi-2D perovskite LEDs achieve a peak external quantum efficiency (EQE) of 32.81% (average 30.74%) and a luminance of 44338 cd m–2, with a lower surface temperature during operation. Moreover, the devices exhibit a 10-fold enhancement in operational stability compared to the control counterparts. Our findings provide a strategy for combining crystallization control and interface passivation in quasi-2D PeLEDs.

articles.title: Synergistic Tuning of Diffusion Enables Surface-Passivation-Directed Electrodeposition of Shaped Bimetallic Nanoparticles
articles.abstract: Many applications for shape-controlled metal nanoparticles require their immobilization on a surface, creating a need for development of direct substrate-based synthesis routes for increasingly complex materials. Colloidal chemical syntheses for shape-controlled nanoparticles are common, but transferring insight from synthesis in solution to growth on a substrate requires accounting for significant differences in reagent diffusion between these two growth environments─a nontrivial challenge. In the present work, we establish fundamental principles for rationally adapting reaction parameters from colloidal syntheses to electrodeposition such that the growth of nanoparticles on the electrode proceeds under comparable reagent diffusion conditions to those that drive shape direction during colloidal growth. To demonstrate these principles, we successfully translate reaction conditions from colloidal synthesis to electrodeposition for a series of dilute bimetallic (silver) gold nanoparticles whose shapes are controlled by surface deposition of silver: concave cubes, octahedra, rhombic dodecahedra, truncated ditetragonal prisms, and tetrahexahedra. By comparing open-circuit potential measurements of the colloidal syntheses with chronopotentiometry measurements from galvanostatic electrodeposition, we determine the adjustments required to establish ideal growth kinetics for each electrodeposition. We identify specific synthetic handles─mode of mass transport, surfactant concentration, applied current density, and secondary metal concentration─required to modulate reagent transport to the electrode surface, as well as the direction they must be modified so that the relative rates of silver and gold ion reduction mimic colloidal growth. These generalizable synthetic parameters for controlling reagent diffusion and concentrations near the electrode surface open possibilities for the electrodeposition of complex multimetallic and shaped nanomaterials.

articles.title: A systematic review of deforestation outcomes in potential other effective area‐based conservation measures across Latin America
articles.abstract: Recognizing conservation contributions from areas outside protected areas (PAs), including other effective area‐based conservation measures (OECMs), is increasingly central to meeting global biodiversity targets. However, little is known about which areas could qualify as OECMs and whether they support forest conservation. Focusing on Latin America, we conducted a systematic literature review following the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta‐Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines synthesizing 93 peer‐reviewed studies published through 2024 that assess the effectiveness of OECMs outside formal PA systems in reducing deforestation. First, we identified and classified area‐based measures that may qualify as potential OECMs into six types based on their conservation objectives and characteristics: strict biodiversity conservation areas, set‐aside areas for ecosystem services, Indigenous peoples’ territories, local communities’ territories, other managed sustainable‐use areas, and ancillary conservation areas. Second, we synthesized the available evidence on their effectiveness in reducing deforestation. Indigenous people's territories were the most frequently evaluated, whereas strict biodiversity conservation areas have received relatively little attention. Methodologically, most evidence relied on nonexperimental comparisons of forest‐cover trends; quasi‐experimental designs were less common but provide stronger causal inference of conservation effectiveness. Disaggregating outcomes by comparator type revealed important patterns: Indigenous territories most consistently showed reduced deforestation relative to both PAs and non‐PAs, whereas local communities’ territories showed more favorable outcomes relative to non‐PAs than to PAs. Set‐aside areas for ecosystem services showed predominantly negative outcomes, largely reflecting weak enforcement. Despite this evidence base, very few of these areas have been formally recognized as OECMs, highlighting a disconnect between available research and reporting under the Kunming–Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. Bridging this gap will require stronger causal evidence, broader geographic coverage, and inclusive recognition processes that account for the governance rights of those who manage these territories. Una revisión sistemática de los resultados de deforestación en otras medidas potenciales de la conservación basada en el área en América Latina Resumen Reconocer las contribuciones a la conservación procedentes de zonas ajenas a las áreas protegidas (AP), incluidas otras medidas de conservación basadas en el territorio (OECM), es cada vez más fundamental para alcanzar los objetivos mundiales en materia de biodiversidad. Sin embargo, se sabe poco sobre qué zonas podrían considerarse OECM y si contribuyen a la conservación de los bosques. Nos enfocamos en América Latina para llevar a cabo una revisión bibliográfica sistemática según las directrices de los Elementos Preferidos para la Elaboración de Informes de Revisiones Sistemáticas y Metaanálisis (PRISMA), en la que se sintetizan 93 estudios revisados por pares publicados hasta 2024 que evalúan la eficacia de las OECM fuera de los sistemas formales de áreas protegidas para reducir la deforestación. En primer lugar, identificamos y clasificamos las medidas basadas en áreas que podrían considerarse OECM potenciales en seis tipos, según sus objetivos y características de conservación: áreas de conservación estricta de la biodiversidad, áreas reservadas para servicios ambientales, territorios de pueblos indígenas, territorios de comunidades locales, otras áreas gestionadas para el uso sostenible y áreas de conservación auxiliares. En segundo lugar, sintetizamos la evidencia disponible sobre su eficacia para reducir la deforestación.…

articles.title: Fifteen years of change in biodiversity conservation across Latin America and the Caribbean
articles.abstract: Latin America and the Caribbean (LACA) is one of the most biodiverse regions globally, yet it continues to experience accelerated biodiversity loss driven by persistent and emerging anthropogenic pressures. In 2009, the Society for Conservation Biology conducted a regional assessment of conservation challenges; however, the evolution of these dynamics over the following 15 years had not been systematically reassessed. We conducted an updated regional synthesis of biodiversity conservation priorities, perceived threats, and implementation barriers across 25 countries, based on a 2024 survey of conservation professionals (n = 244). Respondents were predominantly experienced practitioners affiliated with academic institutions, nongovernmental organizations, and government agencies. Our findings were consistent with the patterns reported in 2009, with deforestation, habitat fragmentation, industrial agriculture, climate change, and pollution persisting as the most severe threats. However, these traditional drivers are now compounded by the intensification of landscape‐scale pressures and a marked shift toward the security–conservation nexus. Respondents explicitly identified organized crime and drug trafficking as primary constraints that compromise both ecosystem integrity and the safety of practitioners. Although conservation tools, such as protected areas and environmental policies, have diversified and improved in many ways, their effectiveness remains limited by a diversification without consolidation trend, characterized by chronic underfunding, corruption, and weak intersectoral coordination. Furthermore, engagement with local communities and citizen science remains predominantly low to moderate, highlighting an enduring gap between policy design and on‐the‐ground implementation. This study underscores that addressing biodiversity loss in LACA has moved beyond the need for technical solutions; it now requires a fundamental transformation in governance quality, institutional integrity, and state capacity to protect the region's natural heritage and the communities that depend on it. Quince años de cambios en la conservación de la biodiversidad en América Latina y el Caribe Resumen América Latina y el Caribe (ALC) es una de las regiones con mayor biodiversidad del mundo; sin embargo, todavía experimenta una pérdida acelerada de biodiversidad impulsada por presiones antropogénicas persistentes y emergentes. En 2009, la Sociedad para la Biología de la Conservación (Society for Conservation Biology) llevó a cabo una evaluación regional de los desafíos de conservación; no obstante, la evolución de estas dinámicas durante los 15 años posteriores no ha sido reevaluada de manera sistemática. Realizamos una síntesis regional actualizada sobre las prioridades de conservación de la biodiversidad, las amenazas percibidas y las barreras para la implementación en 25 países, con base en una encuesta a profesionales de la conservación (n = 244) en 2024. Los encuestados eran mayormente profesionales experimentados afiliados a instituciones académicas, organizaciones no gubernamentales y organismos gubernamentales. Nuestros resultados coincidieron con los patrones reportados en 2009, con la deforestación, la fragmentación del hábitat, la agricultura industrial, el cambio climático y la contaminación como las amenazas más graves. Sin embargo, a estos factores tradicionales se suman ahora la intensificación de presiones a escala de paisaje y un cambio marcado hacia el nexo entre seguridad y conservación. Los encuestados señalaron explícitamente al crimen organizado y al narcotráfico como los principales factores que comprometen tanto la integridad de los ecosistemas como la seguridad de quienes trabajan en el campo.…

articles.title: Systematic mapping of monitoring and evaluation in rewilding
articles.abstract: Rewilding is a landscape recovery approach that seeks to enhance the functioning of degraded ecosystems by reinstating natural processes, and it is increasingly being adopted by organizations and landowners. Despite its popularity, there is no accepted way to assess rewilding's impacts, which is due in part to inconsistent monitoring and evaluation. To address this gap, we developed a systematic map of a unique dataset combining academic and gray literature on monitoring and evaluation in rewilding case studies. We mapped definitions of success, study systems, methods of monitoring, and evaluation metrics for rewilding case studies to compare where the different strands of literature overlap and contrast in focus. We found that researchers and practitioners have been focused on different aspects of rewilding and that the limited recording of case study details and lack of robust experimental design make it difficult to pool and compare data. Researchers and rewilding practitioners face challenges in building a robust evidence base from which to evaluate rewilding outcomes. These challenges include resources as well as spatial and time constraints, which all limit the consistency of data gathering among projects. More comparisons across rewilding projects, better standardization of data collection and data recording methods, and increased collaboration between researchers and practitioners could help remedy these limitations. We developed recommendations for how to monitor and evaluate rewilded landscapes to improve data quality and availability. These include the broad adoption of low‐cost and scalable survey designs with greater focus on comparisons across sites and continued effort toward open‐source data storage. Mapeo sistemático del monitoreo y la evaluación en la renaturalización Resumen La renaturalización es un enfoque de recuperación del paisaje que busca mejorar el funcionamiento de los ecosistemas degradados mediante el restablecimiento de los procesos naturales. Cada vez son más las organizaciones y propietarios de terrenos quienes lo adoptan. A pesar de su popularidad, no existe una forma consensuada de sus impactos, lo que se debe, en parte, a la falta de coherencia en el seguimiento y la evaluación. Para subsanar esta carencia, elaboramos un mapa sistemático a partir de un conjunto único de datos que combina literatura académica y «literatura gris» sobre el seguimiento y la evaluación en casos prácticos de renaturalización. Recopilamos las definiciones de éxito, los sistemas de estudio, los métodos de seguimiento y los indicadores de evaluación de los casos prácticos de renaturalización para comparar en qué aspectos coinciden y en cuáles difieren las distintas corrientes de la literatura. Verificamos que los investigadores y los profesionales se centraran en diferentes aspectos de la renaturalización y que el registro limitado de los detalles de los casos prácticos, junto con la falta de un diseño experimental sólido, dificulta la recopilación y la comparación de datos. Los investigadores y los profesionales de la renaturalización enfrentan retos a la hora de crear una base empírica sólida a partir de la cual evaluar los resultados de la renaturalización. Entre estos retos se encuentran la falta de recursos, así como las limitaciones espaciales y temporales, que restringen la coherencia en la recopilación de datos entre los distintos proyectos. Un mayor número de comparaciones entre proyectos de renaturalización, una mejor estandarización de los métodos de recopilación y registro de datos, y una mayor colaboración entre investigadores y profesionales podrían ayudar a subsanar estas limitaciones. Proponemos una serie de recomendaciones sobre cómo supervisar y evaluar los paisajes sometidos a renaturalización para mejorar la calidad y la disponibilidad de los datos.…

articles.title: Characterization of the First Complete Plastome of Zingiber emeiense: Insights Into Its Phylogenetic Position
articles.abstract: Zingiber emeiense Z. Y. Zhu is an endemic medicinal species restricted to Mount Emei in southwestern China. However, the lack of genomic resources has led to its frequent misclassification and has impeded evolutionary studies. Here, we assembled and characterized the first two complete chloroplast genomes (plastomes) of Z. emeiense. The two plastomes were identical in sequence and structure, each with a total length of 163,865 bp and exhibiting a typical quadripartite structure. Each plastome comprised a large single‐copy (LSC) region of 88,191 bp, a small single‐copy (SSC) region of 15,750 bp, and a pair of inverted repeats (IR) of 29,962 bp each. Each genome encoded 134 functional genes, including 86 protein‐coding genes, 40 tRNA genes, and eight rRNA genes, with an overall GC content of 36.04%. Comparative plastome analyses revealed that IR boundary variation and repeat sequence differences were major sources of genome size variation within Zingiber. Seven hypervariable regions (psbM, trnT‐UGU, ycf1, petA‐psbJ, ndhF, psaC‐ndhE, and rps19) were identified as potential molecular markers. Likelihood‐based selection analyses revealed that plastid gene evolution was primarily driven by purifying selection, but ten genes showed signatures of positive selection; ycf1, petD, and rpl2 exhibited lineage‐specific positive selection on the Z. emeiense clade. Phylogenomic reconstruction based on 70 complete plastomes placed Z. emeiense within sect. Cryptanthium, where it was strongly supported as a sister clade to Zingiber smilesianum and Zingiber teres. This study provides essential genomic resources for conservation and taxonomic studies of this endemic species.

articles.title: Complete Chloroplast Genome of Nepeta griffithii and Comparative Genomics of 10 Nepeta Species
articles.abstract: Nepeta L. (Lamiaceae) is an ecologically and medicinally important genus, yet complete cp genome resources are available for fewer than 10 of the approximately 300 accepted species, with western Himalayan taxa almost entirely unrepresented. Here, we sequenced, assembled, and annotated the complete cp genome of Nepeta griffithii and compared it with nine previously published Nepeta cp genomes. The 10 cp genomes exhibited a highly conserved quadripartite structure, with genome sizes ranging from 151,254 to 152,348 bp, and contained 113 unique genes (79 protein‐coding, 30 tRNA, 4 rRNA). Gene content, guanine‐cytosine content, intron features, and inverted repeat contraction and expansion were highly conserved. SSR analysis identified 387 repeats across the 10 cp genomes, predominantly mononucleotide A/T motifs in intergenic spacers, yielding candidate cpSSR markers for population‐level studies. Codon usage analysis revealed a strong bias toward A/T‐ending codons, with leucine as the most frequent amino acid. Nucleotide diversity analysis showed intergenic spacers were more variable than both introns and genic regions. Highly polymorphic loci, including ccsA‐ndhD, rpl32‐trnL‐UAG, and ndhG‐ndhI, were identified as candidate markers for phylogenetic and population studies. Maximum likelihood phylogeny based on 79 concatenated protein‐coding genes recovered a well‐resolved topology within Nepeta and placed N. griffithii as sister to N. nuda with maximal bootstrap support of 100%. This study provides the first complete cp genome for N. griffithii, improves plastome sampling within the genus, and offers genomic markers for species identification, systematics, and evolutionary studies.

articles.title: p‐Values Are Not Evidence: Navigating the Gap Across Modes of Inference
articles.abstract: The use of p‐values and statistical significance testing as the primary mode of inference in science has been long debated among statisticians and more recently among ecologists. Ecological literature has discussed embracing other modes of inference, such as Bayesian statistics and the use of direct likelihood inference. We reviewed ecology, evolution, and environmental science literature covering the past three decades to investigate trends in the use of different modes of inference over time and to assess the degree of discrepancy between reported p‐values and calculated likelihood ratios. p‐Values and likelihood ratios were found to scale in a more direct way for single degree of freedom tests, but in a more complex manner for models with more than one parameter. These results demonstrate the degree to which the likelihood ratio (a measure of evidence) differs from a p‐value, a measure of uncertainty that is widely presented as a measure of evidence among publications within the fields of ecology and evolution. Additionally, our investigation revealed that modes of inference within ecological studies changed little over the 20‐year time period, indicating a failure to adopt alternative modes of inference. We also found downward trends in the reporting of p‐value thresholds (e.g., “p < 0.05”) in two journals, with no change in three others. The prevalence of the divergence in the measure of evidence and the p‐value measure of uncertainty remains to be confirmed in other journals, time points, and subfields. An overreliance on p‐values alone can alter the conclusions drawn from research, impacting management of species and ecosystems. We recommend that authors report both a measure of evidence and uncertainty, and justify their mode of inference in an attempt to produce statistical results that are comprehensive, replicable, and reliably interpretable.

Elevated nitrogen deposition protects an invasive plant from herbivory through altering leaf volatile‐mediated tritrophic interactions
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Atmospheric nitrogen deposition disrupts plant–herbivore interactions, but its impact on leaf volatile organic compounds (VOCs)‐mediated multi‐trophic herbivore resistance remains unclear within the context of plant invasion. In this study, we initially investigated the differences in leaf feeding damage and number of eggs laid by herbivores between the invasive weed Alternanthera philoxeroides and its native congener, Alternanthera sessilis, in different terrestrial habitats that experienced various levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Furthermore, we compared the quantity and composition of leaf constitutive plant volatiles (CPVs) and herbivore‐induced plant volatiles (HIPVs) between the two plant species under simulated nitrogen deposition and tested olfactory and oviposition responses of herbivores and natural enemies at multi‐trophic levels. Field surveys showed less consumed leaf area and fewer herbivore eggs laid on A. philoxeroides than on A. sessilis in terrestrial habitats experiencing high levels of atmospheric nitrogen deposition. Laboratory bioassays revealed that simulated nitrogen deposition increased the emission and altered the composition of both CPVs and HIPVs in A. philoxeroides compared with A. sessilis. These changes reduced its attractiveness to specialist and generalist herbivores while enhancing its appeal to predatory beetles. Methyl salicylate was identified as the key compound driving these changes in insect behaviours, highlighting its critical role in mediating plant–insect interactions in A. philoxeroides under elevated nitrogen deposition. Synthesis. These findings suggest that leaf VOC‐mediated multi‐trophic interactions may facilitate A. philoxeroides invasion success under elevated atmospheric nitrogen deposition in this specific study system, providing a mechanistic basis for understanding how nitrogen enrichment could influence plant–herbivore–predator interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. 摘要 大气氮沉降会干扰植物–植食性昆虫的相互作用，但其在植物入侵背景下对叶片挥发性有机化合物介导的多营养级抗虫性的影响仍不清楚。 本研究首先调查了在不同大气氮沉降水平的陆生生境中，入侵杂草空心莲子草与其本土同属种莲子草在叶片取食损伤程度和植食性昆虫产卵数量上的差异。随后，我们比较了模拟氮沉降条件下两种植物的叶片组成型植物挥发物和虫害诱导型植物挥发物的数量与组成，并测试了多营养级水平上植食性昆虫和天敌的嗅觉与产卵反应。 野外调查表明，在大气氮沉降水平较高的陆生生境中，与莲子草相比，空心莲子草被取食的叶面积更小、植食性昆虫在其上产卵数量更少。室内生物测定显示，与莲子草相比，模拟氮沉降增加了空心莲子草叶片组成型和虫害诱导型挥发物的释放量并改变了其组成。这些变化降低了其对专食性和广食性植食性昆虫的吸引力，同时增强了其对捕食性甲虫的吸引力。水杨酸甲酯被鉴定为驱动这些昆虫行为变化的关键化合物，凸显了其在模拟氮沉降条件下空心莲子草–昆虫相互作用中的关键介导作用。 综合而言，这些发现表明，在该特定研究系统中，叶片挥发物介导的多营养级相互作用可能促进了高氮沉降条件下空心莲子草的入侵成功，为理解氮富集如何影响植物–植食性昆虫–捕食者相互作用提供了机制基础。

By-layer covalent organic structure as a metal-free PCET catalyst for efficient oxygen evolution in alkaline and neutral media
Synergistic catalysis between Mo2C and acid sites of NbOx toward efficient catalytic transfer hydrogenation
Seed‐derived microbiota in the Medicago holobiont: Associations with host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits
articles.abstract: Seed‐derived bacterial communities tracked host phylogeny across wild Medicago, revealing a phylosymbiotic pattern, whereas fungal communities did not. In cultivated alfalfa, bacterial composition differed between cultivars with high‐yielding and stress‐resistant traits. Trait‐associated bacterial SynComs improved plant growth under non‐stress or combined drought–salinity conditions, respectively, demonstrating the functional relevance of breeding‐associated microbiota. Abstract Seed microbiota occupy unique ecological niches within plants and can form intimate associations with their hosts. However, how seed‐derived microbial communities are related to host phylogeny and breeding‐associated traits across natural and agricultural contexts, and whether trait‐associated microorganisms influence plant performance, remain poorly understood. Here, we characterized endophytic communities in sterile‐grown seedlings from surface‐sterilized seeds of 10 wild Medicago genotypes representing 8 species and 20 domesticated alfalfa cultivars spanning multiple breeding decades. We assessed phylosymbiosis in wild hosts, examined associations between microbial community composition and breeding‐related cultivar characteristics in domesticated alfalfa, and constructed trait‐associated bacterial synthetic communities (SynComs) for functional evaluation. In wild Medicago, bacterial, but not fungal, community composition exhibited significant congruence with host phylogeny, consistent with phylosymbiosis. In domesticated alfalfa, bacterial community composition was associated with cultivar trait category (high‐yielding vs. stress‐resistant), whereas fungal communities were not. Six cultivable candidate bacterial strains associated with the two trait categories were assembled into two SynComs, SynComY (high‐yielding associated) and SynComR (stress‐resistance‐associated). In vitro assays revealed multiple plant growth‐promoting and stress‐tolerance capacities among the constituent strains, while greenhouse experiments showed that SynComY promoted plant growth and SynComR enhanced plant performance under combined drought–salinity stress. Synthesis. Together, these findings show that seed‐derived bacterial community structure is associated with host phylogeny in wild Medicago and breeding‐related trait differentiation in cultivated alfalfa, and further establish that selected bacteria associated with the latter can influence plant performance. Viewed within a holobiont framework, this combined evidence broadens our understanding of seed‐derived microbiota across natural and agricultural contexts and highlights their potential value for microbiome‐informed crop improvement.

articles.title: How the TREX-2 complex associates with the nuclear pore
articles.abstract: Obarska-Kosinska et al. combine cryo-electron tomography, AI-assisted modeling, and crosslinking mass spectrometry to build an extended model of the human nuclear pore. They identify five additional nucleoporins and show how the nuclear basket and TREX-2 complex are attached to the nuclear ring, revealing the spatial organization of mRNP export.

articles.title: Genomic Signatures of Endemic Pathogen Exposure in a Declining Amphibian
articles.abstract: Endemic wildlife diseases can impose strong selection on threatened populations, yet whether persistence is associated with adaptive genomic responses remains poorly understood. We tested whether long‐term exposure to Batrachochytrium dendrobatidis (Bd) following population declines has left detectable selection signatures in the genome of the alpine tree frog, Litoria verreauxii alpina. Because prior work suggests limited immunity to Bd within the species, we did not expect persistence to be explained primarily by repeated shifts at canonical immune genes. Instead, we expected pathogen‐associated differentiation, if present, to be diffuse and weakly shared across contrasts, potentially involving regulatory, signalling or reproduction pathways consistent with tolerance, compensatory recruitment or demographic turnover. Using genome‐wide SNP data, we compared Bd‐naïve and Bd‐endemic populations and two 11‐year temporal resampling contrasts. Candidate SNPs were annotated to identify genomic context, nearby genes, putative functions and overlap with previously reported Bd‐associated transcriptomic responses. Using an empirical 99th‐percentile XtX threshold, scans identified high‐differentiation candidate SNPs in all contrasts. Most occurred in noncoding and putatively regulatory regions, with relatively few canonical immune genes. Candidate‐associated genes were more often linked to signalling, transcriptional regulation and cell‐cycle processes. A descriptive comparison with previous work in the species identified 64 candidate‐associated genes matching Bd‐associated transcriptomic annotations, supporting several immune‐adjacent, regulatory, cellular and reproduction candidates. Persistence under endemic Bd might reflect pathogen‐associated selection, compensatory recruitment and demographic change following recurrent adult mortality rather than uniform adaptive rescue through immune resistance.

articles.title: Active locomotion predictively rescues head direction attractor dynamics in head-fixed mice
articles.abstract: Head direction cells in the anterodorsal thalamic nuclei provide a compass-like signal in the brain. Here, the authors investigate how head fixation and behavioural state impact head-direction attractor dynamics.

articles.title: Complementary axes of functional system integrity and integration with divergent clinical correlates characterize focal epilepsy
articles.abstract: Zhang and colleagues identify two complementary aspects of brain network topology in focal epilepsy, with system integrity showing modest preferential associations with cognition and system integration with clinical features.

articles.title: Dual-point-groups engineering enable multi-ultrahigh-Q resonances via Brillouin zone folding in tetramer metasurfaces
articles.abstract: A dual-point group framework of constructing multiple ultrahigh-Q resonances within tetramer metasurfaces with a C4v symmetry via Brillouin zone folding is developed, enabling high-performance nanophotonic devices like sum frequency generation and laser.

articles.title: Emergence of diffusion models from associative memory through memorization and generalization
articles.abstract: Viewing Diffusion Models through the lens of Dense Associative Memory theory reveals that spurious states, traditionally viewed as memory errors, are in fact a critical intermediate phase of generalization. Here, authors demonstrate their existence across a wide range of architectures and datasets.

articles.title: Evaluating anonymized genome re-identification using polygenic predictions and its implications for data privacy
articles.abstract: Although anonymized genomes can in principle be re-identified by predicting traits through Polygenic Scores, the authors show that in realistic settings the risk is negligible, alleviating privacy concerns around sharing anonymized genomes.

articles.title: Holographic focused ultrasound enables multitarget EV and MSC delivery for neurovascular repair after ischemic stroke
articles.abstract: Noninvasive multitarget delivery to peri-infarct regions after ischemic stroke remains challenging. Here, authors use holographic focused ultrasound to deliver EVs and MSCs to infarct borders, promoting neurovascular repair in mice.

articles.title: NYNRIN safeguards leukemia stem cells by sustaining thioredoxin activity to maintain redox homeostasis
articles.abstract: In patients with acute myeloid leukaemia (AML), the presence of leukaemic stem cells (LSCs) promotes resistance to therapy and is associated with poor prognosis. Here, the authors demonstrate that NYNRIN protects LSCs from oxidative stress by maintaining thioredoxin activity, identifying NYNRIN as a potential therapeutic target in AML.

articles.title: Spatiotemporal proteomics reveals dynamic antiparallel gradients shaping signalling waves
articles.abstract: Researchers map rhythmic protein changes in developing mouse embryos and reveal how dynamic, antiparallel RSPO3 and LGR4 patterns shape signalling waves that control the formation of body segments contributing to the spine.

articles.title: Divarasib as Compared with Sotorasib or Adagrasib in KRAS G12C–Mutated NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundDivarasib, a next-generation, oral KRAS G12C inhibitor, is more potent and selective in vitro than the first-generation KRAS G12C inhibitors sotorasib and adagrasib.MethodsIn this phase 3, international, open-label trial, patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomly assigned to receive divarasib orally at a dose of 400 mg once daily or control treatment (sotorasib orally at a dose of 960 mg once daily or adagrasib orally at a dose of 600 mg twice daily) until the occurrence of disease progression, unacceptable adverse events, loss of clinical benefit, withdrawal of consent, death, or trial termination. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival, confirmed overall response, duration of response, patient-reported outcomes, and safety.ResultsA total of 338 patients received divarasib (167 patients) or control treatment (171 patients; 156 received sotorasib and 15 received adagrasib). The median follow-up was 14.3 months. The median progression-free survival was 9.8 months with divarasib and 5.7 months with control treatment (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.58; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.44 to 0.76; PConclusionsAmong patients with previously treated KRAS G12C-mutated advanced or metastatic NSCLC, divarasib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than control treatment. (Supported by F. Hoffmann-La Roche; Krascendo 1 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06497556.).

articles.title: Osimertinib–Savolitinib in Advanced NSCLC after Progression during EGFR-TKI Therapy
articles.abstract: BackgroundSavolitinib is an oral, potent, highly selective MET-tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI). Combination therapy with savolitinib and osimertinib, an epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-TKI, has shown activity in patients with EGFR-mutated, advanced non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both, after progression during EGFR-TKI therapy.MethodsIn this international, phase 3, open-label trial, we randomly assigned, in a 1:1 ratio, patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression (staining intensity of 3+ for MET in ≥90% of tumor cells on immunohistochemical analysis), MET amplification (≥10 gene copies on fluorescence in situ hybridization), or both whose disease had progressed during osimertinib therapy to receive osimertinib (at a dose of 80 mg once daily) plus savolitinib (300 mg twice daily) or intravenous platinum-pemetrexed. The primary end point was progression-free survival, as assessed by blinded independent central review. Secondary end points included overall survival and safety.ResultsOf the 1746 patients screened, 338 were randomly assigned to receive osimertinib-savolitinib (171 patients) or platinum-pemetrexed (167 patients). Osimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free survival than platinum-pemetrexed (hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.55; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.42 to 0.72; PConclusionsOsimertinib-savolitinib led to significantly longer progression-free and overall survival than platinum-pemetrexed among patients with EGFR-mutated, locally advanced or metastatic NSCLC with MET overexpression, MET amplification, or both that had progressed during osimertinib therapy (Funded by AstraZeneca; SAFFRON ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT05261399.).

articles.title: Sacituzumab Tirumotecan plus Pembrolizumab in PD-L1–Negative Advanced NSCLC
articles.abstract: BackgroundPembrolizumab plus chemotherapy with a platinum-based agent and pemetrexed is a widely used standard first-line treatment option for patients with programmed death ligand 1 (PD-L1)-negative advanced nonsquamous non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) without targetable genomic alterations, but outcomes remain suboptimal.MethodsIn this phase 3, open-label, randomized trial, we evaluated sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab in patients with previously untreated locally advanced or metastatic nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations and a PD-L1 tumor proportion score of less than 1%. Patients were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. The primary end point was progression-free survival as assessed by blinded independent central review. Overall survival was a secondary end point. This report presents the results of the prespecified interim analysis.ResultsA total of 455 patients were randomly assigned to receive sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab (229 patients) or chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (226 patients). After a median follow-up of 9.7 months, the median progression-free survival was significantly longer with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab than with chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab (15.0 months vs. 5.7 months; hazard ratio for disease progression or death, 0.49; 95% confidence interval [CI], 0.36 to 0.65; PConclusionsAmong patients with PD-L1-negative advanced nonsquamous NSCLC without targetable genomic alterations, first-line treatment with sacituzumab tirumotecan plus pembrolizumab led to significantly longer progression-free survival than chemotherapy plus pembrolizumab. (Funded by Sichuan Kelun-Biotech Biopharmaceutical; OptiTROP-Lung06 ClinicalTrials.gov number, NCT06711900.).
