articles.title: A license to disperse: climatic niche lability and geographic expansion shape the diversification of Oleaceae
articles.abstract: SEM for seven variables (rPC1, rPC2, rPC3, rFRic, FRic, dispersal, and speciation) in Oleaceae and that in Jasmineae and Oleeae, respectively. Summary Patterns of species diversity reflect interactions among ecological, biogeographic, and lineage‐specific evolutionary processes. Oleaceae provides a useful comparative system because its five tribes differ markedly in species richness, geographic extent, dispersal history, and genomic background. Using distribution data for 476 species and a time‐calibrated phylogeny of 283 Oleaceae species spanning all five tribes, we integrated ecological niche modelling, ancestral‐range and climatic‐niche reconstruction, diversification‐rate analyses, and phylogenetic comparative methods while accounting for uneven tribal sampling. Climatic niche position and breadth evolved heterogeneously across Oleaceae, while major range expansions beyond the reconstructed ancestral Asian region were concentrated in Jasmineae and Oleeae. Climatic niche evolution and speciation rates were not consistently coupled; rather, their relationships with dispersal and diversification were lineage‐ and climatic‐axis‐specific. Oleeae showed more coordinated associations among niche evolution, dispersal, and speciation, whereas Jasmineae exhibited a more restricted, axis‐specific pattern. The ancient whole‐genome duplication (WGD) in Oleeae may have contributed to its distinctive evolutionary trajectory. Overall, our results support a conditional ‘license to disperse’ framework in which climatic niche lability facilitates geographic expansion, thereby indirectly increasing opportunities for diversification.

articles.title: A single‐nucleus multiome profiling reveals the regulatory programs driving plant nematode–induced syncytium
articles.abstract: Single‐nucleus transcriptome profiles of Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytium on Arabidopsis roots. Summary Plant‐parasitic cyst nematodes induce the formation of specialized feeding structures, known as syncytia, within host roots by orchestrating extensive transcriptional and epigenetic reprogramming. Here, we generated parallel single‐nucleus RNA‐seq and ATAC‐seq libraries from fully developed Heterodera schachtii–induced syncytia on Arabidopsis roots. We analyzed high‐quality transcriptome and chromatin profiles independently and in an integrated framework. We identified multiple transcriptomic cell states, several of which were highly syncytium‐enriched and spanned vascular and cortical identities. Differential expression analysis identified hundreds of syncytium‐enriched genes, and pseudotime trajectory inference points to potential compartmentalization or functional heterogeneity of syncytium nuclei, consistent with the possibility of distinct transcriptional programs within or between mature syncytia. Joint clustering of snATAC‐seq with snRNA‐seq delineated syncytium‐unique chromatin accessibility landscapes, with several cell states exhibiting extensive open chromatin linked to upregulated genes. Motif enrichment across these accessible regions highlighted cis‐regulatory elements mainly for AP2, bZIP, bHLH, MYB, and TCP transcription factors and identified functionally validated members of these families as candidate regulators of syncytium identity. Our study establishes a multiome atlas of syncytial cells and uncovers the regulatory programs driving nematode feeding site maintenance, as well as transcriptionally distinct nuclear states that may reflect functional specialization within or between the syncytia.

articles.title: Frenemies forever: when parasitic fungi become an insect's secret weapon
articles.abstract: Insect symbiotic yeast and fungi shape host–plant interactions. Summary Plant‐feeding insects pose a major threat to global food production, and finding sustainable pest control strategies is challenging. Insect‐associated symbiotic microorganisms fulfill important beneficial functions for their host insects, enabling them to adapt and thrive in a changing environment. Understanding how these interactions evolve and what they mean for insect–plant interactions is key to the development of novel targets and potential tools for pest control. Since yeast and fungal insect symbionts are understudied in comparison to bacterial symbionts, this Tansley Insight explores their role in insect–plant interactions.

articles.title: High‐light adaptation via ferredoxin‐mediated tuning of the photosynthesis–photoprotection trade‐off
articles.abstract: Proposed model of the alternative regulation of the photosynthesis in Fd1‐OE Nicotiana tabacum plants. Summary Plants continuously adjust photosynthesis to balance growth and photoprotection under changing environmental conditions. Environmental fluctuations frequently impose a mismatch between energy production and CO2 assimilation. How photochemical reactions are regulated to maintain performance under these conditions remains a central question in plant biology. We previously developed transplastomic tobacco (Fd1‐OE plants) overexpressing ferredoxin displaying enhanced photoprotection and growth penalties with a variegated leaf phenotype under glasshouse conditions. Here, we investigate how these plants respond to different growth irradiances using physiological, ultrastructural, and photosynthetic analyses, including Pulse‐Amplitude Modulation (PAM), gas exchange, and P700 absorbance measurements, and dynamic‐light assays. Fd1‐OE plants progressively recovered growth, leaf phenotype, and photosynthetic performance as growth irradiance increased, reaching near wild‐type performance at 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. This enhanced adaptation to ‘high‐light’ was associated with a larger fraction of open Photosystem II reaction centers and enhanced nonphotochemical quenching. Dynamic‐light analyses further revealed faster plastoquinone (PQ) turnover, a more oxidized (PQ) pool and enhanced electron withdrawal downstream of Photosystem I. Our results indicate that ferredoxin overexpression redefines the balance between photochemistry and photoprotection. This adjustment shifts adaptation toward higher irradiance and enhances photosynthetic performance under changing light environments. Electron partitioning downstream of Photosystem I emerges as a promising target to improve photosynthetic resilience. Resumen Las plantas regulan continuamente la fotosíntesis para equilibrar el crecimiento y la fotoprotección frente a condiciones ambientales cambiantes. Las fluctuaciones ambientales imponen con frecuencia un desajuste entre la producción de energía y la asimilación de CO2. La forma en que se regulan las reacciones fotoquímicas para mantener el rendimiento bajo estas condiciones continúa siendo una cuestión central en la biología vegetal. Previamente desarrollamos plantas de tabaco transplastómicas (Fd1‐OE) que sobreexpresan ferredoxina y presentan una fotoprotección mejorada, junto con penalizaciones en el crecimiento y un fenotipo foliar variegado bajo condiciones de invernadero. En este trabajo, investigamos cómo estas plantas responden a diferentes irradiancias de crecimiento mediante análisis fisiológicos, ultraestructurales y fotosintéticos, incluyendo mediciones con PAM, intercambio gaseoso y absorbancia de P700, así como ensayos bajo luz dinámica. Las plantas Fd1‐OE recuperaron progresivamente el crecimiento, el fenotipo foliar y el rendimiento fotosintético a medida que aumentó la irradiancia de crecimiento, alcanzando un rendimiento cercano al del tipo silvestre a 1400 μmol m−2 s−1. Esta mayor adaptación a condiciones de ‘alta luz’ se asocia con una mayor fracción de centros de reacción del fotosistema II abiertos y un mayor NPQ. Los análisis bajo luz dinámica revelaron además una mayor velocidad de recambio de las plastoquinonas, un pool de plastoquinonas más oxidado y una mayor extracción de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I. Nuestros resultados indican que la sobreexpresión de ferredoxina redefine el equilibrio entre la fotoquímica y la fotoprotección. Este ajuste desplaza la adaptación hacia irradiancias más altas y mejora el rendimiento fotosintético frente a entornos lumínicos cambiantes. La partición de electrones cadena abajo del fotosistema I emerge como un blanco prometedor para mejorar la resiliencia fotosintética.

articles.title: Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy mediates the strength of diversity–disease relationships in natural grasslands
articles.abstract: Overview of the study sites. Summary The relationship between biodiversity and disease risk is a cornerstone of disease ecology, yet predicting its direction and strength remains challenging. Pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies may be key to resolving this context dependency, but their roles in mediating diversity–disease relationships are poorly understood. Here, we combine a large‐scale survey spanning 2000 km in natural grasslands with advanced statistical modeling to demonstrate that pathogen nutrient acquisition strategy is a critical mediator. We show that diseases caused by biotrophic pathogens (e.g. rusts and powdery mildews), which depend on living host tissues, exhibit a significantly negative diversity–disease relationship, whereas diseases caused by necrotrophic pathogens (e.g. leaf spots and blights) show no significant relationship. Furthermore, the strength of this negative relationship for biotrophic pathogens is amplified in regions with higher disease severity. Bayesian structural equation modeling reveals that plant species richness directly reduces biotrophic disease severity, while for necrotrophic pathogens, precipitation is the primary driver of severity, with no direct effect of richness. Our findings provide a trait‐based framework linking climatic drivers, pathogen nutrient acquisition strategies, and the strength of diversity–disease relationships. These results enhance our ability to predict disease dynamics under biodiversity loss and inform biodiversity‐based disease management strategies.

articles.title: Phosphatidylcholine acyl turnover facilitates thylakoid lipid remodeling and promotes plant survival under heat stress
articles.abstract: Coordinated galactolipid–TAG conversion during heat stress–induced thylakoid lipid remodeling. Summary Heat stress destabilizes chloroplast membranes, requiring rapid lipid remodeling to maintain photosynthetic function. Although thylakoid lipid remodeling and triacylglycerol (TAG) accumulation are established heat responses, the role of phosphatidylcholine (PC) acyl turnover remains unclear. We investigated lysophosphatidylcholine acyltransferase 1 and 2 (LPCAT1/2), REDUCED OLEATE DESATURATION1 (ROD1), phospholipid:diacylglycerol acyltransferase 1 (PDAT1), and lipins in heat‐induced lipid remodeling and thermotolerance in Arabidopsis thaliana. Using genetic, lipidomic, physiological, and photosynthetic analyses, we examined mutants defective in PC acyl editing, PC–diacylglycerol (DAG) interconversion, TAG synthesis, and phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation during heat stress. Loss of LPCAT1/2 severely impaired basal and acquired thermotolerance, caused irreversible photosystem II damage, and disrupted thylakoid lipid remodeling. rod1 showed minor defects, whereas rod1 lpcat1/2 exhibited enhanced thermosensitivity. In mature vegetative plants, pdat1‐2 showed thermotolerance and photosystem II defects comparable to lpcat1/2. Lipin‐mediated phosphatidic acid dephosphorylation provided the major DAG source for heat‐induced TAG synthesis. Defective PC acyl turnover also increased free fatty acids and lipid peroxidation. These findings establish LPCAT1/2‐mediated PC acyl turnover as a central regulator of heat‐induced membrane remodeling and thermotolerance and link lipin‐dependent DAG production and TAG synthesis with chloroplast membrane homeostasis.

articles.title: Neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and chemotherapy versus standard of care for locally advanced rectal cancer (UNION): a prespecified interim analysis of a multicentre, open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial
articles.abstract: BackgroundTo our knowledge, UNION is the first phase 3 trial to assess a neoadjuvant strategy incorporating radiotherapy, immunotherapy, and chemotherapy compared with standard care in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, which reported positive results for the primary endpoint (blinded independent review committee [BIRC]-assessed pathological complete response rate; 39·8% vs 15·3%). Here, we present a prespecified interim analysis of event-free survival.MethodsThis open-label, randomised, phase 3 trial was conducted at nine hospitals in China. Eligible patients were aged 18-75 years with untreated cT3-4 or N+ rectal adenocarcinoma (≤10 cm distance from the anal verge) and an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status of 0 or 1. Patients were randomly assigned (1:1; stratified by clinical T stage and N stage), using permuted blocks, to receive neoadjuvant short-course radiotherapy (25 Gy in five fractions) followed by two cycles of intravenous camrelizumab (200 mg on day 1) plus CAPOX (oral capecitabine 1000 mg/m2 twice daily on days 1-14 and intravenous oxaliplatin 130 mg/m2 on day 1; experimental group) or long-course chemoradiotherapy (50·4 Gy in 28 fractions with concurrent oral capecitabine 825 mg/m2 twice daily) followed by two cycles of CAPOX (standard-of-care group). After surgery, both groups received six cycles of adjuvant CAPOX, and the experimental group additionally received adjuvant camrelizumab for up to 15 cycles. The primary endpoint was BIRC-assessed pathological complete response rate in the intention-to-treat population, which has been previously reported. Here, we performed a prespecified interim analysis of investigator-assessed event-free survival (one of the key secondary endpoints, defined as time from randomisation to radiographic progression precluding surgery, local recurrence or distant metastasis, or death) in the intention-to-treat population (all randomly assigned patients) with a boundary of a two-sided p values less than 0·0102. Safety was evaluated in all patients who received at least one dose of the study treatment according to the assigned regimen. The study was registered with ClinicalTrials.gov, NCT04928807, and is active, but no longer recruiting.FindingsBetween July 23, 2021, and March 1, 2023, 231 patients (153 [66%] males and 78 [34%] females; 227 [98%] were Han Chinese, and four [2%] were other ethnicity Chinese) were randomly assigned to the experimental group (n=113) and standard-of-care group (n=118). As of Oct 1, 2025, the median follow-up duration was 36·7 months (IQR 32·6-39·9) in the experimental group and 34·7 months (31·1-39·1) in the standard-of-care group. The 3-year investigator-assessed event-free survival rate was 91·3% (95% CI 83·9-95·4) in the experimental group versus 77·4% (67·9-84·4) in the standard-of-care group (stratified hazard ratio 0·33 [0·15-0·71]; two-sided log-rank p=0·0029). During the entire treatment period, the most common grade 3 or 4 treatment-related adverse events were decreased lymphocyte count (23 [20%] of 115 in the experimental group vs 31 [28%] of 112 in the standard-of-care group), decreased white blood cell count (13 [11%] vs 16 [14%]), decreased neutrophil count (13 [11%] vs 13 [12%]), and decreased platelet count (seven [6%] vs 15 [13%]). Treatment-related serious adverse events occurred in 22 (19%) versus 15 (13%) patients, with the most common being decreased platelet count (one [1%] vs six [5%]), and radiation gastroenteritis (two [2%] vs four [4%]). Treatment-related deaths occurred in one patient in the experimental group (septic shock related to chemotherapy, but unrelated to camrelizumab) and none in the standard-of-care group.InterpretationIn this interim analysis, short-course radiotherapy followed by camrelizumab and CAPOX significantly improved 3-year event-free survival in patients with locally advanced rectal cancer, with a safety profile similar to long-course chemoradiotherapy followed by CAPOX.…

articles.title: Methyl radicals dynamics on (100)--(2x1):H diamond surfaces based on refined variational transition state calculations of gas-surface reaction rate coefficients
articles.abstract: Theoretical modelling of diamond growth should ideally provide estimates of the growth rate depending on experimental conditions. To that end, a description of all possible reactions related to the competing adsorption, desorption and migration mechanisms is required. Here, we provide precise calculations of the reaction rate coefficient of methyl-related reactions on hydrogen-terminated (100) diamond surface, as $\mathrm{CH_3}$ is known to be the main growth precursor in chemical vapor deposition (CVD) growth of diamond. To achieve this goal, we successfully combined Density Functional Theory (DFT) and variational transition state theory (VTST), allowing to extend our analysis to barrierless reaction. Our rigorous treatment of the quasi-free rotation of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ adsorbates on the surface allows us to overcome numerical errors for the finite difference calculations of the vibrational spectra for evaluating the partition functions of the system. Our results suggest that the mechanism that deplete the $\mathrm{CH_3}$ concentration the most is the absorption on a surface radical site. We also evidence the anisotropy of $\mathrm{CH_3}$ migration along the dimer of the (100)-(2x1):H surface. In a more general perspective, the calculated reaction rates coefficient for methyl reactions and migration presented in this work, together with the data for hydrogen reaction and other main gas surface reactions, bridge the gap between the atomic-scale description and the large-scale modelling of diamond growth.

articles.title: Second order N-Electron Valence state Perturbation Theory for polaritonic systems
articles.abstract: Molecules strongly coupled to optical cavities often show multi-configurational character, which the cavity can enhance by mixing electronic states. Describing them accurately requires a complete treatment of correlation between all the involved quantum particles. The available QED ab-initio methods do not treat it in its completeness except for QED-FCI. We extend second-order N-electron valence state perturbation theory (NEVPT2) to polaritonic chemistry, in its state-specific (QED-NEVPT2) and quasi degenerate (QED-QD-NEVPT2) forms. Here, the correlation due to the interaction of more degenerate configurations comes from a QED-CASSCF reference, while that associated with instantaneous interactions between the particles is added by second-order perturbation theory. Application of the methods to ammonia, ethylene and formaldimine revealed that this approach represents the perfect alternative to the well established QED-Coupled Cluster approach when the molecular system is described by more degenerate configurations. The approaches developed in this work have the potential to become state-of-the-art methodologies for the description of reactivity and photochemistry in polaritonic systems.

articles.title: Disrupting Interfacial Hydrogen-Bonding Networks via Dynamic Reconstruction Strategy for Enhanced CO2-to-C2+ Electrocatalysis
articles.abstract: The morphology and microenvironment of ion-conducting polymers (ionomers) on the catalyst electrode surface critically govern the CO2 electrocatalytic performance. Herein, we report a dual-reconstruction strategy that synergistically tailors the surface structure of the Nafion ionomer using positively charged molecules and solvent effect. By combining a low-dielectric-constant solvent (isopropanol) with arginine cations, the optimized electrode achieves an 83.6% Faradaic efficiency for multicarbon (C2+) products at a high current density of –500 mA cm–2 in 1 M KOH. Based on experimental characterization and MD simulations, we propose a structural model in which the Nafion side chains are oriented away from both the catalyst surface and the electrolyte phase. In situ spectroscopic analyses, theoretical calculation, and experimental evidence suggest that this structural reorganization disrupts the interfacial hydrogen-bonding network, suppresses the competing hydrogen evolution reaction, improves effective gaseous CO2 accessibility, and facilitates C–C coupling along an energetically favorable *OC–COH pathway. This work provides valuable insights into microenvironment engineering of ionomer–catalyst interfaces for efficient CO2 electrolysis.

articles.title: Gallium-Containing ZSM-5 Zeolites Improve Hydrocracking Selectivity to Propane
articles.abstract: Polyolefin hydrocracking over Brønsted acidic ZSM-5 produces light hydrocarbons with narrow product distributions, but further increases in propane and butane selectivity are required to improve process economics and sustainability. Here, we examined the effect of various metal and metal oxide dopants, namely Pt, Pt-Sn, SnOx, ZnOx, and GaOx, on ZSM-5-mediated polyolefin hydrocracking and identified GaOx as a selective promoter for light gas formation. Incorporation of gallium oxide (3 wt % Ga) was shown to increase propane selectivity from 40 c-wt %, achieved over ZSM-5, to near 60 c-wt %, reaching a combined propane and butane selectivity of 85 c-wt %, while maintaining solids conversion. To elucidate the role of gallium oxide, we used ex situ and operando characterization techniques to probe acidity, local coordination environment, and the spatial distribution of GaOx species. Extra-framework gallium oxide introduced via incipient wetness impregnation reduced the measured acid site density from 1275 to 911 μmol g–1, decreased the Brønsted/Lewis acid site ratio, and formed a high-coverage GaOx layer on the external surface of the zeolite. Operando experiments show that Ga is present in both Ga3+ and Ga1+ under reaction conditions. Attempts to disperse gallium oxide through reductive pretreatments led to an increase in the Lewis acid site concentration and a 10 c-wt % decrease in propane selectivity, highlighting the importance of the specific location, structural, and acidic configurations. Systematic variation of impregnation methods to control location and dispersion revealed a synergistic interaction between gallium oxide and zeolite acid sites, with propane selectivity strongly influenced by spatial proximity of GaOx to acid sites. Furthermore, vapor-phase flow reactions with a model compound demonstrated a decrease in intermediate product formation compared to the zeolite alone. The optimized catalyst was validated across diverse polyolefin substrates and resulted in similar increases to propane selectivity, yielding >80 c-wt % combined C3–C4 selectivity across the range of polyolefin substrates.

articles.title: Stabilizing Cobalt Sites with d10-Configured p-Block Cations for Iridium-Free Proton Exchange Membrane Water Electrolysis
articles.abstract: Proton exchange membrane water electrolysis (PEMWE) requires anode catalysts that sustain acidic oxygen evolution in practical stacks with minimal noble-metal content. Cobalt spinel oxides are cost-attractive but dissolve rapidly in acid as cobalt sites over-oxidize under anodic bias. Here we show that incorporation of d10-configured p-block cations (Sb, Ge, In, and Ga) into Co3O4 stabilizes cobalt sites by promoting robust heterometallic Co–O–M interactions. Density functional theory predicts dopant-driven charge redistribution that suppresses over-oxidation of octahedral Co while maintaining favorable binding of oxygen intermediates. Operando Co K-edge X-ray absorption and time-resolved dissolution measurements confirm reduced oxidation-state dynamics and cobalt loss, whereas a d-block d10 control (Zn) shows no such stabilization. In a PEMWE single cell at 80 °C, Sb/Co3O4 reaches >3500 mA cm–2 at 2.0 V and operates for >1000 h at 250 mA cm–2. This work establishes p-block d10 incorporation as a general route to iridium-free PEMWE anodes.

articles.title: Robust Full-Spectrum-Responsive Multi-junction Tandem Solar Cells via Enhanced Near-Infrared Photon Harvesting
articles.abstract: Developing robust multi-junction tandem photovoltaics remains constrained by the instability of mixed-halide perovskite subcells, given their dominating contribution to overall power output. Integrating near-infrared (NIR) PbS quantum dots (QDs) with FAPbBr3 and crystalline silicon (c-Si) broadens spectrum utilization while improving overall operational stability by reducing the perovskite power contribution. However, enlarged (100) facets and the trade-off between film thickness and quality limit efficient NIR photon harvesting. Herein, a Lewis-basic dihydrazide molecule achieves universal passivation across diverse PbS QD facets via synergistic lead chelation and hydrogen-bonding interactions. Consequently, 0.8 eV PbS QD solar cells with a 685 nm-thick active layer achieve a short-circuit current density of 41.31 mA cm–2 and a 1100-nm-filtered efficiency of 1.80%. The resulting FAPbBr3/c-Si/PbS triple-junction tandems achieve a promising efficiency of 31.04%, with the perovskite subcell contributing 30.4% of the total power output, demonstrating a well-matched operational lifetime. This work offers a strategic framework for efficient multi-junction tandem photovoltaics.

articles.title: Think Simple, Communicate Better
All-in-One Mitochondria-Targeted Iron-Based MOF “Nanomissiles” for Synergistically Potentiated Tumor Ferroptosis, Dual Phototherapy, and Chemotherapy
articles.abstract: Pronounced heterogeneity and adaptability of tumors inherently curtail monotherapeutic efficacy, necessitating rationally integrated multimodal regimens that enable precise intervention, overcome resistance, and eradicate heterogeneous cell populations within the complex tumor microenvironment (TME). All-in-one mitochondria-targeted “nanomissiles” were created by emodin (Em)-Fe3+-gated, doxorubicin (DOX)-loaded PCN-600(FeIII) (denoted as DOX@ME) nanoparticles for synergistic multimodal tumor therapy integrating ferroptosis, photodynamic therapy (PDT), mild photothermal therapy (MPTT), and chemotherapy. DOX@ME achieved on-demand release of DOX in response to the TME [such as low pH, glutathione (GSH), hydrogen peroxide (H2O2), and adenosine-5′-triphosphate (ATP)] and near-infrared laser, via the disassembly of the Em-Fe3+ gating films and/or the degradation of the PCN-600(FeIII) nanocarriers. Under both 660 and 808 nm laser irradiation, DOX@ME effectively triggered apoptosis via chemotherapy, PDT, and MPTT while robustly accelerating reactive oxygen species (ROS) generation, GSH depletion, glutathione peroxidase 4 (GPX4) downregulation, and lipid peroxide (LPO) accumulation to enhance ferroptosis. Moreover, DOX@ME could alleviate thermotolerance by depleting intracellular ATP and downregulating protective heat shock protein 70 to boost the curative efficacy of MPTT. DOX@ME exhibited excellent antitumor efficacy and good biocompatibility and biosafety in A549 tumor-bearing nude mice. Collectively, DOX@ME demonstrates robust clinical translational potential for precision cancer therapy.

articles.title: Disulfidptosis-Driven Immune-Activated Multimodal Therapy for Glioblastoma with Systemic Safety Control
articles.abstract: Effective glioblastoma therapy requires simultaneous solutions to poor blood–brain barrier (BBB) penetration, insufficient tumor-selective killing, and treatment-related systemic toxicity. We hypothesized that a BBB-penetrating nanoplatform capable of generating distinct H2S exposures in tumor and normal tissues could enhance antitumor efficacy while mitigating doxorubicin (DOX)-induced cardiotoxicity. Here, DOX-loaded metastable molybdenum disulfide nanoflowers functionalized with an I6P8 peptide (DOX@MSI) were developed. After BBB transport and tumor accumulation, the acidic, H2O2-rich, and GSH-rich microenvironment accelerates nanoplatform degradation, promoting GSH depletion and enhanced H2S/DOX release. High local H2S upregulates xCT, while H2S/DOX-mediated mitochondrial inhibition suppresses NADPH regeneration, synergistically triggering disulfidptosis. Meanwhile, H2S suppresses the JAK2/STAT3/IDO axis, alleviating DOX-induced immunosuppression and enhancing immunogenic cell death and T-cell-mediated antitumor immunity. In contrast, slower degradation under physiological conditions enables sustained low-level H2S release, reducing the level of oxidative stress and ERK-associated apoptosis in cardiomyocytes. Together with NIR-enhanced photothermal therapy, DOX@MSI suppresses orthotopic glioblastoma while reducing cardiac injury, thereby integrating tumor-selective multimodal therapy with active organ protection.

articles.title: Kinetic Access to Focal Conic Domains in Photonic Cellulose Nanocrystal Films
articles.abstract: Cellulose nanocrystals (CNCs) self-assemble into cholesteric structures that enable sustainable photonic films, but controlling their pitch, domain morphology, and angular color response remains challenging. Here, we investigate how salt concentration and sonication dose jointly regulate the evaporation-induced self-assembly of CNC suspensions. Across 24 dish-cast films, polarized optical microscopy, time-lapse imaging, rheology, electron microscopy, and angle-resolved spectroscopy reveal that these processing parameters affect not only the cholesteric pitch but also tactoid nucleation, transport, coalescence, and the onset of kinetic arrest. Increasing NaCl concentration generally blue-shifts the photonic response, whereas sonication red-shifts it by fragmenting CNC bundles, with the magnitude of this effect decreasing as ionic content increases. At intermediate ionic content, low sonication doses produce extended cholesteric domains with comparatively narrow spectral responses, while the abundance of focal conic domains (FCDs) increases with sonication dose, culminating in FCD-rich films at moderate sonication. Refined parameter scans show that FCDs form within a finite processing window. Time-lapse imaging shows that FCDs appear abruptly after tactoid growth and coalescence, as macroscopic motion becomes strongly restricted during late-stage evaporation. Concentration- and residence-time-dependent rheology further demonstrates that the material response evolves throughout the assembly pathway. The FCD-rich film retains a narrow local reflection band while exhibiting the smallest angular displacement of the reflection maximum among the films examined. These findings show that salt and sonication regulate the kinetic accessibility of elastically driven focal conic structures, providing a route to tune domain morphology, spectral bandwidth, and iridescence in CNC photonic films.

articles.title: Mechanics-Guided Conformal Probes Enable Crystallographically Resolved Anisotropic Interlayer Friction Measurements in Low-Symmetry 2D Materials
articles.abstract: Interlayer sliding in two-dimensional (2D) materials is generally assumed to be weakly anisotropic, even as low-symmetry layered crystals with strongly direction-dependent properties continue to emerge. Here we adopt a mechanics-guided conformal probe design that enables quantitative measurement of crystallographically resolved interlayer friction between anisotropic 2D materials. Using Ta2NiSe5 as a model system, we demonstrate pronounced interlayer friction anisotropy approaching 2 orders of magnitude, substantially larger than its moderate in-plane friction anisotropy and the values reported for high-symmetry layered materials. Atomic-resolution lateral force mapping reveals a hierarchical friction landscape composed of atomic lattice corrugation and twist-induced moiré modulation, with the moiré wavelength evolving systematically with relative misorientation. These results show that interlayer friction in low-symmetry 2D materials is governed by a multiscale, orientation-dependent potential energy landscape and constitutes an independent mechanical degree of freedom. The conformal probe platform provides a general route to probe and engineer direction-selective interlayer mechanics in van der Waals systems.

articles.title: Cryo-EM and biochemical characterization of a BRAF/CRAF heterodimer shows that the NtA motif negative charge is dispensable for RAF activation
articles.abstract: Upon RAS-driven membrane recruitment, RAF kinases ARAF, BRAF, and CRAF are activated through homo- or heterodimerization to initiate MAP kinase signaling. Although RAF heterodimers drive physiologic and oncogenic signaling, they remain little studied structurally and biochemically. Here, we report the preparation, biochemical characterization, and cryo-EM structures of 14-3-3-bound BRAF/CRAF heterodimer complexes. The heterodimer exhibits kinetic parameters and RAF inhibitor sensitivities intermediate between, or closely matching, BRAF and CRAF homodimers. Cryo-EM structures reveal an organization identical to RAF homodimers, with an asymmetric interaction unique to the MEK1-bound structure in which the BRAF acidic NtA motif engages the CRAF RKTR motif. Mutagenesis reveals that replacing the acidic NtA sequence with basic RARA yields active dimers, showing that negative charge is dispensable for activity. Collectively, our findings suggest the NtA charge state influences RAF activity through effects on local backbone dynamics and inactive-state stability, rather than via stereospecific recognition across the dimer interface.

articles.title: Infection history and TCR sequence features shape the breadth of TCR cross-reactivity
articles.abstract: The T cell receptor (TCR) repertoire enables recognition of a vast array of pathogens, despite containing far fewer unique TCRs than the diversity of encountered epitopes. This potential contradiction is resolved by TCR cross-reactivity, whereby individual TCRs recognize multiple distinct epitopes. However, the features defining broadly cross-reactive TCRs remain poorly understood. Here we systematically analyze TCRs from mice sequentially infected with influenza viruses containing naturally occurring single amino acid variants of the DbNP366 epitope. We identify 967 unique paired TCR sequences across 18 infection histories and test 22 representative TCRs against 172 epitope variants, yielding 3,784 TCR-epitope interaction measurements. These TCRs exhibit a continuum of cross-reactivity, with infection history influencing both TCR sequence similarity and reactivity profiles. We find specific TCR sequence features associated with broader cross-reactivity, highlighting the interplay between epitope exposure, TCR diversity, and function, and providing insights into CD8+ T cell adaptability, immune memory, and vaccine design.

Is It a “Hybrid Swarm”? Opportunities for More Informative Terminology in Conservation Genomics
articles.abstract: Hybridization is common in wild taxa, which may cause conservation concerns if hybridization occurs following disturbance or species introductions. High throughput DNA sequencing makes genomic analysis of many individuals feasible, vastly improving and promoting more studies on hybridization. However, more precise genomic identification of hybrids has not always extended to more precise use of terminology to describe hybrid ancestry. For hybridizing species of conservation concern, it is critical to understand hybridization dynamics precisely in order to effectively manage imperiled taxa. We conducted a review of 67 representative journal articles that use the term “hybrid swarm” in reference to hybridization, as variation in the usage of the term makes it difficult to understand which biological processes are being described. We found that “hybrid swarm” is used in several contexts across studies using various methods and numbers of genetic markers, reflecting vastly different statistical power and degrees of evidence for extensive hybridization. We encourage researchers working with genomic datasets to use clearer terminology when describing hybridization outcomes. We elaborate on scenario‐specific terminology to strengthen uniformity in hybridization language, which we hope will promote more precise descriptions of hybridization and improve the clarity of future research on hybridization.

articles.title: Turtle Herbivory Suppresses Seagrass Function but Reveals Recovery Potential in a Remote Coral Reef Atoll
articles.abstract: Seagrasses are recognised as ecologically and culturally significant habitats across the globe supporting human livelihoods, biodiversity, and carbon storage. In the Cocos (Keeling) Islands, a remote coral reef atoll in the eastern Indian Ocean, seagrasses provide ecosystem services and support culturally, ecologically, and economically important species. However, these meadows have suffered devastating declines, with ongoing green turtle herbivory identified as a key pressure restricting Thalassia hemprichii persistence. To examine how herbivory shapes seagrass traits and function, we compared plots protected from grazing for over two years using exclusion cages against continuously grazed plots across two sites. Seagrass traits at the meadow‐scale (shoot density, leaf area and biomass), as well as some functionality (primary production and nutrient storage capacity), were improved with protection from herbivory pressure. Substantial reductions in the belowground biomass in the grazed plots indicate that these seagrasses are operating under severe metabolic constraints. In contrast, some plant‐scale traits (photosynthetic rate and growth rate) were not altered despite ongoing herbivory pressure, indicating some capacity for recovery at the individual plant scale. Representing one of the longest turtle exclusion studies in seagrass ecosystems, these results demonstrate that herbivory is driving systemic degradation across multiple biological scales, but these seagrasses currently retain the capacity to recover once grazing pressure is reduced. Synthesis. Tropical seagrass meadows subjected to continuous herbivory pressure can persist in a chronically depleted state. Herbivore exclusion experiments demonstrate that reducing herbivory can unlock the recovery potential of seagrass. These findings highlight the need for nuanced management strategies to safeguard these meadows in a time where seagrasses continue to decline at both localised and global scales, and the global turtle populations are simultaneously on the rise.

articles.title: HOST MATTER: Parasite infection drives chemical reconfiguration of decomposing host and shapes insect behavioural responses
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Host–parasite interactions shape ecosystems by driving species dynamics, yet their influence is typically considered in terms of host mortality rather than the chemical environments generated during infection and decomposition. Here, we show that parasitic infection actively reconfigures the chemical phenotype of decomposing hosts, reshaping ecological interactions through volatile‐mediated signalling. Using soil‐dwelling parasites‐entomopathogenic nematodes (EPNs) and their symbiotic bacteria‐as a model system, we integrate behavioural assays, comprehensive volatolomic characterization and CO2 quantification across three insect orders and two EPN species over four post‐mortem intervals. We demonstrate that EPN‐infection generates a distinct and conserved volatile signature dominated by carboxylic acids, sulphur‐containing compounds and unsaturated hydrocarbons, accompanied by elevated CO2 emissions. These infection‐derived blends elicit contrasting behavioural responses: they repel non‐natural hosts while consistently attracting natural hosts, indicating that infected cadavers function as chemically structured information hubs. In contrast, frozen‐killed insects exhibit fermentation‐type profiles, and bacteria‐only infection produce simplified alkane‐dominated blends, demonstrating that the full chemical phenotype emerges from the nematode–bacteria complex. Our findings reveal parasitic infection as a process that reorganizes decomposition chemistry with measurable behavioural consequences, uncovering a previously underappreciated mechanism by which parasites structure soil food webs and influence multitrophic interactions. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog.

articles.title: Local adaptation to host plants in herbivorous insects: A meta‐analysis
articles.abstract: Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Abstract Local adaptation, wherein populations are well‐adapted to local biotic and abiotic conditions, is a common outcome of natural selection and a driver of diversification. Previous theory identified two criteria to detect local adaptation: (a) the home‐away criterion compares the fitness of a population in its home environment to its fitness in a different environment and (b) the local‐foreign criterion examines differences in fitness between a local and a foreign population when experiencing the local environment. We conducted a meta‐analysis synthesizing empirical evidence of insect herbivores' local adaptation to their host plants using both criteria to assess how diet breadth, geographic distance among populations, herbivore taxonomic affiliation, herbivore clonality, the herbivore response variable measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and features of the study design impact the likelihood of detecting local adaptation. Overall, we found patterns consistent with herbivore local adaptation using both the home‐away and local‐foreign criteria. Herbivore diet breadth, taxonomic affiliation and geographic distance between herbivore populations did not affect the likelihood of finding local adaptation. In contrast, the detection of local adaptation varied with herbivore clonality, the specific response variables measured, taxonomic distance among host plants and elements of the experimental design. These findings clarify the conditions under which local adaptation emerges in the world's most diverse group of multicellular organisms. Read the free Plain Language Summary for this article on the Journal blog. Resumen La adaptación local consiste en el desarrollo de características que permiten un mejor desempeño de las poblaciones en las condiciones bióticas y abióticas de su entorno. Este fenómeno es una consecuencia común de la selección natural y uno de los mecanismos de diversificación biológica. Se han identificado dos criterios para detectar adaptación local: (a) el criterio ‘en casa‐fuera de casa’ que compara la adecuación de una población en su propio ambiente contra la adecuación de esa misma población en un ambiente foráneo; y (b) el criterio ‘local‐forastero’, que compara la adecuación de dos poblaciones, una local y otra foránea, cuando habitan el ambiente natal de cada una de ellas. Utilizamos un meta‐análisis para sintetizar evidencia empírica de la adaptación local de insectos herbívoros a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con cada uno de los criterios anteriores. Este análisis nos permitió evaluar el efecto de la amplitud de la dieta, distancia geográfica, afiliación taxonómica del herbívoro, clonalidad, variable de respuesta, distancia taxonómica entre la planta local y la foránea, y características del diseño experimental, en la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Encontramos patrones consistentes con la noción de que los insectos herbívoros exhiben adaptación local a sus plantas hospederas de acuerdo con ambos criterios. Adicionalmente, encontramos que la amplitud de la dieta, afiliación taxonómica y la distancia geográfica entre las poblaciones de herbívoros no afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local. Por el contrario, variables que sí afectaron la probabilidad de detectar adaptación local incluyen la clonalidad del herbívoro, la variable de respuesta que se utilizó para evaluar el desempeño del herbívoro, la distancia taxonómica entre las plantas local y foránea, y algunos elementos del diseño experimental. Nuestros resultados contribuyen al esclarecimiento de las condiciones que determinan la ocurrencia de adaptación local en el grupo más diverso de organismos multicelulares.

articles.title: Biodegradable and Non‐Biodegradable Microplastics Drive Divergent Microbial Carbon and Nitrogen Metabolism Regimes in Soil–Plant Systems
articles.abstract: The accumulation of microplastics (MPs) in soils worldwide has raised concerns about their potential impacts on microbially mediated carbon (C) and nitrogen (N) cycling. However, whether biodegradable and non‐biodegradable MPs differently affect microbial C and N metabolism and coupling, and whether these responses are modulated by co‐occurring plant identity remain uncertain. We combined a meta‐analysis with a controlled pot experiment comparing soil responses under two congeneric plant species exposed to two biodegradable and two non‐biodegradable MPs at doses ranging from 0% to 2% (w/w). In the meta‐analysis, MPs generally increased CO2 emission and microbial biomass N (MBN), but had no significant overall effect on microbial biomass C (MBC). In the pot experiment, MPs likewise increased CO2 emission, whereas overall effect sizes of MBC and MBN were nonsignificant. Nevertheless, these overall responses did not capture the distinct patterns of microbial C–N metabolic coordination between MP types. Under biodegradable MPs, tighter MBC–MBN coupling with a dose‐dependent shift toward greater respiratory C loss relative to MBC collectively indicated a maintenance‐associated metabolic pattern. In contrast, MBC–MBN decoupling and stronger MBC–CO2 coupling under non‐biodegradable MPs indicated a biomass‐linked metabolic pattern. In addition, plant identity modulated these microbial metabolisms in an MP‐type manner, particularly in N‐related processes. These metabolic responses were accompanied with changes in soil property conditions and substrate availability, weakened DOC–DON coupling, and shifts in microbial community structure and life history strategy. RDA‐based hierarchical and variation partitioning and SEM further indicated that modeled soil property pathways were more prominent under non‐biodegradable MPs, while substrate‐related pathways were prominent under biodegradable MPs. Together, the meta‐analysis reveals the general microbial metabolic patterns under MP type, and the pot experiment further reveals how MP type and plant identity jointly influence microbial C–N metabolism through contrasting associations with soil substrates and property conditions.

articles.title: Conservative Spruce Outperforms Acquisitive Larch Under Warming and CO2
articles.abstract: Predicting boreal forest growth is hindered by limited experimental tests on the compounding effects of climate change and atmospheric CO2. We integrated regional tree‐ring data with a peatland warming and CO2 manipulation experiment, including 45 trait measurements, to assess growth responses of two widespread boreal conifers, Larix laricina and Picea mariana, to temperature, vapor pressure deficit (VPD), soil moisture, and elevated CO2. L. laricina growth was consistently more climate‐sensitive than P. mariana, increasing strongly with soil moisture and declining slightly with VPD at the regional scale, but responding positively to VPD and temperature—not soil moisture or CO2—at the experimental peatland. L. laricina's acquisitive strategy enhanced water and nutrient uptake, sustaining growth but reducing hydraulic safety. By contrast, P. mariana's conservative strategy maintained water‐use efficiency and hydraulic resilience without compromising growth. Our results challenge projections of widespread CO2 fertilization in boreal forests and highlight conservative conifers as potential winners under warming and drying, sustaining growth while maintaining low mortality risk. This dynamic could reshape projections of the boreal carbon sink and its role in global climate feedback.
